=== 0001c2da [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte Watcom NOP (lea eax,[eax+0]) before FUN_0001c2e0.

=== 0001c2e0 [PLATE]
Turns one battle unit to face another, writing the direction code from the unit's tile toward the target's tile into the unit's facing byte.

Algorithm:
Resolves both records through fdps_get_unit_record (0x50-byte records in the array based at 0x00069cd8), reading record byte 0 as the tile x and byte 1 as the tile y. Calls the CRT abs() on the x difference and again on the y difference, both operands zero-extended from bytes. When the absolute x difference is strictly the larger, the facing is horizontal: 1 when the unit's x is greater than the target's (target to the left), otherwise 3. Otherwise -- ties included, so a perfect diagonal and a same-tile call both land here -- the facing is vertical: 2 when the unit's y is greater than the target's (target above), otherwise 0. The chosen code is stored in byte 3 of the unit's own record; the target's record is read only. These are the same direction codes the movement playback uses: 0 is +y/down (0002d360), 1 is -x/left (0002d590), 2 is -y/up (0002d480), 3 is +x/right (0002d6a0), each of which writes the same byte 3 as it walks.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit array at 0x00069cd8 of the unit that turns; its record is the only one modified. Callers pass the acting unit, from fdps_battle_action_menu's own unit argument, from FUN_00027180's caster, or from the current-actor global at 0x00063f74.
  target_unit_index -- index of the unit to be faced; its record is only read. Callers pass the unit under the map cursor (via fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor), the current actor at 0x00063f74, or FUN_00027180's target unit byte.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is left holding a leftover record pointer and no caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [calls game code fdps_get_unit_record, which a third-party library module could not; no Function ID hit in either library set, no strings and no data references]

Rebuild note:
The axis test is asymmetric: the horizontal facing is taken only when the absolute x difference is strictly greater than the absolute y one (JLE at 0001c354 sends ties to the vertical branch), so a target on a perfect diagonal makes the unit face up or down, and calling it with the two units on the same tile does not leave the facing alone -- it forces facing 0 (down). Writing the obvious symmetric form (abs_dx >= abs_dy picks horizontal) flips every diagonal case and visibly turns sprites the wrong way.

=== 0001c399 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea-form NOP plus 0x90, aligning next function to 0x1c3a0.

=== 0001c3a0 [PLATE]
Runs one battle unit's weapon attack on another: plays the attack animation, resolves the damage and drains the target's HP bar, once or twice depending on the attacker's weapon.

Algorithm:
fdps_get_unit_record(target_unit_index) resolves the target's 0x50-byte record. Its side byte at +6 picks which filled bar image the drain uses: image 2 when the byte is 0, image 1 otherwise, passed to fdps_draw_unit_gauge as gfx_index. fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot(attacker_unit_index, 0) then finds the attacker's equipped weapon slot, fdps_unit_get_item_id turns that slot into an item id and fdps_get_item_record into a 23-byte ITEM.DAT record; byte +9 of that record is the weapon's hit_effect field.

The strike count starts at 1 and two independent tests raise it to 2. rand() is called unconditionally and rand() % 100 < 3 raises it -- a flat 3% extra strike on every attack, whatever weapon is held. hit_effect == 2 (the double-strike attribute the equipment tables call double strike) raises it as well; that branch never reads the hit_effect_rate byte at +0x0a, so a double-strike weapon always gets both strikes.

Each strike then, in order: reads the target's current HP from record word +0x40 and its maximum from word +0x42 and works out the bar length ceil(hp * 0x29 / max_hp), 0x29 (41) being the filled interior of the 43-pixel bar; plays the two-combatant animation at 0x0001ef40(attacker, target); resolves the damage with 0x0001c520(attacker, target), which writes the target's new HP back into +0x40 and returns it; works out the bar length that new HP gives; then counts the bar down one pixel per step from the old length to the new one, calling fdps_draw_unit_gauge for each step straight into mode-13h video memory at 0xa0000 + (gauge_pos[1] + 4) * 0x140 + gauge_pos[0] + 4, pitch 0x140, blit mode 0, alpha 0, with delay(8) between steps. The count-down test is >=, so a strike that does no damage still repaints the bar once. A second strike is skipped when the first one leaves the target at 0 HP.

Neither unit index is range-checked, and the weapon lookup is not guarded: when fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot returns -1 for an attacker with no weapon equipped, fdps_unit_get_item_id reads unit record byte +9 and fdps_get_item_record indexes ITEM.DAT with whatever that byte holds.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8 of the unit making the attack; supplies the weapon that decides the strike count and is the first argument of both 0x0001ef40 and 0x0001c520. The caller at 0x00012e50 passes its own attacker for the attack and the unit at DAT_00063f74 for the counterattack.
  target_unit_index -- index into the same array of the unit being hit; its record supplies the side byte at +6 and the HP pair at +0x40/+0x42 the bar is drawn from.
  gauge_pos -- pointer to two ints, the screen pixel x and y of the target's 43x6 HP bar; the bar is painted at (x + 4, y + 4) in the mode-13h frame buffer. The caller passes the four-dword block 0x0001cdc0 returns (DAT_00064014), or that block + 8 for the counterattack, so each combatant gets its own position.

Returns:
  The target's HP after the last strike resolved, exactly as 0x0001c520 returned it. 0 means the target is dead; the caller at 0x00012e50 tests the result against 0 to decide whether the target is still there to counterattack.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its one caller and all seven game callees are fdps, and it writes the 0xa0000 frame buffer]

Rebuild note:
rand() is called on every attack, before and independently of the weapon's double-strike test. Folding the two tests into one condition -- if (hit_effect == 2 || rand() % 100 < 3) -- short-circuits the call away whenever a double-strike weapon is equipped and shifts the whole pseudo-random stream from that attack onward, changing every later hit, critical and status roll. Keep the rand() call unconditional and the two tests separate.

=== 0001c51e [EOL]
Alignment padding: mov eax,eax (8b c0), 2-byte filler before FUN_0001c520.

=== 0001c520 [PLATE]
Resolves one blow of an on-map weapon attack: rolls the weapon's hit effect, the accuracy and the critical, takes the damage off the target's HP and works out the experience the blow earns.

Algorithm:
Sets the flag byte at DAT_00064010 to 1, then fetches both unit records through fdps_get_unit_record and copies out the six stats it works on: the attacker's attack (+0x48) and accuracy (+0x4c), the target's defense (+0x4a), current HP (+0x40), max HP (+0x42) and evasion (+0x4e). Reads the attacker's critical rate from PROMAP.DAT through fdps_get_class_record(class byte +0x20 + 1), byte +8 of that record. Resolves the attacker's equipped weapon through fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot(attacker, 0), fdps_unit_get_item_id and fdps_get_item_record, and takes the weapon's hit effect from item byte +9 and its percentage from byte +0xa.
Terrain: for each combatant that fdps_unit_is_flying reports as ground-bound, calls fdps_map_load_tile_info on that unit's tile (record bytes +0 and +1) and scales the stat by the percentage the tile's terrain type (DAT_00069d09) selects -- attack through the table at 00060040, defense through the table at 00060058, both as stat += table[terrain] * stat / 100.
Hit effect: 3 (critical, the guide's 暴擊) adds the weapon's percentage to the critical rate. 4 (poison, 中毒) and 1 (paralysis, 麻痺) each roll rand()%100 against that percentage and, when the target's class byte +0x20 is not 0x19 (機兵, which is immune), write a duration into the target's status byte -- +0x25 = rand()%4 + 2 for poison, +0x26 = rand()%2 + 2 for paralysis -- and flash the screen green twice through fdps_set_palette_range on the palette at DAT_000643bc with bias (-0x40, +0x40, -0x40), 20 ms lit and 40 ms dark. Effect 2 (double strike, 雙擊) is not handled here: fdps_unit_attack_target reads the same item byte and runs this routine twice for it.
Accuracy: the blow lands when rand()%100 < accuracy - evasion. On a hit it clears DAT_00064010 and rolls rand()%100 against the critical rate; a critical flashes the screen white (bias 0x3f, 0x3f, 0x3f) twice and halves the target's terrain-modified defense. Damage is (attack - defense) * 9 / 10 clamped at 0, plus rand() % (damage / 9) when that ninth is non-zero; it comes off the target's current HP, clamped at 0. A miss leaves HP alone and the damage at 0. The resulting HP is written back to target record +0x40 either way.
Experience: when the attacker's side byte +6 is 2 (player side) and the target's portrait id at +7 is 0x3c or more (an enemy, so fdps_get_enemy_record(id - 0x3c) resolves it in ENEMYDAT.DAT), sets DAT_00069cec -- it assigns, it does not accumulate -- to target level (+0x21) * enemy record byte +9 / attacker level (+0x21), the attacker's level first raised by 30 when its own portrait id is above 10, which is 蘭斯洛特 and every guest or NPC unit rather than the eleven permanent roster characters. When the target survived, that award is then scaled by damage / target max HP, so only a kill pays in full.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit_index -- index of the attacking unit in the 0x50-byte unit array at DAT_00069cd8, the form fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_unit_is_flying and fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot all take; passed straight down from fdps_unit_attack_target.
  target_unit_index -- index of the unit being struck, same array, same source.

Returns:
  The target's current HP after the blow, 0 when it died. fdps_unit_attack_target drains the HP bar down to this value.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set and a unique hash in the image; every non-runtime callee is named game code and it owns game globals 00064010, 000643bc, 00069cec, 00069d09 and the terrain tables at 00060040/00060058]

Rebuild note:
The poison and paralysis rolls happen before the accuracy roll and are not conditioned on it, so the status lands even when the blow misses; moving them into the hit branch, where they look like they belong, changes the game. The white critical flash also ends one delay short of the green status flash -- white, delay 20, dark, delay 40, white, delay 20, dark, and then straight on to the damage with no closing delay -- so folding both flashes into one shared helper inserts a 40 ms pause the original does not have.

=== 0001ca9a [EOL]
6-byte NOP pad, one unreferenced fdps helper at 0001caa0 (ratio -> 41-row open amount, forwards to the window-drawing routine FUN_0001cb00), 11-byte NOP pad to the next entry

=== 0001caa0 [PLATE]
Draws one battle unit's 43x6 gauge bar filled in proportion to a current-over-maximum pair, for callers that hold a stat pair rather than a pixel width. The wrapper over fdps_draw_unit_gauge.

No CALL in the image reaches this body, and no data reference points at it: the compiler inlined it at every call site and emitted the out-of-line copy anyway, the same thing it did to the sibling wrapper fdps_draw_gauge_bar_proportional. There are eight expansions, six in fdps_battle_show_combat_gauges (guards at 0001cf5a, 0001d025, 0001d1a0, 0001d295, 0001d408, 0001d4fe) and two in fdps_play_attack_animation (0001f15c, 0001f252). Each one stages seven values into a block of locals, copies them into a second seven-slot block in this function's argument order, runs this body verbatim -- guard, ceiling division, fill of 0 on the short path -- and then calls fdps_draw_unit_gauge with the computed width and cleans 0x18 bytes.

Algorithm:
  Computes the fill width. max_value <= 0 yields fill = 0 (an empty bar), which is also the
  divide-by-zero guard; otherwise fill = (cur_value * 0x29 + max_value - 1) / max_value, a signed
  division truncating toward zero, i.e. the ceiling of cur_value * 41 / max_value. 0x29 (41) is the
  interior width of the 0x2b-by-6 (43x6, 0x102-byte) bar images in the cache at DAT_000643b4, which
  fdps_load_global_resources decodes out of "EasyBar.cel": a 2-pixel left cap, 41 pixels of interior
  starting at column 2, and a 2-pixel right cap painted over the interior's last two columns.
  Because the division rounds up, any cur_value >= 1 still lights at least one pixel, and
  cur_value == max_value gives exactly 41. There is no upper clamp, here or in the callee.
  Then calls fdps_draw_unit_gauge(dst, dst_stride, gfx_index, fill, blit_mode, alpha). Only
  max_value and cur_value are interpreted here; the other five arguments are passed through
  untouched.

  What the pair measures at every expansion is the unit's HP: the maximum is the unit record's
  signed word at +0x42 and the current value the word at +0x40, read through fdps_get_unit_record
  (0001ce64/0001ce6e in fdps_battle_show_combat_gauges, 0001ef9c/0001efa6 in
  fdps_play_attack_animation). The parameters themselves are plain ints and this body never touches
  a unit record, which is why the name carries no stat.

  fdps_unit_attack_target writes the same expression by hand at 0001c466 and 0001c49e, over the same
  two record words, and calls fdps_draw_unit_gauge itself to animate the bar draining. That code is
  not an expansion of this function: it omits the max_value > 0 guard entirely and forms the
  decrement as LEA EDX,[EAX-1] rather than DEC EDX, so it is a separate statement in the original
  source that happens to compute the same value.

Parameters:
  dst -- pointer to the top-left pixel of the bar in an 8bpp destination surface. fdps_draw_unit_gauge
    offsets it by +2 and +0x29 for the four segments and passes it to the blitters as dst; both
    inlining callers form it as composite_page + (y + 0x18) * 0x168 + x + 0x18, into an offscreen
    composite page.
  dst_stride -- bytes per row of that surface; 0x168 (360) at every expansion.
  gfx_index -- which of the three EasyBar.cel images supplies the filled part. Image 0 is the empty
    track and always supplies the unfilled remainder, whatever this argument says.
  max_value -- the denominator, the value a full bar represents. <= 0 draws an empty bar. Note the
    order: the maximum is the fourth argument and the current value the fifth.
  cur_value -- the numerator, the value to show as a fraction of max_value.
  blit_mode -- selects how fdps_draw_unit_gauge paints the four segments: 0 plain, through
    fdps_blit_transparent_rect; 1 blended against the destination, through
    fdps_blit_blend_transparent_rect; any other value goes through fdps_blit_tint_transparent_rect
    with that same value used as the tint colour index.
  alpha -- blend strength forwarded to fdps_blit_blend_transparent_rect or
    fdps_blit_tint_transparent_rect; unused when blit_mode is 0.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only callee is fdps code built on this
program's globals]

Rebuild note:
  Nothing calls this entry, but it is not dead code to be dropped: it is the source-level function
  the eight expansions came from, and it is the one place the guard-plus-ceiling expression is
  written once. Emit it as a real function and write the eight sites as calls to it; whether the
  rebuild's compiler then inlines them is a code-generation detail that functional equivalence does
  not turn on.

=== 0001caf5 [EOL]
alignment padding after the RET: 8d 80 00 00 00 00, 8d 52 00, 8b db (NOP forms) aligning FUN_0001cb00 at 0001cb00 to 16

=== 0001cb00 [PLATE]
Draws one battle unit's 43x6 gauge bar into a caller-supplied 8bpp surface, filled to a caller-supplied pixel width, in one of three blit modes.

Algorithm:
The bar art is the three 43x6 (0x102-byte) images fdps_load_global_resources decodes out of "EasyBar.cel" at 00029c68-00029d5c into the 0x306-byte buffer whose pointer it leaves in DAT_000643b4. Image 0 is the empty track; the other two are the filled colours (FUN_0001c3a0 asks for image 2 when the unit record's side byte at +6 is 0 and image 1 otherwise). src = DAT_000643b4 + gfx_index * 0x102 selects the filled image. fill_width is then clamped up to 0; there is no upper clamp.

The bar is painted as four segments, always in this order and always at source pitch 0x2b: the 2x6 left cap, src+0 to dst+0; when fill_width is positive, a fill_width x 6 run, src+2 to dst+2; a (0x29 - fill_width) x 6 run taken from image 0, DAT_000643b4 + 2 + fill_width to dst + 2 + fill_width; and last the 2x6 right cap, src + 0x29 to dst + 0x29. 0x2b (43) is the bar width, 0x29 (41) the interior the fill divides, 6 the height. The remainder run reaches column 0x2b, so it covers the right cap's two columns and the cap is painted back over it.

blit_mode chooses the painter for all four segments. 0 uses fdps_blit_transparent_rect: palette index 0 in the art reads as transparent and every other pixel is written through. 1 uses fdps_blit_blend_transparent_rect with the destination passed as its own background and alpha as the blend strength, giving a translucent bar. Any other value uses fdps_blit_tint_transparent_rect with blit_mode itself as the tint colour index and alpha as the blend strength; FUN_0001cdc0 passes 0x1a for two of its frame phases. Both blended painters are handed the game's blend tables at DAT_000653f0 and the inverse-palette lookup at DAT_000643f0.

The callers are the combat presentation code: FUN_0001c3a0 animates the target's HP draining straight into video memory, and FUN_0001cdc0 and FUN_0001ef40 draw both combatants' bars into their offscreen composite pages at the positions fdps_battle_compute_unit_gauge_position works out. fdps_draw_gauge_proportional is the wrapper that turns a current/maximum pair into fill_width and calls here.

Parameters:
  dst -- pointer to the top-left pixel of the bar in an 8bpp destination surface, offset by +2 and +0x29 for the segments. FUN_0001cdc0 and FUN_0001ef40 form it as composite_page + (y + 0x18) * 0x168 + x + 0x18; FUN_0001c3a0 forms it as 0xa0000 + (row + 4) * 0x140 + col + 4, i.e. directly into the mode-13h screen.
  dst_stride -- destination pitch in bytes, passed unchanged into every blit; 0x168 (360) from the two animation pages, 0x140 (320) from FUN_0001c3a0.
  gfx_index -- which of the three EasyBar.cel images supplies the filled part, 0 to 2. Only the filled part honours it; the remainder always comes from image 0.
  fill_width -- filled width in pixels out of the interior's 0x29 (41). Negative is forced to 0, nothing caps it at 0x29. Every caller computes it as ceil(current HP * 0x29 / maximum HP) from the unit record's words at +0x40 and +0x42.
  blit_mode -- 0 plain, 1 blended against the destination, any other value is the palette colour index the whole bar is tinted with.
  alpha -- blend strength forwarded to fdps_blit_blend_transparent_rect or fdps_blit_tint_transparent_rect; never read when blit_mode is 0.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library and a unique hash in the image; it indexes the game's own EasyBar.cel image cache at DAT_000643b4 and hard-codes this game's 43x6 bar geometry, and every caller and callee is in-image game graphics code]

Rebuild note:
The four segments deliberately overlap and the order is load-bearing: the remainder run is 0x29 - fill_width wide starting at column 2 + fill_width, so it reaches column 0x2b and paints over the right cap's two columns, which the fourth blit then paints back on top of. Tidying that up -- trimming the remainder to 0x27 - fill_width, or drawing the two caps first -- changes the picture in blit_mode 1 and in the tint mode, where those two columns are blended twice and so come out more opaque than the rest of the bar. Second, the remainder is always read from image 0 (DAT_000643b4 + 2 + fill_width), never from gfx_index, so writing the obvious "same image, later columns" for that blit paints the whole bar in the filled colour.

=== 0001cdbf [EOL]
single-byte 0x90 NOP alignment pad between FUN_0001cb00 and FUN_0001cdc0

=== 0001cdc0 [PLATE]
Makes the two combatants' HP gauges appear on the battle map before an attack is played out, and hands the caller the screen positions it placed them at.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_battle_compute_unit_gauge_position for defender_unit into the global position pair at DAT_00064014, then asks fdps_check_can_counter_attack whether the defender may strike back: when it returns exactly 1 the attacker's bar is positioned the same way into the pair at DAT_0006401c, otherwise DAT_0006401c is set to -1, which suppresses that bar for the rest of the run. Both unit records come from fdps_get_unit_record; from each it takes the side byte at +6 (side 0 selects EasyBar.cel image 2, anything else image 1) and the HP words at +0x40 (current) and +0x42 (maximum).
It then allocates a 0x15180-byte (360x240) composite page with malloc -- no NULL test -- and turns each position pair into a destination pointer as page + (y + 0x18) * 0x168 + x + 0x18, the 0x18-pixel border the page carries on every side. The attacker's pointer is formed even when DAT_0006401c is -1, but nothing dereferences it in that case.
Seven frames are then composed, each the same way: fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the map into the page, fdps_draw_unit_gauge draws the attacker's bar (skipped while DAT_0006401c is -1) and then the defender's, each filled to (current_hp * 0x29 + max_hp - 1) / max_hp pixels of the bar's 0x29-pixel interior, or 0 when max_hp is not positive; the code spins on bit 3 of VGA port 0x3da until vertical retrace starts and again until it ends, and fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 window at page + 0x21d8 to the screen at 0xa0504, i.e. (4,4) in mode 13h. Every frame but the last then spins until the frame counter DAT_00069d64 leaves the value saved from the previous frame.
The seven frames fall into three phases, differing only in the last two arguments of fdps_draw_unit_gauge: three frames in blit mode 1 with blend strength 0, 6 and 12 out of 16, so the bars blend up out of the background; three frames in blit mode 0x1a, which is the palette index the whole bar is tinted with, at strength 0, 6 and 12; and one closing frame in mode 0, the plain opaque bar. The composite page is freed and the bars are left standing on the screen for the attack animation that follows.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8. Passed straight to fdps_check_can_counter_attack and fdps_get_unit_record; its bar is drawn only when that unit is the one about to take a counter-attack.
  defender_unit -- index of the unit being attacked, in the same array; its bar is always drawn.

Returns:
  &DAT_00064014, the two gauge positions as one array of {x, y} int pairs: pair 0 is the defender's bar, pair 1 (DAT_0006401c/DAT_00064020) the attacker's, whose x is -1 when no counter-attack is coming. FUN_00012e50 hands pair 0 to fdps_unit_attack_target for the attack and pair 1 to it for the counter, so each blow drains the bar this function placed.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library; it calls named game code, owns the game globals at 00064014/00064018/0006401c/00064020 and writes the VGA framebuffer, and at 2055 bytes is far too large to be a linker or compiler product]

Rebuild note:
The local that remembers the previous value of the frame counter DAT_00069d64 is never initialised, so on the first of the seven frames the routine compares the counter against whatever the stack slot happened to hold and usually does not wait at all. Writing the obvious int last_tick = DAT_00069d64; before the loop adds a tick of delay the original does not have; leave it uninitialised.

=== 0001d5c7 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0] plus 3-byte lea edx,[edx+0], aligning FUN_0001d5d0 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001d5d0 [PLATE]
Works out where one battle unit's 43x6 HP gauge goes on screen while a combat animation is playing, and writes the position to the caller.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads three bytes of the record: byte 0 the tile column, byte 1 the tile row, byte 3 the facing (0 down, 1 left, 2 up, 3 right -- the values fdps_animate_move_step_down, fdps_animate_move_step_left, fdps_walk_step_up and fdps_animate_step_right write into that byte at 0002d39e, 0002d5bd, 0002d4ae and 0002d6dd, and that fdps_unit_face_target picks when it turns a unit to face another). It converts the tile to view pixels the same way fdps_draw_map_unit does for the unit sprite itself: out_position[0] = tile_column * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 + 4 and out_position[1] = tile_row * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0, where 0x18 is the tile size and DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0 are the view's scroll origin in world pixels.

It then offsets that point off the unit so the gauge does not sit on top of it, choosing the side opposite the way the unit is facing, so that two combatants facing each other end up with their gauges on opposite outer sides rather than stacked between them:

  facing 0 or 1 (down, left) -- gauge above and to the right. y goes to y - 0x10 unless that would leave y below 5, in which case y + 5; x goes to x + 0x18 unless x + 0x45 has reached 0x13b, in which case x - 0x2d.
  facing 2 or 3 (up, right) -- gauge below and to the left. y goes to y + 0x16 unless that reaches 0xc3, in which case y + 5; x goes to x - 0x2c unless that would leave x below 5, in which case x + 0x1c.

The clamps keep the gauge inside the visible 320x200 screen: 0x45 is the right offset 0x18 plus the 0x2d-pixel box the gauge occupies, tested against 0x13b, and 0xc3 leaves room below for the gauge's 6 rows. The four offsets are not symmetric -- the preferred right step is 0x18 but the fallback right step is 0x1c, and the fallback left step is 0x2d against a preferred 0x2c -- and each branch is written out literally. The two y fallbacks are both a small downward +5, so a gauge that cannot take its preferred vertical offset ends up beside or over the unit rather than on the other side; only x flips sides.

Callers turn the pair into a destination pointer as buffer + (y + 0x18) * 0x168 + x + 0x18, the 360-pixel-pitch composite page with an 0x18 border, and hand it to fdps_draw_unit_gauge along with a fill length of (0x29 * current_hp + max_hp - 1) / max_hp, taken from the unit record's HP word pair at +0x40 and +0x42 and scaled over the gauge's 41 fillable pixels.

No bounds check on unit_index, no test that the unit is on the visible part of the map, and no global is written.

Parameters:
  out_position -- pointer to two ints that receive the gauge's x and y in view pixels, before the caller's 0x18 border is added. fdps_play_attack_animation passes a stack pair; fdps_battle_show_combat_gauges passes the global pairs at DAT_00064014 (defender) and DAT_0006401c (attacker).
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, as taken by fdps_get_unit_record; both callers pass one of the two combatants of the animation they are playing.

Returns:
  Nothing; the result is the pair written through out_position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in Watcom or ailv3.lib; it reads the game's unit records and view-scroll globals and both callers are game code]

=== 0001d6b3 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / nop, aligning next function entry to 16 bytes

=== 0001d6c0 [PLATE]
Plays the death sequence for every battle unit whose HP has reached zero, and marks those units removed from the map.

Algorithm:
Sweeps the unit table with fdps_get_unit_record(i) for i from 0 to DAT_00060150 - 1, the live unit count, and collects into an 80-slot stack array the index of every unit whose flags byte (record+5) has bit 0 clear and whose HP word (record+0x40) is zero. The tile x and y bytes (record+0 and record+1) are loaded in the same pass into locals that nothing reads. It returns at once when the collection is empty; there is no bound check on the 80 slots.
Spin phase: thirteen times over, it stores step % 4 into the facing byte (record+3) of every collected unit -- the four facings 0 down, 1 left, 2 up, 3 right, so the dying unit spins on the spot -- and calls fdps_render_view_frame, which presents one frame and paces the loop to one timer tick each.
It then stores 1 into the flags byte of every collected unit, which marks the unit dead and clears the rest of that byte.
Explosion phase: malloc gives it a 0x15180-byte (360x240) scene buffer, and it builds a 0x24-byte composite sprite request on the stack over that buffer -- buffer pointer at +0, width 0x168 and height 0xf0 at +4 and +8, at +0x14 the "Explo.Saf" image that fdps_vfs_image_get_entry pulls out of the resident archive at DAT_000643a8, and zero at +0x1c and +0x20. For each of the fdps_saf_frame_count(Explo.Saf) frames it repaints the map into the buffer with fdps_draw_scene_layers, then for every collected unit sets the request origin to record[0] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 and record[1] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0 - 6 (0x18 is the tile size, DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0 are the view's scroll origin in world pixels), puts the frame number at +0x18, and calls fdps_draw_composite_sprite with its sound flag set only for the first unit of the list, so the frame's sound effect fires once per frame instead of once per dying unit. It then open-codes what fdps_render_view_frame does to present a frame: spins on port 0x3DA bit 3 until vertical retrace starts and again until it ends, blits the 0x138 x 0xc0 window at buffer+0x21d8 -- pixel (24,24) of the 360-wide buffer -- with fdps_blit_rect to 0xa0504, the 4-pixel inset of the mode 13h screen, and waits for the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change before the next frame. free releases the buffer on the way out.

Parameters:
  None. Every unit it acts on comes from the unit table at DAT_00069cd8 and the count at DAT_00060150.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [walks the game unit table, reads the camera globals and opens Explo.Saf from the game archive, and all seven callers are battle routines; no Function ID hit in the Watcom libraries or in ailv3.lib]

Rebuild note:
Two places where the obvious C differs. Marking the dead is a whole-byte store, unit_record[5] = 1, not a bit set: byte 5 is a multi-bit flags byte -- fdps_map_actor_behavior_step ORs 0x80 into it at 0x00010745, and FUN_00021650 sets and clears bit 0 with OR/AND at 0x00021b11 and 0x00021b51 -- so writing flags |= 1 would leave those other bits standing where the original wipes them. And the local the explosion loop compares against DAT_00069d64 is never initialised, so the first frame does not wait for a tick; declaring it initialised from DAT_00069d64 costs one extra tick, the same way it does in fdps_animate_turn_banner.

=== 0001d986 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4), aligns FUN_0001d990 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001d990 [PLATE]
Runs the death scripts collected from the units a battle action has just killed: pays their item and gold rewards to the acting unit, fires their scripted chapter events and records the battle-end verdicts they carry.

Algorithm:
Does nothing at all when script_count is 0. Otherwise it resolves the acting unit's 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record(actor_unit_index), discards the keystrokes queued during the death animation with fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, and walks the records front to back. Each record is three bytes -- an opcode byte and a signed 16-bit operand at +1 -- the layout fdps_collect_death_scripts and fdps_collect_defeated_unit_events copy out of unit-record field +0x31. The opcode selects:

  0 -- item drop. This opcode and opcode 1 both first require the acting unit to be on the player side (record byte +6 == 2; 0 is the enemy side, 1 the NPC side) and not retired (fdps_unit_is_retired); when either test fails the function returns outright and abandons every record still ahead of it. It publishes operand + 0xc9, the item's name string in the global message table, in the substitution-string global at 00064030, opens the message window on the actor's portrait (record byte +7) with fdps_message_window_open, paints message 0x1e6 of the global text table DAT_000643c4 into the window at 0xaa44a through FUN_0001ff60, and calls fdps_unit_add_item(actor_unit_index, operand). With a slot free it holds the window for fdps_message_window_wait_key(1, 0x1e) -- 0x1e ticks -- closes it and moves on. With the bag full (add returned -1) it closes that window, waits 100 ms through delay, reopens on message 0x1e7 (the bag-full prompt) and runs fdps_prompt_two_choice: answer 0 opens the actor's inventory through FUN_000259c0(actor_unit_index, 0, &slot) so the player picks the slot to give up, and on a pick it reads that slot's id with fdps_unit_get_item_id (result discarded), removes it with fdps_unit_remove_item and adds the dropped item in its place; a cancelled pick, or any other answer to the prompt, shows message 0x1e8 for 0x32 ticks instead and the drop is lost.

  1 -- gold. Same player-side and not-retired guard. Opens the message window on the actor's portrait, puts the operand in the numeric substitution global at 00064038, paints message 0x1e9, waits 0x32 ticks, closes, then adds that global to the party gold at DAT_000643a4.

  2 -- scripted event. Calls slot operand of the chapter-event handler table at 000601c4 with actor_unit_index as its single argument -- the same table fdps_battle_run_turn_events and the phase loops dispatch through.

  3 and above -- scripted line. Unless the operand is 0xff or -1, both of which mean "no message", it paints message operand of the current chapter's FDETXT text table at DAT_00060124 straight onto the mode-13h framebuffer at 0xa0000, pitch 0x140, with the glyph colours 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d. Opcode 4 then sets the battle-end code DAT_00069da0 to 2 (chapter cleared) and opcode 5 sets it to 1 (defeat); any other opcode of 3 or more stops at the line.

Once the last record is done it flushes the keyboard queue again. fdps_collect_defeated_unit_events filters its records down to opcodes 2..5, so the map-AI path that feeds this function never reaches the two reward opcodes.

Parameters:
  actor_unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit array at DAT_00069cd8 of the unit whose action caused the deaths. It receives the items and the gold, its record supplies the message-window portrait, and the player-side/not-retired test is made on it. FUN_00012e50 and FUN_00013c90 pass the current-actor global DAT_00063f74; fdps_battle_action_menu, FUN_000262a0 and FUN_00027c20 pass their own acting-unit argument.
  script_count -- how many records scripts holds: the return value of fdps_collect_death_scripts or fdps_collect_defeated_unit_events. 0 means there is nothing to run.
  scripts -- the packed array of 3-byte records one of those collectors just filled; always a caller stack buffer.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_prompt_two_choice; writes game globals; no Function ID candidate on either library set]

Rebuild note:
The player-side and not-retired tests on opcodes 0 and 1 leave the whole function, not just that record: with an enemy or NPC unit as the actor the first item or gold record aborts the run, every later record is dropped -- including the opcodes 4 and 5 that set the battle-end code -- and the closing fdps_flush_keyboard_queue never happens. Writing the natural continue there changes which battles can end. The "no message" test on opcode 3 and above accepts 0x00ff as well as 0xffff, so testing the sign-extended operand only against -1 would print a message the original suppresses.

=== 0001dd28 [EOL]
8-byte Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + mov edx,edx (2), aligning FUN_0001dd30 to 16 bytes

=== 0001dd30 [PLATE]
Awards the pending battle experience to one unit, floats the amount over it on the map, and when the running total reaches 100 levels the unit up behind the full-screen level-up window.

Algorithm:
1. Resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record and caches its level (record +0x21) and its character/portrait id (record +0x07). Returns at once when the pending-experience accumulator DAT_00069cec is 0, when fdps_unit_is_retired reports the unit has left the battle, or when the unit already sits at its level cap -- 99 for character id 9 (the machine soldier 蓋亞), 40 for every other id. None of these three exits clears DAT_00069cec.
2. Clears the map-cursor draw mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so fdps_draw_map_cursor paints nothing over the animation, parks the cursor on the unit with fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, then clamps DAT_00069cec down to 99.
3. Re-reads the record, takes the FRILEVUP.DAT growth record for character id record +0x07 through fdps_get_growth_record, and forms the running total as DAT_00069cec plus the leftover experience carried in record +0x3c.
4. Builds the floating experience label in a 40x8 buffer: sprite 0x23 of the CEL sheet held at DAT_000643ac, with the awarded amount painted into it at column 18 by fdps_draw_number. The label's screen position is the unit's tile x/y (record +0x00 / +0x01) times 24 pixels per tile, less the view scroll in DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0, plus (0x18, 0x20).
5. Floats it upward over fifteen frames: for rise = 6, 8 ... 0x22, clamped at 24 pixels, each frame composites a fresh 360x240 scene with fdps_draw_scene_layers, blends the label into it at (x, y - rise) through fdps_blit_blend_transparent_rect at alpha rise/3 + 8, waits out one VGA vertical retrace on port 0x3da, copies the 312x192 interior to the mode 13h screen at 0xa0504 with fdps_blit_rect, spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes, and frees the scene.
6. When the running total is still under 100, skips straight to step 11.
7. Otherwise the unit levels. It loads Levup.wav out of MISC.VFS with fdps_vfs_load_entry and starts it with fdps_audio_start_wav(wav, 1, -1, -1), flushes the keyboard with fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, increments the level byte at record +0x21, and paints sprite 0 of the CEL sheet at DAT_000643b0 into a 164x66 window buffer.
8. If the growth record's learn index (growth +0x0a) is not 0xff, it walks the six (level, spell id) pairs of that GETMGTAB.DAT record from fdps_get_spell_learn_record. Every pair whose level byte equals the new level has its spell name -- text entry spell_id + 0x1be of the text block at DAT_000643c4 -- drawn into the window by fdps_draw_text, and fdps_set_flag_bit(unit_index, spell_id) sets that spell in the unit's learned-spell mask at record +0x1a.
9. Takes 100 off the running total, draws the new level into the window with fdps_draw_number, and rolls the five stat gains with fdps_level_up_apply_stat_gain: AP at record +0x37 from growth +0, DP at +0x39 from growth +2, DX at +0x3e from growth +4, maximum HP at +0x42 from growth +6, maximum MP at +0x46 from growth +8, each painted into its own cell of the window. fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats then rebuilds the unit's derived combat stats.
10. Holds the window on screen for up to 250 frames. Each frame composites a scene, blits the window into it at (98, 88) with fdps_blit_rect and the unit's 24x24 walk sprite at (168, 101) with fdps_blit_dispatch in mode 0 -- taken from the sprite cache at DAT_00060138, group record +0x02 times 0x30, frame (tick % 16) / 4 with 3 folded back to 1 so the cycle runs 0, 1, 2, 1 -- then does the same retrace, screen copy and tick wait as step 5. The first make code out of fdps_read_keyboard_queue, meaning any value of 0x7f or less, ends the loop early. The leftover experience is then zeroed when the new level is 99 and the character id is 9, or when the new level is 40; the window is freed; and the routine spins on fdps_audio_sample_is_playing until Levup.wav has finished before freeing the sound.
11. Stores the leftover experience back into record +0x3c as a byte, clears DAT_00069cec, sets the cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 1 -- the plain cursor, not whatever it held on entry -- and flushes the keyboard queue.

Nothing in the body tests the unit's side, so whichever unit index is handed in is the one that collects the experience and levels.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, read from [EBP+0x14]. Handed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_unit_is_retired, fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, fdps_set_flag_bit and fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats. Callers pass the unit that has just acted or has just been acted on.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game callers, game unit records, game asset strings]

Rebuild note:
The leftover-experience test after the level-up does not agree with the level cap the routine gates on at entry: the entry gate lets character id 9 (蓋亞) climb to 99 while everyone else stops at 40, but the post-level-up test zeroes the leftover for any unit that has just reached level 40, id 9 included, so 蓋亞 loses his carried experience once on the 39 -> 40 step. Writing that test as "did this unit just reach its own cap" repairs a loss the original has. The three early exits also return without clearing DAT_00069cec -- only the path that runs to the end clears it -- so experience credited to a retired or already-capped unit stays in the accumulator and is handed to whichever unit is awarded next; a single clear on the way out silently fixes that leak too. Finally, the local that the two frame spins compare against DAT_00069d64 is never initialised, so the first spin of each loop falls straight through, and DAT_00069d64 must be declared volatile or the empty spin never terminates.

=== 0001e369 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea-form NOP plus 0x90, aligning FUN_0001e370 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001e370 [PLATE]
Applies one stat's level-up growth to a unit: rolls the gain from that stat's FriLevUp.dat min/max pair, paints the rolled number into the level-up window, and adds it to the unit's 16-bit stat field.

Algorithm:
Reads growth_pair[0] as the minimum gain and growth_pair[1] as the exclusive upper bound and forms range = growth_pair[1] - growth_pair[0]. When range is non-zero it calls rand() and reduces it modulo range with a signed IDIV; when range is zero it skips the call altogether, so an equal pair consumes no random number and always gains exactly the minimum. It parks growth_pair[0] + offset in the dword scratch global DAT_00064038 -- the only three references to that global in the whole image are this body's own store, push and reload -- and calls fdps_draw_number(dst, 0xa4, gain, 0, 0), which paints the gain as 6x8 digit glyphs at dst at its natural width, unpadded and with no leading '+'; 0xa4 is 164, the row pitch of the 164x66 level-up window fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up built from sprite 0 of the CEL sheet at DAT_000643b0. Finally it reloads the low 16 bits of the global and adds them to *stat, with no clamp and no cap check.

Parameters:
  stat -- pointer to the 16-bit stat field being raised inside the caller's 0x50-byte unit record. fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up passes record+0x37, +0x39, +0x3e, +0x42 and +0x46, in the growth record's pair order ap, dp, dx, hp, mp.
  growth_pair -- pointer to one two-byte {min, max} growth pair inside the character's 11-byte FriLevUp.dat record, as returned by fdps_get_growth_record; the caller passes the record plus 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8. max is exclusive: the largest possible gain is max - 1, which is why the strategy guide lists every growth range one lower than the byte in the file.
  dst -- destination pixel address inside the caller's 164x66 level-up window buffer where the gained amount is drawn; the caller aims it at column 38 or column 147 of the row belonging to that stat.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either library and a hash unique in the image; its only caller is game code and it calls the game's own fdps_draw_number, with rand() as its single vendor call -- the normal game-to-CRT direction]

Rebuild note:
The pair's second byte is an exclusive bound and the zero test in front of the IDIV is not defensive padding: 151 of the 300 growth pairs in FriLevUp.dat have max == min, including the DX pair of every promoted class and of 亞克 (02 02), 布蘭多 (03 03) and 蓋亞 (00 00), and 蘭斯洛特's MP pair (00 00). Those are reached on ordinary level-ups, so dropping the test divides by zero the first time 亞克 gains a level.

=== 0001e3ea [EOL]
Watcom 6-byte alignment NOP (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) between FUN_0001e370 and fdps_battle_advance_turn

=== 0001e3f0 [PLATE]
Advances the battle to the next turn: applies end-of-turn HP recovery to resting units, then runs the enemy phase and opens the next player phase.
Pool: fdps  [walks unit records via fdps_get_unit_record, owns the turn counter at 0x00069ce8, loads game assets REST.WAV / EnyPhase.saf / PlyPhase.saf]
Evidence: Pure game logic on game state -- unit count 0x00060150, unit-record fields +0x05/+0x06/+0x25/+0x26/+0x0a/+0x40/+0x42/+0x44/+0x46, turn counter 0x00069ce8, abort flag 0x00069da0, input flag 0x00060159 -- driving named fdps routines (fdps_draw_scene_layers, fdps_blit_rect, fdps_render_view_frame, fdps_units_clear_status_bit7, fdps_play_sfx, fdps_play_vfs_animation, fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track). Library contact is only malloc/free/delay/inp, the game calling the CRT. No Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the AIL set (fid empty, same_hash_in_image = 1). Both callers are fdps battle code. Too large and too state-specific to be a binary artifact; nothing touches AIL driver state.
Name: no library symbol identified; project name under the fdps_ + snake_case rule, describing the turn-boundary sequence the body performs.
Boundary: 0001e3f0-0001e83b, canonical Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the entry, single epilogue 89 ec 5d 5f 5e 5b c3 at the end that every early exit jumps to; the 4 bytes at 0001e83c are alignment padding and the next function's prologue starts at 0001e840.
Signature: __cdecl, no arguments, no return value -- confirmed by the assembly: no access above [ebp], all callees are stack-arg with caller cleanup, EAX undefined at both exits.

Algorithm:
1. Clears the input-enabled flag at 0x00060159, allocates a 0x15180-byte offscreen map buffer with malloc and renders the battle map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers.
2. Walks every unit (count at 0x00060150, record via fdps_get_unit_record). A unit whose kind byte +0x06 == 2, with none of bits 0x81 set in byte +0x05, zero in bytes +0x25 and +0x26, and current HP (+0x40) differing from max HP (+0x42) recovers maxHP/5 HP clamped to max. Each heal draws a floating value over the unit via 0x0001ee10(buffer, unit_index, 0xff00, 3) and records that at least one unit rested.
3. Waits for the VGA vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA bit 3 (inp), then blits the map viewport from buffer+0x21d8 to 0xa0504 with fdps_blit_rect. If any unit rested, plays REST.WAV through fdps_play_sfx. Delays 40 ticks, frees the buffer and repaints with fdps_render_view_frame.
4. Selects side 1 (0x0002e0c0 / 0x0001fa30) and runs 0x00012b20.
5. Shows the EnyPhase.saf banner, clears status bit 7 on all units, selects side 0 and runs 0x00012960; restarts the CD battle track first.
6. Increments the turn counter at 0x00069ce8, shows the PlyPhase.saf banner, clears 0x00069cd0, replays the CD track and selects side 2.
7. Applies per-unit MP regeneration: looks up 0xa6 then 0xa7 on unit 4, 0xb1 on unit 8, and 0xb3 on every unit via 0x00034520. When the found slot has bit 0x40 set in unit+0x0a[slot], byte +0x05 is zero and current MP (+0x44) differs from max MP (+0x46), the unit gains MP via 0x000275a0(unit, 0x0f), the view scrolls to it (0x0002da50), a type-0x0d floating value is shown (0x0001f510) and the display is waited on (0x0001f340).
8. Sets 0x00069cd0 = 1, centres the view on unit 0 unless 0x000109b0 says otherwise, calls 0x000567b3 and re-enables input at 0x00060159.

Every stage from step 4 on is guarded by the battle-abort flag at 0x00069da0; when it is non-zero the function returns immediately without re-enabling input.

=== 0001e840 [PLATE]
Plays the battle turn banner over a saved screen image: the Turn.saf sign and the current turn number slide in from opposite edges, hold for half a second, then slide back off.

Algorithm:
Copies the 13-entry slide-offset table at 0x0001c280 (-60, -20, 10, 35, 50, 65, 75, 80, 85, 90, 92, 91, 90) onto the stack, allocates a 0x15180-byte (360x240) work surface with malloc, and takes the banner sprite sheet from the resident BaseAni.vfs entry "Turn.saf" through fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit. Builds the 0x24-byte composite-sprite request that fdps_draw_composite_sprite consumes: destination = the work surface, stride 0x168, height 0xf0, origin y 0x5c, sheet = Turn.saf, blit mode 0.

Slide-in, i = 0..12, one step per timer tick:
  - fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312x192) region at byte offset 0x504 of saved_screen (320-byte stride, so pixel (4,4)) into the work surface at offset 0x21d8 (pixel (24,24)), wiping the previous step's banner;
  - request x = table[i] + 0x14 and entry index 0, then fdps_draw_composite_sprite with the sound flag set, so the sheet entry's sound effect is triggered on every step;
  - request x = 0x12c - table[i], then fdps_draw_turn_number, which overwrites the entry index with one digit of the battle turn counter per decimal place and steps 0x1c pixels right for each;
  - fdps_blit_rect copies the same 312x192 region from the work surface to VGA at 0xa0504;
  - spins on the timer-tick global DAT_00069d64 until it changes, then latches the new value.
The two x values always sum to 0x140, so the sign comes in from the left while the number comes in from the right; both overshoot their resting place by two pixels at table[10] before settling on table[12] = 90.

delay(500) then holds the assembled banner for half a second, and the slide-out repeats the identical step for i = 10 down to 0, retracing the table until both pieces are back off the edges. free() releases the work surface.

Parameters:
  saved_screen -- the 320x200 8bpp copy of the screen that was showing before the animation began, allocated and filled from 0xa0000 by fdps_play_vfs_animation. Read only; it is the background the banner slides over, repainted under it on every step.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the Watcom or ail sets; full_hash unique in the image, and it owns the private 13-dword table at 0x0001c280 and the game asset name "Turn.saf"]

Rebuild note:
The slide-out loop starts at table entry 10, not 12. Writing the obvious mirror of the slide-in -- for (i = 12; i >= 0; i--) -- gives two extra steps and loses the two-pixel snap the original shows the instant the banner starts leaving. The local the frame wait compares against is also left uninitialised before each loop, so the first step of each phase does not wait for a tick; declaring it initialised from DAT_00069d64 costs one extra tick per phase.

=== 0001ea77 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 80 00 00 00 00 + 8d 52 00, aligning FUN_0001ea80 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001ea80 [PLATE]
Draws the current battle turn number over the player-phase turn banner, one composite-sprite digit per decimal place, into the sprite request the caller has already set up.

Algorithm:
Formats the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 into an 8-byte stack buffer with sprintf and the "%d" format string at DAT_000617bc. It then walks the buffer with i from 0 while i < strlen(buffer), calling strlen again on every pass. For each character it writes (character - 0x2f) into the request's entry-index field at req+0x18 -- 0x2f is '0' minus one, so digit d selects entry d+1 of the sprite bank the caller loaded, entry 0 of that bank being the banner word graphic the caller draws itself -- then calls fdps_draw_composite_sprite(req, 0) to paint that digit and adds 0x1c (28 pixels, the digit pitch) to the request's X field at req+0x0c.
The request belongs to the caller and is modified in place: on return req+0x0c sits one pitch past the last digit drawn and req+0x18 holds the last digit's entry index. The only caller, the turn-banner animation at 0001e840, rewrites both fields before it uses the request again.

Parameters:
  req -- the composite-sprite request fdps_draw_composite_sprite consumes: destination buffer at +0x00, destination pitch at +0x04, height at +0x08, X at +0x0c, Y at +0x10, sprite bank at +0x14, bank entry index at +0x18. This routine reads nothing out of it and writes only +0x0c and +0x18. The caller at 0001e840 builds it on its own stack, aimed at a 360x240 off-screen buffer with the "Turn.saf" bank loaded by fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game's own fdps_draw_composite_sprite and reads the game global DAT_00069ce8; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The ASCII-to-sprite conversion subtracts 0x2f, not 0x30, so the composite-sprite entry index is digit + 1: entry 0 of the banner bank is the word graphic and the numerals start at entry 1. Writing the obvious buffer[i] - '0' shifts every digit one glyph down and makes a '0' draw the word sprite instead.

=== 0001eb00 [PLATE]
Plays the named MISC.VFS entry as a full-screen animation, dimming the screen that was showing before it and restoring that screen afterwards.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library; calls game code and game data]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty and the body's full_hash is unique in the image, so no library byte match exists. It calls fdps_vfs_load_entry, fdps_blit_tint_rect and the SAF player FUN_0001ecf0, which compiled third-party objects cannot do, and is called only by fdps_load_savegame and fdps_battle_advance_turn. Name: fdps pool, so fdps_ + snake_case; describes the behaviour, no library symbol claimed or available.
Boundary: 0001eb00-0001ecef, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 E5 at the entry and MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET at 0001ece9; gap_after is empty and 0001ecf0 is the identical prologue of the next function.
Signature: __cdecl, void fdps_play_vfs_animation(char *name) -- the single argument is read from [EBP+0x14] and passed to fdps_vfs_load_entry and strcmp; the caller cleans up (no purge, ADD ESP,n after every call). Confirmed by the assembly, not a guess.

=== 0001ecf0 [PLATE]
Plays one loaded .SAF animation through once, full screen, over a background image the caller supplies.

Algorithm:
Allocates a 0x16480-byte page with malloc -- a 368x248 8bpp surface, 48 pixels wider and taller than the 320x200 screen, so a frame may overhang the visible window without being clipped. Builds the 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request on the stack: destination = that page, pitch 0x170 (368), height 0xf8 (248), x = y = 0x18 (24), SAF base (+0x14) = saf_image, blit parameter block (+0x1c) and blit mode (+0x20) both 0. Calls fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 1) to reset the three-dword playback cursor and stores saf_image in cursor[2], the slot fdps_saf_advance_tick reads the SAF header from. Then loops until fdps_saf_advance_tick reports the clip has ended: fdps_blit_rect copies the caller's 320x200 background_page into the visible window of the page at page+0x2298 (24 * 368 + 24), the request's index field (+0x18) takes the cursor's current frame number, fdps_draw_composite_sprite draws that frame with its flag argument 1 so the frame's own sound effect fires, fdps_blit_rect copies the 320x200 window from the page straight to the VGA framebuffer at 0xa0000, the routine spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes, and fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0) advances the cursor by one tick. Mode 0 wraps the frame index back to 0 and returns 1 once the last frame has been held, so the animation plays exactly once and the loop exits there. The page is freed on the way out; the caller owns both saf_image and background_page.

Parameters:
  saf_image -- the loaded .SAF animation image to play. The only caller, fdps_play_vfs_animation, passes the MISC.VFS entry it loaded by name. Used as the composite-sprite bank at request+0x14 and as the SAF pointer in the playback cursor.
  background_page -- a 320x200 8bpp image, 320 bytes per row, repainted under every frame so the animation composites over a static picture. fdps_play_vfs_animation passes its snapshot of the VGA screen that was showing before the animation started.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; game call graph and mode 13h geometry -- calls only game workers plus malloc/free, and the 0xa0000 target, 320x200 window and 368-byte padded pitch are application geometry]

Rebuild note:
The dword holding the previously seen value of the tick counter DAT_00069d64 is never initialised: the first frame's wait loop compares the counter against whatever was left on the stack, so in practice it falls straight through and the first frame is displayed without waiting a tick. Writing the obvious C -- seeding that variable with 0 or with the current value of DAT_00069d64 -- makes the first frame wait a whole tick before it advances, lengthening every playback by one tick. Leave it reading the stale value, or start it from a value the counter cannot currently hold.

=== 0001ee0d [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_0001ee10 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001ee10 [PLATE]
Draws one battle-map unit's 24x24 walk sprite into a scene buffer, in a blit mode the caller picks, so a caller can paint the unit normally or as a flat silhouette.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and converts the record's tile position to buffer pixels the way fdps_draw_map_unit does: x = record[0] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 + 0x18 and y = record[1] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0 + 0x12, where 0x18 is the tile size and DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0 are the camera origin in world pixels. The 0x12 on y is fdps_draw_map_unit's one-tile border with that routine's fixed -6 sprite lift folded into the constant, because the sprites stand taller than their 24-pixel tile.

It draws nothing unless 0 < y < 0xd8 and 0 < x < 0x150. That is the same camera window fdps_draw_map_unit clips against, only tested after the conversion instead of before: its world-space bounds DAT_00069ce4 - 0x18 < x < DAT_00069ce4 + 0x138 and DAT_00069ce0 - 0x18 < y < DAT_00069ce0 + 0xc0 are these bounds rearranged. The test looks at the sprite origin alone, so a unit near an edge is either drawn whole or dropped, never clipped.

The walk-cycle phase is the shared map animation counter DAT_00069cc8 -- which fdps_draw_map_unit steps modulo 16 once per frame tick, and nothing else in the program touches -- taken as DAT_00069cc8 / 4 with the value 3 folded back to 1, giving the ping-pong 0, 1, 2, 1. The sprite index is record[2] * 0xc + record[3] * 3 + phase: record[2] is the unit's slot in the sprite cache at DAT_00060138 that fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group filled, twelve sprites to a slot as four facings (record[3]: 0 down, 1 left, 2 up, 3 right) of three walk frames each. That index selects a self-relative entry of the cache's offset table, whose value added back to the table base gives the packed pixel stream. Finally it calls fdps_blit_dispatch(stream, scene_buffer + y * 0x168 + x, 0x18, 0x18, 0x168, blit_param, blit_mode).

Record byte 4, the unit's sub-tile step counter, is read and scaled by 4 into a local that nothing reads. The facing switch fdps_draw_map_unit uses to turn that counter into a displacement -- (0,+4), (-4,0), (0,-4), (+4,0) per step -- is absent from this body altogether, so a unit caught between tiles is drawn snapped to the tile it is leaving.

Parameters:
  scene_buffer -- the 360x240 8bpp scene buffer the caller allocated (0x15180 bytes) and filled with fdps_draw_scene_layers; the sprite is composited into it, not onto the VGA screen.
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, which bounds-checks nothing.
  blit_param -- forwarded as fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument; its meaning belongs to the kernel the mode selects, and mode 0 ignores it. All three callers pass a palette colour shifted left by 8, which fdps_blit_rle_recolor reads as add 0x00, base = the colour, mask 0x00, turning every pixel into that one palette index: 0xff00 from fdps_unit_rest and fdps_battle_advance_turn, and fdps_flash_units_in_color's own flash_color from there.
  blit_mode -- the kernel selector for fdps_blit_dispatch: 3 (fdps_blit_rle_recolor) from fdps_unit_rest and fdps_battle_advance_turn, alternating 0 (fdps_blit_rle_passthrough) and 3 every two frames from fdps_flash_units_in_color.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no fid hit in either library set; calls and is called by named game functions]

Rebuild note:
The routine computes the unit's sub-tile step offset (record[4] * 4) into a local and then never reads it, so a unit caught mid-step is drawn snapped to its tile. The sibling fdps_draw_map_unit does apply that counter, through a facing switch giving (0,+4)/(-4,0)/(0,-4)/(+4,0) per step, and the rest of this function's geometry is that routine's block trimmed -- same tile scale, same one-tile border, same -6 sprite lift folded into the y constant 0x12. Writing the obvious C, that is, finishing the offset the way the neighbour does, makes flashed and resting units drift up to 20 pixels off where the original puts them. The dead local has to survive into the rebuilt source, or the line has to be dropped, but the offset must not reach the destination address. Separately, the visibility test is strictly greater than zero on both axes, matching the strict comparisons fdps_draw_map_unit uses on the same window; writing >= 0 draws one extra row and column of units along the top and left edges that the original never shows.

=== 0001ef3b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligns FUN_0001ef40 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001ef40 [PLATE]
Plays the on-map animation of one blow landing on the defender, with both combatants' HP bars showing over the map.

Algorithm:
fdps_battle_compute_unit_gauge_position places the defender's bar into a stack position pair, then fdps_check_can_counter_attack(attacker_unit, defender_unit) decides whether the attacker's bar is wanted: when it returns exactly 1 the attacker's bar is positioned the same way into a second pair, otherwise that pair's x half is set to -1, which suppresses the attacker's bar for the whole run. Both unit records come from fdps_get_unit_record; from each it takes the side byte at +6 (side 0 selects EasyBar.cel image 2, anything else image 1) and the HP words at +0x40 (current) and +0x42 (maximum) -- the same reads fdps_battle_show_combat_gauges makes when it first puts the two bars on screen.

malloc gives it a 0x15180-byte (360x240) composite page -- no NULL test -- and each position pair becomes a destination pointer as page + (y + 0x18) * 0x168 + x + 0x18, the 0x18-pixel border the page carries on every side. The attacker's pointer is formed even when its pair is -1, out of a y half that was never written, but nothing dereferences it in that case.

It then builds the 0x24-byte composite sprite request on the stack over that page: page pointer at +0, width 0x168 and height 0xf0 at +4 and +8, the request origin at +0xc and +0x10 as defender_record[0] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 and defender_record[1] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0 - 6 (0x18 is the tile size, DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0 are the view's scroll origin in world pixels, and the -6 is the same sprite lift fdps_draw_map_unit applies), at +0x14 the "EasyAni.Saf" image that fdps_vfs_image_get_entry pulls out of the resident archive image at DAT_000643a8, and zero at +0x1c and +0x20. The entry size fdps_vfs_image_get_entry writes out is thrown away: the same local is immediately overwritten with fdps_saf_frame_count of that image, which is the frame count the loop runs to.

One pass per frame of the animation, frame number in request +0x18: fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the map -- layers, cursor and units -- into the page, fdps_draw_unit_gauge draws the attacker's bar (skipped while its pair is -1) and then the defender's, each filled to (current_hp * 0x29 + max_hp - 1) / max_hp pixels of the bar's 0x29-pixel span and to 0 when max_hp is not positive, and fdps_draw_composite_sprite draws the frame with its sound flag set, so the frame's sound effect fires. The frame is then presented in open code: spin on port 0x3DA bit 3 until vertical retrace starts and again until it ends, blit the 0x138 x 0xc0 window at page+0x21d8 -- pixel (24,24) of the 360-wide page -- with fdps_blit_rect to 0xa0504, the 4-pixel inset of the mode 13h screen, then wait for the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change. free releases the page after the last frame.

The same EasyAni.Saf animation is played for every attack; nothing here varies with the weapon or the damage.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, the unit striking. Only its HP bar and its counter-attack eligibility are used here; the animation itself plays over the defender. fdps_unit_attack_target passes its own attacker_unit_index.
  defender_unit -- same index space, the unit being hit. Its tile fixes where the animation is drawn, and its bar is always drawn. fdps_unit_attack_target passes its own target_unit_index.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit; game call graph and game data -- unit records, the view-scroll globals and the "EasyAni.Saf" asset name]

Rebuild note:
The local the frame loop compares against the tick counter DAT_00069d64 is never initialised, so the first frame does not wait for a tick. Declaring it initialised from DAT_00069d64, which is what writing the loop cleanly in C invites, costs one extra tick of animation -- the same trap as in fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead and fdps_animate_turn_banner.

=== 0001f33b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning FUN_0001f340 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001f340 [PLATE]
Plays back the queue of floating indicators standing over the battle map -- damage and healing numbers, "MISS", the status-cured mark -- bouncing every queued glyph over its unit for 22 frames, then emptying the queue.

Algorithm:
Copies the 25-byte bounce table at 0x0001c2b4 onto the stack: 15,15,15,15, 7,3,1,0,0,1,3,7, 15,15, 11,9,8,8,9,11, 15,15,15,15,15. The values are pixels of downward displacement, so read left to right the run is a rest at 15, a hop 15 pixels up and back, a short rest, a smaller hop 7 pixels up and back, and a rest. Returns immediately when the queue cursor DAT_00064378 is 0, so a playback with nothing queued costs nothing.

Otherwise it runs 22 frames. Each frame allocates a fresh 0x15180-byte (360x240) off-screen page with malloc -- no NULL check -- and repaints the scrolling map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers. It then walks the DAT_00064378 queued cells. Cell i takes its glyph id from DAT_000642b0[i]; 0xff means a blank cell and is skipped, which is what fdps_show_number_indicator writes for the leading padding of a right-aligned number. For a live cell it resolves the owning unit with fdps_get_unit_record(DAT_000641e8[i]), reads the unit's tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1, and blits the glyph out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite in mode 0 at

  x = tile_x * 24 - DAT_00069ce4 + DAT_00064120[i] + 24
  y = tile_y * 24 - DAT_00069ce0 + bounce[i % 4 + frame] + 21

where 24 is the tile size in pixels, DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0 are the camera's pixel scroll x and y, DAT_00064120[i] is the cell's x offset inside its own popup, and the +24 / +21 place the popup inside the scene page's border. The i % 4 term staggers the four cells of a popup by one frame each, so a four-digit number hops as a wave instead of as a block; with frame at most 21 and i % 4 at most 3 the table index reaches exactly 24, the table's last byte.

The frame is then presented: it spins on the VGA input status register (port 0x3da, bit 3) for a whole vertical retrace pulse, first until the bit sets and then until it clears, and blits the page's visible 312x192 window -- page + 0x21d8, i.e. 24 rows down and 24 pixels in -- to the mode-13h screen at 0xa0504 (row 4, column 4) with fdps_blit_rect. It then spins until the timer tick DAT_00069d64 differs from the tick it recorded on the previous frame, records the new tick, and frees the page.

After the 22 frames it waits 500 ms with delay and sets the queue cursor DAT_00064378 back to 0, leaving the queue empty for the next batch.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set, unique hash in the image; calls only game functions plus plain CLIB3S clients, and walks the game's own popup queue arrays]

Rebuild note:
The tick the frame loop waits on is read out of an uninitialized stack slot, so frame 0 compares against leftover stack contents and almost never waits; declaring it initialized, to 0 or to the current tick, adds a tick of delay to the first frame. And the bounce phase is the queue index modulo 4, not the cell's index inside its popup -- fdps_show_sprite_indicator advances the cursor by the number of cells it actually wrote rather than by 4, so a short indicator leaves the cursor off a multiple of four and every popup queued after it bounces out of phase; writing the phase as the per-popup cell index looks cleaner and loses that.

=== 0001f510 [PLATE]
Floats a number over one battle unit -- damage taken, HP healed, MP restored or a stat gain -- by queueing its digits into the shared indicator queue that 0x0001f340 plays back.

Algorithm:
Seeds a 5-byte stack buffer with the four-space string at 0x0001c2cd, sets the right-alignment countdown to 3 and the digit cursor to 0, then resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1.
Culls the request against the visible tile window derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y), each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: tile x must satisfy scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13, both edges exclusive, while tile y must satisfy scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8, both edges inclusive. A unit outside that window queues nothing and leaves the queue untouched.
Otherwise it formats value into the stack buffer with sprintf against the "%d" format at 0x000617bc, the same format fdps_draw_turn_number prints the turn number with, and appends exactly four cells at the shared queue cursor DAT_00064378, one per digit position: DAT_00064120[cursor + i] takes the cell's pixel x offset within the popup, i*6 + 2 for all four cells, where the fixed-word popups fdps_show_miss_indicator and fdps_queue_status_cured_popup instead use i*6 + 1 with a kerning nudge on cell 1; DAT_000641e8[cursor + i] takes the unit index as a byte; DAT_000642b0[cursor + i] takes the Number.cel glyph id glyph_base + digit - '0', or 0xff for a blank cell, which the player skips.
The right alignment comes from the countdown, which starts at 3 and drops by one after every cell: cell i writes a digit only when strlen(buffer) > 3 - i, so a one-digit number lands in the last cell with the three before it blanked, and a four-digit number fills all four. The digit cursor into the formatted string advances only on the cells that emitted, so the digits stay in order. A value of five digits or more keeps only its first four; the fifth and later digits are formatted but never queued.
The cursor DAT_00064378 is then advanced by 4. The queue is drained by 0x0001f340, which blits each cell's glyph out of the Number.cel sheet at DAT_000643d8 over its unit for 22 bouncing frames and then clears the cursor.

Parameters:
  value -- the number to float, as a signed int. Callers pass the return of fdps_unit_apply_heal, of fdps_unit_restore_mp or of the damage helper at 0x00028460, or a literal stat-gain amount of 1, 7 or 0x0f.
  glyph_base -- base glyph id in Number.cel of the ten digit sprites the number is drawn with; each digit's ASCII code is added to it and '0' subtracted, in 8-bit arithmetic. Callers pass 0 for damage, 0x0d for MP restore and stat gains, and 0x27 for healing.
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, naming the unit the number floats over. Passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record and stored as a byte in DAT_000641e8.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record, which a pre-compiled library module could not; shares the battle popup queue globals DAT_00064120 / DAT_000641e8 / DAT_000642b0 / DAT_00064378 and the camera scroll globals with the rest of the battle display code; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The visible-window cull is deliberately asymmetric and writing it symmetrically changes which units get a number at the map edge: the x test rejects the column at scroll_x/24 - 1 (both edges exclusive, columns scroll_x/24 .. scroll_x/24 + 12) while the y test accepts the row at scroll_y/24 - 1 (both edges inclusive, rows scroll_y/24 - 1 .. scroll_y/24 + 8). Also, the x offset written into DAT_00064120 is i*6 + 2 for all four cells here, not the i*6 + 1 with a cell-1 nudge that the fixed-word siblings at 0001f690 and 0001f7d0 use, so folding the three producers onto one shared helper shifts the digits one pixel.

=== 0001f686 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4-byte nop), aligning FUN_0001f690 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001f690 [PLATE]
Queues the four-glyph "MISS" indicator over one battle unit, for the effect code to report that a spell or item did nothing to that target.

Algorithm:
Copies the four Number.cel glyph ids held in the read-only dword at 0x0001c2d2 (0x34 0x35 0x36 0x36 = M, I, S, S) into a stack buffer, then resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record and reads its tile x from record byte 0 and tile y from record byte 1. Culls the request against the visible tile window, derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y) each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: x must satisfy scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13 (both edges exclusive, so columns scroll_x/24 .. scroll_x/24+12) while y must satisfy scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8 (both edges inclusive). A unit outside that window queues nothing and leaves the queue count untouched. Otherwise it appends four cells at the shared indicator-queue cursor DAT_00064378, one per glyph: the cell's x offset in pixels into DAT_00064120 (i*6+1 for the 6-pixel-wide glyphs, except cell 1 which gets i*6+2 = 8 so the narrow I sits clear of the wide M), the unit index into DAT_000641e8, and the glyph id into DAT_000642b0. The cursor then advances by 4. fdps_play_indicator_queue later draws every queued cell out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite, at the unit's tile position minus the camera scroll plus a per-frame bounce offset, and zeroes the cursor when the animation ends. This is the fixed-word member of a four-producer family that shares that queue: fdps_show_number_indicator formats digits into it, fdps_show_sprite_indicator takes the glyph ids from its caller, and fdps_queue_status_cured_popup is the CURE counterpart of this one, queueing the adjacent glyph dword at 0x0001c2d6.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; the callers pass one entry of the target id list they are iterating.

Returns:
  Nothing. The indicator queue at DAT_00064120 / DAT_000641e8 / DAT_000642b0 and its count at DAT_00064378 are the output.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The viewport cull is asymmetric between the axes and the obvious symmetric rewrite changes which units get a popup: x is exclusive on both edges (scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13) while y is inclusive on both (scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8), so a unit one row above the top of the view still gets its MISS drawn but a unit one column left of the view does not. The per-cell x offsets carry the same trap: they are i*6+1 except cell 1, which is 8 rather than 7, and writing the uniform i*6+1 shifts the I of MISS one pixel left. Keep the divisions signed int divisions (the original uses IDIV, truncating toward zero) rather than shifts.
