=== 0001f7d0 [PLATE]
Queues the four-glyph "CURE" indicator over one battle unit, for the effect code to report that a status ailment has just been lifted from that target.

Algorithm:
Copies the four Number.cel glyph ids held in the read-only dword at 0x0001c2d6 (0x37 0x38 0x39 0x3a = C, U, R, E) into a stack buffer, then resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1. Culls the request against the visible tile window derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y), each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: x must satisfy scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13 (both edges exclusive, so columns scroll_x/24 .. scroll_x/24 + 12) while y must satisfy scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8 (both edges inclusive). A unit outside that window queues nothing and leaves the queue cursor untouched. Otherwise it appends four cells at the shared indicator-queue cursor DAT_00064378, one per glyph: the cell's x offset in pixels into DAT_00064120 (i*6 + 1, except cell 1 which gets i*6 + 2 = 8), the unit index into DAT_000641e8, and the glyph id into DAT_000642b0. The cursor then advances by 4. fdps_play_indicator_queue later draws every queued cell out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite, at the unit's tile position minus the camera scroll plus a per-frame bounce offset, and zeroes the cursor when the animation ends.

This is one of the two fixed-word producers of that queue, the same body as fdps_show_miss_indicator (0001f690) with only the glyph dword changed; the other two producers are fdps_show_number_indicator, which formats digits into it, and fdps_show_sprite_indicator, which takes the glyph ids from its caller.

All three call sites fire on the same shape: the caller has resolved the target, has found at least one of the status-ailment bytes at unit record +0x25, +0x26 or +0x27 non-zero, and is about to clear it and play "Cure.saf" over the target. fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets calls here for item effect code 0x16 when +0x25 is set (00026888-00026899, then MOV byte ptr [EAX + 0x25],0x0) and for code 0x18 when +0x26 is set (00026914-00026925); fdps_cast_spell_on_targets calls here when any of the three bytes is set (00028c4b-00028c73) and then memsets all three to 0. So the indicator marks a cure that actually took effect, never a cure applied to a unit that was not ailing.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; the callers pass one entry of the target id list they are iterating.

Returns:
  Nothing. The indicator queue at DAT_00064120 / DAT_000641e8 / DAT_000642b0 and its cursor at DAT_00064378 are the output; whether the indicator was queued or culled away is not reported.

Pool: fdps  [no library match in either Function ID set; calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record and writes only the game's indicator-queue and camera globals]

Rebuild note:
The viewport cull is asymmetric between the axes and the obvious symmetric rewrite changes which units get an indicator at the map edge: x is exclusive on both edges (JGE at 0001f821 rejects the column at scroll_x/24 - 1, JG at 0001f83e rejects scroll_x/24 + 13) while y is inclusive on both (JLE at 0001f85b accepts scroll_y/24 - 1, JGE at 0001f87a accepts scroll_y/24 + 8), so a unit one row above the view still gets its CURE drawn but a unit one column left of the view does not. The per-cell x offsets carry a second trap: they are i*6 + 1 except cell 1, which is 8 rather than 7 (0001f8a5 ADD AL,0x2 against 0001f8bf INC AL). That nudge is positional, not kerning -- it is the same code as the MISS producer, where cell 1 is the narrow I, and here it lands on the U regardless. Writing it as a per-letter kerning rule, or folding it away to a uniform i*6 + 1, moves the U by a pixel. Keep both divisions signed int divisions by 24 (IDIV with the dividend sign-extended by SAR EDX,0x1f), not shifts.

=== 0001f910 [PLATE]
Flashes a list of battle-map units in one palette colour, over eight tick-paced frames, so the units an effect has just been applied to are marked out on screen.

Algorithm:
Runs eight frames, i = 0..7. Each frame allocates an 0x15180-byte (360x240) offscreen scene buffer with malloc and fills it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, which already paints every unit on the map through fdps_draw_map_units; it then redraws just the listed units on top, calling fdps_blit_unit_sprite(buf, unit_indices[j], flash_color << 8, mode) for j = 0..unit_count-1. The mode is 3 when (i / 2) & 1 and 0 otherwise, so frames 0,1 and 4,5 use mode 0 (fdps_blit_rle_passthrough), which redraws each sprite over the identical pixels already in the buffer and changes nothing visible, while frames 2,3 and 6,7 use mode 3 (fdps_blit_rle_recolor), which paints every pixel of the sprite as one palette index: the listed units go flat-coloured twice. flash_color is shifted left by 8 once at entry, which lands it in fdps_blit_rle_recolor's base field with the add and mask fields left at 0.
Presentation repeats fdps_render_view_frame's sequence without the cursor panel and without the palette cycling: poll port 0x3DA until bit 3 sets and again until it clears, spanning vertical retrace; fdps_blit_rect(buf + 0x21d8, 0x168, 0xa0504, 0x140, 0x138, 0xc0) to copy the 312x192 interior of the buffer into the mode 13h screen 4 pixels in from its top left; spin until the interrupt-driven tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the value latched at the end of the previous frame; free the buffer. Unlike fdps_render_view_frame the latched tick is kept in a stack local rather than in DAT_00069d10.

Parameters:
  unit_count -- how many entries of unit_indices to flash. Zero is legal and turns the call into an eight-tick pause. Every caller passes the target count of the effect it has just applied.
  unit_indices -- array of unit_count byte indices into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8. Each index goes straight to fdps_blit_unit_sprite, which silently drops any unit whose sprite origin lies outside the visible view. Every caller passes the target id list of the effect it has just applied.
  flash_color -- the palette index every pixel of a flashed sprite becomes. FUN_000262a0 (the Cure/CureMP branches) and fdps_apply_heal_to_targets pass 0xff; FUN_000288f0 passes 0x2b for effect id 0x11 and calls twice in a row, giving four flashes.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_draw_scene_layers, fdps_blit_unit_sprite and fdps_blit_rect, and drives the game's own VGA presentation geometry and tick global; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The per-frame tick wait compares the tick counter against a stack local that nothing writes before the first frame, so the first frame waits either not at all or a full tick depending on what that slot happened to hold. Initialising the local, or latching into DAT_00069d10 the way fdps_render_view_frame does, changes the pacing of the first flash frame -- and writing DAT_00069d10 would also perturb the next fdps_render_view_frame call. Leave the local uninitialised.

=== 0001fa2b [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0]) + 8b c9 (mov ecx,ecx), 5 bytes to 16-byte boundary.

=== 0001fa30 [PLATE]
Ticks the status effects running on one side's battle units once per turn: the poison damage first, then the countdown of all six effect timers.

Algorithm:
Sweeps unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the battle unit count) twice, taking each 0x50-byte record from fdps_get_unit_record.
First sweep, poison damage. A unit is hit when its poison timer -- record byte +0x25, the slot fdps_unit_apply_status_effect writes for effect id 0x12 -- is running, its side byte +0x06 equals side, and the retired bit 0x01 of byte +0x05 is clear (the test fdps_unit_is_retired makes, inlined here). The damage is the unit's maximum HP (unsigned word +0x42) divided by 10, published as a dword in the shared damage-value global DAT_00064038; it comes off current HP (word +0x40) and the result is floored at 0, so poison can leave a unit at 0 HP but never below it. Then the presentation: DAT_00069cd0, the map-cursor overlay mode fdps_draw_map_cursor dispatches on, is set to 0 so no cursor is drawn; fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit brings the view onto the unit; 0x00026e00(1, &unit_index_byte, "PosEff.saf") plays the poison animation over it; fdps_show_number_indicator(DAT_00064038, 0, unit_index) queues the damage figure and 0x0001f340 plays the indicator queue back; DAT_00069cd0 is set to 1.
Between the sweeps, 0x0001d6c0 plays the destruction sequence for anything the poison just brought to 0 HP, and the current chapter's post-action handler is called through the table at 0x0006028c indexed by the chapter index DAT_00069cf4 -- the same win/lose test the AI phases and fdps_battle_unit_turn run after a unit acts, so a poison death can end the battle.
Second sweep, countdown. For every unit whose side byte +0x06 equals side and whose retired bit is clear, each of the six status timers at record +0x22 .. +0x27 that is non-zero is decremented by one; that is the three buff slots fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats reads followed by the three ailment slots, poison's own +0x25 among them, so a poison timer ticks down after its damage has already been applied this turn. A timer that reaches zero sets DAT_00069cd0 to 0 and calls fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(unit_index) so the expired buff drops back out of the unit's derived stats. Nothing on that path puts DAT_00069cd0 back.

Parameters:
  side -- the side whose units are ticked, compared against unit record byte +0x06 as a zero-extended byte: 2 is the player side, 1 the NPC side, 0 the enemy side. fdps_battle_advance_turn is the only caller and passes 1, then 0, then 2, each call immediately after fdps_battle_run_turn_events for the same side.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is not set on the exit path and the caller does not look at it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the watcom or ail sets, hash unique in the image; walks the game unit records through fdps_get_unit_record and is called only by fdps_battle_advance_turn]

Rebuild note:
The two sweeps are not symmetric about the cursor-mode global DAT_00069cd0: the poison sweep sets it to 0 and back to 1, but the timer-expiry branch sets it to 0 and leaves it there, so after any status effect runs out the map cursor is not drawn again until something else sets the mode. Writing the obvious restore, or deleting the write as pointless because fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats draws nothing, changes what the phase that follows looks like.

=== 0001fbff [EOL]
Alignment padding: single 0x90 NOP between FUN_0001fa30 and FUN_0001fc00.

=== 0001fc00 [PLATE]
Queues a floating indicator over one battle unit out of sprites the caller supplies: up to four Number.cel sprite ids that rise over the unit's tile when the indicator queue is played back. It is the member of the indicator-producer family whose message is an argument rather than a constant.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and takes the unit's tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1.
Culls the request against the visible map window derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y), each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: nothing is queued unless tile_x > scroll_x/24 - 1 (0001fc4c) and tile_x < scroll_x/24 + 13 (0001fc67) and tile_y >= scroll_y/24 - 1 (0001fc86) and tile_y <= scroll_y/24 + 8 (0001fca3). The two lower edges are not written the same way -- x is exclusive, y inclusive -- so a unit one row above the window still gets its indicator while one column left of it does not. fdps_show_number_indicator and fdps_show_miss_indicator apply the identical predicate.
Then for each cell i of 0..3 it reads sprite_ids[i]. A zero id skips that cell and the loop moves straight on to the next one; it does not stop the loop. A non-zero id appends one entry at slot DAT_00064378 + i -- indexed by the loop counter, not by how many cells have been written -- of the three parallel byte queues: DAT_00064120 takes the cell's x offset in pixels within the unit's tile, i*6+1, except cell 1 which takes 8 so a narrow second letter sits clear of a wide first one; DAT_000641e8 takes unit_index as a byte; DAT_000642b0 takes sprite_ids[i].
Finally it adds the number of cells it actually wrote, not 4, to the queue cursor DAT_00064378.

fdps_play_indicator_queue drains the queue: for 22 frames it blits each entry's sprite out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8, loaded by fdps_load_global_resources) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite at (tile_x*24 - DAT_00069ce4 + x_offset + 24, tile_y*24 - DAT_00069ce0 + bounce offset + 21), skipping any entry whose sprite id is 0xff, then zeroes the cursor. The sibling plates call the DAT_000642b0 bytes glyph ids -- Number.cel is a 65-sprite 6x8 font sheet of digits and letters, and each of those producers knows which word its own ids spell -- but they are the same bytes as this function's sprite_ids.

The other three producers sharing the queue are fdps_show_number_indicator, which formats digits into the cells, and fdps_show_miss_indicator and fdps_queue_status_cured_popup, which push the fixed words at 0x0001c2d2 and 0x0001c2d6.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit the indicator floats over, into the 0x50-byte record array behind DAT_00069cd8; passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record and stored as a byte in DAT_000641e8. Its one caller fdps_cast_spell_on_targets passes an id out of its target list.
  sprite_ids -- pointer to up to four Number.cel sprite ids for the indicator's four 6-pixel cells, a zero id marking an unused cell. fdps_cast_spell_on_targets passes one 4-byte row of the three-label table at 0x00027668, each row being three ids followed by a zero. Decoding Number.cel gives sprite 0x3b='A', 0x3c='t', 0x3d='D', 0x3e='e', 0x3f='f' and 0x40='x', so the three rows spell Att, Def and Dex -- the three 神之祝福 buff slots that fdps_unit_apply_status_effect writes to unit-record bytes +0x22, +0x23 and +0x24. Nothing in this body depends on that; the ids are copied unread.

Returns:
  Nothing. Whether the unit was on screen is not reported, so the caller cannot tell a culled request from a queued one.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record and touches only game draw-list and camera state]

Rebuild note:
The queue cursor DAT_00064378 advances by the number of non-zero sprite ids while the slots are indexed by the loop counter (cursor + i), so the two agree only while the non-zero ids form a prefix -- which holds solely because every label the caller passes is ids-then-zero. Writing the obvious DAT_00064378 += 4 that the sibling producers use leaves an unwritten slot inside the drawn range for a three-id label, and turning the skip into a blank-cell write is wrong too, because the consumer's blank marker is 0xff, not 0. The viewport cull is deliberately lop-sided as well: the x lower edge is exclusive but the y lower edge is inclusive, so writing the two range tests symmetrically changes which units get an indicator along the top and left edges of the view. Keep both divisions signed (the original uses IDIV, truncating toward zero) rather than shifts.

=== 0001fd4e [EOL]
Two zero bytes of alignment padding after FUN_0001fc00, aligning to 0001fd50.

=== 0001fd58 [EOL]

=== 0001fd70 [EOL]

=== 0001fd80 [PLATE]
Draws one glyph of the game's 1bpp font into an 8bpp surface together with its background cell and its outline or drop shadow, doing every actual pixel write through fdps_blit_glyph_1bpp.

Algorithm:
Advances the font_base parameter in place by glyph_index * DAT_00064046 (the bytes-per-glyph stride of the font sheet) to reach this glyph's bitmap. If bg_color is non-zero, fills the glyph cell at dst with it first: DAT_0006403d rows of DAT_0006403c bytes, stepping one pitch per row -- both globals are read as zero-extended bytes and are the cell height and width in pixels, taken from the font, not from the caller. Then draws the decoration underneath the glyph, choosing between two styles on the flag byte DAT_0006404a: when it is non-zero the glyph is blitted four times in outline_color at dst+pitch, dst-1, dst-pitch and dst+1, a 4-connected one-pixel outline; when it is zero a single drop shadow is blitted instead, and only if outline_color is non-zero, at dst + DAT_00064042 * pitch + DAT_0006403e, i.e. displaced by the row count in DAT_00064042 and the column count in DAT_0006403e. Finally, if fg_color is non-zero, the glyph itself is blitted at dst in fg_color, so the foreground lands on top of the decoration.

Parameters:
  dst -- destination pixel, the top-left corner of the glyph cell in an 8bpp surface; the caller at 0001ff60 walks it across the line one glyph advance at a time
  pitch -- destination row stride in bytes; also the one-row step used to place the outline and the shadow
  font_base -- base of the 1bpp font sheet, glyph n at font_base + n * DAT_00064046; the caller passes the global font pointer DAT_000643cc
  glyph_index -- which glyph of that sheet to draw; the caller passes a message token value, or a decimal digit reduced by '0'
  fg_color -- palette index of the glyph body; 0 suppresses the foreground blit
  bg_color -- palette index the cell is filled with before anything is drawn; 0 skips the fill
  outline_color -- palette index of the outline or of the drop shadow; 0 suppresses the shadow but not the outline

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no FID candidate in either library set, and neither the Watcom runtime nor Miles contains a glyph renderer; reads the game's font/display globals 0x6403c-0x6404a and its only callee is game rendering code]

Rebuild note:
The four outline blits at 0001fdfd-0001fe62 are NOT guarded by outline_color != 0, while the drop-shadow blit at 0001fe67 and the foreground blit at 0001fe9c both are. Writing the obvious symmetric C -- one `if (outline_color != 0)` around the whole decoration step -- silently drops the outline whenever a caller passes 0, where the original paints four palette-index-0 copies of the glyph around it. Also, the cell dimensions and the glyph stride come from the globals DAT_0006403c/0006403d/00064046, not from the glyph or from the caller, and the two size globals are byte-sized and zero-extended (XOR EAX,EAX; MOV AL,[...]), so declaring them as signed char breaks cells wider or taller than 127 pixels.

=== 0001fec1 [EOL]
Alignment padding: multi-byte LEA NOP forms aligning FUN_0001fed0 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001fed0 [PLATE]
Blits one 1bpp glyph bitmap into an 8-bit destination surface, painting a single palette colour wherever a source bit is set and leaving every other pixel untouched.

Algorithm:
Loops row from 0 while row is below the glyph cell height at DAT_0006403d, and inside it column from 0 while column is below the glyph cell width at DAT_0006403c; both bounds are zero-extended bytes re-read from the globals on every iteration. A shift register -- a full dword local -- holds the current source byte: on each column whose low three bits are zero it takes the next byte from glyph_bits and advances that pointer, otherwise it shifts the register left by one. When bit 7 (0x80) of the register is set it stores the low byte of color at dst[column]; when it is clear it writes nothing, so unset bits leave the destination as it was. After each row dst advances by pitch, which is also what makes DAT_0006403c the horizontal extent and DAT_0006403d the vertical one: the inner index is a byte offset inside a single destination row, the outer step is a whole row. Source rows are byte-aligned -- the fetch condition is true again at column 0 of every row, so one row consumes ceil(width/8) bytes and the spare bits of a row's last byte are skipped rather than carried into the next row. There is no clipping and no bounds check of any kind; the caller owns keeping the destination inside its surface.

Parameters:
  dst -- destination 8bpp pixel at the top-left corner of the glyph cell. fdps_draw_glyph passes its own destination offset by +pitch, -1, -pitch or +1 to lay down the four outline copies, by the shadow displacement for the drop-shadow style, and unoffset for the body pass.
  pitch -- bytes from one destination row to the next; added to the working destination pointer once per row. The values that reach it from fdps_draw_text are 0x140 for the visible screen and 0x138 for the 312-wide offscreen pages.
  glyph_bits -- start of this glyph's 1bpp bitmap, most significant bit first, rows padded to whole bytes. Only the local copy is advanced, so the caller's pointer survives and the same glyph can be blitted repeatedly; fdps_draw_glyph depends on that for its outline passes.
  color -- palette index stored for set bits; only the low byte is used.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX at RET holds the zero-extended DAT_0006403d height byte left by the final row test, which no call site reads.

Pool: fdps  [no match in either FID set and the body hash is unique in the image; it shares the glyph cell width/height globals DAT_0006403c/DAT_0006403d with its application caller fdps_draw_glyph and touches no CRT, DOS or AIL state]

=== 0001ff56 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4), aligning FUN_0001ff60 to 16 bytes

=== 0001ff60 [PLATE]
Draws one entry of a game text block into an 8bpp surface, interpreting the control codes embedded in the entry, and hands back the destination cursor it stopped at. Every piece of text the game shows -- menu labels, item names, save-slot dates and the chapters' spoken lines -- is drawn by this one routine.

Algorithm:
Adds the signed 16-bit word text_base[text_id] to text_base as a byte offset, landing on that entry's token stream, and walks the stream word by word until the -1 terminator. The line height is read out of DAT_0006404f once, at entry. Each signed 16-bit token is handled as:
  -2  line break: bumps the line counter and puts the cursor at dest + pitch * DAT_0006404f * line_count.
  -3  page break: fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, then fdps_message_window_wait_key(1, 0x64), then composes a fresh panel in a malloc'd 0x15180-byte 360x240 scratch canvas -- on the battle map (DAT_00060070 == 0) fdps_draw_scene_layers rebuilds the map into it and the Message.cel sheet DAT_000643d0 is blitted at (0x1d, 0x8c); in the village (DAT_00060070 != 0) fdps_blit_rect copies the visible screen in at scratch (24, 24) and the ShopWin.Cel sheet DAT_00069d84 is blitted at (0x18, 0x8d). When a speaker portrait is loaded (DAT_00060120, the FACE.CEL image that fdps_load_and_draw_portrait keeps) its 125x100 picture goes in at scratch (32, 110) through fdps_blit_dispatch. It then sits out one whole vertical retrace pulse on port 0x3da (spins until bit 3 sets, then until it clears again), copies the 312x192 window back to screen address 0xa0504, frees the scratch, clears the line counter and restarts dest at the panel's text origin -- 0xaa44a on the battle map, 0xaa3d4 in the village.
  -4, -5  substitution: calls itself on the global text block DAT_000643c4 at the entry ids held in DAT_00064030 and DAT_00064034, always in the standard message colours 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d rather than the caller's, and carries on from the cursor that call returns.
  -6  number: sprintf's DAT_00064038 through the format at DAT_000617e8 into a 12-byte stack buffer, takes its strlen, and draws it one digit at a time with fdps_draw_glyph as glyph index (digit - '0'), advancing the cursor by 0x10 per digit rather than by the glyph width.
  -0x11  speaker by character id: closes the window this call has already opened, if any (fdps_message_window_wait_key(1, 0x64) then fdps_message_window_close), reads the character id from the following word, resolves it with fdps_battle_find_unit_by_character_id, and takes the portrait index from byte +0x07 of the record whenever that call handed one back. It then opens the window with fdps_message_window_open_from_tile at the speaker's tile (record bytes +0x00 and +0x01) or, when the character is not standing on the map, at (-1, 0). Clears the line counter, puts dest at 0xaa44a and steps the stream by two words.
  -0x12  speaker by unit index: the same, except the following word is a unit index passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, so the portrait always comes from byte +0x07 of that record.
  anything else  a glyph index: fdps_draw_glyph(cursor, pitch, DAT_000643cc, token, fg_color, bg_color, outline_color), then cursor += DAT_0006404b, the glyph advance.
On the -1 terminator it waits out and closes the message window if one of the speaker codes opened it, and returns the cursor.

Parameters:
  text_base -- start of a text block: a table of signed 16-bit byte offsets followed by the token streams those offsets point at. Callers pass the global game-text pointer DAT_000643c4, the current chapter's text at DAT_00060124, or a block they have just loaded themselves.
  text_id -- which entry of that table to draw, a 0-based index into the offset table. Callers pass literal ids and computed ones alike (fdps_shop_draw_item_entry passes item_id + 0xc9).
  dest -- the byte address the first glyph goes at, and the line origin that the -2 line break measures from. Either an offscreen surface or a raw VGA address; the -3, -0x11 and -0x12 codes overwrite it with a fixed screen address, so an entry carrying them only comes out right from a caller drawing straight to the screen at pitch 0x140.
  pitch -- bytes per row of dest: 0x140 for the visible screen, 0x138 for the game's 312-wide offscreen pages.
  fg_color -- glyph fill colour, handed to fdps_draw_glyph unchanged. 0xd0 for ordinary text, 0xc8 for a menu entry that is not available.
  bg_color -- glyph background colour for fdps_draw_glyph; 0 everywhere, which leaves the background untouched.
  outline_color -- glyph outline/shadow colour for fdps_draw_glyph; 0x6d everywhere.

Returns:
  The destination cursor one glyph past the last glyph drawn, so a caller can chain a second entry onto the end of the first.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game call graph and game globals]

Rebuild note:
dest is a parameter, but the body writes to it: the -3 page break and both speaker codes replace it with a fixed screen address (0xaa44a / 0xaa3d4) and the -2 line break then measures from that new value. The obvious rewrite -- leave the parameter alone and keep the cursor in a separate local -- drops every line after a page break or a speaker change back at the caller's original origin. The -4 and -5 substitution calls likewise hard-code the glyph colours 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d instead of forwarding fg_color / bg_color / outline_color, so a substituted string stays in the standard message colours even inside text the caller asked for in another colour.

=== 000203ce [EOL]
2-byte alignment padding (mov eax,eax) before 16-byte aligned entry FUN_000203d0

=== 000203d0 [PLATE]
Holds the message window that fdps_message_window_open left standing on screen, repainting it over a live background once per game tick, until the player presses a key or the tick budget runs out.

Algorithm:
Allocates a 0x561e-byte (302 x 73) buffer and copies the message window straight off the visible mode-13h screen into it with fdps_blit_rect, from 0xa9609 = 0xa0000 + 120*320 + 9 at pitch 320 -- the exact place and size fdps_message_window_open puts the Message.cel panel, so the copy carries whatever text FUN_0001ff60 has already written into it. The four corner pixels of that copy (offsets 0, 0x12d, 0x54f0 and 0x561d) are then set to palette index 0, so the window's corners read as transparent when it is put back.
One pass per game tick follows, at most timeout_ticks of them:
  - fdps_read_keyboard_queue takes the next scancode, and the loop ends as soon as that byte is below 0x80, i.e. a key-press make code. 0xff (the queue-empty report) and 0x80-0xfe (key-release break codes) let it carry on; the scancode itself is discarded either way.
  - Allocates a 0x15180-byte (360 x 240) frame. The frame carries the scene layer's 24-pixel margin: frame (24, 24), byte offset 0x21d8, is screen (4, 4), so a frame position is a screen position plus 20 rows and 20 columns.
  - Background. When the flag at 00060070 is clear -- the battle map, where fdps_run_village_phase has not set it -- fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the whole scrolling scene into the frame, so the map keeps animating behind the window. When it is set, the 312 x 192 viewport is copied off the visible page at 0xa0504 into the frame instead, leaving a static backdrop.
  - fdps_blit_transparent_rect puts the saved window back at frame offset 0xc4fd, screen (9, 120), with palette index 0 transparent.
  - When show_wait_indicator is set, fdps_blit_command_sprite draws Command.cel sprite 0x48 + (tick / 3 & 3) at frame offset 0x106bc, screen (280, 166) -- the bottom right corner of the window -- so the four-phase prompt indicator advances one phase every three ticks. The tick it divides is the value read from DAT_00069d64 on the previous pass, so the first pass always draws phase 0.
  - When a portrait is loaded, i.e. the FACE.CEL cache pointer at 00060120 that fdps_load_and_draw_portrait fills is not null, fdps_blit_dispatch mode 0 draws it 125 x 100 at frame offset 0x9ad0, screen (12, 90).
  - Waits on VGA input status port 0x3da for bit 3 to go high and then low -- for the vertical retrace to start and then finish -- then copies the frame's 312 x 192 viewport to 0xa0504 on the visible page.
  - Spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the value recorded on the previous pass, records the new value, frees the frame and decrements timeout_ticks; the loop repeats while that count is not 0.
The saved window is freed on the way out. The 360 x 240 frame is allocated and freed inside the loop, once per pass.

Parameters:
  show_wait_indicator -- nonzero draws the blinking four-phase prompt indicator in the bottom right corner of the window, zero leaves it out. All nine call sites pass 1.
  timeout_ticks -- the most game ticks to keep waiting, decremented once per pass and tested against 0 at the bottom of the loop, so a key press can end the wait earlier. Callers pass 0x1e, 0x32 or 0x64. Nobody passes 0, which would wrap and spin for 2^32 ticks.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; both callers are game code, it reads the game's own globals at 00060070, 00060120 and 00069d64, and touches the C runtime only as a consumer of malloc, free and inp]

Rebuild note:
The frame pacing spins on DAT_00069d64, which nothing in this function writes -- fdps_timer_tick_handler increments it from the timer interrupt. Written as the obvious while (last_tick == g_frame_tick) ; over a plain int global, wcc386 loads the counter once into a register and the loop never ends. The counter has to be declared volatile.

=== 000205af [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP aligning FUN_000205b0 to a 16-byte boundary.

=== 000205b0 [PLATE]
Opens the game's message window over whatever is on screen: slides the Message.cel panel up from the bottom while fading it in, then leaves it standing with the speaker's FACE.CEL portrait drawn in it.

Algorithm:
Copies the six-entry row table at 0001fd50 (190, 170, 150, 135, 127, 120) onto the stack. Allocates a 64000-byte work page, a 64000-byte screen backup and a 0x561e-byte (302 x 73) panel buffer; grabs the visible mode-13h screen from 0xa0000 into the backup, zeroes the panel buffer and renders Message.cel sprite 0 -- the sheet in the global at 000643d0, loaded by fdps_load_global_resources -- into it at pitch 302.
Six animation steps then run, i = 0..5: restore the work page from the backup, take row = table[i], clip the band height to min(200 - row, 73), and alpha-blend the panel over the work page in place at (9, row) through fdps_blit_blend_rects, passing the [18][256] weighted-palette table at 000653f0 (Mer1.tmp) as its blend_table and the 16x16x16 inverse-palette cube at 000643f0 (Mer2.tmp) as its rgb444_lut -- both filled by fdps_build_palette_tables -- with blend weight i*2+5. fdps_blit_blend_rects divides by 16, so the panel comes in at 5/16, 7/16, 9/16, 11/16, 13/16 and 15/16 of full strength. Each step waits on VGA input status port 0x3da for bit 3 to go high and then low -- for the vertical retrace to start and then finish -- and copies the work page to 0xa0000, so the copy starts at the top of active display rather than inside the blanking interval.
Finally it restores the work page once more, draws Message.cel sprite 0 fully opaque at (9, 120) through fdps_cel_blit_sprite -- the 16/16 step, done as a plain blit rather than a blend -- waits on the same retrace edge, presents that page and frees all three buffers. The window is left standing: callers write their text into it with fdps_draw_text at 0xaa44a and take it down again with fdps_message_window_close, which walks the identical row table at 0001fd68 backwards and runs the weight ramp in reverse.
The portrait is last. A face_index of 0 or more is handed to fdps_load_and_draw_portrait with destination 0xa708c (screen x 12, y 90) and pitch 320, which loads that FACE.CEL entry into the cache at 00060120 and blits it 125x100 over the left edge of the window. A negative face_index means no speaker: the cached portrait at 00060120 is freed and the pointer cleared in line, rather than through fdps_load_and_draw_portrait, whose own no-portrait test is == -1 and not < 0.

Parameters:
  face_index -- index of the speaker's portrait in FACE.CEL, or negative for a window with no portrait. Callers pass a fixed index (3, 0x23, 0x28, 0x77, 0x7a, 0x81), byte 7 or byte 8 of a unit record, or, by way of fdps_message_window_open_from_tile, a signed character id read out of a message token that stays negative when that speaker is not standing on the map.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the Watcom or AIL sets, unique hash in the image; all fourteen callers are game code and the C runtime appears only as callees]

Rebuild note:
The retrace wait is two-phase -- spin until 0x3da bit 3 is set, then spin until it is clear -- so the 64000-byte page copy begins at the start of active display, not inside the blanking interval. The usual single-phase wait-for-bit-3-set alone starts each copy one blanking period earlier and changes what the six-step reveal looks like on screen.

=== 00020817 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + lea edx,[edx+0] (3-byte nop), aligning next function to 0x20820.

=== 00020820 [PLATE]
Closes the game's message window: slides the empty Message.cel panel down off the bottom of the screen while fading it out, over a freshly rebuilt map scene, and leaves that clean scene standing on the visible page. The counterpart of fdps_message_window_open, which every caller pairs it with.

Algorithm:
Copies the six-entry row table at 0001fd68 (190, 170, 150, 135, 127, 120) onto the stack -- byte-identical to the table fdps_message_window_open walks at 0001fd50, but read from the far end.
It builds its backdrop instead of grabbing it. It mallocs an 0x15180-byte (360x240) scene scratch buffer, composites the live scrolling scene into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, mallocs a 64000-byte (320x200) base page and zeroes it, and fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312x192) view window from scratch+0x21d8 (x=24, y=24 at stride 0x168) to base+0x504 (x=4, y=4 at stride 0x140), leaving the four-pixel border black. It then mallocs a 64000-byte work page, frees the scratch buffer, mallocs an 0x561e-byte (302x73) panel buffer, zeroes it and renders Message.cel sprite 0 -- the sheet in the global at 000643d0 -- into it at pitch 302. That panel carries no text and no portrait.
Six animation steps then run, i = 5 down to 0: restore the work page from the base page, take row = table[i], clip the band height to min(200 - row, 73), and alpha-blend the panel over the work page in place at (9, row) through fdps_blit_blend_rects, using the [18][256] weight table at 000653f0 and the 4096-entry inverse-palette lookup at 000643f0 that fdps_build_palette_tables fills, with blend weight i*2+5. Each step waits on VGA input status port 0x3da for bit 3 to go high and then low -- for the vertical retrace to start and then finish -- and copies the work page to 0xa0000, so the copy starts at the top of active display rather than inside the blanking interval.
Because i descends, row runs 120, 127, 135, 150, 170, 190 and the blend weight runs 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, 5 out of the 16 that fdps_blit_blend_rects divides by, so the panel drops toward the bottom of the screen and thins out as it goes. The height clip bites from row 135 on, shortening the visible band from 73 rows to 10 as the panel runs off the bottom edge.
Finally it waits on the same retrace edge once more and presents the base page -- the bare scene, no panel -- then frees the work page, the base page and the panel buffer. Nothing else is released: the FACE.CEL portrait fdps_message_window_open cached at 00060120 is left in place.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the Watcom or AIL sets, unique hash in the image; all fourteen callers are game code and the C runtime appears only as callees]

Rebuild note:
Two things the natural close animation gets wrong. It does not retract the window that is on screen: it throws the visible page away and recomposites the map with fdps_draw_scene_layers, and the panel it slides is a bare Message.cel with nothing drawn into it, so the message text and the speaker portrait are gone from the first animation frame instead of riding the window down. And the retrace wait is two-phase -- spin on port 0x3da until bit 3 is set, then spin until it is clear -- so each 64000-byte copy to 0xa0000 begins at the start of active display; the obvious single-phase wait starts every copy one blanking period earlier and changes what the six steps look like.

=== 00020a65 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx (11 bytes to align next function at 0x20a70)

=== 00020a70 [PLATE]
Opens the game's message window for a speaker standing on the map: grows the Message.cel panel out of the speaker's tile over seven scaled steps until it reaches the window's resting place, then paints the speaker's FACE.CEL portrait into it.

Algorithm:
When tile_x is -1 the speaker is not on the map, so the zoom is skipped entirely and fdps_message_window_open plays its slide-up open instead; control then joins the portrait draw below.
Otherwise it clears the map-cursor draw mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so no cursor is painted, walks the view and the cursor onto the speaker with fdps_map_cursor_move_to(tile_x * 0x18, tile_y * 0x18) -- 0x18 is the tile size in pixels -- and then sets DAT_00069cd0 back to 1, the ordinary cursor mode, rather than restoring what it held on entry. The speaker's position in view pixels is taken after that scroll: vx = tile_x * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 and vy = tile_y * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0, the camera's pixel scroll x and y.
Seven steps then run with i = 0..6. Each one allocates a fresh 0x15180-byte (360 x 240) scene page, composites the scrolling map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, and derives the panel's destination size as width = i * 0x12e / 6 (forced to 4 when that comes out 0) and height = i * 0x49 / 6 (forced to 2 when 0), 0x12e x 0x49 being Message.cel's full 302 x 73 sprite size. The corner interpolates from the speaker to the window's resting place over the same six intervals: x = vx + 0x14 + (9 - vx) * i / 6 and y = vy + 0x14 + (0x78 - vy) * i / 6, so the last step lands on (9, 0x78) in view coordinates, exactly where fdps_message_window_open leaves the panel. The constant 0x14 converts view coordinates into page coordinates, because the visible window sits at page pixel (24, 24) and screen pixel (4, 4).
The panel is sprite 0 of the Message.cel sheet in the global at 000643d0, drawn by fdps_cel_blit_sprite at pitch 0x168 with the packed destination size height << 16 | width and blit mode 4, which is fdps_rle_blit_scaled in fdps_blit_dispatch. Each step then spins on bit 3 of VGA input status port 0x3da until the vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, blits the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312 x 192) window at page offset 0x21d8 to the screen at 0xa0504 with fdps_blit_rect, waits for the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change and latches the new value, and frees the page.
Both paths finish with fdps_load_and_draw_portrait(0xa708c, 0x140, face_index) -- mode-13h screen at column 12, row 90, pitch 320. On the tile_x == -1 path that repaints the portrait fdps_message_window_open has already drawn for the same face_index.

Parameters:
  tile_x -- column of the speaker's tile on the battle map, 0-based; FUN_0001ff60 passes byte 0 of the speaker's unit record. -1 means the speaker is not standing on the map and selects the slide-up open.
  tile_y -- row of the speaker's tile, 0-based, from byte 1 of the same unit record. Unread when tile_x is -1; the caller passes 0 there.
  face_index -- index of the speaker's portrait in FACE.CEL, forwarded unchanged to fdps_message_window_open and fdps_load_and_draw_portrait. FUN_0001ff60 supplies byte 7 of the unit record when the speaker was found on the map, and otherwise the signed character id read out of the message token; negative means no portrait, and -1 additionally releases the cached portrait buffer.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; its only caller and every non-runtime callee are game code]

Rebuild note:
The tick latch the end-of-step spin compares against DAT_00069d64 is read before it is ever written, so on the first of the seven steps it holds stack garbage and the spin normally falls straight through; declaring it initialised from DAT_00069d64 costs one extra tick on that step. The retrace wait is also two-phase -- spin on port 0x3da until bit 3 is set, then spin until it is clear -- so each blit to the screen begins at the start of active display, not inside the blanking interval; the usual single-phase wait starts every step one blanking period earlier.

=== 00020c60 [PLATE]
Shows the current chapter's title card: the chapter's graphic fades up out of black over a black screen, holds for a second, fades back down to black and leaves the screen cleared.

Algorithm:
Loads "Chapter.saf" and "Chapter.pal" from MISC.VFS through fdps_vfs_load_entry. Clears the mode-13h frame buffer at 0xa0000 with memset (0xfa00 = 320*200 bytes), then blacks the DAC out by re-uploading the game's current palette at DAT_000643bc through fdps_set_palette_range over entries 0..0xff with a -0x40 bias on all three channels, which clamps every entry to 0.
Allocates a 0x16480-byte off-screen surface with malloc -- 0x170 * 0xf8, i.e. 368x248 -- and fills the 0x24-byte composite-sprite request on the stack: surface pointer, destination stride 0x170, height 0xf8, draw origin (0x18, 0x18), sprite bank = the loaded Chapter.saf image, entry index = the current chapter index at DAT_00069cf4 (0-based, 0..29), and zero in the request's last two dwords so fdps_draw_composite_sprite takes its per-part blend path. fdps_draw_composite_sprite renders that chapter's title graphic into the surface, and fdps_blit_rect copies the 320x200 window starting at surface+0x2298 -- 0x18*0x170 + 0x18, the draw origin -- to the VGA frame buffer at 0xa0000.
Fade up: for i from 0x10 down to 0 inclusive, spin on inp(0x3da) until VGA status bit 3 (vertical retrace) is set, upload Chapter.pal over entries 0..0xff with a bias of -4*i on every channel, then delay(0x50) = 80 ms. The last step, i = 0, leaves the card at full brightness. delay(0x3e8) holds it there for one second. Fade down is the same loop with i running 1 to 0x10, ending at a -0x40 bias, i.e. black again; the two loops are asymmetric on purpose so the full-brightness step is played once, not twice.
On the way out it clears the frame buffer again, reinstalls the game's palette at DAT_000643bc at zero bias -- so the caller inherits a live palette over a black screen and has to repaint whatever comes next -- and frees the Chapter.saf buffer, the Chapter.pal buffer and the off-screen surface.

Parameters:
  none. The chapter is taken from the global chapter index at DAT_00069cf4, which the chapter-progress routines set before the chapter entry handler runs.

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the Watcom libs or ailv3.lib; game strings, game callees, and all 30 callers are the chapter entry handlers fdps_chapter_01_init .. fdps_chapter_30_init]

Rebuild note:
The off-screen surface is 368x248 with the sprite drawn at (24,24), and only the 320x200 window at that origin is blitted -- a deliberate 24-pixel margin on all four sides, because the composite sprite's part records carry signed dx/dy offsets and nothing clips them. Allocating a tight 320x200 surface and drawing at (0,0), which is the obvious rewrite, lets any part that hangs off the picture write outside the allocation.

Why unit 3 is 法蓮娜: unit slot i is roster slot i. fdps_build_map_unit_array memmoves the roster record at DAT_00064108 + i * 0x50 straight into unit slot i for every i below the roster count DAT_00064114, and the roster is in join order -- fdps_roster_add_character writes at index DAT_00064114 and then increments it (00023bcc, 00023e12), nothing in the image decrements or permutes the roster, and fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units matches battle units back to roster entries by the character id at +8 rather than by position, so a chapter cannot reorder it. The chapter handlers call fdps_roster_add_character with 0, 6, 4, 1, 3, 2, 8 and 9, 7, 5 in chapters 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 15, which against the FRIAPRDA.DAT character ids gives the roster 蘭迪斯, 尤利安, 亞克, 法蓮娜, 裘娜, 費塔加, 布蘭多, 蓋亞, 琴琴, 瑪麗安. Slot 3 is character id 1, 法蓮娜.

The cursor argument is what separates this handler from most of the family: twenty-seven of the thirty park the cursor on unit 0, and only this one, fdps_chapter_22_init (00021410) and fdps_chapter_23_init (00021450) pass 3. Those three are exactly the three chapters that turn on 法蓮娜 -- chapter 17 is lost the moment she dies, and both fdps_chapter_22_event_boss_defeat and fdps_chapter_23_event_boss_defeat branch on whether she landed the killing blow -- so the family's one deviation is each of her chapters opening with the cursor already on her. This is otherwise the plain four-step form of the family: it hands no new character to the roster before the reset and clears no unit status bits after the title card.

The cursor argument is what separates this handler from most of the family: twenty-seven of the thirty park the cursor on unit 0 -- 蘭迪斯, roster slot 0 -- and only this one, fdps_chapter_17_init and fdps_chapter_22_init pass 3. === 00021650 [PLATE]
Runs one IconAni event script: loads the named entry out of IconAni.vfs and interprets its byte-opcode stream until the script says stop. Every scripted cutscene in the game is one of these -- each chapter's opening scene (Icon%02d.dat) and each chapter's victory scene (Win%02d.dat).

Algorithm:
Clears status bit 7 on every unit through fdps_units_clear_status_bit7, saves the current map number DAT_00069cf4, and opens "IconAni.vfs" with fdps_vfs_open; when that fails it prints "file not found: '%s'", waits for a key and carries on with the null handle anyway. fdps_vfs_load_file(script_name, archive) then reads the script into a buffer, and a null buffer waits for a key and gives up.
The interpreter loop clears DAT_00069cd0 on every pass, reads the opcode byte at script[offset] and dispatches it through a compare ladder; each handler advances offset past its own operands. b1/b2/b3/b4 below are the operand bytes following the opcode, and the number in brackets is how far offset moves.
  0x00  end of script -- and so is every opcode the ladder does not recognise
  0x01  fdps_icon_script_walk_units
  0x02  fdps_icon_script_set_unit_facing
  0x03  fdps_draw_text: text entry b1 of the block at DAT_00060124, drawn straight onto the VGA screen at 0xa0000, pitch 0x140, colours fg 0xd0 / bg 0 / outline 0x6d [2]
  0x04  fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, b1, b2); b1 == 0xff means "the branch the player picked at opcode 0x63" instead of a literal wave number [3]
  0x05  fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile
  0x06  loads "Icon%04d.saf" b1 out of the archive, fdps_saf_play_over_scene, free [2]
  0x07  fdps_cd_set_music_track(b1), with 0xff turned into -1, i.e. silence [2]
  0x08  loads "Icon%04d.wav" b1 and starts it with fdps_audio_start_wav(buf, 1, -1, -1); the buffer is parked in a 20-slot stack table and freed only when the script ends. Past the twentieth sound in one script the file is not loaded and nothing plays [2]
  0x09  fdps_icon_script_blink_units_out
  0x0a  writes b2, b3 and b4 into unit b1's record bytes +0, +1 and +3, when b1 < the unit count DAT_00060150 [5]
  0x0b  sets bit 0 of unit b1's record byte +5, same bounds check [2]
  0x0c  clears that bit and zeroes the six bytes at record +0x22, same bounds check [2]
  0x0d  view bounds in pixels: DAT_00069ce4 = b1 * 24, DAT_00069ce0 = b2 * 24, with DAT_00069cd4 and DAT_00069ccc one 24-pixel tile past each [3]
  0x0e  fdps_icon_script_fade_to_black(b1)
  0x0f  fdps_icon_script_fade_in(b1)
  0x10  fdps_icon_script_animate_view_offset
  0x11  switches map: DAT_00069cf4 = b1, then fdps_chapter_state_reset [2]
  0x12  writes b3 into unit b1's record byte 0x25 + b2 -- the one unit opcode with no bounds check on b1 [4]
  0x13  DAT_000640d8[b1] = b2, then fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes [3]
  0x14  writes a 16-bit map cell: the tile layer at DAT_00069cb0 has an 0xb-byte header and a row stride taken from the word at +7, and the cell at column b1, row b2 takes the script's next two bytes [5]
  0x15  fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, b1, b2, b3) -- b1/b2/b3 are the per-channel biases [4]
  0x61  ten times over: sets the pending experience award DAT_00069cec to 99 and hands it to unit 3 through FUN_0001dd30, then banks the party with fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units [1]
  0x62  fdps_map_actor_behavior_step(b1, b2) [3]
  0x63  runs fdps_icon_script_prompt_three_way_choice and keeps the answer for the next opcode 0x04 [1]
On the way out it frees the script buffer and the archive handle, frees every .wav buffer it parked, and sets DAT_00069cd0 back to 1.

Parameters:
  script_name -- name of the script entry inside IconAni.vfs, passed on to fdps_vfs_load_file. Every caller hands it a string literal: "Icon00.dat" is chapter 1's opening scene, "Win00.dat" chapter 1's victory scene.

Returns:
  Nothing. The epilogue does leave DAT_00069cf4 in EAX and compare it against the copy saved on entry, but the flags are dead and no caller reads the result.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; it writes the game's own globals and its only vendor callees are free, memset, sprintf and printf]

Rebuild note:
The .wav buffers opcode 0x08 loads have to stay allocated until the whole script has finished. fdps_audio_start_wav only starts the voice, so freeing each buffer right after the call -- the way opcode 0x06 does for its .saf, which plays synchronously -- leaves the mixer reading freed heap. The 20-slot table is also a hard cap: the twenty-first and later sounds of one script are silently skipped, and the missing bounds check on opcode 0x12 is likewise original and must stay.

=== 00021e30 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 5: scrolls the map view to a scripted tile, one tile-step per rendered frame, and leaves it parked there with the map cursor just inside the new view.

Algorithm:
Reads two unsigned operand bytes -- script[offset+1] is the target tile x, script[offset+2] the target tile y -- and converts each to map pixels by multiplying by 0x18, the 24-pixel tile size. Takes the pixel distance from the current view origin (DAT_00069ce4 is the view's x, DAT_00069ce0 its y -- the pair fdps_draw_scene_layers scrolls the layer table by) through abs on each axis, and makes the step count the larger of the two divided by 0x18, i.e. the tile distance along the dominant axis. When that count is zero the view jumps straight to the target. Otherwise it computes one fixed per-axis increment, target_delta / step_count, from the origin as it stood on entry, and then loops step_count times: add the x increment to DAT_00069ce4, add the y increment to DAT_00069ce0, and call fdps_render_view_frame, which waits for vertical retrace before it presents -- so the scroll runs at one step per frame and the dominant axis advances exactly one tile per frame while the other axis advances by a truncated share of that. After the loop it writes the exact target pixels into DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0, which absorbs the truncation left on the minor axis, and puts the map cursor globals DAT_00069cd4 (x) and DAT_00069ccc (y) at target + 0x18, one tile in from the new view's top-left corner. Unlike fdps_map_cursor_move_to it applies no clamping against the map extents; the tile the script names becomes the view origin as written.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; FUN_00021650 loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte 5, script[offset+1] the target tile x and script[offset+2] the target tile y.

Returns:
  offset + 3, the stream offset one byte past this instruction's two operands. FUN_00021650 stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it owns the game's view-origin and map-cursor globals and its only game callee is fdps_render_view_frame]

=== 00021f57 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] aligning 00021f60 to 16.

=== 00021f60 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 1: walks a list of battle units a scripted number of tiles, each in its own scripted direction, playing the six-step walk animation as they go.

Algorithm:
Clears the cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 and the cursor/info-panel flag DAT_00060159 to 0, so fdps_draw_map_cursor draws no cursor and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel draws no panel while the scripted walk is on screen. Reads three unsigned operand bytes: script[offset+1] is how many rendered frames each of the six walk sub-steps is held for, script[offset+2] is how many tiles the group walks, script[offset+3] is how many units follow; then skips the 4-byte opcode header. Each unit is a 2-byte pair of a unit index and a direction code.
Three nested loops follow: tile 0..tile_count-1 outermost, walk sub-step 1..6 inside it, hold 0..frame_delay-1 inside that. Every hold pass walks the whole unit list. fdps_get_unit_record turns the pair's first byte into a pointer to that unit's 0x50-byte record; the second byte is written to the facing code at record+3 (0 down/+y, 1 left/-x, 2 up/-y, 3 right/+x -- the codes fdps_unit_face_target writes); and for sub-steps 1 through 5 the sub-tile step counter at record+4 is set to the sub-step number. fdps_draw_map_unit displaces a unit by 4 pixels per step counter along its facing, so the six sub-steps carry it across one 0x18-pixel tile. On sub-step 6, and only on the first hold pass of it, the step counter is cleared to 0 instead and the tile is committed: facing 0 increments the tile y at record+1, 1 decrements the tile x at record+0, 2 decrements the tile y, and any other value increments the tile x. After each hold pass over the list it calls fdps_render_view_frame, which waits for vertical retrace before presenting, and fdps_cycle_scene_palette, so all the listed units advance on the same frame and the scene's colour cycling keeps running under them; one tile therefore costs 6 * frame_delay rendered frames.
Nothing here scrolls the view, tests the terrain or reports an arrival tile to fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event, which is what separates it from the interactive playback family reached through fdps_animate_move_path: the listed units walk straight through whatever is in the way for exactly the scripted number of tiles. Finally it writes the constants 1 into DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159 -- cursor mode 1 is the bare cursor tile -- and returns the stream offset just past the operands it consumed.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; FUN_00021650 loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte 1, script[offset+1] the frames held per walk sub-step, script[offset+2] the number of tiles walked and script[offset+3] the unit count.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, i.e. offset + 4 + 2 * unit_count. FUN_00021650 stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the watcom or ail sets and the body hash is unique in the image; every callee is game code, and the body walks the game's script stream while mutating unit records]

Rebuild note:
The exit path stores the literals 1 into DAT_00069cd0 and 1 into DAT_00060159 rather than restoring what they held on entry, so an area-of-effect cursor mode does not survive the opcode; writing it as the obvious save/restore pair changes behaviour. Separately, the tile commit and the record+4 write both sit inside the per-frame hold loop (the commit guarded by hold index 0), so hoisting the unit update out of that loop -- the natural way to write 'update the units, then render frame_delay frames' -- makes the units still move when the frames-per-sub-step operand is 0, where the original moves them not at all.

=== 000220f9 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea nop plus one 0x90, aligning FUN_00022100 to 16 bytes.

=== 00022100 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 2: turns a list of battle units to face given directions and holds the view there for a fixed number of rendered frames.

Algorithm:
Clears the map cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 and the cursor/info-panel display flag DAT_00060159 to 0, so fdps_draw_map_cursor draws no cursor and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel draws no panel while the scripted pose is on screen. Reads two unsigned operand bytes: script[offset+1] is how many frames the pose is held for, script[offset+2] is how many units follow; then skips the 3-byte opcode header. Each unit is a 2-byte pair: the first byte is a unit index, which fdps_get_unit_record turns into a pointer to that unit's 0x50-byte record, and the second byte is written to record+3, the unit's facing code (0/1/2/3, the same codes the walk handlers reached from fdps_animate_move_path set). Every listed unit is turned first, then fdps_render_view_frame is called frame_count times, each call waiting for vertical retrace before it presents, so all of them appear to turn on the same frame. Finally it writes the constants 1 back into DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159 -- cursor mode 1 is the bare cursor tile -- and returns the stream offset just past the operands it consumed.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; FUN_00021650 loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte 2, script[offset+1] the hold length in frames and script[offset+2] the unit count.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, i.e. offset + 3 + 2 * unit_count. FUN_00021650 stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; both callees and the sole caller are game code, and the body walks the game's script stream and mutates unit records]

Rebuild note:
The exit path writes the literals 1 and 1 into DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159; it does not save and restore them, even though the sibling opcode handler fdps_icon_script_animate_view_offset does save and restore DAT_00060159. Rewriting this as a save/restore pair -- the obvious way to write 'clear the flags for the duration' -- changes behaviour whenever the cursor mode was not 1 on entry.

=== 000221d7 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] multi-byte NOPs aligning next function to 0x10.

=== 000221e0 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 9: flashes a list of battle-map units on and off, then leaves them off.

Algorithm:
Reads the unit count from script[offset+1], then advances offset past the 2-byte opcode header so the count unit indices sit at script[offset] .. script[offset+count-1]. Clears the map-cursor shape selector DAT_00069cd0 and the cursor-panel flag DAT_00060159, so that fdps_draw_map_cursor and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel put nothing on top of the effect while it runs.
Then seven phases, phase = 1 to 7. Each phase stores phase & 1 into byte +5 of every listed unit's record -- fdps_get_unit_record turns each index into a record pointer -- and then calls fdps_render_view_frame three times, so each phase lasts three retrace-paced frames. Bit 0 of record byte +5 is the retired flag that FUN_0002cda0 tests before drawing a unit at all, so odd phases hide the listed units and even phases show them: hidden, shown, hidden, shown, hidden, shown, hidden. Phase 7 is odd, so the units are left hidden, with byte +5 holding the value 1 that fdps_unit_mark_retired writes -- the listed units are retired from the battle, not merely blinked.
The write is a whole-byte store, not a bit operation, so every other bit of record +5 is cleared as a side effect. That includes bit 7, the flag fdps_battle_mark_unit_done sets to record that a unit has finished acting. The single-unit retire and un-retire opcodes 0x0b and 0x0c inside FUN_00021650 edit the same bit with OR 1 and AND 0xfe and do preserve it.
On exit DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159 are both set to 1 -- the bare-cursor shape and the panel enabled -- rather than restored to whatever they held on entry.
The shipped IconAni.vfs scripts use this opcode with one unit index (ICON04.DAT, ICON11.DAT, WIN00.DAT, WIN26.DAT, WINGA26.DAT) or two (ICON28.DAT).

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image. FUN_00021650 loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and hands the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image. script[offset] is the opcode byte 9, script[offset+1] is the number of unit indices that follow, and script[offset+2] onward are those indices, each one an index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, offset + 2 + count. FUN_00021650 stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [both callees are game code (fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_render_view_frame) and the only state it touches is unit records and the game globals DAT_00069cd0 / DAT_00060159; no Function ID candidate in the watcom or ail sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
This opcode assigns unit record byte +5 outright (MOV byte [EDX+0x5],AL at 0002226b), where the neighbouring script opcodes 0x0b and 0x0c in FUN_00021650 set and clear the same retired bit with OR 1 / AND 0xfe. Writing the obvious `rec[5] |= 1` and `rec[5] &= ~1` for the blink phases, or calling fdps_unit_mark_retired, preserves bit 7 -- the finished-acting flag -- where the original clears it on every listed unit, so a unit blinked out and later un-retired comes back able or unable to act depending on which version is running. The second trap is the ending state: the phase counter runs 1..7 and stops on an odd phase, so the effect deliberately ends with the units hidden and retired; a rewrite that treats this as a pure blink and restores the units' previous visibility afterwards leaves scripted units standing on the map that the original removed.

=== 000222b4 [EOL]
Watcom 16-byte alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs before FUN_000222c0.

=== 000222c0 [PLATE]
Plays one loaded .SAF animation through once over the live scrolling scene, presenting it in the game's framed 312x192 main view.

Algorithm:
Allocates an 0x15180-byte page with malloc -- a 360x240 8bpp surface, wider and taller than the presented window so a frame may overhang it without being clipped. Builds the 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request on the stack: destination = that page, pitch 0x168 (360), height 0xf0 (240), x = y = 0x18 (24), SAF base (+0x14) = saf_image, blit parameter block (+0x1c) and blit mode (+0x20) both 0. fdps_saf_frame_count(saf_image) gives the frame total; for each frame index i from 0 to count-1 the request's index field (+0x18) takes i, fdps_saf_get_frame(saf_image, i) resolves the frame record, and that frame is held for the tick count in the frame record's i16 at +0x02 (the SAF frame's dwell time, 1..45). On every held tick: fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the scrolling layer table into the page from scratch, fdps_draw_composite_sprite draws frame i over it with flag argument 1, so the frame's own sound effect fires -- a frame that carries a sound retriggers it once per tick it is held; the routine then spins on port 0x3da until vertical retrace begins and again until it ends; fdps_blit_rect copies the 312x192 (0x138 x 0xc0) window at page+0x21d8 (24 * 360 + 24) with source pitch 360 to 0xa0504, row 4 column 4 of the mode 13h framebuffer, so the animation origin lands at screen (4,4) and the outer 4-pixel border and the strip right and below the window keep whatever was on screen already; finally it spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes and latches the new value. free releases the page on the way out; saf_image belongs to the caller, and both callers free it immediately after the call returns. This is fdps_render_view_frame's presentation loop with a SAF frame in place of the cursor information panel: no panel is drawn and the scene palette is not cycled, so both are absent for the length of the animation.

Parameters:
  saf_image -- the loaded .SAF animation image to play, allocated and freed by the caller. 0x00021650, the IconAni script interpreter, passes the Icon%04d.saf entry it has just loaded from the VFS; 0x000288f0, the magic-effect executor, passes Emg33-1.saf. Used as the composite-sprite bank at request+0x14 and as the argument of fdps_saf_frame_count and fdps_saf_get_frame.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls game drawing routines and reads the game's frame counter; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The dword holding the previously seen value of the tick counter DAT_00069d64 is never initialised: the first tick-wait of the first frame compares the counter against whatever the stack happened to hold, so in practice it falls straight through and that tick is presented without waiting. Writing the obvious C -- seeding that variable with 0 or with the current value of DAT_00069d64 -- makes the animation start one tick late. Leave it uninitialised, or start it from a value the counter cannot currently hold.

=== 0002240a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte Watcom NOP (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_00022410 to 16 bytes.

=== 00022410 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 0x0e: fades the screen to black over sixteen retrace-paced steps, so a scripted scene can black out between pictures.

Algorithm:
Walks a darkening bias i from 0 down to -0x3c in steps of 4 -- sixteen steps in all. Each step first waits for VGA vertical retrace, polling the input status register at port 0x3da through inp until bit 3 (mask 0x8) reads set; then calls fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, -i, -i, -i), which re-uploads all 256 DAC entries out of the game's master palette image (Fde.pal, loaded into DAT_000643bc at startup) with that bias added to every channel and clamped to 0..0x3f; then calls the Watcom CRT delay() for step_delay_ms milliseconds to hold the step. Because every step re-derives the DAC entries from DAT_000643bc, the ramp always runs from the master palette, not from whatever palette is on the DAC when the opcode is reached.
The last step's bias is -0x3c, not -0x40, so on the VGA's 6-bit DAC any entry brighter than 60 finishes at 1..3 rather than 0. The counterpart handler fdps_icon_script_fade_in, opcode 0x0f, runs the same ramp backwards from -0x40 up to 0 to bring the picture back.

Parameters:
  step_delay_ms -- how long each of the sixteen steps is held, in milliseconds, passed straight to the CRT delay(). fdps_icon_script_run reads it from the unsigned operand byte script[offset+1] of the 0x0e instruction, so 0..255.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only substantive callee is the game's fdps_set_palette_range acting on the game palette pointer DAT_000643bc, and its only caller is the game's IconAni script interpreter]

Rebuild note:
The loop bound is 0x40 with the last bias reached being -0x3c, one step short of the -0x40 its counterpart fdps_icon_script_fade_in starts from. Writing the symmetric loop (i <= 0x40, or mirroring the sibling's range) blacks the screen out completely instead of leaving it very dark, and changes what is on the DAC between the two opcodes.

=== 0002247e [EOL]
Alignment padding: mov eax,eax (8b c0) filling 2 bytes to the 16-byte entry at 00022480.

=== 00022480 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 0x0f: fades the screen up out of black over seventeen retrace-paced steps, bringing the picture back after a scripted scene has blacked out.

Algorithm:
Walks a darkening bias i from -0x40 up to 0 in steps of 4 -- seventeen steps in all, the loop counter at [EBP-0x4] counting down from 0x40 to 0 and the bias being its negation. Each step first waits for VGA vertical retrace, polling the input status register at port 0x3da through the CRT inp until bit 3 (mask 0x8) reads set; then calls fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, -i, -i, -i), which re-uploads all 256 DAC entries out of the game's master palette image (Fde.pal, loaded into DAT_000643bc at startup) with that bias added to every channel and clamped to 0..0x3f; then calls the Watcom CRT delay() for step_delay_ms milliseconds to hold the step. The first step's bias of -0x40 clamps every channel to 0, so the ramp always begins from true black whatever was on the DAC; the last step's bias of 0 uploads the master palette unmodified, so the handler always finishes with the DAC holding exactly Fde.pal. The counterpart handler fdps_icon_script_fade_to_black, opcode 0x0e, runs the ramp in the other direction, but not symmetrically: it takes sixteen steps and stops at -0x3c.

Parameters:
  step_delay_ms -- how long each of the seventeen steps is held, in milliseconds, passed straight to the CRT delay(). fdps_icon_script_run reads it from the unsigned operand byte script[offset+1] of the 0x0f instruction, so 0..255.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only substantive callee is the game's fdps_set_palette_range acting on the game palette pointer DAT_000643bc, and its only caller is the game's IconAni script interpreter]

Rebuild note:
The ramp is not the mirror of its 0x0e counterpart: this handler runs seventeen steps from bias -0x40 (which clamps every channel to 0, true black) up to and including bias 0, while fdps_icon_script_fade_to_black runs sixteen steps and stops at -0x3c. Writing the obvious mirror of the sibling loop -- starting at -0x3c, or stopping the loop before the bias reaches 0 -- costs the final step that re-uploads Fde.pal unmodified, so the screen stays permanently dimmed instead of returning to full brightness, and the fade takes one step less time than the original.

=== 000224ee [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8b c0 (mov eax,eax) two-byte no-op aligning the next entry to 16 bytes.

=== 000224f0 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 0x10: displaces the map view by a scripted list of pixel offsets, holding each one for a fixed number of rendered frames, then puts the view back.

Algorithm:
Saves the current view origin -- DAT_00069ce4 is the view's x in pixels and DAT_00069ce0 its y, the pair fdps_draw_scene_layers scrolls the layer table by -- and saves the display flag byte DAT_00060159, then clears that flag so fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel draws nothing while the effect runs. Reads two unsigned operand bytes: script[offset+1] is how many frames each step is held for, script[offset+2] is how many steps follow; then skips the 3-byte opcode header. For each step it takes two more bytes and sign-extends each by subtracting 0x100 when it exceeds 0x7f, writes saved_x + dx into DAT_00069ce4 and saved_y + dy into DAT_00069ce0 -- each step's offset is measured from the saved origin, not added to the previous step's -- and calls fdps_render_view_frame frame_count times, each call waiting for vertical retrace before it presents. After the last step it writes the saved origin and the saved flag byte back, and returns the stream offset just past the operands it consumed.
The shipped scripts use two shapes of offset list: an eight-entry circular wobble of one pixel repeated four times (ICON00.DAT, ICON02.DAT), and monotone ramps of 6 or 8 pixels a step that slide the view off its origin and let the restore snap it back (ICON06.DAT, ICON08.DAT). The separate opcode 5 handler fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile is the one that scrolls the view to a new tile and leaves it there.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; fdps_icon_script_run loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this 0x10 opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte, script[offset+1] the per-step frame count (1 or 2 in the shipped scripts) and script[offset+2] the step count.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, i.e. offset + 3 + 2 * step_count. fdps_icon_script_run stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either the watcom or the ail set; its only callee fdps_render_view_frame is game code, and it shares the view-origin globals and the display flag with the game's rendering layer]

Rebuild note:
The two operand bytes per step are offsets from the origin saved on entry, not increments: rewriting the loop as DAT_00069ce4 += dx turns ICON06.DAT's ramp of -6,-12,-18,-24 into -6,-18,-36,-60. And unlike its sibling opcode handlers fdps_icon_script_walk_units, fdps_icon_script_set_unit_facing and fdps_icon_script_blink_units_out, which all end by forcing DAT_00060159 to 1 and DAT_00069cd0 to 1, this one restores DAT_00060159 to whatever it was on entry and never touches DAT_00069cd0 at all -- writing the family uniformly makes the cursor panel reappear after a cutscene that had hidden it.

=== 000225f2 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov eax,eax, aligning FUN_00022600 to 16 bytes

=== 00022600 [PLATE]
Runs the IconAni event script's three-way player choice: asks up to two two-option questions and hands the interpreter back the branch the player picked, 1, 2 or 3.

Algorithm:
Preloads the answer with 3, the value that survives when the player takes the second option twice. Reveals the message panel (FUN_000205b0, panel id 0x7a), renders message 0x10 of the loaded chapter text at DAT_00060124 with FUN_0001ff60, runs fdps_prompt_two_choice, and retracts the panel with FUN_00020820. Rebuild note:

=== 00022be0 [PLATE]
Builds the unit-record array for one map: puts the party roster on the battlefield at the map's scripted start tiles and brings on the map's opening wave of scripted units.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_field_load_chapter_resources first, which reloads the resource set for the map named by DAT_00069cf4 and publishes the two map%02d.dat header bytes this routine runs on -- DAT_00064118 (byte +1, how many player slots the map fields) and DAT_0006410c (byte +2, how many scripted deployment records the map has).

The file is the placement table: an 0xb-byte header followed by 6-byte records of two signed 16-bit tile coordinates. Its first DAT_0006410c records belong to the scripted deployment table; the party's start tiles follow them.

The previous map's unit array is dropped -- when the unit count DAT_00060150 is non-zero the array at DAT_00069cd8 is freed -- and DAT_00060150 takes the map's player-slot count DAT_00064118. When that count is not zero, DAT_00069cd8 gets a fresh malloc of DAT_00064118 * 0x50 bytes and slot i, for i from 0 to DAT_00064118-1, is filled two ways:

Finally the placement table is freed and DAT_00060140 set back to NULL, ICON.CEL is closed, and fdps_deploy_wave(map_no, 0, 1) appends the map's wave-0 units past the player slots, growing the array and DAT_00060150 as it goes.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the Watcom set or ailv3.lib; game strings "ICON.CEL", "map%02d.cod" and "Field.vfs", game globals and game callees, with malloc/free/memmove/memset/sprintf/fopen/fclose used only as leaf services]

Rebuild note:
The party's placement records are not the first records of map%02d.cod. === 00022e30 [PLATE]
Loads one numbered entry of an offset-table archive file into a buffer slot the caller owns, replacing whatever that slot held before.

Algorithm:
Frees *buffer when it is not NULL, then opens filename with fopen in mode "rb" (the mode string at 00061a00). A failed open prints the format at 00061a1c, "\n\n File not found %s!!! \a\n", with the file name and calls exit(1), so the routine does not come back from that path. On success it mallocs an 8-byte scratch block into *buffer, seeks to file offset 6 + entry_index * 4 and freads 8 bytes there: the archive's offset table begins at file offset 6 and holds one 32-bit absolute file offset per entry followed by a sentinel, so those two dwords are the start of entry entry_index and the start of the entry after it. Their difference is the entry's byte size. It frees the scratch block, mallocs the entry's size into *buffer, seeks to the entry's start offset, freads the whole entry into *buffer and fcloses the file. Neither malloc result is checked and no failure after the open is detected; the routine returns with *buffer holding the entry.

The 6-byte header plus u32 offset table is not the layout of the .VFS containers the rest of the game reads (those have a 35-byte header and a 26-byte named entry table, and are read by fdps_vfs_open, fdps_vfs_load_file and fdps_vfs_load_entry); it is the packed-archive layout the studio's previous game used, and this is that loader carried over. Nothing in the image calls this function or points at its entry, and no file shipped with the game has this layout.

Parameters:
  filename -- name of the archive file to open, handed straight to fopen and used as the %s of the not-found message. No search path of its own.
  buffer -- the caller's buffer pointer slot, both in and out. On entry it must hold NULL or a malloc'd block, because a non-NULL value is freed; on return it holds the malloc'd entry, which the caller then owns.
  entry_index -- 0-based index into the archive's offset table. Not range-checked, and the table must also hold the entry after it, because the loaded entry's size is the difference between the two offsets.

Returns:
  Nothing. The entry is handed back through *buffer. On a failed open the function never returns: it exits the process with status 1.

Pool: fdps  [no FID hit in either library set and the body hash is unique in the image; it hard-codes a game archive layout and exits with a game message, using the CRT only as a leaf service]
