=== 000232b0 [PLATE]
Deploys one unit of a map's scripted deployment table onto the battle map, appending its 0x50-byte record to the end of the unit array.

Algorithm:
Grows the unit array first. With the unit count DAT_00060150 still 0 it mallocs one 0x50-byte record into DAT_00069cd8, otherwise it reallocs the array to (DAT_00060150 + 1) * 0x50, and fdps_get_unit_record(DAT_00060150) resolves the new last slot.

The anchor tile comes from the map%02d.cod placement table at DAT_00060140 that fdps_deploy_wave loaded: placement record deploy_index sits at DAT_00060140 + 0xb + deploy_index * 6 and holds two signed 16-bit tile coordinates.

When place_exact is non-zero the unit is put on that tile as it stands. When it is 0 the tile is searched for instead: fdps_map_grid_reset blanks the occupancy grid at DAT_00060144, fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control(0) and (1) between them mark every unit still in play, and the whole grid is scanned row by row -- cell (x, y) at DAT_00060144 + 4 + (y * width + x) * 2, width and height being the header words at +0 and +2. A cell whose byte 0 has bit 0x40 set has a unit standing on it and is skipped; the zone-of-control bit 0x80 is deliberately not tested, so a deployed unit may land beside an enemy but never on top of one. For each remaining cell whose Manhattan distance to the anchor is no greater than the best so far it calls fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) and keeps the cell when the terrain code that publishes at DAT_00069d09 -- the index class_move_cost is read with -- is below 5. The best-so-far distance starts at 0xff. fdps_map_grid_reset runs once more afterwards, leaving the grid blank for the movement code.

Everything else comes from deployment record deploy_index of the resident map%02d.dat table, at DAT_0006013c + 0x83 + deploy_index * 0x1a, 0x1a bytes wide: +0 side, +1 character id, +4 level, +5 and +6 the two equipped items, +7..+0xc six carried items, +0xd..+0x10 the four spell-mask bytes, +0x11 the AI behaviour byte whose low nibble fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on, +0x12..+0x14 three more per-unit bytes, +0x15 the wave number fdps_deploy_wave matched on, +0x16 the death-script opcode with its signed 16-bit operand at +0x17, and +0x19 one further byte.

Base stats are computed from the character id. Below 0x3c the unit is a roster-side character: fdps_get_character_base_record gives the 24-byte FRIAPRDA.DAT record and fdps_get_growth_record the 11-byte FriLevUp.dat record, and attack (+0x37) = ap_base + level * ap_min, defense (+0x39) = dp_base + level * dp_min, dexterity (+0x3e) = dx_base + level * dx_min, HP = hp_base + (level - 1) * hp_min, MP = mp_base + (level - 1) * mp_min -- the multiplier is level for the three combat stats but level - 1 for HP and MP. Race (+0x1f), class (+0x20) and movement (+0x3b) are copied straight out of the base record. At 0x3c and above the unit is an enemy: fdps_get_enemy_record(id - 0x3c) gives the 10-byte EnemyDat.dat record and every stat is a flat multiple of level -- HP = level * word[+2], MP = level * byte[+4], attack = level * [+5], defense = level * [+6], dexterity = level * [+7] -- with race [+0], class [+1] and movement [+8] copied over.

The record is then written out: tile column (+0) and row (+1) from the resolved tile; sprite cache slot (+2) from fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group(character id, fp), which pulls the unit's walk sprites out of the open ICON.CEL; facing (+3), sub-tile step (+4) and status flags (+5) cleared; side (+6); the character id in both +7 and +8; +9 cleared. The eight 2-byte inventory slots at +0xa each carry a flag byte and an item id: slot 0 takes deployment byte +5 flagged 0x40 (equipped) and slot 1 takes byte +6 flagged 0x40, except that when byte +5 is 0xff the item from byte +6 moves into slot 0, still flagged 0x40, and slot 1 is flagged 0x80 (empty) with its id byte left as the allocator returned it; slots 2..7 take bytes +7..+0xc, flagged 0 when the id is not 0xff and 0x80 when it is. The six status timers at +0x22 are memset to 0, the four spell-mask bytes memmoved to +0x1a, and +0x1e, +0x21 (level), +0x31 (death-script opcode), +0x32 (its operand word), +0x34 (behaviour byte), +0x35, +0x36 and +0x3d filled from the deployment record. +0x3c takes 0 when the side is 2, the player side, and 0xff otherwise. Current and maximum HP (+0x40, +0x42) and MP (+0x44, +0x46) all take the computed values, so the unit arrives at full health.

Last, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(DAT_00060150) derives the four combat stats at +0x48..+0x4e from what was just written, and DAT_00060150 is incremented so the new record counts as in play.

Parameters:
  deploy_index -- index of the deployment record, 0 .. map%02d.dat header byte +2 minus 1. It selects both the 0x1a-byte record in DAT_0006013c and the 6-byte placement record in DAT_00060140. The only caller, fdps_deploy_wave, passes its loop variable over the deployment table.
  fp -- the ICON.CEL stream fdps_deploy_wave fopens before its loop and fcloses after it; used for nothing here but passing to fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group.
  place_exact -- non-zero puts the unit on the tile the placement record names; 0 searches the map for the nearest unoccupied walkable tile to it. fdps_deploy_wave hands its own third argument down unchanged.

Returns:
  Nothing. The new unit is the record at the index DAT_00060150 held before the call, and DAT_00060150 is one larger afterwards.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; shared game globals and game callees, with malloc, realloc, abs, memset and memmove used only as leaf services]

Rebuild note:
The nearest-tile search accepts a cell whose Manhattan distance merely ties the best so far (CMP EAX,[EBP-0x14] / JLE at 000233e6), so the tile actually used is the last tie in row-major scan order, not the first; writing the obvious "if (dist < best)" moves every searched-for deployment onto a different tile. And when the deployment record's weapon byte +5 is 0xff, the item from byte +6 still goes into inventory slot 0 with the equipped flag 0x40 even when it is 0xff too, which sends fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats into fdps_get_item_record(0xff), past the end of ITEM.DAT's 251 records; the guard that obviously belongs there is not in the original.

=== 00023830 [PLATE]
Deploys every unit of one wave of a map's scripted deployment table onto the battle map.

Algorithm:
fopens ICON.CEL in mode "rb" (the mode string at 00061a00) -- the sheet each deployed unit takes its walk sprites from -- and opens the Field.vfs archive with fdps_vfs_open. When that archive will not open it prints "file not found: '%s'", waits for a keypress through fdps_wait_any_key and carries straight on holding a NULL handle. It then formats "map%02d.cod" from map_no into a 20-byte stack buffer and loads that archive entry through fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit into DAT_00060140; that entry is the placement table fdps_deploy_unit reads, 6-byte tile-coordinate records after an 0xb-byte header.

Next it walks the resident map%02d.dat deployment table already held in DAT_0006013c: header byte +2 is the number of scripted deployment records, record i sits at DAT_0006013c + 0x83 + i * 0x1a, and for every record whose byte +0x15 -- its wave number -- equals wave_no it calls fdps_deploy_unit(i, icon_cel_stream, place_exact), which appends one 0x50-byte unit record to the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 and bumps the unit count DAT_00060150. The loop bound is re-read from DAT_0006013c on every pass, which changes nothing because fdps_deploy_unit grows the unit array, never the deployment table.

Finally it fcloses ICON.CEL, frees DAT_00060140 and sets it back to NULL, and releases the archive handle with a plain free -- the VFS has no close routine of its own.

Parameters:
  map_no -- map number, 0-based, selecting the "map%02d.cod" placement file; callers pass DAT_00069cf4, the map the chapter is playing, or a literal map number
  wave_no -- the wave tag matched against byte +0x15 of each deployment record. 0 is the group placed when the map opens; higher numbers are the reinforcement groups the chapter event handlers bring on, and the turn-scheduled events pass the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 here
  place_exact -- 0 lets fdps_deploy_unit search outward for the nearest unoccupied walkable tile around the recorded position; non-zero puts the unit exactly on the tile the record names

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [game strings, game VFS calls and the game's own unit record array; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The missing-archive branch is not an early exit. After the message and the keypress control falls through into fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit with a NULL archive handle, and the game does not survive that call; writing the obvious return after the message would instead leave the game running with the wave silently never deployed.

=== 00023950 [PLATE]

Multiplies roster_index by the 0x50-byte roster record stride and adds the array base pointer held in the global at 0x00064108 -- the same base and stride fdps_roster_add_character computes inline when it appends a member. Declaring the obvious C struct for it lets the compiler insert padding, which pushes sizeof past 0x50 and shifts every field from 0x37 onward, so the stride this accessor multiplies by no longer matches the array the save file restores. Keep the record packed (or address it by byte offset) and keep the stride literal 0x50.

=== 00023980 [PLATE]
Banks the party at the end of a battle: copies every battle-map unit's record back over the party roster record of the same character, and resets the fields that must not survive the chapter.

Algorithm:
Outer loop over unit_index 0 .. [0x00060150]-1, the live battle unit count; each unit record comes from fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index). Inner loop over roster_index 0 .. [0x00064114]-1, the roster member count, addressing the roster record as [0x00064108] + roster_index * 0x50 -- the same base and stride fdps_get_roster_record uses. A roster slot is matched when its character id byte at +0x08 equals the unit's. There is no break on a match, so every slot carrying that id is written.
One case is exempt: when the character id is 0 (Randis) and fdps_unit_is_retired(unit_index) reports the unit has left the battle, the slot is left untouched and the scan moves on to the next slot.
For a matched slot the routine then, in order:
  1. memmove(slot, unit, 0x50) -- the whole record;
  2. memset(slot + 0x22, 0, 6) -- clears the six status-effect timers at +0x22..+0x27, so no buff or ailment carries out of the battle;
  3. slot[+0x05] &= 1 -- keeps only bit 0, the retired/dead flag that fdps_unit_is_retired returns, and drops every other status bit;
  4. when that byte is now 0, i.e. the member is not retired, copies maximum HP (word +0x42) into current HP (word +0x40) -- a full heal for every survivor, skipped for the dead;
  5. copies maximum MP (word +0x46) into current MP (word +0x44) unconditionally, dead members included;
  6. reads the experience byte at +0x3c as an unsigned byte and stores 0 when it is above 99, which catches both an experience count that has run past a level boundary and the 0xff sentinel the deployment path writes for units that are not roster characters;
  7. calls fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats(roster_index), rebuilding the four derived combat stat words at +0x48..+0x4e from the record just installed.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing. The result is the rewritten roster array at [0x00064108].

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_unit_is_retired and fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats and works only on the game's own unit and roster globals; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail library set]

Rebuild note:
The experience byte at +0x3c must be read unsigned. The test is MOV AL,[slot+0x3c] / AND EAX,0xff / CMP EAX,0x63 / JLE, a zero-extended byte against 99; typing that field as a plain signed char makes the 0xff sentinel compare as -1, so it is not reset, it survives into the roster, and the status panel takes its 0xff branch and prints 1000 instead of an experience count.

=== 00023abd [EOL]
Alignment padding: 3-byte NOP form 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_00023ac0 to a 4-byte boundary.

=== 00023ac0 [PLATE]
Recomputes one roster member's four derived combat stats from the record's base stats and the items equipped in it.

Algorithm:
Forms the record pointer as [0x00064108] + roster_index * 0x50 -- the party roster array, the same base and 0x50 stride fdps_get_roster_record uses -- and seeds four running totals from the record's base stats: attack from the signed word at +0x37, defense from the word at +0x39, and both hit and evade from the single dexterity word at +0x3e (there is no separate evade base). It then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries starting at record+0x0a, and for every entry whose flag byte has bit 0x40 (equipped) set it looks the item id in that entry's second byte up with fdps_get_item_record and adds the item record's four signed word modifiers: +0x01 (ap) to attack, +0x05 (dp) to defense, +0x03 (hit) to hit, +0x07 (ev) to evade. Entries flagged empty (bit 0x80) or merely carried contribute nothing. The four totals are stored back as words at record +0x48 (attack), +0x4a (defense), +0x4c (hit) and +0x4e (evade) -- the fields fdps_draw_unit_status_panel prints.

This is the roster half of a pair. fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats is the battle half: it runs the identical seed-and-equipment sum over a record of the battle/map unit array at [0x00069cd8], and additionally adds 15 to the dexterity seed while the buff timer byte at +0x24 runs and scales the attack and defense totals by 1.15 while the timers at +0x22 and +0x23 run. This function makes neither adjustment and never reads +0x22..+0x24: base stats plus equipment is the whole computation on the roster side. The third member of the family is fdps_roster_preview_combat_stats_with_item, which derives the same four values for a candidate item in the shop without storing them.

Parameters:
  roster_index -- position in the party roster array, 0 .. [0x00064114]-1. fdps_roster_add_character passes the slot it has just filled in; fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units passes a loop counter bounded by the roster count at 0x00064114. Not range-checked.

Returns:
Nothing. The result is the four stat words written into the roster record.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; walks the game's 0x50-byte roster record through the game global at 0x00064108, and its only callee is the game's own item-record lookup]

Rebuild note:
Hit and evade are both seeded from the one dexterity word at record+0x3e; there is no separate evade base field (record+0x40 is current HP), so writing the obvious 'one base field per derived stat' version gives a wrong evade. In the same loop the equipped scan covers all eight inventory entries at record+0x0a, not just the two equipment slots that fdps_roster_add_character marks 0x40, so an item sitting in a later slot with bit 0x40 set does contribute to the totals. Third, the roster and battle recomputes are not interchangeable despite writing the same four fields from the same sources: this body applies none of the +0x22/+0x23/+0x24 status modifiers that fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats applies, so folding the obvious duplication into one shared routine changes roster stats wherever a roster record happens to carry a non-zero byte at those offsets.

=== 000241e0 [PLATE]
Runs the save-game screen: lets the player choose a slot and writes the current game state into FDE.SAV, over and over until the player backs out.

Algorithm:
Sets the save/load mode flag DAT_00064104 to 0 (0 = save, 1 = load; fdps_save_slot_select_loop reads it to decide whether an empty slot may be picked), builds the menu page with fdps_saveload_screen_build("Save.cel"), and mosaic-reveals that page onto the VGA screen at 0xa0000 with fdps_transition_random_blocks (320x200 at pitch 0x140, a 16x16 phase grid of 4x3 blocks, delay 1).
Then loops for as long as the last selection was 1:
  - fdps_save_slot_select_loop(page, &slot_index) returns 1 for a confirmed slot or -1 for Esc.
  - On 1, mallocs a 0x59cb-byte image of FDE.SAV. If fopen succeeds it freads the whole file, decrypts it in place with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer and fcloses; if the file is not there it memsets the whole image to 0xff instead, and that fresh image is deliberately not run through the cipher.
  - The slot record sits at image + 0x312b + slot_index * 0xa28. memmove copies 0xa00 bytes of live game state out of the block DAT_00064108 points at into that record, and then the last 0x14 bytes of that same 0xa00 region are overwritten with the stamp: month at +0x9fc and day at +0x9f8 from _dos_getdate, hour at +0x9f4 and minute at +0x9f0 from _dos_gettime, and DAT_00064110 at +0x9ec.
  - The header bytes follow the copied region: chapter index DAT_00069cf4 at +0xa00 (fdps_saveload_screen_build treats 0xff here as an empty slot), party member count DAT_00064114 at +0xa01, party gold DAT_000643a4 as a dword at +0xa02, then the four option bytes fdps_options_menu maintains -- DAT_00060158 at +0xa06, DAT_00060010 at +0xa07, CD-music enable DAT_00060008 at +0xa08 and sound-available DAT_00069d70 at +0xa09.
  - Reopens FDE.SAV for writing, stores fdps_compute_save_checksum(image, 0x59cb) at image + 0x59c7, encrypts all 0x59cb bytes with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer, fwrites them, fcloses, frees the image, then frees the menu page and rebuilds it with fdps_saveload_screen_build("Save.cel") so the slot list shows the save just made.
On leaving the loop it frees the menu page and mosaic-reveals restore_page onto the VGA screen with the same fdps_transition_random_blocks call.

Parameters:
  restore_page -- the caller's 64000-byte 320x200 8bpp page that the display is transitioned back to when the save screen closes. fdps_run_village_phase passes a freshly zeroed page, so the screen fades to black; fdps_run_bar_shop passes the page holding the bar screen.

Returns:
  Nothing. Whether anything was saved is not reported to the caller.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image, and it calls named game routines while using the CRT only as a consumer]

Rebuild note:
The timestamp fields and DAT_00064110 land inside the 0xa00-byte block that was just memmoved, at +0x9ec..+0x9ff, not after it; appending them after the copied block shifts every header field and breaks fdps_load_game_screen and fdps_draw_save_slot_panel. A missing FDE.SAV is initialised with memset 0xff and not 0, because 0xff in the record's chapter byte at +0xa00 is what marks a slot empty.

=== 00024a40 [PLATE]

Reads the slot's chapter byte at slot_record+0xa00. When it is 0xff the slot has never been written, so the routine prints message 0x209 of the text sheet in DAT_000643c4 through FUN_0001ff60 at dest+0x1aa4 (row 21, column 100 at a 320-byte pitch) and returns without drawing anything else.

Parameters:

Rebuild note:
The portrait is fetched from the fixed address DAT_00060138 + 4 -- sprite 1 of cache slot 0 -- and that is the right face only because the routine freed the ICON.CEL cache and zeroed DAT_00069cf0 immediately beforehand, forcing the group it loads into slot 0. Writing the obvious thing, indexing the cache by the slot number fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group hands back instead of throwing the cache away first, draws the wrong portrait from the second panel onward. The same teardown is why fdps_saveload_screen_build reloads every roster member's icon group after its slot loop finishes: drop that and the rest of the game paints from a one-entry cache.

=== 00024d70 [PLATE]
Recomputes one battle-map unit's four derived combat stats from its base stats, the items it has equipped and the buffs currently running on it, and writes them back into the unit record.

Algorithm:
Resolves the record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and seeds four 32-bit running totals from the record's base stats: attack from the signed word at +0x37, defense from the signed word at +0x39, and both hit and evade from the single dexterity word at +0x3e -- there is no separate evade base. When the buff timer byte at +0x24 is non-zero it adds 15 to that dexterity seed before it is copied into the second total, so that buff lifts hit and evade together. It then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries starting at record+0x0a, i from 0 to 7. An entry contributes only when its flag byte carries the equipped bit 0x40; its item id, the entry's second byte, is resolved through fdps_get_item_record and the ITEM.DAT record's four modifier words are added -- +0x01 (ap) to attack, +0x05 (dp) to defense, +0x03 (hit) to hit, +0x07 (ev) to evade. With the sum complete, if the buff timer byte at +0x22 is non-zero the attack total is multiplied by the double 1.15 held at 00061b1c and truncated toward zero by __CHP, and if the buff timer byte at +0x23 is non-zero the defense total is scaled the same way by the 1.15 held at 00061b24. The four totals are finally stored as words at record +0x48 (attack), +0x4a (defense), +0x4c (hit) and +0x4e (evade) -- the fields fdps_draw_unit_status_panel prints, highlighting attack while +0x22 runs, defense while +0x23 runs, and hit, evade and dexterity while +0x24 runs. Nothing is bounds-checked and no total is clamped.

Bytes +0x22 through +0x27 are the unit's six status timers, counted down one per turn by FUN_0001fa30, which calls this function for the unit whenever one of them reaches zero so the expired buff drops out of the stats again. The roster-side counterpart is fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats, which runs the same equipment sum over a party roster record but applies neither the 15-point dexterity bonus nor the two 1.15 multipliers.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte battle/map unit array based at [0x00069cd8], 0 .. [0x00060150]-1; the index fdps_get_unit_record takes. Callers pass the unit whose equipment or status has just changed.

Returns:
Nothing. The result is the four stat words written into the unit record at +0x48, +0x4a, +0x4c and +0x4e.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set and the body hash is unique in the image; game domain logic over the FDPS unit record and ITEM.DAT, with all fifteen callers ordinary game bodies -- the one runtime contact, __CHP between FILD/FMUL and FISTP, is the Watcom float-to-int helper being consumed here]

Rebuild note:
The two buff multipliers are the double 1.15 applied as an x87 multiply followed by a truncate-toward-zero, i.e. exactly (int)(total * 1.15) in double precision; rewriting them as the obvious integer form total * 115 / 100 diverges wherever the double product lands just under an integer -- a buffed attack of 100 must come out 114, not 115, and 180, 200, 220, 340, 360 and 380 are wrong the same way. Second, hit and evade both seed from the one dexterity word at +0x3e: writing an evade base read at +0x40 because the other stats are consecutive would read the unit's current HP instead.

=== 00024e98 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] (6-byte nop) + mov edx,edx (2-byte nop), aligning next function to 16 bytes.

=== 00024ea0 [PLATE]
Draws one unit's eight-slot inventory list into an 8bpp surface: the selection bar on the highlighted row, then, for every filled slot, the item's category icon, its name and its headline number.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index). When selected_slot is 0..7 it blits sprite 0 of the SelBar.cel sheet held in DAT_000643c0 through fdps_cel_blit_sprite at x=0, y=selected_slot*0x11+8, so the highlight sits under the row drawn next; any other value leaves the list unhighlighted.
Then for each slot i of 0..7 it reads the slot pair at unit record offset 0xa+2*i: the flag byte at +0xa and the item id at +0xb. Flag bit 0x80 marks the slot empty and skips it; bit 0x40 marks the item equipped.
For a filled slot it fetches the item record with fdps_get_item_record(item_id) and picks the category icon from the record's type byte at +0x00: type 1..0x15 (weapons) gives 0x1d, type 0x16..0x27 (armour) gives 0x1e, everything else -- type 0 included -- gives 0x1f; an equipped item adds 4, giving 0x21/0x22/0x23. fdps_blit_command_sprite draws that Command.cel sprite at x=3, y=i*0x11+9.
The item name is message 0xc9+item_id out of the message table in DAT_000643c4, rendered by FUN_0001ff60 at x=0x13, y=i*0x11+8 with glyph arguments 0xd0, 0, 0x6d.
The right-hand column, at x=0x66, y=i*0x11+0xd, is one more Command.cel caption sprite plus a four-digit number drawn 0x16 pixels further right by fdps_draw_number: type 1..0x15 gives caption 0x40 with the record's ap (i16 at +0x01); type 0x27 or below -- which here also catches type 0 -- gives caption 0x41 with dp (i16 at +0x05); otherwise the use_effect byte at +0x0d decides, 0x0b (restore HP) giving caption 0x3e with use_amount (u16 at +0x0e), 0x0c (restore MP) giving caption 0x3f with the same field, and every other item giving caption 0x43 on its own with no number.
Rows are 0x11 = 17 pixels apart, and every coordinate is folded into the destination pointer as dest_base + y*pitch + x, so the routine never touches a surface descriptor.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, handed straight to fdps_get_unit_record; the callers pass on the unit they were opened for.
  selected_slot -- which inventory row carries the selection bar, 0..7; anything outside that range draws no bar. fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window passes -1, FUN_000259c0 and FUN_00025da0 pass 0, FUN_00025b20 passes its live cursor position.
  dest_base -- base of the 8bpp destination surface. All four callers pass their 320x200 window buffer + 0x3b58, i.e. the list starts at pixel (0x98, 0x2f).
  pitch -- bytes per destination row; all four callers pass 0x140 (320).

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls and is called only by game code, and reads the game's own resource globals]

Rebuild note:
The item type byte is classified twice with two different tests, and type 0 falls in a different bucket each time: the icon test sends type 0 to the catch-all icon 0x1f, while the caption test lets it fall into the armour branch and print caption 0x41 with dp. A rewrite that computes the category once and reuses it changes what a slot holding an id past the end of Item.dat draws (the 0xFF bug item, or 0xE2..0xFA whose records are all zero) -- the original shows the plain item icon beside a DP figure. Keep the two tests apart. In the same vein only use_effect 0x0b and 0x0c print a recovery amount: 0x20, which also restores HP, falls through to caption 0x43 and no number.

=== 0002513d [EOL]
Alignment padding: 3-byte NOP form 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning next function to 0x25140.

=== 00025140 [PLATE]
Finds which of a unit's eight inventory slots holds the weapon, or the armor, that the unit currently has equipped.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte record, then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. For each entry it forms record + 0x0a + i*2 and tests bit 0x40 of that flag byte, the equipped bit -- the same bit FUN_00026070 writes when it equips a slot and FUN_00024ea0 reads to pick the equipped icon variant; a slot without it is skipped. For an equipped slot it passes the entry's second byte, the item id fdps_unit_get_item_id returns, to fdps_get_item_record and reads the record's first byte, the ITEM.DAT type field. When want_armor is 0 the slot matches if that type lies in 1..0x15, the whole weapon span of the type field; otherwise it matches if the type lies in 0x16..0x27, the armor span. The index of the first matching slot is returned immediately. Falling out of the loop after all eight entries returns -1. Neither argument is range-checked and no byte of the record is written.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes; the unit whose equipment is being looked up.
  want_armor -- which piece of equipment to look for: 0 for the equipped weapon (item type 1..0x15), non-zero for the equipped armor (item type 0x16..0x27). Every caller but the shop loop passes a literal 0; FUN_00033b80 passes 1 when the shop item under the cursor has a type above 0x15.

Returns:
The inventory slot index, 0..7, of the first equipped item of the requested kind, or -1 when the unit has no such item equipped. Callers feed the index back to fdps_unit_get_item_id or to the shop's trade-in price, and treat -1 as "nothing equipped".

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_get_item_record, and all nine references are direct calls from game code; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The weapon test rejects item type 0 as well as everything above 0x15, so it is `type != 0 && type <= 0x15`, not `type <= 0x15`. Writing the obvious single-sided comparison would make an equipped slot whose item record reads back type 0 -- the all-zero tail records of ITEM.DAT past id 0xe1, which a bad item id resolves to -- count as an equipped weapon, and the caller would then charge a trade-in price for, or attack with, a blank item.

=== 000251fb [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning FUN_00025200 to 16 bytes.

=== 00025200 [PLATE]
Returns the item id held in one inventory slot of a unit.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte unit record in the array based at DAT_00069cd8, then returns the unsigned byte at record + slot*2 + 0x0b. The unit's inventory is eight 2-byte entries starting at record offset 0x0a: byte 0 of an entry is its flag byte (bit 7 set means the slot holds nothing, bit 6 means the item is equipped -- see FUN_00025240 and FUN_00025140) and byte 1, the byte this function returns, is the item id that fdps_get_item_record indexes with. Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; its only callee is the game routine fdps_get_unit_record and all 14 references are direct calls from game code]

Rebuild note:
The slot index is not validated, and FUN_0001c520 at 0001c5d4 passes the result of FUN_00025140 straight in without testing it for -1, so a unit with no equipped weapon reads record+0x09 -- one byte before the inventory -- and hands that to fdps_get_item_record. === 00025237 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 80 00 00 00 00 + 8d 52 00, aligning next function entry to 0x25240.

=== 00025240 [PLATE]
Returns how many of a unit's eight inventory slots are holding an item.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte unit record in the array based at DAT_00069cd8, then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. For each entry it forms the address record + i*2 + 0x0a and tests bit 7 of that flag byte; bit 7 set means the slot holds nothing (the item id itself is the second byte of the entry, which fdps_unit_get_item_id returns), so every entry whose bit 7 is clear adds one to the running total. It is a battle unit index on the battle side (fdps_battle_action_menu, FUN_00013040) and a party member index on the village/shop side, where FUN_0003b800 and FUN_0003ab30 pass the constants 0 and 4.

The number of occupied inventory slots, 0 to 8. 0 means the unit is carrying nothing, which is how FUN_00034000 and FUN_00034210 refuse a sale or a transfer; 8 means the inventory is full, which is how FUN_00033b80, FUN_000388b0, FUN_00038b60, FUN_00039060, FUN_0003ab30 and FUN_0003b800 refuse to hand the unit another item. FUN_00034520 uses it as the bound of a 0..count-1 sweep over fdps_unit_get_item_id.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its sole callee is the game routine fdps_get_unit_record and every call site is game code, including fdps_battle_action_menu]

=== 000252b0 [PLATE]
Runs the item command of the battle action menu for one unit: a four-entry ring menu that uses, hands over, equips or discards the items in that unit's bag.

Algorithm:
Copies the four-entry icon template at 0x00024d50 and the matching disabled-flag template at 0x00024d60 onto the stack and sets the result accumulator to -1; both copies happen once, outside the loop. Then it loops:
  - fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index); when the bag is empty it returns the accumulator.
  - Probes for a neighbour with fdps_collect_targets_in_range over the cursor tile, followed by fdps_map_grid_reset. DAT_00069cd4 and DAT_00069ccc hold the map cursor's pixel x and y and are divided by the 0x18-pixel tile size everywhere they are read. When nothing is adjacent it marks entry 1 unselectable in the stack copy of the disabled-flag table.
  - fdps_menu_find_first_enabled_entry, fdps_menu_animate_open, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop, fdps_menu_animate_close, fdps_render_view_frame; then it saves the cursor pixel position for the branches below. A cancel (-1) returns the accumulator.
  - Entry 0, use: fdps_unit_item_select_window(unit_index, 1, &slot) picks a usable item and fdps_get_item_record turns the slot's item id into an Item.dat record. It publishes use_radius (record +0x12) + 2 in the cursor-footprint global DAT_00069cd0, sweeps the reachable targets with fdps_collect_targets_in_range at use_distance (+0x10), passing 1 in the minimum-distance slot only when use_effect (+0x0d) is 0x1c, and runs fdps_map_cursor_select_loop in the record's select_mode (+0x15). It then re-collects the units the effect actually covers: fdps_collect_targets_in_range at use_radius when use_distance is below 0x10, otherwise fdps_collect_targets_in_line along a line of use_distance - 0x10 tiles from the saved cursor tile. For use_effect 0x19 and 0x1c a second pick, fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 6, supplies a destination tile, written as tile coordinates to DAT_0006437c (x) and DAT_00064380 (y). On confirm it applies the effect through FUN_000262a0(unit_index, slot, target_count, target_ids), calls fdps_battle_mark_unit_done and returns 1; on cancel it puts the cursor back on the acting unit with fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit and reopens the item list.
  - Entry 1, hand over: picks any item, mallocs a 100-byte candidate buffer, collects the adjacent units, lets the player pick one with fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 3, identifies it with fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, restores the cursor with fdps_map_cursor_move_to, frees the buffer and calls fdps_flush_keyboard_queue. fdps_unit_add_item puts the item in the recipient's first free slot; when the recipient's bag is full it opens fdps_unit_item_select_window on the recipient and trades the two items instead, removing and re-adding on both sides. Either way it runs fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats on every unit it touched and sets the accumulator to 2.
  - Entry 2, equip: fdps_unit_equip_window(unit_index) and nothing else.
  - Entry 3, discard: picks any item, fdps_unit_remove_item, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats. The accumulator is left as it was.
DAT_00069cd0, the map cursor's overlay footprint, is set to 0 across every fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit call and put back to 1 afterwards, so the cursor does not paint while it snaps.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; fdps_battle_action_menu passes the unit whose action menu it is running.

Returns:
  1 when the unit used an item and its turn is over, 2 when an item changed hands, -1 when the player backed out with neither having happened. fdps_battle_action_menu reads 1 as "the command was carried out" and 2 as "count a later cancel of the whole action menu as an action anyway".

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image]

Rebuild note:
Only the hand-over branch sets the result to 2. Equipping (entry 2) and discarding (entry 3) leave it at -1, so backing out of the action menu after only equipping or throwing something away still leaves the unit free to move and attack, while doing so after a hand-over spends its turn. Writing the obvious "every branch that changed the bag returns 2" costs the unit its turn for an equip.

Alignment padding: 8d 80 00 00 00 00 + 8d 54 22 00, aligns FUN_000259c0 to 16 bytes

=== 000259c0 [PLATE]
Opens the unit status window on one unit's inventory and lets the player pick one of its items.

Algorithm:
Plays "OpWin1.wav" through fdps_play_sfx, then fdps_load_status_cel_image loads the 320x200 Status.cel window image. Saves the visible mode 13h screen with malloc(0xfa00) plus memmove from 0xa0000, so fdps_close_status_window can put it back later. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) is then called and the byte at record+2 is read into a local that nothing afterwards reads.
fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame(saved_screen, window_image, step) runs for step = 0..8, the nine-frame slide-in of the window over the saved screen. fdps_unit_item_select_loop(unit_index, usable_only, window_image, list_backdrop, selected_slot) then runs the modal cursor loop and its result is held. fdps_close_status_window(window_image, saved_screen) takes the window away and puts the screen back, the three buffers are freed in the order window image, list backdrop, saved screen, and the loop's result is returned unchanged.

Parameters:

  usable_only -- passed straight through as fdps_unit_item_select_loop's usable_only: 0 lets confirm accept any occupied slot, non-zero lets it accept only an item whose ITEM.DAT use_effect byte is non-zero. Only the battle "use item" path in 0x000252b0 passes 1; 0x000184f0, 0x0001d990, 0x00034000, fdps_village_item_transfer_loop and the other three call sites in 0x000252b0 pass 0.

Returns:
  1 -- the player confirmed a slot; the slot index is in *selected_slot.
  -1 -- the player cancelled; every caller tests for -1 and skips the action.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game asset string and game-only callees, with malloc/memmove/free used as an ordinary consumer]

Rebuild note:
The list backdrop has to be copied out of the window image before fdps_draw_unit_inventory paints the item rows into it. Writing it in the intuitive order -- draw the panel and the item list, then snapshot the rectangle you will erase with -- captures the rows and the slot-0 selection bar as part of the backdrop, and every redraw inside fdps_unit_item_select_loop then leaves the old highlight showing under the new one.

=== 00025b17 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte and 3-byte LEA NOP forms filling to the 32-byte-aligned entry of FUN_00025b20.

=== 00025b20 [PLATE]
Modal item-list cursor loop of the unit status window: lets the player move a highlight over one unit's eight inventory slots and either confirm a slot or back out.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and caches the character id byte at record+2. Counts the slots in use once, before the loop, applying the same test fdps_unit_item_count applies: for i = 0..7 the flag byte at record[0xa + 2*i] with bit 0x80 clear means that slot holds an item. That count is the cursor's wrap point and is never recomputed, so the loop assumes the inventory does not change under it.
Each iteration does three things in order. fdps_blit_rect copies the untouched 0x97 x 0x95 list panel out of list_backdrop over window_image + 0x3b58 (pitch 0x140, i.e. row 47, column 152 of the 320x200 window) to erase the previous highlight. The routine at 0x00024ea0 then redraws the eight item rows into the same place, putting the selection bar on the row named by *selected_slot (rows are 0x11 pixels tall). Finally fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input(window_image, record[2], 0) presents the frame and blocks until it has one keyboard scancode.
The scancode is dispatched: 0x48 (up) plays Beep.wav and steps *selected_slot back, turning 0 into count-1; 0x50 (down) plays Beep.wav and steps it forward, turning count-1 into 0. 0x1c (Enter) and 0x39 (Space) confirm -- with usable_only zero the routine returns 1 immediately, otherwise it reads the item id at record[0xb + 2 * *selected_slot], looks the record up with fdps_get_item_record and returns 1 only when the ITEM.DAT use_effect byte at +0x0d is non-zero; an item that cannot be used is refused silently, with no sound and no message, and the loop starts over. 0x01 (Esc) and 0x53 (Del) return -1. Every other scancode falls through and repaints.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the 0x50-byte record in the unit array based at DAT_00069cd8; the unit whose inventory is on show. Callers pass the same index they opened the status window with.
  usable_only -- 0 lets confirm accept any slot; non-zero lets it accept only an item whose use_effect is non-zero. Only the battle "use item" path (0x000252b0, through 0x000259c0) passes 1; the equipment screen, the shop sell loop, the item-transfer loop and the script handlers all pass 0.
  window_image -- base of the 320x200 status window image being shown; the item list occupies the rectangle at +0x3b58. Handed on unchanged to fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input.
  list_backdrop -- 0x57e3-byte copy (0x97 x 0x95, stride 0x97) of that list rectangle as it looks with no highlight on it, blitted back over the list at the top of every iteration. 0x00025da0 allocates it with malloc(0x57e3) and fills it with the reverse fdps_blit_rect.
  selected_slot -- in and out: the inventory slot the highlight sits on, 0..count-1. The caller seeds it and reads it back afterwards to learn which item was picked.

Returns:
  1 -- the player confirmed; the chosen slot is in *selected_slot.
  -1 -- the player cancelled; *selected_slot is left wherever the cursor had got to.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; every caller and callee is game code and the only string is the asset name "Beep.wav"]

Rebuild note:
The cursor wraps by comparing against count-1, not by taking a remainder, and 0x00025da0 enters this loop without first checking that the unit carries anything -- so count can be 0. Writing the wrap the obvious way, *selected_slot = (*selected_slot + 1) % count, divides by zero on the equipment screen for a unit with an empty bag; the original simply lets the index walk out of 0..7, draws no highlight for it and does no harm, because 0x00025da0 tests fdps_unit_item_count after the loop returns.

=== 00025cb9 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] + nop, 7 bytes to align next entry at 00025cc0

=== 00025cc0 [PLATE]
Removes one item from a unit's eight-slot inventory, closing the gap so the items that are left stay packed at the front.

Algorithm:
Resolves the record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index). The inventory is eight 2-byte slots starting at record+0x0a: byte 0 of a slot is a flag whose bit 0x80 means "slot empty", byte 1 is the item id -- the layout fdps_unit_add_item fills and fdps_unit_get_item_id reads. memmove then copies the (7 - slot) slots above the removed one down by one slot, from record+0x0c+slot*2 to record+0x0a+slot*2, so slots slot+1..7 become slots slot..6. Finally it stores 0x80 into the flag byte of the last slot at record+0x18, marking it empty. Only that single byte is written: the item id byte at record+0x19 keeps whatever the shift left there. Nothing bounds-checks slot -- slot 7 makes the move zero-length, and anything above 7 hands memmove a negative, therefore huge unsigned, byte count.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array whose base is at 0x00069cd8; callers pass the same index they hand to fdps_unit_item_count and fdps_unit_get_item_id.
  slot -- which inventory slot to drop, 0..7; the shop sell loop at 00034000 and the item transfer loop at 00034210 pass the slot the player just selected and read back with fdps_unit_get_item_id.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX still holds the unit record pointer at the RET, and no caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and edits the returned game record; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The empty marker is written as a single byte -- record[0x18] = 0x80 -- so the item id byte at record+0x19 is left holding the value the memmove shifted into it. Writing the obvious `slots[7] = 0x0080` or clearing the whole 2-byte slot zeroes that id byte, and since fdps_unit_get_item_id returns the id byte without checking the empty flag, any consumer that reads slot 7 unguarded would then get 0 instead of the original's stale id. Keep the store one byte wide.

=== 00025d14 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs aligning FUN_00025d20 to 32 bytes.

=== 00025d20 [PLATE]
Adds one item to a unit's inventory, filling the first empty slot.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte unit record in the array based at DAT_00069cd8, then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. For each entry it forms the address record + i*2 + 0x0a and tests bit 7 of that flag byte; bit 7 set means the slot holds nothing, the same test fdps_unit_item_count uses. At the first such entry it stores 0 over the whole flag byte -- clearing bit 7 so the slot counts as occupied and bit 6 so the item is not marked equipped -- writes item_id into the entry's second byte, the byte fdps_unit_get_item_id returns, and returns 1. If all eight entries are occupied the loop runs out and it returns -1 without touching the record. Neither the unit index nor the item id is range-checked, and the slot is taken as found: nothing is shifted or compacted (removal is the side that compacts, in FUN_00025cc0).

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes; the unit that is to receive the item.
  item_id -- item id to store, 0..0xff; only the low byte of the pushed argument is read. Comes from a shop line (FUN_00033b80), another unit's inventory slot (FUN_00034210), a map cell's contents (FUN_000184f0) or a script record's operand (FUN_0001d990).

Returns:
1 when the item was stored, -1 when all eight inventory slots were already full. FUN_000184f0 and FUN_0001d990 branch on -1 to withhold the reward or to offer the player a replacement; the other callers ignore the result.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only callee is the game routine fdps_get_unit_record and all 21 references are direct calls from game code]

Rebuild note:
Filling a slot means writing 0 over the entry's flag byte, not just storing the id: the obvious C, record[0x0a + i*2 + 1] = item_id with the flag byte left alone, leaves bit 7 set, so fdps_unit_item_count keeps counting the slot as empty and the next add overwrites the item. Two more things a rewrite must copy verbatim: the empty test is flags & 0x80, not flags == 0x80, and the failure return is -1, not 0 -- FUN_000184f0 tests the result with CMP EAX,-1.

=== 00025d9b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning FUN_00025da0 to 16 bytes.

=== 00025da0 [PLATE]
Unit equipment window: opens the status window on one unit's inventory and equips whatever the player picks, one item after another, until they back out.

Algorithm:
fdps_load_status_cel_image loads the 320x200 Status.cel window image. malloc(0xfa00) plus memmove from 0xa0000 saves the visible mode 13h screen so fdps_close_status_window can put it back afterwards. Two more buffers take pristine copies of the two rectangles that get repainted later: malloc(0x57e3) for the item list (0x97 x 0x95 = 151 x 149 pixels at window_image + 0x3b58, i.e. row 47, column 152 of the 320x200 image) and malloc(0x2981) for the stats block (0x7d x 0x55 = 125 x 85 at window_image + 0x8ad3, row 111, column 19, the area holding the HP and MP gauges and the stat figures). fdps_blit_rect copies both out of the image while it is still unpainted. Only then does it paint: fdps_draw_unit_status_panel(unit_index, window_image) fills in the stats side and fdps_draw_unit_inventory(unit_index, 0, window_image + 0x3b58, 0x140) draws the eight item rows with the selection bar on row 0. "OpWin1.wav" plays through fdps_play_sfx, and fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame(saved_screen, window_image, step) runs for step = 0..8, the nine-frame slide-in of the window over the saved screen.

The rest is one loop. fdps_unit_item_select_loop(unit_index, 0, window_image, list_backdrop, &selected_slot) runs the modal cursor loop over the eight inventory slots; the usable_only argument is the literal 0, so confirm accepts any occupied slot. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) then resolves the record and the item id byte at record + 0xb + 2 * selected_slot is read, whichever way the loop ended. The loop stops when the select loop returned -1 (the player cancelled) or when fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index) is 0 -- that count test is the only way out for a unit carrying nothing. Otherwise fdps_unit_can_equip_item(unit_index, item_id) decides. When the unit's class may not wear that item, nothing at all happens -- no sound, no message -- and the select loop is entered again. When it may, "Equip.wav" plays, fdps_unit_equip_slot(unit_index, selected_slot) puts the item on in place of whatever was worn in the same category, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(unit_index) refreshes the derived stats, fdps_blit_rect copies the stats backdrop back over window_image + 0x8ad3 to erase the old figures, and fdps_draw_unit_status_panel redraws them. The item list is not repainted here; fdps_unit_item_select_loop redraws it from list_backdrop at the top of every one of its own passes.

On the way out fdps_close_status_window(window_image, saved_screen) takes the window away and puts the screen back, and the four buffers are freed in the order window image, list backdrop, stats backdrop, saved screen.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the 0x50-byte record in the unit array based at DAT_00069cd8; the unit whose equipment is being changed. Handed on unchanged to every callee that takes a unit index. fdps_village_member_equip_loop passes the party member the player picked, FUN_000252b0 passes the unit whose battle turn it is.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_load_status_cel_image / fdps_draw_unit_status_panel / fdps_get_unit_record / fdps_play_sfx and the game's own "OpWin1.wav" and "Equip.wav" strings, using malloc/memmove/free only as services; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
Both backdrops have to be copied out of the window image before fdps_draw_unit_status_panel and fdps_draw_unit_inventory paint into it. Allocating and snapshotting after the drawing -- the intuitive order -- captures the item rows and the stat figures as part of the backdrops, and every later erase then leaves the old highlight, and the old digits, showing under the new ones. The empty-bag path is load-bearing too: the window opens and plays its slide-in even for a unit carrying nothing, and the fdps_unit_item_count test that closes it runs only after fdps_unit_item_select_loop has returned, so an early "nothing to equip" guard would change what the player sees.

Alignment padding: 8b c0 (mov eax,eax), 2-byte nop aligning FUN_00025fe0 to 16 bytes.

=== 00025fe0 [PLATE]
Reports whether one unit's class is allowed to equip a given item.

Algorithm:
calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads the class code from byte +0x20 of the record; passes that code unchanged to fdps_get_class_equip_types, which returns the six permitted item-type codes of the class from PROEQU.DAT; calls fdps_get_item_record(item_id) and takes byte 0 of the record, the item's type code (weapon categories 0x01-0x15, armour 0x16-0x27, consumables and story items 0x28-0x2c). It then walks the six class entries in order and returns 1 as soon as one equals the item's type, or 0 once all six have been compared. The class code is used raw here, without the +1 that callers of fdps_get_class_record apply.

Parameters:

  item_id -- ITEM.DAT record index of the item being tested, from the inventory slot or the shop item list

Returns:

Pool: fdps  [no library match; calls only named game code, and all three callers are game screens]

=== 00026070 [PLATE]
Equips the item held in one of a unit's eight inventory slots, unequipping whatever the unit already wore in the same category.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record twice through fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) -- both calls return the same 0x50-byte record out of the array based at DAT_00069cd8 -- and reads the item id of the slot being equipped from record + slot*2 + 0x0b. fdps_get_item_record turns that id into an ITEM.DAT record and its byte at +0 is the item's type code. Then it walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. An entry whose flag byte has bit 0x40 clear is skipped, so only entries currently equipped are considered. For an equipped entry it looks its item id up with fdps_get_item_record too and compares the two type codes against the threshold 0x15: type codes 0x01-0x15 are the weapon kinds and 0x16 upward are armour and the non-weapon items, so the two items are in the same category exactly when both are <= 0x15 or both are > 0x15. In that case the entry's whole flag byte is stored back as 0, taking the equipped bit off it (bit 7, the slot-is-empty bit, is already clear on an occupied slot). An equipped entry whose item record type byte is 0 -- which no real item has -- is left alone. Finally it stores 0x40 into the flag byte at record + slot*2 + 0x0a unconditionally, marking that slot equipped. Nothing is range-checked and nothing verifies that the slot is occupied or that the unit's class may wear the item; FUN_00025fe0 is the check the status screen runs first.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes.
  slot -- inventory slot to equip, 0..7. FUN_00025da0 passes the slot under the menu cursor; FUN_00033b80 passes fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index) - 1, the slot fdps_unit_add_item has just filled.

Returns:
Nothing. Both callers discard EAX.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_get_item_record; no Function ID hit in the Watcom or Miles sets, and its call site plays s_Equip.wav]

Rebuild note:
Only one item per broad category may be worn, and the category test is the coarse split at item type 0x15 (weapons 0x01-0x15, armour and the rest 0x16 up) -- not equality of the type byte and not the class's PROEQU.DAT equip list. Writing the obvious 'unequip the other slot holding an item of the same type' gives the wrong answer: equipping a 刀 (type 0x02) must unequip an already equipped 劍 (type 0x01), and equipping any armour must unequip any other armour whatever its sub-kind.

=== 00026174 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte LEA NOP forms filling to the 16-byte-aligned entry at 00026180.

=== 00026180 [PLATE]
Collects the death-script record of every battle unit the action just carried out has reduced to zero HP, so the caller can pay out and fire those scripts once the death sequence has played.

Algorithm:
Walks unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the unit count of the map currently in play), resolving each record with fdps_get_unit_record. A unit contributes when all three tests pass: bit 0 of the flag byte at record+0x05 is clear, i.e. the unit has not already been taken off the map (the same bit fdps_unit_is_retired returns and fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead sets); the opcode byte at record+0x31 is not 0xff, the "no script" sentinel; and the signed hit-point word at record+0x40 is <= 0 (CMP word ptr [EAX + 0x40],0x0 / JLE to the copy block at 000261e9). For each qualifying unit it memmoves the 3 bytes at record+0x31 -- an opcode byte followed by a signed 16-bit operand -- to out_scripts + 3*n, then bumps n. n is returned.

Where the record comes from: fdps_deploy_unit fills record+0x31 and +0x32 from bytes +0x16 and +0x17 of the map%02d.dat deployment record, so only the map's scripted units carry a script, while fdps_build_map_unit_array stamps 0xff into +0x31 of every player-roster slot it lays out, which is why the party never pays a reward for its own losses.

What the records mean is settled by the consumer, fdps_run_death_scripts, which the same callers hand this array to: opcode 0 gives the operand to the acting unit as an item, 1 adds it to the party gold at DAT_000643a4, 2 calls slot operand of the chapter-event handler table at 000601c4, and 3 or above paints line operand of the chapter text table, with 4 additionally setting the battle-end code DAT_00069da0 to 2 (chapter cleared) and 5 setting it to 1 (defeat). All four callers -- fdps_battle_action_menu, fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets and fdps_battle_spell_command -- use the same three-step idiom: this function into a stack buffer, then fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead to play the destruction sequence and retire the dead units, then fdps_run_death_scripts to run the collected records against the acting unit. The sibling fdps_collect_defeated_unit_events reads the same field under the same retired and hit-point tests but accepts only opcodes 2..5, so the map-AI path that reaches it hands out no item or gold rewards.

Nothing bounds the write: the loop can emit one record per unit on the map, while the tightest caller, fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, has only 0x0c bytes -- four records -- between its buffer at EBP-0x18 and its next live local.

Parameters:
  out_scripts -- caller-supplied array that receives the collected records, three bytes each, packed from the front with no gaps. Every caller passes the address of a local stack buffer; the buffer's capacity is never communicated to this function.

Returns:
  int -- how many 3-byte records were written; 0 when no unit qualifies. The callers pass it straight to fdps_run_death_scripts as its record count, and that function does nothing at all when it is 0.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and reads the game's unit-count global DAT_00060150; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the AIL set]

Rebuild note:
The collect must run before fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, not after: that function stores 1 into record+0x05 for every unit at zero HP, which sets the retired bit this function's first test rejects, so reordering the two -- play the death animation, then hand out the rewards, which reads as the natural order -- silently returns 0 and every item, gold and scripted chapter event owed for those kills is lost. All four callers already have it in the right order. Second, the routine writes one 3-byte record per qualifying unit with no capacity check at all, and the caller buffers are sized by nothing but the original's frame layout -- fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack leaves it four records -- so a rebuild must keep each caller's buffer at least as large as the original's rather than trust this routine to stop, and must not add the bound check that obviously belongs here.

=== 00026225 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx, aligning FUN_00026230 to 16 bytes.

=== 00026230 [PLATE]
Applies one damaging item or spell effect to a list of battle-map targets: damages each target, floats the damage number over it, then plays all of those numbers out at once over the unit shake animation.

Algorithm:
Loops i from 0 to target_count-1. For each i it zero-extends target_ids[i] to a unit index and calls FUN_00028460(unit_index, base_damage), which rolls base_damage*9/10 + (rand()%100)*base_damage/1000, subtracts that from the unit record's current HP (word +0x40, clamped at zero) and returns the rolled amount. The returned amount goes straight into FUN_0001f510(amount, 0, unit_index), which queues a four-cell floating number over that unit in the popup tables at 00064120 / 000641e8 / 000642b0 and advances the queue counter at 00064378; the glyph base 0 selects the damage digit sprites, where the healing path at FUN_00026fd0 passes 0x27 for its own digit set. After the loop it calls FUN_0001f340 once, which plays the 22-frame unit shake with the queued numbers riding over it and clears the queue counter at the end -- so every target's number appears together, after all the damage has already been applied. FUN_0001f340 is gated on that counter being non-zero, so a target_count of 0 leaves the screen alone.

Parameters:
  target_count -- how many entries of target_ids to hit; the size of the area-of-effect target list FUN_000262a0 was given.
  target_ids -- array of target_count bytes, each a unit index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8.
  base_damage -- the effect's power before the damage roll; FUN_000262a0 reads it from the signed word at offset 0x0e of the item record of the item or spell being used.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image, and every callee is unit-record game code]

Rebuild note:
The number floated over each target is the rolled damage FUN_00028460 returns, not the HP actually removed: a unit on 3 HP hit for 20 has its HP clamped to 0 but still shows 20. Recomputing the popup value as (HP before - HP after), which is the obvious way to write it, changes what the player sees on every overkill.

=== 0002629c [EOL]

=== 000262a0 [PLATE]
Applies the effect of one item out of a unit's inventory to a list of battle-map targets, and settles the deaths that effect causes.

Algorithm:
Clears the floating-indicator queue count at DAT_00064378, reads the acting unit's record through fdps_get_unit_record, and takes the item id from the inventory entry at record + 0xb + 2 * item_slot. fdps_get_item_record turns that id into an ITEM.DAT record, from which it reads use_effect (byte at +0x0d) and use_amount (signed word at +0x0e), then dispatches on use_effect:

  0x01/0x07, 0x02/0x08, 0x03/0x09 -- plays EMg00.saf, EMg05.saf or EMg08.saf over the targets with fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units, then fdps_apply_damage_to_targets with use_amount.
  0x04/0x0a -- loads EarQu.wav out of MISC.VFS with fdps_vfs_load_entry, starts it with fdps_audio_start_wav, shakes the view over 25 fdps_render_view_frame passes by offsetting the scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0 by rand() % 4 - 2 each frame, restores both globals, then fdps_apply_damage_to_targets.
  0x0b/0x20 -- fdps_apply_heal_to_targets with use_amount.
  0x0c -- CureMP.saf over the targets and a fdps_flash_units_in_color flash in colour 0xff, then for every target either fdps_show_miss_indicator when its maximum MP (record +0x46) is 0, or fdps_unit_restore_mp followed by the restored figure floated over it.
  0x0f, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14 -- the permanent stat-up items, all under Cure.saf and all applied to target_ids[0] only: +15 maximum HP (+0x42), +15 maximum MP (+0x46), +7 AP (+0x37), +7 DP (+0x39), +7 DX (+0x3e), +1 MV (+0x3b). The three that move a combat stat follow with fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats. Every amount is a constant here, not use_amount.
  0x16, 0x18 -- clears the poison byte (+0x25) or the paralysis byte (+0x26) of target_ids[0], queueing the cured popup through fdps_queue_status_cured_popup first when the byte was set, then Cure.saf and a 0xff flash over the targets.
  0x1e -- damages every target directly through fdps_unit_apply_damage with use_amount and floats the figure over it, with no effect animation and without consuming the item.
  0x21 -- 蓋亞's 強化套件: opens the message window on the target's form id (record +0x07), and when that id is 9 draws text 0x21e, adds +30 AP, +30 DP and +1 MV, grants the 轟神砲 spell with fdps_set_flag_bit bit 0x1d, and recomputes the combat stats; any other form id gets the refusal text 0x21d.
  0x22 -- the other 強化套件: the same shape, text 0x21f and +100 maximum HP when the form id is 9.
  0x23 -- 布蘭多's 高能量裝置: opens the message window on the target's original character id (record +0x08) and acts only when that id is 8. With no 金屬礦 (item 0xa3) in the target's bag it draws text 0x220; otherwise text 0x221, then it removes the device, looks the 金屬礦 slot up a second time, removes that too and hands over the 高能量砲 (item 0xbe).

Each consumable branch calls fdps_unit_remove_item on the acting unit's slot; the weapon-borne codes paired with them -- 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x20 and 0x1e -- leave the item alone. use_effect values 0x05, 0x06, 0x0d and 0x1b reach no branch at all, so the items carrying them do nothing when used. All the message text goes through fdps_draw_text against the text block pointer in DAT_000643c4, between fdps_message_window_open and fdps_message_window_close.

Finally it clears DAT_00069cec, collects the death scripts of everything the effect killed into a stack buffer with fdps_collect_death_scripts, plays those deaths out with fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, and runs the scripts with fdps_run_death_scripts so the acting unit collects the rewards.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit using the item, into the 0x50-byte unit array whose base is at DAT_00069cd8. Both callers pass the unit whose turn it is.
  item_slot -- which of that unit's eight inventory slots holds the item. 0x000252b0 gets it from fdps_unit_item_select_window, fdps_map_actor_use_item from the slot the map AI picked.
  target_count -- how many entries target_ids holds; the callers get it from fdps_collect_targets_in_range or fdps_collect_targets_in_line.
  target_ids -- array of target unit indices, one byte each. Several branches only ever touch target_ids[0].

Returns:
  Nothing. Both callers ignore EAX.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit; game unit records, ITEM.DAT records, view globals and named .saf/.wav resources]

Rebuild note:
The 0x23 branch deliberately looks the 金屬礦 slot up a second time after fdps_unit_remove_item has already removed the device: removing an item compacts the eight-slot inventory, so reusing the index from the first fdps_unit_find_item_slot would delete the wrong item. The permanent stat-up amounts (15, 15, 7, 7, 7, 1, 30/30/1, 100) are constants in this function and not the item's use_amount, which is 0 for every one of those items, so the obvious `stat += use_amount` silently does nothing. Effects 0x21/0x22 test the current form id at unit record +0x07 while 0x23 tests the original character id at +0x08; unifying them onto +0x07 would break the 高能量砲 trade for a 布蘭多 who has already class-changed, and onto +0x08 would change which portrait the message window shows. The earthquake jitter is rand() % 4 - 2, i.e. -2..+1, not a symmetric shake.

=== 00026dfb [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning to 00026e00

=== 00026e00 [PLATE]
Plays one named MISC.VFS animation over a list of battle-map units, drawing a copy of the animation on each listed unit's map cell over the live scrolling scene and presenting it in the game's framed 312x192 main view.

Algorithm:
malloc(0x15180) takes a 360x240 8bpp page -- wider and taller than the presented window, so a frame may overhang it without being clipped. That page becomes field +0x00 of the 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request built on the stack; the request's pitch (+0x04) is 0x168 (360), its height (+0x08) 0xf0 (240), and its blit parameter block (+0x1c) and blit mode (+0x20) are both 0. fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", anim_name) loads the animation into a fresh buffer, which becomes the request's SAF base at +0x14, and fdps_saf_frame_count gives the frame total.

Each frame index from 0 to that total minus 1 is played for exactly two timer ticks; the dwell field the SAF frame record carries is not consulted, unlike fdps_saf_play_over_scene. On every one of those ticks:
  - fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the scrolling layer table into the page from scratch;
  - the request's frame index (+0x18) takes the current frame number;
  - for each i from 0 to unit_count - 1, fdps_get_unit_record(unit_ids[i]) resolves the unit's 0x50-byte record and the request origin is set from its tile position and the camera: x (+0x0c) = record[0] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 - 0x18, y (+0x10) = record[1] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0 - 0x1e, where record[0] and record[1] are the unit's tile column and row, 0x18 is the 24-pixel tile size, and DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0 are the view origin in map pixels. fdps_draw_composite_sprite then draws the frame there. Its sound flag is 1 only when i == 0 and this is the first of the frame's two ticks, and 0 otherwise, so a frame that carries a sound effect fires it once per animation frame instead of once per unit per tick. Nothing culls a unit that has scrolled outside the visible window;
  - the routine spins on port 0x3da until vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, then fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312x192) window at page + 0x21d8 -- row 24, column 24 of the 360-wide page -- with source pitch 0x168 to 0xa0504, row 4 column 4 of the mode 13h framebuffer;
  - it then spins until the frame-tick global DAT_00069d64 differs from the value latched at the end of the previous tick, and latches the new value.

When the last frame has been played it frees the page and then the loaded animation.

Parameters:
  unit_count -- how many entries of unit_ids to draw the animation over. 1 from the poison and status-effect call sites, the effect's target count from the item and spell effect handlers.
  unit_ids -- array of unit_count unit indices into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; each element is zero-extended and passed to fdps_get_unit_record. Callers pass either their target-id list or the address of a single-byte local.
  anim_name -- name of the entry to play inside MISC.VFS, such as "Cure.saf", "CureMP.saf", "Posion.saf", "PosEff.saf" or "EMg00.saf". Handed straight to fdps_vfs_load_entry, which ends the program if the archive holds no entry of that name.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library; game callees and game globals]

Rebuild note:
The frame-tick value this routine spins against is a stack local that is never initialised, so the first tick of the animation compares against whatever the frame happened to hold and in practice skips its wait entirely. Giving that local an initialiser -- 0, or the current DAT_00069d64, either of which is the obvious thing to write -- adds a tick of delay to the start of every effect animation. Leave it uninitialised.

=== 00026fc9 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) plus 0x90, aligning next entry to 0x26fd0.

=== 00026fd0 [PLATE]
Applies one HP-restoring item effect to a list of battle-map targets, animation included: plays the effect animation over them, heals each one, floats the restored amount over it, then plays all of those numbers out at once over the unit shake animation.

Algorithm:
Calls FUN_00026e00(target_count, target_ids, "Posion.saf") to play that MISC.VFS animation over the battle scene with the listed units drawn into every frame; the string literal sits at 00061b98 and is spelled "Posion", not "Poison". FUN_0001f340's work is gated on that cursor being non-zero, so a target_count of 0 floats nothing -- but the two animations ahead of the loop still run in full.

Parameters:
  target_count -- how many entries of target_ids to heal, 0 or more; the size of the area-of-effect target list FUN_000262a0 was given.
  target_ids -- array of target_count bytes, each a unit index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8.
  base_heal -- the effect's power before the healing roll. FUN_000262a0 reads it from the signed word at offset 0x0e of the item record (use_amount) and reaches this function for use_effect 0x0b, the consumable HP restores B4 藥草 / B5 回復劑 / B6 再生藥 / C2 神聖之水, and for use_effect 0x20, the healing staves, spears and bows such as 1C 女神之杖 and 34 天使之杖. Both codes arrive here with identical arguments.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [feeds a game resource filename to a MISC.VFS loader, no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image]

Rebuild note:

Writing the obvious "Poison.saf" makes the MISC.VFS lookup miss the entry and the heal plays no animation. The same misspelled literal is emitted a second time at 0006155c for the map-AI callers, so it is written that way in more than one source module.

=== 00027067 [EOL]
