=== 00027070 [PLATE]
Applies one healing effect to a battle unit's HP and credits the battle experience earned for it.

Algorithm:
Resolves the 0x50-byte unit record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its current HP (signed word +0x40) and maximum HP (signed word +0x42). Rolls the heal as amount*9/10 plus (rand()%100)*amount/1000, so a request of N restores between 0.900*N and 0.999*N. Adds the roll to current HP, clamps the total to maximum HP, and stores it back to +0x40. Then, when the record's portrait/character id byte +0x7 is below 0x3c -- the unit is a roster character rather than an EnemyDat entry -- it adds (effective level * 25 * HP actually restored) / maximum HP to the pending experience accumulator DAT_00069cec, where the effective level is the unit's level byte +0x21 plus 30 for portrait ids 0x0f..0x21, the promoted character forms whose levels restart at 1. FUN_0001dd30 is what later clamps DAT_00069cec to 99 and awards it to the acting unit. The value handed back is the rolled heal, not the HP that was actually restored.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; the callers pass the battle target's unit index.
  amount -- the requested heal. FUN_00026fd0 passes the item record's use_amount word (+0x0e) for the use_effect 0x0b consumables and 0x20 healing staves; fdps_spell_heal_unit and FUN_000288f0 pass the power word (+0x00) of a spell record.

Returns:
  The heal that was rolled -- amount*9/10 + (rand()%100)*amount/1000 -- before the clamp against maximum HP. FUN_00026fd0 passes it straight to FUN_0001f510 as the number to float over the target.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and writes the game global DAT_00069cec; no Function ID hit against the Watcom 10.0x libraries or ailv3.lib, and the only library callee is rand]

Rebuild note:
The return value is the heal that was rolled, not the HP actually restored, and FUN_00026fd0 prints it as the floating number over the target -- writing the obvious `return new_hp - old_hp` would make a near-full-HP target display a smaller number than the original does. Separately, the +30 effective-level bonus is tested here as portrait id 0x0f..0x21 while FUN_00027c20 tests portrait id > 8 for the same +30 (000280cf), so folding the two into one shared helper changes the experience awarded.

=== 0002717a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0] before FUN_00027180.

=== 00027180 [PLATE]
Carries out the item action the map AI has just chosen for one battle-map actor: re-collects the target list for the chosen item, plays the map-side presentation of the hit, then applies the effect.

Algorithm:
The item comes out of the acting unit's own inventory. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) gives the record, and the byte at record + 0xb + DAT_00063f7c * 2 is the item id of the slot the map-AI scorer at 00013040 picked; fdps_get_item_record turns that id into an ITEM.DAT record. The side filter comes from the item's use_target byte +0x11: with side_select non-zero (an NPC-side actor) it is passed on as written, with side_select 0 (an enemy-side actor) it is replaced by (use_target == 0), which mirrors the item's normal player-side sense onto the enemy side.
fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit puts the cursor on the actor, then the item's use_distance byte +0x10 chooses the shape. Below 0x10 it is an area item and the targets come from fdps_collect_targets_in_range(DAT_00063f98, DAT_00063f94, targets, use_radius +0x12, 0, side filter). At 0x10 and above it is a straight-line item and they come from fdps_collect_targets_in_line(DAT_00063f98, DAT_00063f94, targets, record +0 = actor tile x, record +1 = actor tile y, use_distance - 0x10, side filter). DAT_00063f98 and DAT_00063f94 are the x and y of the target tile the scorer chose; targets is a 32-byte stack array whose length neither collector checks.
fdps_map_grid_reset then wipes what the collector painted on the working grid, delay(200) holds, and the cursor overlay mode DAT_00069cd0 is set to use_radius + 2 -- the area-of-effect diamond fdps_draw_map_cursor draws at that mode.
  Area item: fdps_map_cursor_move_to(DAT_00063f98 * 0x18, DAT_00063f94 * 0x18) walks the cursor to the target tile carrying that diamond, and the routine drops straight to the effect. It leaves the cursor mode at use_radius + 2; both callers clear it on their way out.
  Straight-line item: fdps_unit_face_target turns the actor toward targets[0], delay(200) holds, and the screen flashes white and fades back -- fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, i, i, i) applies the same bias to all three channels with i counting 0x40 down to 0 and delay(4) between steps, so 0x40 saturates the whole DAC to white and 0 restores it. Cursor mode becomes 6, the mode in which fdps_draw_map_cursor draws nothing and instead clears the marked byte of every grid cell the cursor crosses, so the sweep leaves the beam's path highlighted behind it. The far end of the beam is extrapolated from the actor's own tile -- the cursor globals DAT_00069cd4 (x) and DAT_00069ccc (y) divided by the 0x18 pixel tile size -- along the direction of the target tile, (use_distance - 0x10) times over, then clamped (see the rebuild note). DAT_0006015c is reset to 0x14 so the highlight blend ramp starts from a fixed phase, fdps_map_cursor_move_to sweeps the cursor out to that tile, cursor mode goes back to 0, eight calls to fdps_render_view_frame hold the trail on screen, fdps_map_grid_reset wipes it and the cursor returns to targets[0].
Finally FUN_000262a0(unit_index, DAT_00063f7c, target count, targets) applies the item's effect to every unit collected, and DAT_00069cec -- the pending experience accumulator FUN_0001dd30 hands to the acting unit -- is zeroed, so a map-AI actor is credited nothing for the action.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte record array at DAT_00069cd8; both callers, fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, pass the actor they are stepping.
  side_select -- which side the actor stands on, and with it how the item's use_target byte +0x11 is read: 0 for an enemy-side actor, reaching here from fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase, and 1 for an NPC-side actor, from fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase. Both callers pass their own second argument straight down.

Returns:
  0 on every path. Both callers discard it.

Pool: fdps  [no FID hit in either library set; game call graph and game globals]

Rebuild note:
The clamp on the extrapolated sweep tile reads its bounds from the wrong place. It takes signed words at +0 and +2 of layer 0's .MPL blob (the pointer at DAT_00069cb0), but an .MPL carries its dimensions at +7 and +9 and its first four bytes are the magic "MPL\0" -- so the bounds it actually gets are 0x504d = 20557 for x and 0x004c = 76 for y. Only the lower clamp to 0 ever fires, and a beam aimed right or down off the edge of a map (maps run about 30x24 tiles, beams up to 15 tiles) sweeps the cursor past the edge, where cursor mode 6 marks grid cells of the following row. Clamping against the real map size -- the words at +0 and +2 of the working grid DAT_00060144, which is what fdps_collect_targets_in_line uses -- stops the sweep at the map edge and does not reproduce the original.

=== 000274df [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP aligning FUN_000274e0 to a 16-byte boundary.

=== 000274e0 [PLATE]
Collects the event half of the death scripts carried by every battle unit the action just resolved has brought to 0 HP, so the caller can run them once the kill has been played out: the scripted chapter events and battle-end verdicts, but not the item and gold rewards.

Algorithm:
Walks unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the battle unit count), fetching each 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record. A unit contributes when all three tests pass: bit 0 of the flag byte at record+0x05 is clear -- not retired, the same bit fdps_unit_is_retired returns and fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead sets; the signed hit-point word at record+0x40 is <= 0; and the opcode byte at record+0x31 is between 2 and 5 inclusive, which also excludes the 0xff "no script" sentinel. For each accepted unit the three bytes at record+0x31 -- an opcode byte followed by a signed 16-bit operand, the same death-script record fdps_collect_death_scripts copies -- are memmoved to out_events + 3*count, and count is bumped. count is returned.

Why the opcode window is 2..5:
fdps_run_death_scripts, which the caller hands the collected array to, splits its opcodes in exactly this place. Opcodes 2 (call slot operand of the chapter-event handler table at 000601c4), 3 (paint scripted line operand of the chapter text table), and 4 / 5 (the same line plus the battle-end code at DAT_00069da0 set to 2 for cleared or 1 for defeat) run unconditionally. Opcodes 0 (item drop) and 1 (gold) first require the unit index that executor was given to be player-side (its record byte +6 == 2) and not retired, and on failure return from the whole executor rather than skipping the one record. The sole caller here, fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell, is the map AI casting a spell, and it passes DAT_00063f74 -- the melee target the physical-attack scorer picked, which on this path is left over from an earlier action -- as that unit index; immediately after the call it zeroes the pending-experience accumulator DAT_00069cec instead of awarding it. Both halves of the same policy: an AI spell kill pays the player nothing. Withholding the reward opcodes here rather than letting the executor reject them is what keeps that suppression from also truncating the list, since the executor's rejection is a return and would take opcodes 4 and 5 -- the battle-end verdicts -- down with it. The sibling fdps_collect_death_scripts keeps every opcode except 0xff, and each of its four callers hands the executor a unit that can satisfy the guard: the AI's melee path fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack passes that same DAT_00063f74, but there it is the live player-side unit the AI just struck, the one it also awards the accumulated experience to.

Parameters:
  out_events -- caller-supplied array that receives the collected 3-byte records back to back, packed from the front with no gaps; the only caller passes a 12-byte (four-record) stack buffer, and nothing here checks that bound.

Returns:
  The number of 3-byte records written to out_events; 0 when no defeated unit carries an event record. fdps_run_death_scripts does nothing at all when handed 0.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the AIL set; the loop bound is the game's unit-count global DAT_00060150, the per-unit fetch is fdps_get_unit_record, and its only caller is game code]

Rebuild note:
Three things a rebuild gets wrong by writing the obvious C. (1) The collect must run before fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, never after: that routine stores 1 into record+0x05 for every unit at zero HP, setting the retired bit this function's first test rejects, so the natural-reading order -- play the deaths, then settle what they owed -- silently returns 0 and every scripted chapter event and battle-end verdict owed for those kills is lost. The caller's order at 00013db1 / 00013dc1 is collect, repaint, then mark dead. (2) This and fdps_collect_death_scripts differ only in the +0x31 test, so folding them into one shared helper, or copying the sibling's "opcode != 0xff" condition here, makes this path hand out the item and gold rewards it deliberately drops -- and because fdps_run_death_scripts *returns* instead of skipping when a reward record's player-side guard fails, and the unit index this call site gives it is a stale melee target, letting one through also abandons every record behind it, including the opcodes that end the battle. (3) There is no capacity check: one 3-byte record is written per matching unit into a caller buffer that holds four, so the buffer must stay at least as large as the original's rather than the routine be trusted to stop.

=== 00027595 [EOL]
Watcom 16-byte alignment padding (lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx)

=== 000275a0 [PLATE]
Restores magic points to one battle unit: adds a slightly randomised fraction of the requested amount to the unit's current MP, clamps the result to the unit's maximum MP, and hands back the amount it rolled rather than the amount it actually applied.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and zero-extends the record's two 16-bit MP fields, current MP at +0x44 and maximum MP at +0x46. Splits the restore in two: a fixed part, amount * 9 / 10, and a random part, (rand() % 100) * amount / 1000, so the total lands between 90% and just under 100% of amount. Adds both to current MP; if the sum exceeds maximum MP it is replaced by maximum MP. Re-reads the +0x44 field, subtracts it from the clamped result to get the gain actually applied, and stores that gain in a stack local it never reads again. Stores the clamped result back into the +0x44 field as a 16-bit word, then returns the fixed part plus the random part. Nothing else in the record is touched and no experience is credited, which is what separates it from its HP twin fdps_unit_apply_heal, whose roll formula is otherwise identical.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array reached through fdps_get_unit_record; no bounds check. fdps_battle_advance_turn passes the fixed indices 4 and 8 and its loop index over every unit holding item 0xb3; fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets passes a target id out of the target list it was given.
  amount -- nominal MP to restore, in MP points. fdps_battle_advance_turn passes the constant 15 at all three of its call sites; fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets passes the signed word at offset 0x0e of the item record, the item's use_amount.

Returns:
  The restore the routine rolled, amount * 9 / 10 + (rand() % 100) * amount / 1000. This is the value before the clamp against maximum MP, so it overstates the gain whenever the unit was already near full MP. All four call sites -- 0001e6d9, 0001e763 and 0001e7f8 in fdps_battle_advance_turn, 00026a3a in fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets -- store the return value and pass it straight to fdps_show_number_indicator with glyph base 0xd, so the rolled value is exactly the number the player sees float over the unit. The three turn-based sites refuse to call at all when current MP already equals maximum MP; the item site guards only against a maximum MP of 0, sending those targets to fdps_show_miss_indicator instead.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image; called only by game code and its only non-CRT callee is fdps_get_unit_record]

Rebuild note:
The routine computes the MP it actually applied (clamped result minus the old +0x44 value) at 0002763b and then throws it away, returning the unclamped amount*9/10 + (rand()%100)*amount/1000 instead. The discarded delta is not a harmless dead store: every call site feeds the return value to fdps_show_number_indicator, so the figure the player sees is the roll and not the gain. Writing the obvious C -- returning the real gain, which the HP twin fdps_unit_apply_heal also declines to do -- makes the CureMP popup show a smaller number than the original whenever the target was near full MP, and show 0 where the original shows the full roll when an effect-0x0c item is used on a unit already at full MP, a case fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets does not filter out. Keep the dead local and return the pre-clamp amount.

=== 000278e0 [PLATE]
Frame-paced presentation and input-wait loop for the spell-list window: once per game tick it repaints the caster's spell page, its scroll arrows and his animated sprite over a live background, presents the result to VGA memory, and returns the first input code the keyboard poller reports as a real key.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_unit_collect_known_spells(unit_index, <stack buffer>) once on entry and keeps only the returned spell count, which is what decides whether the down arrow is drawn. It then loops on fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat: a code <= 0x7f leaves the loop and becomes the result, anything above it is the poller's no-key sentinel and means another frame is due. The frame is skipped entirely unless the live tick at DAT_00069d64 differs from the tick of the last drawn frame latched in DAT_00064390.

Per frame: fdps_cycle_ui_palette advances the UI palette; the blink phase is (DAT_00064390 / 8) & 1, taken from the latch, which at this point still holds the previous frame's tick. fdps_blit_rect restores the 0x97 x 0x95 panel background from panel_src into window_buf + 0x3b58 (column 152, row 47) and fdps_draw_spell_list_page redraws the eight rows over it. fdps_blit_command_sprite then paints Command.cel sprite blink + 0x44 at window_buf + 0x3e1c (column 220, row 49) when list_top is non-zero, and sprite blink + 0x46 at window_buf + 0xef9c (column 220, row 191) when list_top + 8 is below the spell count -- the up and down scroll arrows, each alternating between two sprites every 8 ticks.

It allocates a 0x15180-byte scene buffer and a 0xfa00-byte 320x200 frame buffer. With the mode flag DAT_00060070 clear it composites the live scrolling map into the scene buffer with fdps_draw_scene_layers, zeroes the frame and blits the 0x138 x 0xc0 view window (source stride 0x168) into frame + 0x504 (column 4, row 4); with the flag set it copies the saved 320x200 page at DAT_00063fb4 into the frame instead, after blitting that same page into the scene buffer, which is freed without ever being read. The scene buffer is freed on both paths.

The walk-cycle frame index is (DAT_00064390 % 16) / 4 with 3 folded back to 1, giving the 0, 1, 2, 1 cycle; the clamp to 0 that follows cannot fire for a non-negative tick. A 0x240-byte 24x24 scratch buffer receives cel sprite 3 of the sheet at DAT_000643dc as its backdrop, and fdps_blit_dispatch draws the walk frame over it in blit mode 0. The sprite row is unit_index itself when DAT_00060070 is set, and otherwise byte +2 of the record fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) returns; row * 0x30 + walk * 4 indexes the table based at DAT_00060138 and the dword found there is an offset added back to that same base to form the sprite pointer. fdps_get_unit_record is called on both paths, so its result is fetched and dropped when the flag is set.

The scratch buffer is blitted into window_buf + 0xd21 (column 161, row 10), window_buf + 0xf is blitted into frame + 0xf as a 0x123 x 0xc8 region, the whole 0xfa00-byte frame is copied to the VGA aperture at 0xa0000, the frame and scratch buffers are freed, and DAT_00064390 is set to DAT_00069d64.

Parameters:
  window_buf -- the composed 320-pitch window image the spell page lives in; the list area at +0x3b58, the two arrow positions at +0x3e1c and +0xef9c and the caster's sprite at +0xd21 are rewritten in it every frame, and it is then stamped into the presented screen at column 15
  panel_src -- the pristine 151 x 149 (0x97 x 0x95) spell-panel background, source stride 0x97; blitted over the list area first each frame so the previous frame's rows are erased before the new ones are drawn
  unit_index -- index of the battle unit whose spells are listed; handed to fdps_unit_collect_known_spells, fdps_draw_spell_list_page and fdps_get_unit_record, and used directly as the row in the sprite table at DAT_00060138 when DAT_00060070 is set
  list_top -- index of the spell on the top row of the eight-row page; non-zero draws the up arrow, list_top + 8 below the spell count draws the down arrow, and it is passed to fdps_draw_spell_list_page
  cursor_index -- index of the highlighted spell row, passed straight through to fdps_draw_spell_list_page

Returns:
  The first code fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat hands back that is <= 0x7f, i.e. a BIOS scancode; the caller maps it to cursor movement, confirm or cancel. Codes above 0x7f are the poller's no-key sentinel and are never returned.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; calls only game routines and uses the CRT as a client]

Rebuild note:
Both animation phases -- the arrow blink (DAT_00064390 / 8) & 1 and the walk-cycle frame (DAT_00064390 % 16) / 4 -- are computed from the latch DAT_00064390 while it still holds the tick of the previously drawn frame; the latch is only advanced to DAT_00069d64 on the last line of the frame. Writing the obvious loop, which latches the new tick at the top and derives the phases from the live counter, shifts both animations by one tick.

=== 00027c12 [EOL]

=== 00027c20 [PLATE]
Battle "spell" command: runs one player-controlled unit's whole cast -- opens the caster's known-spell list over the battle map, walks the player through target selection, and plays the chosen spell out on the targets it settles on.

Algorithm:
Zeroes the spell list's scroll position and cursor row once, then repeats this cycle until a spell is actually cast:
  - fdps_load_status_cel_image builds the status window page. A 0xfa00-byte malloc'd buffer takes a memmove copy of the live VGA screen at 0xa0000, and a second 0x57e3-byte buffer takes a fdps_blit_rect copy of the pristine 0x97 x 0x95 list area at window+0x3b58, which is what fdps_spell_list_select_loop erases each frame's list with.
  - fdps_draw_unit_status_panel and fdps_draw_spell_list_page paint the caster's panel and the first page of its spell list, fdps_get_unit_record caches the caster's record (the byte at record+0x02 is loaded into a local that nothing reads), and nine fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame steps slide the window in.
  - fdps_spell_list_select_loop takes the player's choice, fdps_close_status_window puts the screen back and the three buffers are freed. -1 from that loop is the player backing out of the spell list, and the function returns -1 with the unit not having acted.
  - fdps_unit_collect_known_spells rebuilds the id list and fdps_get_spell_record looks the chosen id up in the MagicDat.dat table: byte +3 is the cast distance (bit 0x10 set means a straight line, the low nibble its length), byte +4 the blast radius, byte +6 the target side. The map cursor mode at 00069cd0 is set to radius + 2, which is how fdps_draw_map_cursor picks the diamond footprint painted round the cursor.
  - distance != 0: fdps_collect_targets_in_range lists what is in reach of the cursor tile (00069cd4 is the cursor's map pixel x and 00069ccc its y, 0x18 = 24 pixels to the tile) and fdps_map_cursor_select_loop, in the mode the spell's target-side byte names, lets the player aim. The hit list is then recomputed about the confirmed tile: distance <= 0x0f takes fdps_collect_targets_in_range again with the blast radius in place of the distance, distance >= 0x10 takes fdps_collect_targets_in_line from the caster's own tile (unit record +0 and +1) for distance - 0x10 tiles and plays "Chess.wav".
  - distance == 0 (the map-wide spells): the radius is read back out of 00069cd0, the cursor drops to mode 1, fdps_collect_targets_in_range gathers every enemy within the radius of the caster's tile, and fdps_map_cursor_select_loop runs as mode 4 -- or as mode 5, which never confirms, when the radius caught nobody.
  - Spell 0x15 (傳送術) then takes a second pick: when the first unit of the hit list is the caster itself the pick is thrown away, otherwise fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 6 asks for a tile that unit may stand on and the answer is left in tiles in the destination globals 0006437c (x) and 00064380 (y), after which fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit walks the cursor back to the caster.
  - On a confirmed cast, 0x0001a4c0 plays the animation and applies the spell (the MP cost comes off in there), fdps_collect_death_scripts, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead and fdps_run_death_scripts settle whatever died, and the experience banked in 00069cec is divided by the caster's level (unit record +0x21, plus 0x1e when the class byte at +7 is above 8, i.e. a promoted class) before 0x0001dd30 awards it.
  - The cursor returns to the caster and the loop ends. Cancelling target selection instead reopens the spell list, still on the same page with the same spell highlighted.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array based at 00069cd8, handed straight down from fdps_battle_action_menu.

Returns:
  1 when the unit cast a spell, -1 when the player backed out of the spell list without acting. No other value is produced; fdps_battle_action_menu marks the unit done for anything that is not -1.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; hash unique in the image, and the sole caller plus every non-CRT callee are game routines]

Rebuild note:
The spell list's scroll position and cursor row are initialised before the retry loop, not inside it, so a cancelled target selection reopens the menu on the same page with the same spell still highlighted; declaring the two locals inside the loop body -- the obvious C -- sends the player back to the top of the list every time. The experience award is an integer division of 00069cec by the caster's level, so a haul smaller than the divisor rounds away to nothing.

=== 0002812d [EOL]
Alignment padding: 3-byte NOP form 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0]) aligning next function to 0x10.

=== 00028130 [PLATE]
Interactive spell-selection loop of the battle spell submenu: redraws the caster's known-spell list and reads keys until the player either confirms a spell the unit can pay for or cancels, handing the choice back through cursor_index.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_unit_collect_known_spells(unit_index, ids) into a 40-byte stack buffer and keeps the count, then fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) for the caster's record. The byte at unit record +2 is loaded into a local that nothing ever reads (the caller at 0x00027c20 does the same). Then it loops without an exit condition:
  - fdps_blit_rect restores the pristine 0x97 x 0x95 (151x149) list area from panel_src into window_buf + 0x3b58, erasing the previous frame's list. 0x3b58 is row 47, column 152 of a 0x140-byte-pitch 320x200 page.
  - 0x000276f0 draws the page of the list that begins at *list_top with row *cursor_index highlighted, into window_buf + 0x3b58 with pitch 0x140.
  - 0x000278e0 runs the animated window redraw and the input poll, and returns a BIOS scancode.
  - 0x48 (up): when *cursor_index is not 0, steps the cursor up one row and pulls *list_top down to it once the cursor has scrolled off the top of the window.
  - 0x50 (down): while *cursor_index is below count-1, steps the cursor down one row and, when *list_top + 8 <= *cursor_index, scrolls to *cursor_index - 7. The visible window is eight rows tall.
  - 0x1c (Enter) or 0x39 (Space): looks the selected id up with fdps_get_spell_record and compares that spell's MP cost (record byte +5) with the caster's current MP (signed word at unit record +0x44). Returns 1 when the MP covers the cost; when it does not, it drops back into the loop with no sound, message or cursor change of any kind.
  - 0x01 (Esc) or 0x53 (Del): returns -1.
  - any other scancode: redraw and poll again.
Those two keys are the only exits. Nothing here spends MP; the deduction is fdps_spell_deduct_mp_cost's job, later in the caller.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the casting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array; the caller passes the unit whose battle turn is running.
  window_buf -- the 320x200, 0x140-pitch status-window page the menu is composed into; the spell list occupies the 151x149 block at +0x3b58.
  panel_src -- 151x149 copy of that block as it looked before the list was drawn over it, taken by the caller with fdps_blit_rect; used to erase the list ahead of every redraw.
  list_top -- in/out. Index of the first list row shown in the eight-row window. The caller initialises it to 0 and keeps it across repeat entries into the menu.
  cursor_index -- in/out. Index of the highlighted row, and the way the choice comes back: on a confirm the caller re-runs fdps_unit_collect_known_spells and reads ids[*cursor_index] to recover the spell id.

Returns:
  1 -- the player confirmed a spell whose MP cost the caster can pay.
  -1 -- the player cancelled with Esc or Del.
  No other value is ever returned.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_unit_collect_known_spells, fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_blit_rect; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx multi-byte NOPs before 000282b0

=== 000282b0 [PLATE]
Sets one bit in a per-unit flag bitfield: resolves a record from the handle and ORs mask[bit_index % 8] into the byte at record + 0x1a + bit_index / 8.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; calls and is called only by game code]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty with zero candidates and the full hash is unique in the image. The only callee is fdps_get_unit_record at 0002d210, and all five call sites are game functions (one already named fdps_title_demo), so a third-party library object could not contain it. It reads the game-owned 8-byte mask table at 00027660 (01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80) and writes a fixed field offset inside a game record; it touches no CRT state, no FPU, no DOS service and no AIL data, and a 99-byte body with a full stack frame is not a linker island or shim.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code, describing the observed effect record[0x1a + n/8] |= 1 << (n % 8); no vendor symbol is involved.

Signature: __cdecl void fdps_set_flag_bit(int handle, int bit_index) — both arguments read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], plain RET with the caller cleaning up; the SAR EDX,0x1f before the divide shows bit_index is signed. === 00028313 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / nop, aligning next function to 0x28320

=== 00028320 [PLATE]
Damages one battle unit with one spell: rolls the spell's hit rate and, when it lands, works out what that spell does to that target and takes it off the target's HP.

Algorithm:
fdps_get_unit_record(target_unit_index) resolves the target's 0x50-byte record, and the class code in its byte +0x20 plus one indexes fdps_get_class_record for the target class's 10-byte PROMAP.DAT record, whose byte +0x09 holds 100 minus that class's magic resistance. fdps_get_spell_record(spell_id) then supplies the 7-byte MAGICDAT.DAT record, and the signed word at its +0x00 -- the spell's power -- selects the damage formula:
  - power >= 0: a flat magic figure. damage = power * (100 - target class magic resistance) / 100. Neither the caster's stats nor the target's defense enters it, so the same spell hits for the same amount whoever casts it.
  - power < 0: power is the negative of an attack multiplier in percent, -250 meaning 2.50x. fdps_get_unit_record(caster_unit_index) supplies the caster's derived attack word at +0x48, and damage = attack * -power / 100 minus the target's derived defense word at +0x4a, floored at 0. Those two words are the ones fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats writes.
Byte +0x02 of the spell record is the hit rate in percent. rand() % 100 is drawn and compared against it; a draw that is not below the rate returns 0 with the target untouched. On a draw that lands, spell ids 0x0a (裂地術) and 0x0b (封神裂震), the two ground-shaking spells, also return 0 when fdps_unit_is_flying says the target travels above the terrain. Every other case hands the figure to fdps_unit_apply_damage(target_unit_index, damage), which rolls the final 90.0%-99.9% of it into the target's HP word and credits the battle experience.

Parameters:
  caster_unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8. Read only on the power < 0 path, and only for the attack word at +0x48. FUN_0001a4c0 and FUN_000288f0 both pass the unit that is casting.
  target_unit_index -- index of the unit being hit, in the same array. Both callers pass one entry of their target id list.
  spell_id -- MAGICDAT.DAT record index, 0..0x27; the spell being cast. 0x0a and 0x0b additionally select the flying-target immunity.

Returns:
  The damage fdps_unit_apply_damage rolled, or 0 -- 0 covering all three of a failed hit roll, a flying target under spell 0x0a/0x0b, and a computed damage floored at 0. FUN_000288f0 floats a non-zero return over the target as the damage number through fdps_show_number_indicator and paints fdps_show_miss_indicator on 0. FUN_0001a4c0 takes the target's HP word +0x40 before the call and puts that old value back afterwards, keeping only the two endpoints, so its combat animation can interpolate the drop frame by frame -- the HP write this function makes through fdps_unit_apply_damage is real and has to happen here for that to work.

Pool: fdps  [game logic over the unit, class and spell records with a literal 0x64 percent divisor; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
rand() is drawn before the flying-target test, so a target that is immune to spell 0x0a or 0x0b still consumes one value from the PRNG. Hoisting that test into a guard clause at the top of the function -- the obvious shape, since it is an immunity -- leaves the draw untaken and shifts every later damage roll of the battle.

=== 00028453 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / nop, aligning next function to 0x28460

=== 00028460 [PLATE]
Applies one damaging effect to a battle unit's HP and credits the experience the party earns for it.

Algorithm:
Resolves the target through fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its current HP (word +0x40) and
maximum HP (word +0x42). Rolls the damage actually dealt as base_damage * 9 / 10 plus
(rand() % 100) * base_damage / 1000, each term truncated on its own, so the roll lands between 90.0%
and 99.9% of base_damage. Subtracts the roll from current HP, clamps the result at 0, and stores it
back into word +0x40.
When the target is enemy-side (byte +0x6 == 0) it also credits experience. fdps_get_enemy_record is
called with the target's class byte +0x7 biased down by 0x3c, and byte +0x9 of that EnemyDat.dat
record -- the enemy's base experience value -- is multiplied by the target's level (byte +0x21). A
target still standing after the hit (clamped HP non-zero) has that award prorated by
damage / maximum HP; a target just killed keeps the whole of it. The award is added into the pending
battle-experience accumulator at 00069cec, the same counter fdps_unit_apply_heal adds to and
0x0001dd30 clamps to 0x63 before handing it to the unit that acted.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the target in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; used only as
    the argument to fdps_get_unit_record. Callers read it out of a target id list.
  base_damage -- nominal damage of the item, spell or skill effect before the roll.
    fdps_apply_damage_to_targets and 0x000262a0 pass the effect's damage figure; 0x00028320 passes
    the magnitude it computed from the effect record.

Returns:
  The rolled damage. All three callers hand it to 0x0001f510, which floats it over the target as the
  damage number. It is the amount rolled, not the HP the unit actually lost, so an overkill reports
  more than the target had left.

Pool: fdps  [game data structures and game rules; no fid hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The value returned is the damage rolled, not the HP the unit actually lost: the clamp at 0 happens to the stored HP only, and the callers float the returned figure over the target. Writing the obvious 'return hp_before - hp_after' changes every overkill's on-screen damage number. The roll itself is also never the full nominal figure -- base*9/10 + (rand()%100)*base/1000 tops out at 99.9% of base_damage and each division truncates separately, so folding it into one expression such as base*(900 + rand()%100)/1000 gives different numbers.

=== 00028561 [EOL]
15 bytes alignment filler, one cdecl 2-arg wrapper function at 00028570 (65 bytes, ends RET at 000285b0), then 15 bytes filler to 000285c0

=== 00028570 [PLATE]
Heals one battle unit by the power value of a spell record.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_spell_record(spell_id) for the 7-byte MagicDat.dat record, sign-extends the signed 16-bit power field at record+0x00 (the spell's damage-or-heal amount; it is signed because the eight special attacks store an attack-power multiplier there as a negative percentage), and calls fdps_unit_apply_heal(unit_index, power). That routine rolls the heal as power*9/10 + (rand()%100)*power/1000, adds it to the unit record's current HP at +0x40, clamps the total to the maximum at +0x42, and -- only when the record's portrait id byte +0x7 is below 0x3c, i.e. a roster character rather than an EnemyDat entry -- credits (effective level * 25 * HP actually restored) / maximum HP into the pending battle-experience accumulator DAT_00069cec. Its return value is passed back unchanged. Nothing else happens here: no hit-rate roll against the record's +0x02 chance byte, no MP deduction of the +0x05 cost (that is the sibling fdps_spell_deduct_mp_cost), and no test of the +0x06 target field, so a spell whose power is negative would subtract HP rather than add it.

Nothing in the image reaches this entry: no call, no data word and no other reference. The two live heal paths bypass it -- fdps_cast_spell_on_targets calls fdps_unit_apply_heal on each target itself, and fdps_apply_heal_to_targets does the same for item effects -- so this is an unused packaged form of that step, unlike its counterpart fdps_spell_damage_unit, which has two callers.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at the global 0x00069cd8; forwarded unchanged to fdps_unit_apply_heal, which resolves it through fdps_get_unit_record. Not bounds-checked anywhere on the path.
  spell_id -- MagicDat.dat record index, 0..0x27; selects the record whose power field is read and is not used for anything else.

Returns:
  int -- what fdps_unit_apply_heal returns: the heal it rolled, power*9/10 + (rand()%100)*power/1000, before the clamp. This is not the HP actually restored, which is smaller whenever the clamp at maximum HP bites.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in any library; both callees are game code over game globals]

Rebuild note:
The power field at spell record +0x00 is a signed 16-bit value and eight spells store it negative (an attack-power multiplier percentage, see assets/tables/spells.md); the body sign-extends it with MOVSX and passes it through with no sign test, so writing the field as unsigned short/uint16 in C -- the obvious choice for a byte-packed table -- turns a -250 into 65286 and heals for tens of thousands of HP instead of behaving as the original does.

=== 000285b1 [EOL]
Watcom alignment filler after the RET, up to the next function at 000285c0: same three multi-byte LEA NOP forms

=== 000285c0 [PLATE]
Deducts a spell's MP cost from the caster's current MP.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_spell_record(spell_id) for the 7-byte MAGICDAT.DAT record and fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) for the caster's 0x50-byte record in the array based at the global 0x00069cd8. Sign-extends the caster's current MP out of the signed 16-bit field at record+0x44, subtracts the record's MP cost byte at spell+0x05 (read unsigned) from it, and stores the low 16 bits back into record+0x44. That is the whole body: there is no test that the caster can afford the cost, no floor at zero, and no reference to the maximum MP at record+0x46, so a cost larger than the current MP leaves the field negative.

The one caller, FUN_0001a4c0, runs this once after the action's animation loop has finished and does so for every action it animates, not only for spells; a plain attack costs nothing because its MAGICDAT record carries a zero cost byte.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at the global 0x00069cd8, identifying the unit that just acted. Forwarded unchanged to fdps_get_unit_record, which bounds-checks nothing.
  spell_id -- MAGICDAT.DAT record index, 0..0x27, the action just performed. Forwarded unchanged to fdps_get_spell_record and used only to reach the cost byte at record+0x05.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game-only fdps_get_spell_record and fdps_get_unit_record and mutates the game's unit record array; no Function ID hit in either library set]

=== 0002860f [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP aligning next function entry to 0x28610.

=== 00028610 [PLATE]
Plays spell 11 (封神裂震)'s full-screen Mag11.saf animation, then hands the screen back to the battle map through a white flash.

Algorithm:
fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", "Mag11.saf") loads the animation and malloc gives a 0x16480-byte page -- a 368x248 8bpp surface, 48 pixels wider and taller than the 320x200 screen, so a frame may overhang the visible window without being clipped. A 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request is built on the stack over that page: pitch 0x170 (368) at +0x04, height 0xf8 (248) at +0x08, x = y = 0x18 (24) at +0x0c/+0x10, the SAF image at +0x14, blit mode 9 at +0x20 -- fdps_rle_blit_translucent -- and at +0x1c a three-dword blend descriptor holding the shade-ramp table DAT_000653f0, the blend level, and the inverse colour cube DAT_000643f0. The three-dword playback cursor is set up by hand -- cursor[2] takes the SAF image at 00028683 -- and fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 1) then zeroes the frame index and the dwell accumulator. A second malloc of 0xfa00 takes a memmove snapshot of the mode 13h screen at 0xa0000, the picture the spell was cast over.

Fade-in, 31 ticks, counter i running 0x1f down to 1: the blend level is i / 2, stepping 15 down to 0, and since fdps_rle_blit_translucent reads level 0 as an opaque source and level 16 as an invisible one, the animation comes up out of the frozen screen. Each tick copies the 320x200 snapshot into the page's visible window at page+0x2298 (24 * 368 + 24) with fdps_blit_rect, takes the current frame number from cursor[0] into request+0x18, draws it with fdps_draw_composite_sprite, and advances the cursor with fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0), discarding the result -- so the clip wraps rather than stopping when it reaches its end. It then spins on port 0x3da until vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, blits the page's 320x200 window to 0xa0000, and spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes. The snapshot buffer is freed at the end of the phase.

Main phase, running until fdps_saf_advance_tick reports the clip has ended: the same tick, except that memset clears the whole 0x16480-byte page to 0 first, so the rest of the animation plays on black instead of over the frozen screen, and the return of fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0) is kept as the loop's exit condition. Mode 0 wraps the frame index back to 0 and returns 1 once the last frame has been held, so this phase runs from wherever the fade-in left the cursor to the end of the clip, exactly once.

Clip timing: Mag11.saf holds 22 frames and every one of them dwells for a single tick, so the 31-tick fade-in outlasts it. The fade-in shows frames 0 through 21 on its first 22 ticks, wraps, and shows frames 0 through 8 again on the remaining 9, leaving the cursor on frame 9; the main phase then runs frames 9 through 21, 13 ticks. The presentation is 44 ticks long and the clip is played through exactly twice, with the seam between the two passes falling inside the fade-in rather than at the phase boundary.

The flag argument to fdps_draw_composite_sprite is 0 in both phases, and that callee only reaches fdps_sfx_play when the flag is non-zero (000142ac), so neither of the two sound effects embedded in Mag11.saf -- frame 0 fires sound 0 and frame 15 fires sound 1 -- is ever played. The audio for this spell comes from the caller, which starts EarQu.wav itself.

Exit: the SAF image and the page are freed. fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, 0x3f, 0x3f, 0x3f) re-uploads the game palette with the maximum per-channel bias, which clamps every DAC entry to white, and memset blanks the 0xfa00-byte frame buffer at 0xa0000. Six steps then run, i = 5 down to 0: fdps_set_palette_range with bias i * 10 -- 50, 40, 30, 20, 10, 0 -- each followed by fdps_render_view_frame, which repaints and presents the live battle view. The screen therefore whites out and fades back into the map at its true palette over six frames; the opening 0x3f bias is not part of that arithmetic progression.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [references the game's own strings, data tables and helpers: it calls fdps_vfs_load_entry, fdps_saf_advance_tick, fdps_draw_composite_sprite, fdps_blit_rect, fdps_set_palette_range and fdps_render_view_frame, which a compiled library object could not, and Function ID matched nothing in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set]

Rebuild note:
The dword both frame loops compare against DAT_00069d64 is never initialised: on the first tick of the fade-in it holds stack garbage, so that wait falls straight through and the frame is presented without waiting a tick. Seeding it with 0 or with the current value of the counter -- the obvious C -- costs an extra tick there and lengthens the fade-in. DAT_00069d64 is written only by the timer interrupt, so it also has to be declared volatile, or wcc386 loads it once into a register and neither spin ever ends.

The fade-in's 31 ticks against Mag11.saf's 22 are also not to be reconciled. The cursor is deliberately not reset between the two phases, so the main phase picks the clip up mid-way at frame 9; resetting it, or shortening the fade-in to the clip's length, or letting the fade-in stop at the end of the clip, each changes what the player sees.

=== 000288e4 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs between FUN_00028610 and FUN_000288f0.

=== 000288f0 [PLATE]
Applies one spell to a list of battle-map targets and plays that spell's presentation over the map, instead of on the full-screen combat screen: MP is deducted from the caster, the spell's Emg animation runs on every target's map cell, and the spell's actual effect -- damage, healing, a status ailment, a buff, a teleport -- is resolved target by target.

Algorithm:
Copies the 12-byte buff-indicator sprite table at 00027668 onto the stack as three 4-byte groups, one per buff slot, and clears the map-cursor mode global DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so no cursor is drawn while the spell plays. fdps_play_spell_palette_flash(spell_id) flashes the screen in the spell's colour.

It then deducts the cost: the caster's current MP, the signed word at unit-record +0x44, minus the spell record's cost byte at +0x05, written back as a word. That is the same read-modify-write fdps_spell_deduct_mp_cost performs; the sequence is repeated inline here rather than called.

The map animation's name is formatted into a stack buffer as "Emg%02d.saf" with the spell id in decimal -- except for spell 0x0b (封神裂震), which formats spell_id - 1 and so plays Emg10.saf, 裂地術's animation, because MISC.VFS has no EMG11.SAF. Spell 0x0b then plays its own full-screen cutscene through fdps_play_spell_11_cutscene; spell 0x21 (鎮魂之歌) instead loads Emg33-1.saf out of MISC.VFS with fdps_vfs_load_entry, plays it with fdps_saf_play_over_scene and frees it.

Spells 0x0a (裂地術) and 0x0b shake the ground: EarQu.wav is loaded from MISC.VFS and started with fdps_audio_start_wav(buf, 1, -1, -1), then 25 iterations of fdps_render_view_frame run with the scene view origin globals DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0 each offset from their saved values by rand() % 4 - 2 -- a range of -2..+1, not a symmetric jitter -- and both globals are put back to the saved values when the loop ends.

fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units(target_count, target_unit_indices, name) draws that animation on every listed target's cell. The spell is then resolved, dispatching on spell_id:

  0x0e-0x10 and 0x21 -- the healing spells 恢復之光, 治癒之風, 痊癒之泉 and 鎮魂之歌. Each target gets fdps_unit_apply_heal by the spell record's power word at +0x00, and the amount it returns floats over the target through fdps_show_number_indicator with glyph base 0x27.

  0x15 (傳送術) -- fdps_map_cursor_move_to takes the cursor tile globals DAT_0006437c (x) and DAT_00064380 (y) scaled by the 0x18-pixel tile size, those two tile coordinates are written into target 0's record bytes +0x00 and +0x01, and the animation is replayed so it appears at the tile the target arrived on. Only the first target is moved.

  0x16 (神行術) -- clears bit 7 of each target's record byte +0x05, the bit fdps_battle_mark_unit_done sets, so the target may act again this turn.

  0x18 (甦癒術) -- for each target whose ailment bytes at +0x25..+0x27 are not all zero, fdps_queue_status_cured_popup queues the cured mark; then memset clears those three bytes.

  0x11 (封魔咒術) -- fdps_flash_units_in_color(target_count, target_unit_indices, 0x2b) runs twice back to back, then fdps_unit_apply_status_effect(0x11, target) is rolled on each target, with fdps_show_miss_indicator on the targets it fails against.

  0x12 and 0x13 (腐毒術, 麻痺術) -- fdps_unit_apply_status_effect(spell_id, target) per target, MISS on failure.

  0x14 (神之祝福) -- three passes, one per buff slot 0, 1, 2. Each pass rolls fdps_unit_apply_status_effect(slot, target) on every target and, where it lands, floats that slot's four sprites from the stack copy of the 00027668 table over the target with fdps_show_sprite_indicator and calls fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats; fdps_play_indicator_queue plays the pass out before the next slot starts.

  anything else -- fdps_spell_damage_unit(caster_unit_index, target, spell_id) per target. A non-zero result floats over the target with glyph base 0, and for spell 0x0d (鬼動死靈陣) fdps_unit_inflict_random_ailments is rolled on that target as well; a zero result shows MISS instead.

Every path converges on a final fdps_play_indicator_queue, sets DAT_00069cd0 to 1 so the plain map cursor is drawn again, and frees the EarQu.wav buffer if one was loaded.

The two callers both reach it with the same four arguments. fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell calls it directly when the battle-animation option byte DAT_00060010 is not 1, and otherwise goes through FUN_0001a4c0, which forwards to this function anyway for spell ids 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0e-0x16, 0x18 and 0x21 -- the spells that have no full-screen presentation of their own.

Parameters:
  caster_unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit array at DAT_00069cd8 of the unit casting the spell. Its MP pays the cost and it is the attacker fdps_spell_damage_unit scores the damage from. Both callers pass their own unit index straight through.
  spell_id -- MagicDat.dat spell id, 0x00..0x27; selects the record fdps_get_spell_record returns, the Emg%02d.saf animation and the branch that resolves the effect. In practice only 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0d-0x16, 0x18 and 0x21 reach here.
  target_count -- how many entries of target_unit_indices are valid; the bound of every per-target loop, and the unit count handed to fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units and fdps_flash_units_in_color.
  target_unit_indices -- caller-owned byte array of unit indices, one per target, built by fdps_collect_targets_in_range. Each byte is widened to a full index for fdps_get_unit_record and the per-target callees.

Returns:
  Nothing. Every branch falls into the single epilogue at 00028ed6; EAX at the RET is whatever free left there and neither caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [game strings and game call graph; no Function ID hit in either set]

Rebuild note:
Spell 0x0b's animation name is built from spell_id - 1 on purpose: it shares 裂地術's Emg10.saf because MISC.VFS holds no EMG11.SAF. Writing the obvious sprintf(name, "Emg%02d.saf", spell_id) for every spell -- or "fixing" the -1 as an off-by-one -- makes 封神裂震 ask for Emg11.saf, and fdps_vfs_load_entry ends the process when the entry is not in the archive.

=== 00028edd [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_00028ee0 to 4 bytes.

=== 00028ee0 [PLATE]
Inflicts the status ailments that ride on 鬼動死靈陣 (spell id 0x0d) onto one battle unit: each of the unit's three ailment slots is rolled independently at a flat 20% chance.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) once to resolve the unit's 0x50-byte record, then loops i from 0 to 2 over the three ailment timer bytes at record offsets 0x25 (腐毒術), 0x26 (麻痺術) and 0x27 (封魔咒術). Each pass calls the CRT rand() and takes the result modulo 100; when the remainder is below 0x14 -- the flat 20% chance -- it calls fdps_unit_is_ailment_immune(unit_index), and only when that reports the unit is not immune it calls rand() a second time and writes rand() % 2 + 2 into the byte at record + 0x25 + i, i.e. an ailment duration of 2 or 3, the same duration formula fdps_unit_apply_status_effect writes. The immunity test sits inside the loop and is reached only after the chance roll has already succeeded, so the first rand() is drawn three times per call whatever the unit is. Unlike fdps_unit_apply_status_effect, which lands one named effect, this routine consults no hit rate -- the 20% is a hard-coded literal, not a MAGICDAT.DAT lookup; it does not test whether a slot already holds an ailment, so an existing ailment is overwritten and its duration refreshed; and it touches no global at all, so nothing is credited to the pending battle experience at DAT_00069cec that fdps_unit_apply_status_effect adds to. Ailments landed this way therefore earn the party no experience.

Both callers reach it only for spell id 0x0d and only after that spell landed: fdps_cast_spell_on_targets tests spell_id == 0xd at 00028e7c on the branch where fdps_spell_damage_unit returned non-zero, and fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets tests spell_id == 0xd at 0001ae89 together with its own hit flag.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, in 0 .. unit count at 0x00060150 - 1. The callers pass one entry of the target id byte array they are iterating. Not range-checked.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is not set on the exit path and neither caller looks at it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls fdps_get_unit_record and writes a game record field]

Rebuild note:
The immunity test must stay inside the loop and stay second in the &&. It depends only on unit_index and on record fields this loop never writes, so it is loop-invariant and reads as an obvious hoist, but hoisting it -- or writing the condition as !immune && rand() % 100 < 20 -- skips rand() calls the original makes and desynchronises the shared RNG stream. The absent already-afflicted check is likewise load-bearing: the sibling has one and this does not, so refreshing an ailment already on the unit is the original behaviour.

=== 00028f64 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs between FUN_00028ee0 and FUN_00028f70.

=== 00028f70 [PLATE]
Applies one status effect to a battle unit, rolling the effect's hit rate and crediting the experience the party earns when it lands.

Algorithm:
Resolves the target's 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index), then maps effect_id onto one of the six status-effect timer bytes of that record: 0x11 (封魔咒術) selects +0x27, 0x12 (腐毒術) selects +0x25, 0x13 (麻痺術) selects +0x26, and any other id selects +(0x22 + effect_id) and rewrites the id to 0x14 -- the only caller passes 0, 1 or 2 there, the three 神之祝福 buff slots at +0x22, +0x23 and +0x24 that fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats reads as a 1.15x attack multiplier, a 1.15x defence multiplier and a flat +15. fdps_get_spell_record(effect_id) then supplies the effect's hit rate in byte +2 of its MAGICDAT.DAT record, and rand() % 100 is compared against it. The effect lands only when that roll passes, when the chosen timer byte is still 0, and -- for ids 0x11 through 0x13 only -- when fdps_unit_is_ailment_immune(unit_index) reports the unit is not immune; the 神之祝福 slots skip the immunity test. Landing writes rand() % 2 + 2 into the timer byte, so every effect runs for two or three turns, sets the result to 1, and adds ten times the target's level (record byte +0x21) to the pending battle experience at DAT_00069cec, the same accumulator fdps_unit_apply_damage and fdps_unit_apply_heal credit and FUN_0001dd30 later clamps to 99 before awarding it.

Parameters:
  effect_id -- selects the status effect. 0x11, 0x12 and 0x13 are the spell ids of the three ailment spells and double as the MAGICDAT.DAT index of the hit-rate lookup; 0, 1 and 2 are the three 神之祝福 buff slots, whose hit rate always comes from spell 0x14 instead. FUN_000288f0 is the only caller and passes nothing else.
  unit_index -- index of the target unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array based at 00069cd8, taken from the caller's array of target id bytes. Not range-checked.

Returns:
  1 -- the timer byte was written and the effect is now running on the unit.
  0 -- the hit-rate roll failed, the unit already carries this effect, or the unit is immune. FUN_000288f0 draws the miss indicator through fdps_show_miss_indicator on 0.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls fdps_get_unit_record and writes a game global]

Rebuild note:
effect_id is a spell id only on the 0x11-0x13 paths; for the 神之祝福 slots it arrives as a 0-2 index and the body overwrites it with 0x14 before calling fdps_get_spell_record. Writing the obvious fdps_get_spell_record(effect_id) reads spells 0, 1 and 2 (業火 / 狂暴巨燄 / 烈獄之火, hit rate 95) instead of 神之祝福's 100 and makes the blessing miss one time in twenty. The ailment offset table is not sequential either: 0x11 maps to +0x27, not to +0x25.

=== 00029076 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4), aligning FUN_00029080 to 16.

=== 00029080 [PLATE]
Reports whether one battle unit is immune to the three status ailments, so the code that inflicts them can skip it.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads two bytes out of the 0x50-byte record: the class code at +0x20 and the portrait/template id at +0x7. Returns 1 when the class code is 0x19 (機兵), 0x21-0x22 (守護獸, 將軍) or 0x24-0x26 (？？, 惡靈, 活尸), or when the template id falls in 0x3c-0x44; template ids of 0x3c and up index ENEMYDAT.DAT as id - 0x3c, so that range is the first nine enemy records. Anything else returns 0. The two class ranges are not contiguous: 0x23 (傭兵) sits between them and is not immune, and 0x1a (魔神) is below the first range and is not immune either.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; the callers pass the index of the unit that is about to be afflicted.

Returns:
  1 when the unit cannot be given a status ailment, 0 when it can. All three callers use it as a gate on a zero result: FUN_00019f80 writes the poison byte at record+0x25 for weapon effect 4 and the paralysis byte at +0x26 for weapon effect 1 only when this returns 0; FUN_00028f70 applies the same gate before writing any of the ailment bytes for spells 0x11-0x13 (封魔咒術 -> +0x27, 腐毒術 -> +0x25, 麻痺術 -> +0x26); FUN_00028ee0 checks it before seeding all three bytes at +0x25..+0x27.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record and compares hard-coded ids at fixed offsets of the game's unit record; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The immune class set has a deliberate hole and a rewrite that tidies it away changes the game: the code tests +0x20 == 0x19, then 0x21-0x22, then 0x24-0x26, so class 0x23 (傭兵) is NOT immune even though it sits between the two ranges. Writing the obvious `c >= 0x21 && c <= 0x26` makes mercenaries immune to poison, paralysis and 封魔咒術. The second half of the test is on a different field (+0x7 template id, 0x3c-0x44), not on the class, so it cannot be folded into the class comparison either.

=== 000290ff [EOL]
Single-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler between FUN_00029080 and FUN_00029100

=== 00029100 [PLATE]
Flashes the screen in one spell's signature colour, four times, while the spell is being cast.

Algorithm:
Copies three 40-byte colour planes out of read-only data onto the stack -- red from 0x00027674, green from 0x0002769c, blue from 0x000276c4 -- one entry per spell id 0x00-0x27. Then loops four times. Each pass selects VGA DAC entry 0 by writing 0 to port 0x3c8 through outp, writes red[spell_id], green[spell_id] and blue[spell_id] to port 0x3c9, and calls fdps_render_view_frame to paint and present one frame with that palette in force; it then selects DAC entry 0 again, writes (0,0,0), and calls fdps_render_view_frame once more. Eight presented frames in all, alternating the spell's colour with black, so everything drawn in palette index 0 strobes four times at the render loop's frame rate. The stored values are 6-bit VGA DAC levels and follow the spell's element: (63,0,0) red for the fire spells 0x00-0x02, (57,42,25) earth brown for 0x0a-0x0b 裂地術/封神裂震, (0,63,0) green for 0x18 甦癒術, (63,9,0) for 0x20 審判之雷, and full white (63,63,63) for every other spell. DAC entry 0 is left black on return; the routine never puts back whatever colour it held before.

Parameters:
  spell_id -- MAGICDAT.DAT spell table index, 0x00-0x27. Comes straight from the caller at 0x000288f0, which passes the same value to fdps_get_spell_record. Used unchecked as the index into all three colour planes.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; calls the game symbol fdps_render_view_frame, which no compiled vendor object could reference]

Algorithm:
Shifts the argument right by 16 and masks it with 0xff, so bits 16-23 of the packed word -- the red

=== 0002af20 [PLATE]
Packs three colour channels into one 0x00RRGGBB colour word: the constructor counterpart of fdps_get_rgb_red, fdps_get_rgb_green and fdps_get_rgb_blue, which take that word apart again.

Algorithm:
Zero-extends the low byte of r and shifts it left 16, ORs in the low byte of g shifted left 8, ORs in the low byte of b unshifted, spills the word to a stack local and reloads it as the return value. Only the low byte of each argument contributes; anything above bit 7 of a channel is dropped, so the result never has bits above 23 set. There are no globals, no callees and no bounds or range checks.

Nothing in the image calls this function and no data word points at it, so it is unused game code the linker kept because the object defining it is linked whole. The packing it performs is the one fdps_build_palette_tables (0002af60) open-codes inline for each of the 256 palette entries it reads.

Parameters:
  r -- red channel, 0..255, taken from the low byte of the argument slot; lands in bits 16-23.
  g -- green channel, 0..255, low byte only; lands in bits 8-15.
  b -- blue channel, 0..255, low byte only; lands in bits 0-7.

Returns:
  The packed colour word (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b, in the same 0x00RRGGBB layout that fdps_get_rgb_red, fdps_get_rgb_green and fdps_get_rgb_blue decode.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID match in the Watcom 10.0x or ailv3 library sets, and it sits inside one game object's run of colour helpers alongside the three accessors and fdps_build_palette_tables]

=== 0002af54 [EOL]
alignment padding: two 6-byte lea NOP forms, aligns fdps_build_palette_tables at 0002af60

=== 0002af60 [PLATE]
Builds the game's palette lookup tables from a 256-entry VGA palette: packs each entry into a nibble-per-channel RGB word at 000657f0, scales that row by 16 brightness coefficients into 000653f0, and fills a 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index cube at 000643f0.
Pool: fdps  [no library match; game-owned globals and call graph]
Evidence: Called only by fdps_load_global_resources and calls fdps_palette_find_nearest_color plus three local component extractors (0002ae90/0002aec0/0002aef0); writes the game tables 000643f0, 000653f0 and 000657f0 and reads the 18-dword coefficient table at 0002ae40. Function ID finds no match in the Watcom or ail sets and the hash is unique in the image; no CRT or AIL entry point, no driver state, and far too large for a linker artifact.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case describing what the body builds; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 0002af60-0002b1a3, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 to the matching MOV ESP,EBP/POP/RET epilogue; the 12 bytes after it are LEA-form alignment padding before fdps_palette_find_nearest_color at 0002b1b0.
Signature: __cdecl, void fdps_build_palette_tables(uchar *palette) -- the single argument is read from [EBP+0x14], the RET purges nothing, and the calls it makes clean up with ADD ESP,n.
Algorithm:
1. Copies the 18-dword brightness coefficient table at 0002ae40 onto the stack, indexed by shade level.
2. For each of the 256 palette entries: reads the three bytes (r,g,b) of the source palette (6-bit VGA components, scaled by 4 to 8 bits), packs them as r<<16|g<<8|b, then calls the three component extractors. Each result is masked with 0xF0 and repositioned so red lands in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11 and blue in bits 0-3. Row 0 of the ramp table (000653f0) is zeroed and the packed value is stored into row 1 (000657f0 = 000653f0 + 0x400).
3. For levels 2..17, each of the 256 row-1 values is multiplied by the level coefficient and stored at 000653f0[level*256 + index]. Because each channel occupies only the low nibble of its own byte, one multiply scales all three channels without carrying between them.
4. Fills the 16x16x16 inverse lookup cube at 000643f0: for every (r,g,b) triple of 4-bit components (passed as component*4) it calls fdps_palette_find_nearest_color with the source palette and stores the returned index as a byte, written sequentially over 4096 entries.

=== 0002b1b0 [PLATE]
Returns the index of the palette entry closest to a target colour, by minimum squared RGB distance over a 256-entry, 3-bytes-per-entry table.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image; called only by game graphics code]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty and same_hash_in_image is 1, so there is no library byte match. Its only reference is a static call from fdps_build_palette_tables@0002af60, which writes the returned index into the game's 16x16x16 colour lookup table at DAT_000643f0. Nearest-colour matching is not a CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 or Miles AIL service, and 202 bytes of real loop logic cannot be a linker thunk or merged epilogue.
Name: game code, so fdps_ + snake_case describing the algorithm; no vendor symbol claimed or available.
Boundary: 0002b1b0-0002b279, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the call target through the matching MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET; no body holes, and the gap after 0002b27a is defined data with no instructions.
Signature: __cdecl, int (int r, int g, int b, uchar *palette). Arguments are read from [EBP+0x14/0x18/0x1c/0x20], RET takes no immediate, and the caller cleans with ADD ESP,0x10; result in EAX.
Algorithm: best distance seeded with 10000000 and best index with 0x100, then 256 fixed iterations over an advancing byte cursor forming dr = r - pal[0], dg = g - pal[1], db = b - pal[2] and dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db in signed 32-bit arithmetic. The strict less-than test makes the first of several equally close entries win. The palette buffer must therefore hold at least 768 bytes. The palette bytes are zero-extended but the target components are not masked, so the caller is responsible for keeping r/g/b in range; with in-range targets the 0x100 seed can never survive and the result is always 0..255.
