=== 00030830 [PLATE]
Parses an in-memory RIFF/WAVE image and fills a caller-supplied 14-byte packed descriptor with the sample format and the location of the PCM data.

Algorithm:
Checks the four bytes at wav_data for 'R','I','F','F' (0x52/0x49/0x46/0x46) and the four at wav_data+8 for 'W','A','V','E' (0x57/0x41/0x56/0x45); either mismatch returns -1 without touching info_out. Otherwise it sets a cursor to wav_data+0xc, the first chunk header, clears its two chunk pointers and walks the chunk list: each pass compares the cursor's four id bytes against 'fmt ' (0x66/0x6d/0x74/0x20) and against 'data' (0x64/0x61/0x74/0x61), remembering the cursor in the matching slot, and stops as soon as both slots are non-NULL. When neither test has completed the pair it advances the cursor by the chunk's 32-bit payload size at +4 plus the 8-byte chunk header and repeats; there is no end-of-buffer test and no pad-to-even-boundary step. On the break it writes, in this order: byte fmt+0xa (WAVEFORMAT payload+2, the low byte of nChannels) to info_out+0; byte fmt+0x16 (payload+0xe, wBitsPerSample) to info_out+1; dword fmt+0xc (payload+4, nSamplesPerSec) to info_out+2; dword data+4 (the data chunk's payload size) to info_out+6; and data+8 (the address of the PCM bytes) to info_out+0xa. Returns 0. The dwords sit at unaligned offsets 2, 6 and 0xa, so the descriptor is byte-packed, not naturally aligned.

Parameters:
  wav_data -- pointer to a whole .WAV file already read into memory; in practice a MISC.VFS/IconAni.vfs entry such as Levup.wav loaded by the caller. Never NULL-checked.
  info_out -- pointer to a 14-byte packed descriptor the caller owns (FUN_00030a00 passes a stack local): channels (byte), bits per sample (byte), sample rate (dword at +2), PCM byte count (dword at +6), PCM data pointer (dword at +0xa). Written only on success.

Returns:
  0 when both the RIFF/WAVE tags matched and the descriptor was filled; -1 when either tag check failed, in which case info_out is left untouched. The sole caller, FUN_00030a00, discards the value and reads the descriptor's channel byte immediately.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set; sole caller is game code that drives AIL through its public entry points and reads this descriptor at exactly these packed offsets]

Rebuild note:
The chunk walk advances by exactly payload_size + 8 with no RIFF pad-to-even-boundary and no end-of-buffer guard, and it only stops once BOTH 'fmt ' and 'data' have been seen. Writing the correct RIFF loop -- rounding odd chunk sizes up to an even stride, or bounding the walk by the RIFF size and bailing out -- diverges from the original: the original desynchronises on an odd-sized chunk and runs off the end of a WAV that is missing either chunk, where the careful version would stop cleanly.

=== 000309fc [EOL]
Alignment padding: 4-byte Watcom NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0] before FUN_00030a00.

=== 00030a00 [PLATE]
Starts one in-memory .WAV sound playing on the first of the game's eight AIL digital sample voices that is not busy, and hands the caller back the voice it used.

Algorithm:
Returns -1 immediately unless both audio flags are set: the digital-driver-present flag at 00069d71, which fdps_audio_init sets only when AIL_install_DIG_INI succeeded, and the sound-on option flag at 00069d70, which fdps_options_menu toggles with XOR 1 and the save code restores. Then it scans the eight-entry AIL sample handle table at 00069d30 from slot 0 upward, stopping at the first slot whose AIL_sample_status is not 4 (playing); if all eight are playing it returns -1 without touching anything. With a free slot in hand it calls fdps_wav_parse_header on wav_data, filling a 14-byte packed descriptor on its own stack -- channels at +0, bits per sample at +1, sample rate at +2, PCM byte count at +6, PCM data pointer at +0xa -- and turns the (channels, bits) pair into an AIL format code: (1,8) gives 0, (1,16) gives 1, (2,8) gives 2, and anything else, (2,16) included, gives 3, i.e. DIG_F_MONO_8, DIG_F_MONO_16, DIG_F_STEREO_8, DIG_F_STEREO_16. A playback_rate of -1 is replaced here by the descriptor's sample rate. It then configures the voice in this order: AIL_init_sample, AIL_set_sample_address with the descriptor's PCM pointer and byte count, AIL_set_sample_type with the format code and the fixed flags word 2, AIL_set_sample_loop_count, AIL_set_sample_playback_rate, and AIL_start_sample. Volume is set last, after the sound is already running: AIL_set_sample_volume with the caller's volume, or with 0x3c (60) when the caller passed -1. The voice index is the return value.

Parameters:
  wav_data -- pointer to a whole .WAV file image already read into memory, in practice a VFS entry such as Levup.wav. Not NULL-checked and not validated; see the rebuild note.
  loop_count -- passed straight to AIL_set_sample_loop_count. Every caller passes 1, one playthrough.
  playback_rate -- sample rate in Hz to play at, or -1 to use the rate in the .WAV header. Every caller passes -1.
  volume -- AIL sample volume, or -1 to use the game's default of 0x3c (60). Every caller passes -1.

Returns:
  The index 0..7 of the sample voice the sound was started on, which the caller can hand to fdps_audio_sample_is_playing or fdps_audio_stop_sample; -1 when sound is off, when the digital driver is absent, or when all eight voices are already playing.

Pool: fdps  [calls the public Miles AIL entry points and game code; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the AIL set]

Rebuild note:
The return value of fdps_wav_parse_header is discarded. On a buffer that is not RIFF/WAVE the parser leaves the 14-byte descriptor untouched, and this function goes on to hand AIL whatever uninitialised stack bytes are sitting there as the PCM address, length and format. Adding the obvious guard -- return -1 when the parse fails -- makes the rebuild behave differently from the original, so do not add it. The same applies to the format ladder's final else: it is reached by any (channels, bits) pair the first three tests missed, not only by (2,16), and it must stay a plain else rather than becoming an error path.

=== 00030bf0 [PLATE]
Sets the CD background music: records which music track the game wants playing and makes the CD-ROM drive match, stopping playback instead when music is switched off or the caller asks for silence.

Algorithm:
Copies the requested music index into the working slot, and when the music-enabled setting at DAT_00060008 is 0 forces that slot to -1, so a music-off setting discards whatever the caller asked for. Publishes the result in the current-music global DAT_00069d54, which fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll reads to restart the track when it runs out. If that value is -1 it calls fdps_cd_stop_audio and returns; otherwise (the music-enabled setting is retested, and is always non-zero on this path) it calls fdps_cd_play_track with DAT_00069d54 + 1 -- the CD track number is one more than the music index the game uses.

Parameters:
  music_index -- 0-based background-music index, or -1 to stop the music. fdps_title_screen and FUN_0001ba40 pass 1, fdps_run_village_phase passes 2 on entering the village and -1 on leaving it, and FUN_00021650 passes the byte operand of an IconAni script opcode, mapping the operand 0xff to -1.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [game state and game-only call graph; no library match -- calls only fdps_cd_stop_audio and fdps_cd_play_track and drives the game globals DAT_00060008 and DAT_00069d54]

Rebuild note:
When the music-enabled setting DAT_00060008 is 0 this routine does not just skip playing -- it overwrites the current-music global DAT_00069d54 with -1 and calls fdps_cd_stop_audio, discarding the index the caller asked for. Writing the obvious early-out (if (!music_enabled) return;) leaves the previous selection in DAT_00069d54, so the CD keeps playing and fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll goes on restarting the stale track after the player turns music off.

Waits until the disc required by the given chapter is inserted, then starts that chapter's CD audio track.
Pool: fdps  [game strings, game globals, five named game callers]
Evidence: References "%s\\Pack.vfs" and the VFS entry "Pass.Dat", the game path global at 000643e8 and the draw context at 000643c4; writes the current-track global at 00069d54 that fdps_cd_play_track / fdps_cd_stop_audio use. Name: fdps_ + snake_case describing the behaviour; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 00030cc0-00030f31, ends at the epilogue MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET; the 14 bytes after it are Watcom alignment padding before the next function at 00030f40.
Signature: __cdecl void (int chapter, int slot) - both arguments read as dwords from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], bare RET so the caller cleans; confirmed by the assembly, not a guess.

Algorithm:
1. Copy the 60-byte constant table at 000304a0 onto the stack (15 dwords). It is 30 chapter rows of 2 bytes; the row is the chapter, the column is the slot, and the byte is a zero-based CD audio track index (0xff means no track).

3. Loop until the inserted disc is acceptable:
   - Release the keyboard ISR (FUN_00056818) and drain pending input (kbhit / getch).

4. Reinstall the keyboard ISR (fdps_install_keyboard_isr).

Parameters:
  chapter - chapter index; also selects the required disc (>= 18 means disc 2).

Returns:

After the bar-shop arm this function re-tests the chapter number and forces the selection back to 0 for the chapters that have no village. Poll 0x000567b3 and repeat while the selection is non-zero and no abort is pending; on exit free both cached cel handles and clear 0x00060070, 0x00060150 and 0x00069cd8.
6. Save and clear the input-enable byte at 0x00060158, fade out via 0x00030bf0(-1), and unless an abort is pending call the chapter script taken from the per-chapter function pointer table at 0x00060074 indexed by the chapter number. Restore 0x00060158, clear 0x00060131, and call fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track(chapter, 0).

Returns: the menu selection left when the loop exited, 0 on a normal exit and 0 when the abort flag was already set on entry.

=== 00031700 [PLATE]
Collects the item ids one village shop is stocking this chapter into a caller-supplied array, and returns how many there are.

Algorithm:
Walks all twelve bytes of row shop_index of the 12-byte-per-row table pointed to by DAT_00069d80 -- the chapter's "Shop%02d.dat" image that fdps_load_field_chapter_resources loads out of "Field.vfs" and fdps_run_village_phase frees. The row base is DAT_00069d80 + shop_index * 0xc; each byte is read zero-extended. 0xff marks an empty slot and is skipped wherever it appears, including between two stocked entries, so the scan never stops early; every other byte is stored as an int in the next free element of out_item_ids and the write counter is bumped. That counter is the return value. The loop is a fixed twelve iterations with no bounds check on shop_index, and out_item_ids must therefore have room for twelve ints. The shipped SHOP%02d.DAT members are 36 bytes, i.e. exactly three rows: 0 the item shop, 1 the weapon shop, 2 the secret shop.

Parameters:
  shop_index -- which shop's row to read; 0 item shop, 1 weapon shop, 2 secret shop. Comes down unchanged from the second argument of the shop transaction loop at 0x00033b80, which fdps_village_item_menu, fdps_run_weapon_shop and fdps_run_secret_menu set to 0, 1 and 2 respectively.
  out_item_ids -- caller's array, one int per stocked slot, receiving item ids in the item table's numbering (the ids fdps_get_item_record takes). The shop item picker at 0x00032710 passes a twelve-int stack array.

Returns:
  The number of ids written, 0 to 12. 0 means the shop stocks nothing this chapter; the picker at 0x00032710 uses the count to clamp its highlight and scroll window.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its one data reference is the game's shop stock table and its only caller is game menu code]

Rebuild note:
The 0xff byte marks an empty slot, not the end of the row: shipped data such as SHOP01.DAT's weapon row (02 71 FF FF 72 73 FF ...) and SHOP05.DAT's (03 04 FF 1F 20 30 31 65 FF 74 75 83) stock items after empty slots, so the obvious `for (i = 0; i < 12 && row[i] != 0xff; i++)` truncates most shops' stock. The row must also be typed unsigned char: as signed char the 0xff compares as -1, the skip never fires, and empty slots are sold as item id 255.

Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx, aligning next function to 0x31780.

=== 00031780 [PLATE]
Plays the village and shop screen zoom transition: brings a 320x200 picture out of a roughly four-times magnification centred on a chosen screen point up to the normal 1:1 view while the palette brightens out of black, or runs the same nine steps backwards and leaves the screen blank.

Algorithm:
Copies the nine-entry camera-height ramp at 0x00031040 -- {50, 200, 500, 800, 1000, 1200, 1300, 1400, 1500} -- onto the stack, then runs nine steps. zoom_out picks the direction: nonzero makes the step index run 0,1,...,8, zero makes it run 8,7,...,0.
Each step does four things.
  1. Spins on inp(0x3da) until bit 3 of the VGA input status register (vertical retrace) is set, calls fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, bias, bias, bias) with bias = -3 * (8 - step), so the Fde.pal palette held at 0x000643bc is uploaded 24 units dark at step 0 and unbiased at step 8, then spins on 0x3da again until that bit clears.
  2. Works out the blit centre in quarter pixels: (center_x - (center_x - 0x9f) * step / 8) * 4 and (center_y - (center_y - 0x63) * step / 8) * 4, both divisions truncating toward zero. The centre therefore slides from the caller's point at step 0 to the screen centre (159, 99) at step 8.
  3. At step 8 it puts the picture up with a plain memmove of 0xfa00 bytes from src_image to the mode-13h framebuffer at 0xa0000. At every other step it calls fdps_blit_rotated_scaled(0xa0000, src_image, ramp[step], 0.0, cx, cy, 0.0); in that routine camera height 50 magnifies about four times and 1500 is 1:1, so the ramp is a pull-back from a close-up to the full picture.
  4. Waits for the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change before starting the next step.
After the loop, when zoom_out is zero it memsets the 0xfa00-byte framebuffer to palette index 0, and in both directions it ends with fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, 0, 0, 0), leaving the DAC holding the unbiased Fde.pal.

Parameters:
  src_image -- the 320x200 8bpp page holding the picture to show. fdps_village_item_menu, fdps_run_church_screen, fdps_run_bar_shop, fdps_run_weapon_shop and fdps_run_secret_menu pass the offscreen page they have just drawn their background into; fdps_run_village_phase passes the town page.
  center_x -- screen x, 0..319, of the point the magnified view is centred on at step 0. The five shop screens pass 0x9f (the screen centre); fdps_run_village_phase passes the selected signboard entry's x out of the table at 0x00060174.
  center_y -- screen y, 0..199, the same role for the vertical axis. The five shop screens pass 0x63; fdps_run_village_phase passes the entry's y out of the table at 0x0006018c.
  zoom_out -- direction, tested as a byte against 0. Nonzero runs the steps forward, so the view pulls back out of the magnification while the palette brightens out of black; every caller passes 1 when it opens a screen. Zero runs them backwards, so the view zooms into center_x/center_y while the palette darkens, and the framebuffer is cleared at the end; every caller passes 0 as it leaves the screen.

Returns:
  Nothing. The result is left in the mode-13h framebuffer at 0xa0000: the full picture when zoom_out is nonzero, a blank screen when it is zero.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit; called only by the village and shop screens, and it reads the game's Fde.pal handle at 0x000643bc and the timer tick at 0x00069d64]

Rebuild note:
The local this routine compares against DAT_00069d64 is never initialised before the loop, so the first of the nine steps is not tick-paced; giving it the current tick before the loop, which is what writing the loop cleanly leads to, adds a tick to every transition. DAT_00069d64 is written by the timer interrupt, so that spin loop needs a volatile read or an optimising build folds the reload away and hangs.

=== 00031911 [EOL]
Watcom inter-function alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / lea eax,[eax+0]

=== 00031920 [PLATE]
Draws one 320x200 8bpp image into another, scaled about a chosen source point and, when the angle
arguments are non-zero, rotated and tilted into perspective.

Algorithm:
Takes sin and cos of tilt and of rotation through the CRT sin/cos (each result arrives in EDX:EAX as
a double and is stored down to a float local). Sets the projection distance d = 2000 -
camera_height, and derives the clip window from the centre: an x offset must lie in
[-center_x*32, (0x4f8-center_x)*32] and a y offset in [-center_y*32, (0x318-center_y)*32], which is
the source's usable 318x198 area expressed in 1/128-pixel offsets from a centre given in quarter
pixels. Then for each destination row `row` from -99 to 98:
  z = (row * 2000) / (d*cos(tilt) + row*sin(tilt)), truncated toward zero by __CHP;
  u = camera_height - z*sin(tilt), so with tilt 0 every row shares the same scale;
  the per-column source step is (u*32)/d + 32 and the row's leftmost x offset is
  -5088 - (u*5088)/d, 5088 being 159 columns of 32;
  z is then scaled by 32 and the pair (x0, z) rotated by `rotation` into the row's starting offsets
  X = x0*cos + z*sin and Y = -x0*sin + z*cos, with per-column deltas dX = step*cos, dY = -step*sin.
  For each of the 318 columns (-159..158) it writes one byte to *dst++: palette index 0 when X or Y
  falls outside the clip window, otherwise the byte at
  src + (center_y/4)*320 + center_x/4 + 4 + (Y/128)*320 + (X/128), every one of those divisions
  truncating toward zero rather than flooring. After the columns dst is advanced two more bytes, so
  the destination is walked at a 320-byte stride; the last two columns of each row and the bottom
  two rows of a 320x200 destination are never written.

Parameters:
  dst -- destination 8bpp surface walked at a 320-byte stride; only the first 318 bytes of each of
    the first 198 rows are written. FUN_00031780 passes the mode-13h screen at 0xa0000.
  src -- source 8bpp image, 320 bytes per row, of which 318x198 is reachable. FUN_00031780 passes
    the 0xfa00-byte screen image it also memmoves to 0xa0000 at full size.
  camera_height -- projection height, 0..1999. The view covers 500/(2000-camera_height) source
    pixels per destination pixel, so 0 magnifies four times, 1500 is 1:1, and larger values shrink.
    FUN_00031780 reads it out of the nine-entry ramp table at 0x00031040.
  tilt -- perspective tilt angle in radians, handed to sin and cos; it is what makes the source step
    and the row origin vary from row to row. FUN_00031780 passes 0.0.
  center_x -- the source x that lands on the middle destination column, in quarter pixels, 0..0x4f8.
  center_y -- the source y that lands on the middle destination row, in quarter pixels, 0..0x318.
  rotation -- rotation angle in radians about (center_x, center_y), handed to sin and cos.
    FUN_00031780 passes 0.0.

Returns:
  Nothing; the result is the destination buffer.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ailv3.lib set, and the body carries
game-specific screen geometry -- source stride 0x140, rows -99..98, columns -159..158, bounds 0x4f8
and 0x318 -- that no library routine could hold]

Rebuild note:
Every divide in the sampling path is a signed division that truncates toward zero, not a shift: the compiler emitted the SAR/SHL/SBB/SAR idiom for X/128, Y/128 (00031b45-00031b72) and center_x/4, center_y/4 (00031a28-00031a55). Writing X >> 7 instead, which is the obvious thing for a fixed-point sampler, shifts the whole left half of the picture by one source pixel because X is negative for every column left of the centre. Two more things must be copied rather than tidied: the sample base carries an unconditional + 4 bytes (00031a57), so the image is drawn four pixels off its nominal centre and the rightmost columns read into the start of the next source row; and the loops cover 318 columns and 198 rows, not 320x200, leaving the destination's last two columns and bottom two rows untouched.

=== 00031bb2 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d80.. / 8d92.. / 8bc0 nop forms filling to the 16-byte entry of fdps_village_signboard_menu

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game resource strings, game callees, and a game caller]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty with zero candidates and the full hash is unique in the image. Data references are game resources ("CanBan.cel", "MISC.VFS", "Beep.wav") and the callees are the game's own fdps_vfs_load_entry, fdps_cel_blit_sprite, fdps_blit_dispatch, fdps_play_sfx, fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll and FUN_00031f60, with the runtime used only for malloc/memmove/free/inp/outp. Link direction is decisive both ways: the single caller is fdps_run_village_phase, whose own plate names this routine as the signboard menu of the village phase, and FUN_00031f60 - the travel animation - is called from nowhere else, so this function is inside the game's own call graph and no library module references it. Boundary: 00031bc0-00031f58, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 / SUB ESP,0x48 at the entry and the matching MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET at 00031f58; the 7 bytes that follow are LEA EAX,[EAX+0x0] / NOP alignment padding before FUN_00031f60.

This is not a Ghidra frame mis-assignment: SUB ESP,0x48 places the three nine-byte palette ramps at [EBP-0x48], [EBP-0x3c] and [EBP-0x30] (ending at -0x40, -0x34 and -0x28), leaving -0x24 as a distinct dword slot no table overlaps, and the slot is only ever accessed as a dword. The effect is bounded, not a crash - the value is reduced by (v/5)&3 and (v/3)%5 - so the first frame starts on an arbitrary animation cell and palette phase and the tick wait at 00031f22 falls straight through. Initialising this local from DAT_00069D64 before the loop would be the intuitive C and would diverge from the original.

=== 00031f60 [PLATE]
Plays the walk animation that carries the village map's party-member marker from one signboard destination to the next when the signboard menu's cursor moves, swapping the destination name plate as it goes.

Algorithm:
Reads both destinations' screen positions out of the two six-entry coordinate tables at DAT_00060174 (x) and DAT_0006018c (y) -- the tables are exactly six dwords each, since 0x00060174 + 0x18 == 0x0006018c and 0x0006018c + 0x18 == 0x000601a4 -- and picks the marker's facing from the dominant axis of the delta through abs(): when |dx| > |dy| it is 3 (right) if dx > 0 and 1 (left) otherwise, and when |dx| <= |dy| it is 0 (down) if dy > 0 and 2 (up) otherwise. Those are the same direction codes fdps_animate_move_path dispatches on. Six frames then run with i = 0..5, each one:
  1. Resolves the marker sprite as *(int *)(DAT_00060138 + DAT_000601a4 * 0x30 + facing * 0xc) + DAT_00060138. DAT_00060138 is the CEL sprite cache fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group fills; a group is 0x30 bytes of 4-byte stream offsets holding four facings of three walk cells each, and only cell 0 of the chosen facing is ever read, so the marker slides across without cycling its legs. DAT_000601a4 is the cache slot the signboard menu is showing, which that menu cycles over 0..DAT_00064114-1, the party roster member count.
  2. Takes a 0xfa00-byte (320x200) composing page from malloc and copies background over it with memmove.
  3. Interpolates the marker position as x = x_from - (x_from - x_to) * i / 5 and y = y_from - (y_from - y_to) * i / 5, and hands the 24x24 sprite to fdps_blit_dispatch at page + y * 0x140 + x with pitch 0x140 and mode 0 (fdps_blit_rle_passthrough).
  4. Draws sprite 6 of signboard_cel -- the empty name-plate frame -- through fdps_cel_blit_sprite at (3, 174) in mode 0.
  5. Draws one name plate scaled, in blit mode 4 (fdps_rle_blit_scaled), centred inside the 72x24 box at (3, 174): while i < 3 it is from_destination's plate at (6 - i) * 0xc wide by (6 - i) * 4 high, shrinking 72x24 -> 48x16, and once i > 2 it is to_destination's plate at (i + 1) * 0xc by (i * 4 + 4), growing 48x16 -> 72x24. The destination size travels packed as height << 16 | width in the argument fdps_cel_blit_sprite forwards to the kernel, and the corner is x = 3 + (0x48 - width) / 2, y = 0xae + (0x18 - height) / 2. Exactly one plate is drawn per frame; no frame carries both.
  6. Trails the marker with up to two fading afterimages, drawn in mode 9 (fdps_rle_blit_translucent) through the three-dword blend descriptor built on the stack -- shade-ramp base DAT_000653f0, blend level, inverse colour cube DAT_000643f0: the interpolated position of step i-1 at level 8 whenever i > 0, and that of step i-2 at level 0xc only while 1 < i < 5, so the last frame carries a single ghost. A higher level is fainter.
  7. Spins on bit 3 of VGA port 0x3da until it is clear and then until it is set, memmoves the whole page to video memory at 0xa0000, spins until the tick counter at DAT_00069d64 changes, and frees the page.

Parameters:
  background -- the caller's 320x200 8bpp page holding the painted village map; read only, copied afresh under every frame. fdps_village_signboard_menu passes the page it composed the town screen into.
  from_destination -- the destination the marker starts on, 0..5; the menu selection as it stood before the keystroke. Indexes both coordinate tables and, while i < 3, the name-plate sprite of signboard_cel.
  to_destination -- the destination the marker walks to, 0..5; the menu's new selection, already wrapped mod 5 by the caller, or 5 when the secret-shop code has just been completed. Indexes both coordinate tables and, once i > 2, the name-plate sprite.
  signboard_cel -- the "CanBan.cel" sheet fdps_village_signboard_menu loaded out of "MISC.VFS"; sprites 0..5 are the destination name plates and sprite 6 is the empty plate frame.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is not set before the epilogue and the single call site ignores it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls the game's own blit routines]

Rebuild note:
The tick local the frame wait compares against DAT_00069d64 is never initialised before the loop, so the first of the six frames does not wait for a tick at all; declaring it and seeding it from DAT_00069d64, which is the intuitive C, adds a tick to the first frame. The second afterimage is likewise guarded by 1 < i && i < 5 rather than i > 1, so the final frame deliberately shows only one ghost.

=== 000323e0 [PLATE]
Runs the modal selection loop for a village screen's horizontal row of command icons, handing the player's choice back through selected_index.

Algorithm:
Loops until the player confirms or cancels. Each pass first calls fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll to keep the CD background music alive, then takes one keyboard event from fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat and dispatches on the scancode:
  - 0x01 (Esc) or 0x53: writes -1 through selected_index and ends the loop.
  - 0x1c (Enter) or 0x39 (Space): ends the loop, leaving *selected_index as it stands.
  - 0x48 (Up) or 0x4d (Right): *selected_index = (*selected_index + 1) % icon_count, then plays "Beep.wav" through fdps_play_sfx.
  - 0x4b (Left) or 0x50 (Down): *selected_index = (*selected_index + icon_count - 1) % icon_count, then plays "Beep.wav".
  Any other scancode does nothing.
Every pass then calls fdps_menu_draw_command_icons(icon_ids, icon_count, *selected_index) to repaint the row with the current entry highlighted -- including the pass that ends the loop, so the cancel path repaints the row once with -1 (nothing highlighted) before returning.

Parameters:
  icon_ids -- the caller's array of icon ids, one per menu entry, passed straight through to fdps_menu_draw_command_icons; the callers build it as a local int array on their own stack.
  icon_count -- how many entries the row has, 4 to 6 across the five village screens; the modulo divisor that wraps the selection.
  selected_index -- pointer to the caller's selection variable, the loop's only real output: read and written each pass, left at the confirmed entry index or set to -1 on cancel. The callers keep it across calls, so the loop starts on the entry the player left the cursor on.

Returns:
  Always 1, both on confirm and on cancel; the two cases are told apart only by the -1 written through selected_index. All five callers discard the return value.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; called only by named game screens -- fdps_village_item_menu, fdps_run_church_screen, fdps_run_bar_shop, fdps_run_weapon_shop, fdps_run_secret_menu]

Rebuild note:
Cancel and confirm set the loop's done flag and then fall into the redraw, they do not return early. Writing the obvious `*selected_index = -1; return 1;` inside the Esc branch drops the final fdps_menu_draw_command_icons call, so the icon row keeps its old highlight instead of being repainted with none. Keep the redraw at the bottom of the loop body unconditional.

=== 000324c9 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + nop, aligning next function to 0x324d0.

=== 000324d0 [PLATE]
Draws the row of command icons for a village-screen menu straight onto the mode-13h VGA screen, with the entry at selected_index sitting on the highlighted cell frame.

Algorithm:
Computes the strip's left edge as 0x12b - 26 * icon_count, so however many entries there are the row always ends at the same right-hand edge; 26 is the cell pitch in pixels. Then for each entry i in 0..icon_count-1 it forms the destination address 0xa8480 + (0x12b - 26 * icon_count) + 26 * i. 0xa8480 is the mode-13h frame buffer base 0xa0000 plus 320*106, so the strip is painted directly on the visible screen at row 106, not into the 0xfa00-byte offscreen page the surrounding village screens compose their backdrop into. Each cell is two calls to fdps_blit_command_sprite with pitch 0x140 (320) at that one address: first the cell frame -- Command.cel sprite 0x1a when i equals selected_index, sprite 0x1b otherwise (0x1a here is a sprite index and has nothing to do with the 26-pixel pitch that shares its value) -- and then the entry's own icon, Command.cel sprite icon_ids[i], which lands on top because fdps_blit_command_sprite draws through blit mode 0, whose skip op steps over a run without writing it.

Nothing clears the strip before a pass and nothing needs to: both frame sprites cover the whole 25x22 cell opaquely -- decoding COMMAND.CEL shows sprites 0x1a and 0x1b writing all 550 pixels, with no skip op and no stretch op in either stream -- so each pass paints out the icon the previous pass left behind. The 25-pixel-wide sprite inside a 26-pixel cell leaves a one-column seam between neighbouring cells that this routine never touches; it keeps whatever the screen already held there.

After the loop it calls fdps_cycle_ui_palette, which waits for VGA vertical retrace and advances the palette-cycling animation, so one call to this routine is also one displayed frame and it is what paces the caller's input loop.

Parameters:
  icon_ids -- array of icon_count Command.cel sprite indices, one per menu entry, left to right. The callers build it on their own stack; the church screen's is {0x24, 0x12, 0x04, 0x10}.
  icon_count -- number of menu entries, 4 to 6 in the five village screens that reach here. Sets both the loop bound and the strip's left edge.
  selected_index -- index of the entry to highlight, or -1 for none. fdps_menu_command_icon_select_loop passes the menu cursor it is stepping, and writes -1 into it when the player cancels.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set, hash unique in the image; game-specific screen work with the game's own Command.cel blitter, reached only from application code]

Rebuild note:
The destination is hardwired video memory, not a surface the caller chose. Every neighbouring village-screen routine takes a page pointer and composes into the caller's 0xfa00-byte offscreen page -- fdps_village_animate_window_zoom is handed one and pushes the finished result to 0xa0000 itself -- so giving this function the same shape is the natural thing to write and it is wrong. Nothing pushes a page to the screen while fdps_menu_command_icon_select_loop is running, so an icon row composed into the caller's page would never reach the display at all.

=== 00032570 [PLATE]
Plays the open or the close animation of the village screens' window frame, one zoom step per vertical retrace.

Algorithm:
Frees the cached FACE.CEL portrait buffer at DAT_00060120 and clears the pointer, then allocates a 0xfa00-byte (320x200) mode-13h composing page. Nine steps run with i = 0..8, each taking t = closing ? 8 - i : i, so the frame grows on an open and shrinks on a close. Each step copies the caller's page over the composing page with memmove, then derives the window's destination size as width = t * 0x138 / 8 (forced to 4 when that comes out 0) and height = t * 0x4c / 8 (forced to 2 when 0), and its destination corner as x = 0x8c + t * (4 - 0x8c) / 8 and y = 0x50 + t * (0x79 - 0x50) / 8 -- the frame sweeps from a 4x2 sliver at (140,80) out to the full 312x76 window at (4,121) across the bottom of the screen. It draws sprite 0 of the ShopWin.Cel sheet held in DAT_00069d84 through fdps_cel_blit_sprite at that corner with pitch 0x140, handing the packed size height << 16 | width to the scaled blit kernel and 4 as the blit mode, which is fdps_rle_blit_scaled in fdps_blit_dispatch. It then spins on bit 3 of port 0x3DA until the vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, and memmoves the whole 0xfa00-byte page to video memory at 0xa0000. The composing page is freed on the way out; the caller's page is never written.

Parameters:
  screen_page -- the caller's 320x200 8bpp page holding the village screen the window opens over; read only, and copied afresh under every step. Every caller passes the offscreen page it allocated for its own screen.
  closing -- 0 plays the window opening, non-zero plays it closing. Only the low byte of the argument is tested; the village screens pass a literal 0 or 1.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; all twelve callers are village screens and it calls fdps_cel_blit_sprite, which linked library objects cannot reference]

Rebuild note:
The free of DAT_00060120 at the top is not incidental to the animation. That global is the cached FACE.CEL portrait buffer that FUN_000177d0 loads, and fdps_prompt_two_choice and FUN_000203d0 draw the portrait whenever the pointer is non-NULL. Writing this function as a pure window animation and dropping the free leaks the buffer and leaves a stale portrait drawn over the town prompts.

=== 00032702 [EOL]

=== 00032710 [PLATE]
Village shop item picker: lets the player choose which of the shop's stocked items to buy, and hands the caller that item's id.

Algorithm:
Fills a twelve-int stack array with the shop's stock through fdps_shop_collect_stock_items(shop_index) and keeps the count it returns. The highlight DAT_000601ac and the window top DAT_000601a8 are statics that no other function in the program references and that survive between calls, so the picker reopens on the entry picked last time; both are reset to 0 only when the saved highlight is past the end of this shop's stock. Then one pass per timer tick until the player confirms or cancels:
  - fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll keeps the CD track alive, then fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat yields one scancode.
  - 0x01 Esc sets the loop result to -1 (cancel); 0x1c Enter and 0x39 Space set it to 1 (confirm).
  - 0x4d moves the highlight one entry right while it is short of the last entry, 0x4b one left while it is not on the first, 0x50 two entries (one row) down while two more entries remain, 0x48 two up while it is not in the top row. The window top follows in steps of two, forward when the highlight reaches top + 6 and back when it drops below top. Every accepted move plays fdps_play_sfx("Beep.wav").
  - The frame is rebuilt from scratch each pass: malloc a 0x5ca0-byte page, 312x76 at pitch 0x138, and lay sprite 0 of ShopWin.Cel (DAT_00069d84) into it with fdps_cel_blit_sprite. Six cells are visible, two columns by three rows: cell i sits at x = 0x10 + 0x91 * (i & 1), y = 0x0b + 0x13 * (i / 2) and shows entry top + i, skipped when that is past the stock count. The highlighted cell first gets sprite 1 of the selection-bar sheet DAT_000643c0 at (x - 5, y - 1); each cell is then drawn by fdps_shop_draw_item_entry into the page at y * 0x138 + x.
  - The scroll arrows blink on (tick / 5) & 1: the up arrow, Command.cel sprites 0x44/0x45 at page offset 0x6ae, is drawn only when the window top is not 0, and the down arrow, sprites 0x46/0x47 at page offset 0x4e96, only while top + 6 is still short of the stock count; both go through fdps_blit_command_sprite.
  - fdps_cycle_ui_palette advances the UI colour animation, fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x130 x 0x43 (304x67) window at page offset 0x3ad onto the mode-13h screen at 0xa9c48, i.e. x 8, y 125, and the pass ends spinning on the timer tick DAT_00069d64 until it advances, latching the new value and freeing the page.
The tick snapshot that the blink phase and the spin share is read on the first pass before anything has written it, so the first frame neither waits nor has a settled blink phase.

Parameters:
  shop_index -- which shop's stock to offer: 0 item shop, 1 weapon shop, 2 secret shop. Comes down unchanged from the shop transaction loop at 0x00033b80 and is handed straight to fdps_shop_collect_stock_items.

Returns:
  The item id of the highlighted entry, in the Item.dat numbering that fdps_get_item_record takes, or -1 when the player cancels with Esc.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game-only callees, the game's shop stock and UI globals, and the "Beep.wav" asset string]

Rebuild note:
Each pass ends in an empty spin over the tick counter DAT_00069d64, which only the timer callback fdps_timer_tick_handler writes; declare that counter volatile or the compiler keeps the loaded value in a register and the picker hangs on the first frame. The down arrow is also drawn out of bounds: fdps_blit_command_sprite writes a fixed 25x22 block with no clipping, and page offset 0x4e96 is row 64 of a 76-row page, so its last ten rows scribble 25 bytes each as far as 0x6846, past the end of the 0x5ca0 block. Keep the arrow where it is -- the screen window only ever shows its top six rows, so moving it to fit the page changes what is displayed; enlarging the page silences the overrun without changing the picture.

=== 00032a70 [PLATE]
Draws one item's entry in the village shop's item list: the item's name, its price, and the one figure that matters for its kind.

Algorithm:
Renders the item name first: fdps_draw_text with the message table base held in DAT_000643c4 and message index item_id + 0xc9, writing at dest and forwarding the glyph colours 0xd0 (foreground), 0 (background) and 0x6d (outline). Looks the item record up with fdps_get_item_record and works out the second-line origin dest + pitch * 8 + 0x54. Blits the price caption -- Command.cel sprite 0x29, the same money mark fdps_draw_party_gold puts in front of the party's gold -- through fdps_blit_command_sprite at dest + 0x54 - pitch (one row above the entry's top edge) and draws the record's price, the unsigned 16-bit field at +0x13, as a five-digit figure at dest + 0x64 through fdps_draw_number.
The second line is then chosen from the record's type byte at +0:
  type 1..0x15 (the weapon types) -- caption sprite 0x40 ("+AP") and the signed 16-bit AP at +1
  type 0 or 0x16..0x27 (the armour types) -- caption sprite 0x41 ("+DP") and the signed 16-bit DP at +5
  type 0x28 and up with use_effect (+0xd) == 0x0b (HP recovery) -- caption sprite 0x3e ("+HP") and use_amount at +0xe
  the same with use_effect == 0x0c (MP recovery) -- caption sprite 0x3f ("+MP") and use_amount at +0xe
  anything else (badges, story items, consumables with any other effect) -- caption sprite 0x43, which is literally "????", alone with no figure beside it
Every caption goes at the second-line origin and every figure 0x16 bytes further right, as a four-digit field. Type 0 is steered away from the weapon branch by an explicit test before the <= 0x15 test.
fdps_draw_unit_inventory at 00024ea0 runs the same five-way caption dispatch over the same item record for the eight-slot carried-item list; the price line is what this one adds.

Parameters:
  item_id -- index into the Item.dat table (0..250) of the item this entry shows; also the item name's message index once 0xc9 is added
  dest -- byte pointer at the top-left corner of the entry's cell inside the caller's 8bpp off-screen page; fdps_shop_select_item lays the six cells out at x = 0x10 + 0x91 * (i & 1), y = 0x0b + 0x13 * (i / 2)
  pitch -- bytes per row of that surface; the only caller passes 0x138 (312)

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set; hash unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
The price at item+0x13 is read zero-extended (MOV AX / AND EAX,0xffff) while the stats at +1, +5 and +0xe are sign-extended (MOVSX). Shipped Item.dat prices reach 45000, so typing the price field as a signed short prints a negative number in the shop list. The type test also keeps 0 out of the weapon branch (CMP byte ptr,0 / JBE before the <= 0x15 test), so writing a plain type <= 0x15 would label a blank type-0 record with the "+AP" caption instead of the "+DP" one.

=== 00032c3a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0x0] NOP form between FUN_00032a70 and FUN_00032c40.

=== 00032c40 [PLATE]
Village shop buy-target picker: lets the player choose which roster member the item on offer is being bought for, and hands the caller that member's roster index.

Algorithm:
Reads the offered item's record through fdps_get_item_record and takes its type byte. Types outside 0x01-0x27 are not equipment (0x28 is consumables, 0x29-0x2c badges and plot items), so the whole screen is handed to the compact roster picker at 0x000336d0 and its result is returned unchanged. For equipment it runs its own modal loop, one pass per timer tick:
  - fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll keeps the CD track alive, then fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat yields one scancode.
  - 0x01 Esc and 0x53 Del set the loop result to -1 (cancel). 0x1c Enter and 0x39 Space set it to 1 (confirm), except that from chapter index 0x17 (DAT_00069cf4, chapter 24) onward the confirm is silently dropped while the cursor sits on roster slot 3 -- the slot of the fourth character to join, 法蓮娜, who is out of the party from that chapter on. The entry is still drawn and the cursor still stops on it; only the confirm does nothing.
  - 0x4d/0x4b move the cursor one entry right/left, 0x50/0x48 one row down/up, each guarded against the roster count DAT_00064114 and each announced with fdps_play_sfx("Beep.wav"). A move that changes the visible row plays a seven-frame slide: fdps_render_roster_select_frame is called with the source row stepped by i * 0x43 / 8 for i = 1..7, so the 67-pixel row scrolls in eight sub-steps.
  - The frame is then rebuilt from scratch: malloc plus memset a 0x19848-byte offscreen grid of pitch 0x138 (312x335), draw every roster member into it with fdps_shop_draw_member_entry at row (index / 3) * 0x43 + 0xc and column (index % 3) * 0x65 + 9, hand the grid to fdps_render_roster_select_frame at the settled cursor and scroll position, and free it again.
  - Spins on the timer tick DAT_00069d64 until it advances, latches the new value and loops.
The cursor DAT_000601b4 and the scroll top DAT_000601b0 are statics that no other function in the program references, and nothing resets them here, so the screen reopens on the member picked last time. One row of three entries is visible at a time, which is why the scroll top is always the cursor rounded down to a multiple of 3 and why the arrow keys keep the two in lockstep.

Parameters:
  item_id -- index into the Item.dat table of the item the shop is selling, 0x00-0xe1. Passed straight through to fdps_get_item_record and to fdps_shop_draw_member_entry, which uses it to show what each member's stats would become with that item.

Returns:
  The roster index of the chosen member, 0 to DAT_00064114 - 1, or -1 when the player cancels. For a non-equipment item the value is whatever the picker at 0x000336d0 returned, with the same meaning.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls fdps_play_sfx and fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll, and its only caller is the shop transaction loop at 0x00033b80]

Rebuild note:
The offscreen grid is allocated at the bottom of the loop and read at the top, so the slide animation blits from the pointer left over from the previous pass -- which has already been freed -- and on the very first pass from an uninitialised stack slot. It works only because Watcom's near heap hands the same block back to the next malloc of the same size with its contents intact, so hoisting the allocation out of the loop, or clearing the pointer after free, changes what the animation draws. Note also that the block on roster slot 3 is written literally as chapter index >= 0x17 with no upper bound, not as a "this member has left the party" test; rewriting it as one would let 法蓮娜 be bought for again once she rejoins for the end of the game.

=== 000330d3 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / nop, aligning next function to 0x10

=== 000330e0 [PLATE]
Draws one frame of the village shop's buy-target list onto the visible mode-13h screen: the window, the selection bar behind the chosen column, one 312x67 row of the caller's pre-rendered entry grid, and the two blinking scroll arrows, timed against the vertical retrace.

Algorithm:
Allocates a 0x5ca0-byte scratch panel with malloc -- 312 x 76 at pitch 0x138, exactly the dimensions of the ShopWin.Cel sheet -- and composes it back to front. fdps_cel_blit_sprite lays sprite 0 of ShopWin.Cel, the sheet the village screen at 0x00031210 loads from Misc.vfs into DAT_00069d84, at (0,0) as the window; that sprite writes every pixel of the panel but four, and those four sit in panel rows 0 and 74, neither of which reaches the screen -- which is why the panel is never cleared after the malloc. Sprite 2 of the SelBar.cel sheet held in DAT_000643c0 goes down next at (cursor_x, 0x14): a 101 x 17 bar, 101 being 0x65, the column stride of the three-column grid, so it covers exactly one column. fdps_blit_transparent_rect then copies the 0x138 x 0x43 strip that starts at list_bitmap + src_row * 0x138 over both, so palette index 0 in the entry strip lets the window and the bar show through.
The arrow blink phase is (DAT_00069d64 / 5) & 1 taken through an unsigned DIV, the timer tick counter flipping it every five ticks. When scroll_top is not 0 there is a row above the window, so fdps_blit_command_sprite draws Command.cel sprite 0x44 + phase at panel offset 0x6ae (row 5, column 150); when scroll_top + 3 is still below the roster member count in DAT_00064114 there is a row below, so it draws sprite 0x46 + phase at offset 0x4e96 (row 64, column 150). Command.cel's cells are 25 x 22 and the down arrow starts at panel row 64 of 76, but all four arrow sprites are 7 x 5 triangles in the top-left corner of their cell and every row below the fifth is a single skip run, which stores nothing -- so neither blit writes a byte outside the panel.
fdps_cycle_ui_palette then advances the UI palette animation, and the routine spins on inp(0x3da) until bit 3 goes high and spins again until it goes low. fdps_cycle_ui_palette has itself just waited for retrace to begin, so in practice the first spin falls straight through and only the second blocks: the screen copy starts as the active display resumes, with the 125 scan lines above the panel as head room, rather than during blanking. fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x130 x 0x43 (304 x 67) region at panel offset 0x3ad (row 3, column 5) to 0xa9c48 -- VGA memory at x=8, y=125 -- with a destination pitch of 0x140, and free releases the panel. Because that copy starts three rows and five columns into the panel, the strip's own top three rows and leftmost five columns never reach the screen, and panel rows 67..69 contribute window edge in their place.

Parameters:
  list_bitmap -- the caller's pre-rendered grid of list entries, pitch 0x138, three entries per row of 0x43 pixels. fdps_shop_select_buy_target allocates it at 0x19848 bytes, fills every roster member into it with fdps_shop_draw_member_entry, calls here, and frees it again.
  cursor_x -- pixel x of the selection bar inside the panel; fdps_shop_select_buy_target passes (cursor index % 3) * 0x65 + 5, so 5, 0x6a or 0xcf.
  src_row -- pixel row of list_bitmap at which the visible strip starts. fdps_shop_select_buy_target passes (scroll_top / 3) * 0x43 when the list is parked, and steps it in eighths of 0x43 above or below that to slide the list one row.
  scroll_top -- index of the first visible entry, always a multiple of 3. It decides which of the two scroll arrows are drawn and nothing else.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls only game blitters plus malloc/free/inp]

=== 0003322b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning next function entry to 0x10

=== 00033230 [PLATE]
Draws one party member's entry in the village shop's buy-target list: the member's animated icon and name, and the four combat stats that member would have with the item on offer, each coloured against the stat the member has now.

Algorithm:
Resolves the member with fdps_get_roster_record. Takes the icon's walk-cycle phase from the frame counter DAT_00069d64 as an unsigned (DAT_00069d64 / 6) & 3 with the value 3 folded back to 1, giving the ping-pong 0, 1, 2, 1, and forms the sprite index roster_index * 0xc + phase -- twelve sprites per member in the field sprite bank, the same numbering fdps_village_select_member uses. Blits Command.cel sprites 0x2a and 0x2b through fdps_blit_command_sprite at dst + pitch * 0x11 - 2 and dst + pitch * 0x11 + 0x17, one sprite width apart: decoding the sheet shows 0x2a is the sandy mound the icon stands on and 0x2b its right tail, only 18 opaque pixels of the 550 in the cell. The icon's own RLE stream is the self-relative dword at sprite_index * 4 of the offset table based at DAT_00060138, added back to that table's base, and is drawn 0x18 by 0x18 by fdps_blit_dispatch: in mode 0 normally, or in mode 9 (translucent) with the three-dword blend descriptor { shade-ramp table 0x000653f0, blend level 10, inverse colour cube 0x000643f0 } when the chapter index DAT_00069cf4 has reached 0x17 and the record's character id (byte +8) is 1. Character id 1 is 法蓮娜: fdps_chapter_04_init passes 1 to fdps_roster_add_character, which writes that argument into record bytes +7 and +8, and the four earlier joins make her roster slot 3 -- the same member the caller's confirm gate locks out from the same chapter index on. So her entry is ghosted from chapter 24 on; the test has no upper bound, so it stays ghosted for the rest of the game, including after she rejoins for the hidden chapters. fdps_draw_text then draws message character_id + 1 -- the member's name -- at dst + pitch * 9 + 0x1e in glyph colour 0xd0 with outline colour 0x6d, on a pitch given as the literal 0x138 rather than taken from the pitch argument.
fdps_roster_preview_combat_stats_with_item(roster_index, item_id, stats) then fills a four-int local with the attack, defense, hit and evade the member would have with the item equipped. fdps_unit_can_equip_item(roster_index, item_id) decides what is drawn under the name. When it returns 0 the only thing drawn is message 0x1f7, the cannot-equip line, at dst + pitch * 0x23 + 0xe in glyph colour 0x2b. When it returns non-zero the four figures go down in two labelled columns. Each column's caption is one Command.cel sprite carrying both of that column's labels on its two text lines: sprite 0x2c reads "EV :" over "HIT:" and goes at dst + pitch * 0x22 + 4, sprite 0x2f reads "AP :" over "DP :" and goes at dst + pitch * 0x22 + 0x33 (both read off the decoded sheet). fdps_draw_number then prints the figures zero-padded to three digits beside them: stats[3] at row 0x22 column 0x1a under EV, stats[2] at row 0x2b column 0x1a under HIT, stats[0] at row 0x22 column 0x49 under AP, stats[1] at row 0x2b column 0x49 under DP -- which is the artwork confirming both the record field names (+0x4e evade, +0x4c hit, +0x48 attack, +0x4a defense) and fdps_roster_preview_combat_stats_with_item's out_stats order of attack, defense, hit, evade. Before each figure the Number.cel colour-row selector DAT_0006000c is set from the comparison with the stat the member has now: 2 when the previewed value is lower than the current one, 3 when it is higher, 0 when they are equal. It is put back to 0 after the last figure, and is left untouched on the cannot-equip path.
fdps_unit_can_equip_item resolves its first argument through fdps_get_unit_record on DAT_00069cd8 rather than through the roster array, and the same index still reaches the same record here because fdps_load_field_chapter_resources points DAT_00069cd8 at the roster base DAT_00064108 for the field and village phase.

Parameters:

  pitch -- destination row stride in bytes, handed on to fdps_blit_command_sprite, fdps_blit_dispatch, fdps_draw_number and the cannot-equip message. The only caller passes 0x138 (312), which is also the literal the name message is drawn with.
  roster_index -- position in the party roster array, the index fdps_get_roster_record takes. fdps_shop_select_buy_target loops it from 0 to the roster count DAT_00064114 - 1.   item_id -- ITEM.DAT id of the shop item being offered, forwarded unchanged from fdps_shop_select_buy_target's own argument to fdps_roster_preview_combat_stats_with_item and fdps_unit_can_equip_item.

=== 0003356f [EOL]

=== 00033570 [PLATE]
Computes the four combat stats one party roster member would have if it equipped a given item, so a status panel can show the resulting figures beside the member's current ones.

Algorithm:
Looks the candidate item up with fdps_get_item_record and keeps its type code, the ITEM.DAT record byte at +0 -- codes 0x01 through 0x15 are the weapon kinds, 0x16 and above the armour and the non-weapon items. Resolves the member with fdps_get_roster_record and seeds four running totals from the record's base stats plus the candidate's own modifiers: attack from the signed word at +0x37 plus item word +0x01 (ap), defense from the word at +0x39 plus item word +0x05 (dp), hit from the word at +0x3e plus item word +0x03 (hit), and evade from that same word at +0x3e plus item word +0x07 (ev) -- there is no separate evade base, both derive from the one dexterity word. It then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries starting at record+0x0a, i from 0 to 7, resolving each entry's item id (second byte) through fdps_get_item_record. An entry contributes its four modifiers only when its flag byte has the equipped bit 0x40 set and its type code sits on the opposite side of the 0x15 threshold from the candidate's -- that is, only when the candidate would not displace it. Same-category equipped items are dropped from the sum because equipping the candidate would take them off, which is the rule fdps_unit_equip_slot applies when the equip actually happens. The four totals are stored as ints to out_stats[0..3] in the order attack, defense, hit, evade: the order of the stat words at record +0x48, +0x4a, +0x4c and +0x4e that fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats maintains and that FUN_00033230 compares these values against. Nothing is range-checked, and the candidate's modifiers are added whether or not the member's class may wear it; FUN_00025fe0 is the separate check the caller runs before it prints the numbers.

Parameters:
  roster_index -- position in the party roster array, the index fdps_get_roster_record takes, 0 .. [0x00064114]-1. FUN_00033230 passes the member whose panel it is drawing.
  item_id -- ITEM.DAT id of the item being tried on, 0x00..0xe1 for the ids that have content. Passed straight to fdps_get_item_record.
  out_stats -- caller-supplied array of four ints, all four always written: attack, defense, hit, evade.

Returns:
Nothing. The result is the four ints written through out_stats.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set and the hash is unique in the image; the body is game domain logic over the roster record and ITEM.DAT, and both callees are the game's own record-lookup helpers]

Rebuild note:
Hit and evade are both seeded from the single roster-record word at +0x3e; the record has no separate evade base. Writing the obvious symmetric version -- four base fields feeding four modifiers, with evade taken from its own word at +0x40 -- produces an evade figure that disagrees with the one fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats stores at record +0x4e, so the status panel would light an up or down arrow on a stat the item did not change.

=== 000336c9 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP (8d 80 00 00 00 00) + 90, aligning next function to 000336d0.

=== 000336d0 [PLATE]
Village party-member picker: runs the 3x2 icon grid of party roster members across the bottom of the screen and hands the caller the roster index of the member the player chose.

Algorithm:
Runs one pass per timer tick until a confirm or a cancel settles the loop result. The cursor and the scroll top live in the file-scope statics at 0x000601bc and 0x000601b8, which no other function in the program references and which nothing resets on entry, so the grid always reopens on the member picked last time -- including when the last pick was made from a different village screen.
Each pass calls fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll to keep the CD track alive, then takes one scancode from fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat:
  - 0x01 Esc and 0x53 Del settle the result at -1 (cancel).
  - 0x1c Enter and 0x39 Space settle it at 1 (confirm), except that from chapter index 0x17 (DAT_00069cf4, chapter 24) onward a confirm while the cursor sits on roster slot 3 is dropped without a sound. Slot 3 is the fourth character to join, 法蓮娜, who is out of the party from that chapter on.
  - 0x4d/0x4b step the cursor one entry right/left, 0x50/0x48 three entries (one row) down/up, each guarded against the roster member count DAT_00064114 and each followed by fdps_play_sfx("Beep.wav"). The scroll top follows in steps of 3: down by 3 when the cursor falls below it, up by 3 when the cursor reaches scroll top + 6.
The frame is then built from scratch in a 0x5ca0-byte malloc'd page, 312x76 at pitch 0x138. fdps_cel_blit_sprite lays sprite 0 of the ShopWin.Cel sheet held in DAT_00069d84 at (0,0) as the window frame. Six cells follow, for roster entries scroll_top through scroll_top + 5, cell i at x = (i % 3) * 0x65 + 0xb and y = (i / 3) * 0x1b + 9; fdps_get_roster_record resolves the entry's record before the entry is tested against DAT_00064114, so a slot past the end forms a pointer that is never dereferenced and the cell is left as bare window. For a cell that is drawn:
  - when the entry is the cursor, sprite 2 of the UI selection-bar sheet DAT_000643c0 goes down first at (x - 6, y + 5) as the highlight;
  - Command.cel sprites 0x2a and 0x2b through fdps_blit_command_sprite at (x - 2, y + 0x10) and (x + 0x17, y + 0x10), the two halves of the stand the icon sits on;
  - the member's walking icon, sprite roster_index * 0xc + phase of the field sprite bank, phase being (DAT_00069d64 / 6) & 3 taken unsigned off the timer tick with the value 3 folded back to 1, giving the ping-pong 0, 1, 2, 1. Its pixel stream is the self-relative dword at sprite * 4 of the table based at DAT_00060138, added back to that base, and fdps_blit_dispatch draws it 0x18 by 0x18 at (x, y): in mode 0 normally, or in mode 9 (translucent) with the stack-built blend descriptor { shade ramp 0x000653f0, blend level 10, inverse colour cube 0x000643f0 } when the chapter index has reached 0x17 and the record's character id (byte +8) is 1, which ghosts 法蓮娜's entry;
  - the member's name, message character id + 1 of the resident Fdetxt00.txt table held in DAT_000643c4, drawn by FUN_0001ff60 at (x + 0x1c, y + 6) in glyph colour 0xd0 with outline colour 0x6d.
Two blinking scroll arrows close the frame: Command.cel sprite 0x44 + b at (150, 5) when the scroll top is not 0, and 0x46 + b at (150, 64) when entries remain below the window, with b = (DAT_00069d64 / 5) & 1. fdps_cycle_ui_palette advances the UI palette animation, the loop polls port 0x3da until the vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, and fdps_blit_rect copies the 304x67 interior of the page from (5,3) onto the mode-13h frame buffer at 0xa9c48, i.e. (8,125), before free releases the page. The pass ends spinning on the timer tick DAT_00069d64 until it advances, comparing against the value latched at the end of the previous pass, which is an uninitialised stack slot on the first pass.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  The roster index of the chosen member, 0 to DAT_00064114 - 1, read out of the cursor static at DAT_000601bc, or -1 when the player cancelled.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; every reference is a static call from village screen code, it shares the game's roster and cursor globals with that cluster, and it passes the asset name "Beep.wav"]

Rebuild note:
The refusal to accept roster slot 3 from chapter index 0x17 on is written literally as chapter index >= 0x17 && cursor == 3, while the ghosting of the same member is a separate test on the record's character id (byte +8 == 1); writing one test for both, greying the entry out, or beeping on the refused confirm all change what the player sees -- the entry stays selectable, the cursor still stops on it, and the confirm is simply silent. The cursor and the scroll top are file-scope statics shared by every caller and never reset on entry, so making them locals seeded to 0 loses the "reopens where you left it" behaviour.

=== 00033b77 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + lea edx,[edx+0] (3), aligning FUN_00033b80 to 16 bytes.

=== 00033b80 [PLATE]
Village shop purchase loop: lets the player buy one item after another out of a shop's stock for a chosen party member, crediting three quarters of the price of the gear that member already has equipped, until the player cancels out of the item list.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 1) once to sweep the caller's menu window shut, then loops until the item picker returns -1. Each pass sweeps the window back open with fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 0) and repaints the gold readout with fdps_draw_party_gold(0xa8208, 0x140) before every picker, asks fdps_shop_select_item(shop_index) for an item id and fdps_shop_select_buy_target(item_id) for the party member to buy it for, and abandons the pass when either hands back -1. It keeps fdps_unit_can_equip_item(member, item_id) as the auto-equip flag, publishes the item's price -- the 16-bit field at offset 0x13 of the ITEM.DAT record fdps_get_item_record returns -- in the message number global DAT_00064038, and asks fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot for the slot holding the member's equipped weapon, passing want_armor = 1 when the record's type byte is above 0x15 so armor is looked for instead.
When such a slot exists and the member may equip the new item, the trade-in offer runs: the member's name id (roster record byte at +8, plus 1) goes into the message substitution global DAT_00064030 and the equipped item's name id (its item id plus 0xc9) into DAT_00064034, FUN_0001ff60 renders message 0x1f6 into the text area at 0xaa3d4 with pitch 0x140, and fdps_prompt_two_choice() == 0 accepts it: the trade-in flag is set and DAT_00064038 loses old_price * 3 / 4. From that offer on, the pass's remaining messages are drawn 0x26 rows further down the 0x140-stride buffer so they do not land on the prompt already there.
Without a trade-in, a member whose fdps_unit_item_count is already 8 gets message 0x1fa and the pass ends. Otherwise the balance in DAT_00064038 decides: a positive price above the party gold at DAT_000643a4 draws message 0x213 and nothing moves; a positive price the party can afford draws message 0x1f8, and an accepted prompt plays "Incom.wav" through fdps_play_sfx, subtracts the price from DAT_000643a4, repaints the gold and waits delay(200); a balance of zero or less -- the trade-in credit came to more than the price -- is negated, drawn as message 0x1f9, and an accepted prompt pays that amount into DAT_000643a4 the same way.
Only when money actually moved does the inventory change: fdps_unit_remove_item drops the traded-in slot when the trade-in was accepted, fdps_unit_add_item hands over the bought item, the auto-equip flag makes fdps_unit_equip_slot equip the slot fdps_unit_item_count has just filled (count - 1), and fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats brings the member's derived stats up to date.

Parameters:
  screen_page -- the shop screen's 320x200 8bpp page, allocated by the calling screen driver and handed straight to fdps_village_animate_window_zoom, which reads it but never writes it.
  shop_index -- which shop's stock list to sell from, passed through fdps_shop_select_item to fdps_shop_collect_stock_items; 0 from fdps_village_item_menu, 1 from fdps_run_weapon_shop, 2 from fdps_run_secret_menu.

Returns:
  Nothing. The loop ends when the player cancels out of the item picker.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; called only by the named village screen drivers and touching only game-owned data]

Rebuild note:
The member index this loop hands to fdps_get_roster_record (array at DAT_00064108) is the same value it hands to the fdps_unit_* accessors (array at DAT_00069cd8): during the village phase fdps_load_field_chapter_resources has pointed DAT_00069cd8 at the roster array, so both reach one record. Converting between a "roster index" and a "unit index", or reaching for a separate roster inventory accessor, breaks the shop. The bag-full refusal is also skipped once the trade-in is accepted, because the traded item leaves the bag first; hoisting the "already holding eight items" test above the trade-in prompt would refuse purchases the original allows.

Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, 5 bytes to 16-byte boundary at 00033f80.

=== 00033f80 [PLATE]
Village-screen party status browser: lets the player look at one party member's status window after another until they cancel.

Algorithm:
Keeps a selection variable, seeded with 0 so the first pass always runs, and loops until that variable is -1. Each pass calls fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 0), which zooms the member-select window open over the caller's backdrop page; then fdps_village_select_member, the 3x2 party-member icon grid, which returns the index of the member the player confirmed or -1 when the player cancels; then fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 1), which zooms the same window shut. When the returned index is not -1 it memmoves 0xfa00 bytes (320x200) from screen_page to the mode-13h frame buffer at 0xa0000, so the clean backdrop is what the status window snapshots and restores around itself, and calls fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window with the index. Then it jumps back to the top of the loop; cancelling in the picker is the only way out.
The index is a roster index that is simultaneously a valid active-unit index for the whole time this function can run. fdps_village_select_member produces it against the roster array DAT_00064108 and bounds it against the roster count DAT_00064114; fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window resolves it through fdps_get_unit_record on the active-unit pointer DAT_00069cd8. The two agree because fdps_run_village_phase calls fdps_load_field_chapter_resources -- which assigns DAT_00060150 = DAT_00064114 and DAT_00069cd8 = DAT_00064108 at 000315ed and 000315f2 -- before its menu loop can dispatch to any of this function's three callers, and only clears the pair again after that loop exits. The sibling fdps_village_member_equip_loop leans on the same alias, feeding the picker's index straight to fdps_get_unit_record.
Nothing here guarantees a window actually appears: fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window returns without drawing for class bytes 0x24-0x27, and this function neither tests for that case nor sees a result, so a pick that draws nothing simply reopens the picker.

Parameters:
  screen_page -- pointer to the calling village screen's 0xfa00-byte (320x200) mode-13h page holding that screen's backdrop. All three callers pass the malloc'd page they blitted their own .cel background into (Item.cel, Church.cel, Secret.cel), the same page they hand to fdps_village_animate_window_zoom.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; called only by named game menu code and it calls game symbols, which a crt or ail object cannot]

Rebuild note:
The member index the picker returns is fed to fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window, which looks it up in the active-unit array at DAT_00069cd8 -- correct only because fdps_load_field_chapter_resources aliases DAT_00069cd8 to the roster base DAT_00064108 (and the count DAT_00060150 to DAT_00064114) for the whole field/village phase. Writing the obvious thing -- treating the picked index as a roster index and resolving it with fdps_get_roster_record, or giving the village its own separate unit array -- shows a different record. The alias also makes ownership of DAT_00069cd8 conditional: fdps_load_field_chapter_resources guards its free with an explicit DAT_00069cd8 != DAT_00064108 test at 000315cb-000315d0, while fdps_build_map_unit_array frees DAT_00069cd8 unguarded whenever DAT_00060150 is non-zero (00022c6d-00022c76) and is safe only because fdps_run_village_phase zeroes both globals on the way out of the village. Adding the 'missing' guard to one, or dropping the existing guard from the other, either leaks the battle array or double-frees the roster.
Second trap in this function's own body: the memmove of the backdrop to 0xa0000 before every status window is not a redraw for the player's benefit -- fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window snapshots VGA and restores that snapshot when it closes, so dropping the memmove because 'the screen already looks right' makes the window save the closing zoom frame and paint it back over the screen afterwards.

=== 00034000 [PLATE]
Village sell screen: lets the player sell one party member's carried item after another for three quarters of its listed price, until they back out of the member picker.

Algorithm:
Plays the village window frame shut with fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 1), then loops until the member picker hands back -1. Each pass reopens the frame (closing = 0) and runs the 3x2 icon-grid picker FUN_000336d0, which returns the unit index of the chosen party member, or -1 to leave; closes the frame again and asks fdps_unit_item_count how many of that member's eight inventory slots are filled.
When the member carries nothing, it reopens the frame, takes the member's 0x50-byte record from fdps_get_unit_record, publishes byte +8 of it (the character id) plus 1 in the message system's name-substitution slot DAT_00064030, and draws message 0x1fb -- the refusal -- with FUN_0001ff60 from the text base in DAT_000643c4 to screen address 0xaa3d4, which is VGA (20,131), inside the window frame.
Otherwise it wipes the screen back to the caller's page with memmove(0xa0000, screen_page, 0xfa00) and opens the inventory picker fdps_unit_item_select_window(unit_index, 0, &slot), where a -1 return means the player backed out of it. Message 0x1fc -- the sell confirmation, which prints both substitutions -- goes to the same screen address, and fdps_prompt_two_choice runs the yes/no cursor over it.
Only a 0 from that prompt sells: fdps_unit_remove_item drops the slot, fdps_play_sfx plays "Incom.wav", the offer standing in DAT_00064038 is added to the party gold at DAT_000643a4, the gold readout is redrawn, delay(200) holds the result on screen, and fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats reworks the member's derived stats in case what was sold had been equipped. Every path then falls back to the loop head, so a completed sale sends the player to the member picker again rather than back into the same member's bag.

Parameters:
  screen_page -- the caller's 0xfa00-byte (320x200) 8bpp page holding the village screen this one runs over. Never written: it is handed to fdps_village_animate_window_zoom as its screen_page and memmoved to the VGA framebuffer. All three callers -- fdps_village_item_menu, fdps_run_weapon_shop and fdps_run_secret_menu -- pass the page they blitted their own .cel background into and published at DAT_00063fb4.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [game callers and callees, game globals and the VGA framebuffer; no Function ID hit in the Watcom or ail sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

=== 00034210 [PLATE]
Village item hand-over screen: lets the player give one party member's carried item to another, one hand-over after the next until they cancel.

Algorithm:
Closes the caller's command-icon window with fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 1), then loops until the picked member index is -1; that picker result is the only exit, so the window is left open on the way out and the caller reopens it. Each pass reopens the window with fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 0) and runs the 3x2 party-member picker FUN_000336d0, which hands back the roster index of the giver or -1 on cancel. On a pick it sets the message-substitution slot DAT_00064030 to byte 8 of the giver's record from fdps_get_unit_record plus 1 -- byte 8 is the character id, and id + 1 is that character's name string, which the -4 token of FUN_0001ff60 expands inline -- then closes the window again to wipe the picker grid off it.

fdps_unit_item_count picks the branch. When the giver carries nothing, the window is reopened and message 0x1fb of the resident Fdetxt00.txt table at DAT_000643c4 -- "<name>身上沒有攜帶任何道具！", the giver is not carrying a single item -- is painted through FUN_0001ff60 into the village text box at 0xaa3d4 (VGA 0xa0000 plus row 131, column 20) with pitch 0x140 and the box geometry 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d, and the pass ends.

When the giver carries at least one item, memmove lays the caller's clean 0xfa00-byte (320x200) page over the mode-13h frame buffer at 0xa0000 so the status window has a clean background to save and restore, and FUN_000259c0(giver, 0, &slot) opens that member's status window and runs its inventory selection, returning -1 on cancel and otherwise leaving the chosen slot, 0..7, in slot. fdps_unit_get_item_id(giver, slot) reads the item id out of that slot and DAT_00064034 is set to item id + 0xc9, which is that item's name string in the same message table (item id 0 gives string 0xc9, 岩石) and is what the -5 token expands. The window is reopened and message 0x1fd -- "<name>的<item>要交給誰？", who is <name>'s <item> to be given to -- is painted, then FUN_000336d0 runs a second time for the receiver.

A receiver of -1 ends the pass. When fdps_unit_item_count says the receiver already holds 8 items, the window is closed and reopened to wipe the picker grid and message 0x1fa -- "道具滿了，帶不下！", the bag is full -- is painted instead of moving anything. Otherwise fdps_unit_remove_item(giver, slot) drops the item and repacks the giver's eight-slot list, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(giver) refreshes the giver's derived stats because the item may have been equipped, and fdps_unit_add_item(receiver, item_id) stores the bare id in the receiver's first free slot, unequipped. The receiver's stats are not recomputed. The giver index survives into the next pass, so the loop just asks for another giver.

Both pickers walk the roster through fdps_get_roster_record while fdps_unit_item_count, fdps_get_unit_record and the status window index the battle unit array; on the village screens those are the same array, because fdps_load_field_chapter_resources points the unit-array base DAT_00069cd8 at the roster base DAT_00064108 and copies the roster count DAT_00064114 into the unit count DAT_00060150.

Parameters:
  screen_page -- the caller's 0xfa00-byte (320x200) 8bpp page holding the village screen that the window opens over. Handed straight to fdps_village_animate_window_zoom, which names it screen_page, and used as the memmove source that repaints the screen before the status window runs. fdps_village_item_menu (slot 3 of its menu), fdps_run_church_screen, fdps_run_weapon_shop and fdps_run_secret_menu each pass the page they blitted their own .cel background into.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; called only by named game screens and it calls game symbols, with memmove as its one vendor routine, used as a client]

Rebuild note:
The item crosses as a bare id -- fdps_unit_get_item_id here, fdps_unit_add_item there, and add zeroes the receiving slot's whole flag byte. Moving the giver's 2-byte inventory slot across instead, the obvious way to write "move an item", would carry the equipped bit 0x40 over with it, and since only the giver's stats are recomputed the receiver would silently gain the item's bonuses without ever wearing it.

=== 00034520 [PLATE]
Finds which of a unit's eight inventory slots is holding a given item, so the caller can consume or check for that item.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index) for the number of occupied slots and returns -1 immediately when that is zero. Otherwise it walks slot indices 0..count-1, reading each slot's item id with fdps_unit_get_item_id(unit_index, slot), and returns the first slot index whose id equals item_id. Falling off the end of the scan also returns -1. The scan is bounded by the occupied-slot count rather than by the eight physical slots, which relies on the inventory staying packed at the front -- the invariant fdps_unit_add_item (fills the first empty slot) and fdps_unit_remove_item (closes the gap) maintain. Both slot accessors resolve unit_index through fdps_get_unit_record into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, where slot n occupies the two bytes at record+0xa+2n: the flag byte, whose bit 0x80 marks the slot empty, and the item id at record+0xb+2n.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; not bounds-checked here or by either callee
  item_id -- the item id to look for, 0-255 as stored in the slot's id byte; callers pass constants such as 0xa0, 0xb3, 0xdc and the promotion items 0xdb/0xe0/0xe1

Returns:
The 0-based slot index of the first slot holding item_id, suitable for passing straight to fdps_unit_remove_item; -1 when the unit carries nothing or no slot holds that item.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in image, all 12 callers and both callees are game-side]

Rebuild note:
The scan runs over slots 0..fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index)-1, not over all eight slots, so it silently depends on the inventory being packed at the front. Rewriting it as the obvious for (slot = 0; slot < 8; slot++) changes behaviour whenever an empty slot precedes an occupied one: the empty slot's stale id byte at record+0xb+2n is still compared (fdps_unit_get_item_id never looks at the 0x80 empty bit), so the rewrite can return the index of an empty slot and the caller will then remove an item that is not there.
