=== 000345a0 [PLATE]
Village church class-change screen: promotes one party member after another -- level 20 or over and still in one of the nine promotable base forms -- until the player cancels or nobody is left who can change class.

Algorithm:
Closes and reopens the caller's window with fdps_village_animate_window_zoom(screen_page, 1) then (screen_page, 0), and loops until it is done. Every pass rebuilds the candidate list from scratch, so a member just promoted drops out of it.

The sweep runs i over the roster count DAT_00064114 and takes each record from fdps_get_unit_record; on the village screens that is the roster array, because fdps_load_field_chapter_resources points the unit-array base DAT_00069cd8 at the roster base DAT_00064108. A record qualifies when its level (byte 0x21) is 0x14 (20) or more and its character id (byte 0x07) is below 9 -- the nine characters RANKUP.DAT holds a promotion record for, which is also what keeps out anyone already promoted, since promoted forms carry character ids 0x0f and up. The unit index goes into a 10-entry stack array (at most nine members can ever qualify) and a parallel array takes the promotion route the member's bag selects, probed with fdps_unit_find_item_slot: character id 0 (蘭迪斯) carrying item 0xdb 勇者徽章 gives route 3, otherwise item 0xe0 光之徽章 gives route 1, item 0xe1 暗之徽章 gives route 2, and carrying no badge gives route 0, the free promotion every eligible member gets.

With no candidates it paints message 0x214 of the resident text table at DAT_000643c4 through FUN_0001ff60, into the village text box at 0xaa3d4 (VGA 0xa0000 plus row 131, column 20) with pitch 0x140 and the 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d box geometry, closes the window and returns.

Otherwise FUN_000352c0 runs the member picker over the two arrays and hands back the chosen slot, or -1 to cancel and end the loop. For the chosen member fdps_get_promotion_record(byte 0x08, the original character id) fetches the 12-byte RANKUP.DAT record: four 3-byte routes of (new character id, new class code, movement bonus). Message slot DAT_00064030 is set to character id + 1, that character's name string, and DAT_00064034 to the route's class code + 0xa1, that class's name string; message 0x215 asks the question and fdps_prompt_two_choice takes the answer, anything but 0 backing out.

On yes, FUN_00034c10(unit_index, route) plays the transformation and writes the route's new character id and class code into bytes 0x07 and 0x20, memmove lays the caller's page back over the mode-13h framebuffer at 0xa0000, and the badge is consumed through fdps_unit_find_item_slot plus fdps_unit_remove_item -- but only for a route 1..3 whose target character id differs from route 0's, so a badge that leads where the free promotion already leads is kept.

The gains are then paid out a line at a time, each staged through the number slot DAT_00064038 that the -6 token of FUN_0001ff60 prints: message 0x216, the route's third byte into DAT_00064038, message 0x217, and that byte added to movement (byte 0x3b). fdps_get_growth_record(the route's new character id) then supplies the FRILEVUP.DAT row of the form being entered and its five maximum-growth bytes are added to the base stats -- byte 1 to AP (word 0x37) with message 0x218, byte 3 to DP (word 0x39) with 0x219, byte 5 to DX (word 0x3e) with 0x21a, byte 7 to both current and maximum HP (words 0x40 and 0x42) with 0x21b, byte 9 to both current and maximum MP (words 0x44 and 0x46) with 0x21c. The lines alternate between the three text rows 0xaa3d4, 0xabb94 and 0xad354 (rows 131, 150 and 169), with a window close/open between pages to clear them.

Finally the level (byte 0x21) is reset to 1, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats refreshes the derived combat stats, the window is closed and reopened, and the loop asks for another member.

Parameters:
  screen_page -- the caller's 0xfa00-byte (320x200) 8bpp page holding the church screen the window opens over. Handed straight to fdps_village_animate_window_zoom, which names it screen_page, and used as the memmove source that repaints the screen after the transformation animation. fdps_run_church_screen passes the page it blitted Church.cel into, from slot 1 of its menu dispatch.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no FID candidate in either library set; unique hash in image, and memmove is its one vendor call, used as a client]

Rebuild note:
The eligibility test is on the character id in byte 0x07, not on the class code in byte 0x20; writing the obvious "class < 9" lets 蓋亞, 珊 and 蘭斯洛特 and every already-promoted unit through and indexes RANKUP.DAT, which holds only nine records, out of bounds. The stat bonuses are the raw *_max bytes of FRILEVUP.DAT, which are one greater than the growth maximum the tables show, so a rebuild that normalised those bytes down by one on parse hands out one point less on every stat.

=== 00034c07 [EOL]

=== 00034c10 [PLATE]
Promotes one roster member at the village church: writes the new form id and class code into its unit record, then plays the full-screen transformation animation that shows the change.

Algorithm:
Swaps the two shared palette-blend tables to their fight-palette copies, reading FMer1.tmp into the 0x4800-byte table at 000653f0 and FMer2.tmp into the 0x1000-byte table at 000643f0 with fopen/fread/fclose ("rb", the mode string at 00061f30). Those are the tables fdps_draw_composite_sprite reads for its blend setup, and the matching field copies are read back from Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp at the end.

Takes the unit record from fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and the character's 12-byte RankUp.dat record from fdps_get_promotion_record(record byte 0x8, the character id). Entry promotion_entry of that record is the three bytes at +promotion_entry*3: byte 0 is the new form id, stored to record byte 0x7, and byte 1 is the new class code, stored to record byte 0x20. Both are written before any frame is drawn.

Loads three SAF clips with fdps_vfs_load_entry and resets a three-dword playback cursor for each with fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 1): "Stand%03d.saf" of the character id and "Stand%03d.saf" of the new form id, both from Fight.vfs, and the transformation effect from MISC.VFS. The effect is one of "magic0gg.saf" and "magic0bb.saf" -- the 25-byte table at 0003107f, indexed by the new class code, yields 0 or 1, which picks one of the two 20-byte names in the table at 00031098.

Clears the 64000-byte VGA page at 0xa0000, uploads the fight palette through fdps_set_palette_range from the Fight.pal image at 000643e4, and allocates a 0x16480-byte offscreen canvas of pitch 0x170 and height 0xf8. The composite-sprite request built on the stack points at that canvas and draws at origin (0x18, 0x18); every presented frame is the 0x140 by 0xc8 window at canvas+0x2298, that is the pixel at (0x18, 0x18), blitted to 0xa0000 by fdps_blit_rect.

Four loops follow. Each frame clears the canvas, sets the request's clip pointer (+0x14) and frame index (+0x18) from a cursor, draws with fdps_draw_composite_sprite, advances that cursor with fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0), then spins on inp(0x3da) bit 3 until vertical retrace has come and gone, blits, and spins until the timer tick at 00069d64 changes:
  1. 25 frames of the old Stand clip alone, drawn with flag 0 so its frame sounds are suppressed.
  2. the old Stand clip with the effect clip over it, both drawn with flag 1 so the effect's frame sounds play, until the request's frame-index field reaches 30. That field holds the effect cursor's frame on every pass after the first; on the first test it still holds the Stand cursor's frame, which is always below 30 because every Stand%03d.saf has four frames.
  3. the new Stand clip with the same effect clip, continuing from effect frame 30, until fdps_saf_advance_tick reports that the effect clip has passed its last frame -- this is where the figure changes shape.
  4. 25 frames of the new Stand clip alone, flag 0 again.

Then frees the canvas and the three clips, uploads the field palette from the Fde.pal image at 000643bc and reloads the Mer tables.

The "before" sprite is built from the character id at record byte 0x8, not from the form id at byte 0x7 that this function overwrites; the two carry the same value for every unit the church offers promotion to, because fdps_church_promote_loop only offers it while byte 0x7 is below 9.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit record to promote, into the 0x50-byte array based at 00069cd8; on the village screens that array is the party roster. fdps_church_promote_loop passes the roster index of the member the player picked.
  promotion_entry -- which of the four 3-byte entries of that character's RankUp.dat record to apply, 0..3. fdps_church_promote_loop picks 3 when the unit carries item 0xdb (勇者徽章), 1 for 0xe0 (光之徽章), 2 for 0xe1 (暗之徽章) and 0 when it carries none of the three.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls six fdps_ functions and loads the game's own resource files, using the CRT only as a client]

=== 000352c0 [PLATE]
Runs the class-change candidate list of the village church: shows up to three of the caller's candidates side by side with their walk icon, name, target class and level, and hands back which one the player picked.

Algorithm:
Loops until the player confirms or cancels. Each pass takes one key event from fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat: scancode 1 (ESC) leaves the loop in the cancel state, 0x1c and 0x39 (Enter, Space) leave it in the confirm state, and the four arrow keys move the cursor -- 0x4d right and 0x4b left by one, 0x50 down and 0x48 up by three -- each guarded so the cursor stays inside 0 .. candidate_count-1 (candidate_count-3 for the downward move), each keeping the window base a multiple of three, and each playing "Beep.wav" through fdps_play_sfx.
It then rebuilds the panel from scratch every pass. malloc(0x5ca0) gives a 0x138-pitch off-screen page and fdps_cel_blit_sprite paints sprite 0 of the window sheet DAT_00069d84 over it. The three window slots i = 0,1,2 sit at (i*0x65 + 0xb, 9) and a slot is drawn only while window_base + i is still below candidate_count. For such a slot it resolves roster_indices[window_base+i] through fdps_get_roster_record, that record's character id (byte +8) through fdps_get_promotion_record, and the target class from byte +1 of the 3-byte promotion entry that promotion_choices[window_base+i] selects. The slot then carries: the selection frame (sprite 2 of DAT_000643c0) when it is the slot the cursor sits on, Command.cel sprites 0x2a and 0x2b to the left and right of the icon, the member's 24x24 walk icon blitted in mode 0 through fdps_blit_dispatch out of the sprite cache DAT_00060138 at the group given by that roster index times 0xc plus the animation frame (DAT_00069d64/6 & 3, with 3 folded back to 1, so the cycle runs 0,1,2,1), the character's name as message character_id+1 and the target class as message class_code+0xa1, both through FUN_0001ff60 with the text bank DAT_000643c4, Command.cel sprite 0x3a, and the roster record's level (byte +0x21) as a two-digit figure through fdps_draw_number.
Two scroll arrows follow, blinking on DAT_00069d64/5 & 1: sprite 0x44/0x45 at page offset 0x6ae when the window is not at the top of the list, sprite 0x46/0x47 at page offset 0x4e96 when more candidates follow it. The pass ends with fdps_cycle_ui_palette, a wait for one VGA vertical retrace on port 0x3da, a fdps_blit_rect of the 0x130 by 0x43 panel from page+0x3ad to the screen at 0xa9c48, free() of the page, and a spin until the timer tick DAT_00069d64 differs from the value the previous pass saved.
On the way out it returns the cursor position when the loop ended in the confirm state and -1 otherwise.

Parameters:
  candidate_count -- how many entries the two arrays hold; the caller counts the party members it found eligible to change class.
  roster_indices -- one party-roster index per candidate; each is resolved through fdps_get_roster_record and is also the sprite-cache group of that member's walk icon.

Returns:

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; hash unique in image]

Rebuild note:
This screen resolves its indices through fdps_get_roster_record, that is the party roster array at DAT_00064108, while its caller fdps_church_promote_loop resolves the same indices through fdps_get_unit_record, the map unit array at DAT_00069cd8. The two arrays are parallel copies with the same 0x50-byte record and the same index, so routing both sides through one accessor compiles and reads right, but it changes which copy the level and the name on screen come from.

=== 000357a0 [PLATE]
Feeds one keyboard scancode into the current chapter's secret-shop unlock code and reports whether that keystroke just completed it.

Algorithm:
Copies the 24-row, 8-byte-per-row scancode table at 0x000310c0 into a 192-byte stack buffer (REP MOVSD with ECX = 0x30). Selects the chapter's row as row (DAT_00069cf4 - 1): the effective address is buffer - 8 + DAT_00069cf4 * 8, so the table covers chapter indices 1..24, the chapters the player sees as 2..25. Compares scancode with the row byte at the running match position DAT_000601c0, a global no other function touches. On a match it increments DAT_000601c0 and returns 1 when the next row byte is 0 (the code's terminator) or the position has reached 8 (the row is full), otherwise 0. On a mismatch it resets DAT_000601c0 to 0, then sets it back to 1 if scancode happens to equal the first byte of the row, so a new attempt can start on the same keystroke that broke the previous one. Four rows are all zero (chapter indices 16, 17, 21, 22) and the caller never passes 0, so those chapters have no code.

Parameters:
  scancode -- one keyboard make code, 0x01..0x7e. fdps_village_signboard_menu takes it from fdps_read_keyboard_queue, masks it to a byte and calls only when it is below 0x7f, so the empty-queue value 0xff and every break code are filtered out before it arrives.

Returns:
  1 when this keystroke completed the chapter's code, 0 otherwise. fdps_village_signboard_menu answers a 1 by writing 5 into the caller's selection word -- the hidden sixth signboard entry, which fdps_run_village_phase dispatches to fdps_run_secret_menu.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set, hash unique in the image; calls nothing and works purely on game state]

Rebuild note:
The row selector is off by one: the effective base is the stack buffer minus 8, so the chapter's row is code[DAT_00069cf4 - 1], not code[DAT_00069cf4]. Writing the obvious code[chapter_index][pos] over the 24-row table copied from 0x000310c0 shifts every chapter's secret code one chapter earlier. The buffer must also stay a plain local array filled by an initializer copy rather than a static const table: for chapter index 0 the original reads uninitialized stack below ESP, whereas a static table would read the eight zero bytes that sit at 0x000310b8.

=== 00036460 [PLATE]
Runs the bar's hidden lucky-draw bonus game, which happens only on 28 January 1998 and only once per program run.

Algorithm:
Copies the ten-entry prize-class table at DAT_000311e0 ({0,3,1,2,3,2,1,3,2,3}) onto the stack, calls _dos_getdate, and returns doing nothing unless the run-once flag DAT_00064110 is still 0 and the system date is year 0x7ce (1998), month 1, day 0x1c (28). When it does run:
  1. Saves the 320x200 VGA page at 0xa0000 into a 0xfa00-byte buffer, opens the village window frame over it with fdps_village_animate_window_zoom, prints message 0x224 of the text table DAT_000643c4 through FUN_0001ff60 at 0xaa3d4 (screen row 131, column 20), and closes the frame.
  2. Loads "Bonus-1.saf" from "MISC.VFS", puts its playback cursor {frame index, tick, resource} on the stack and resets it with fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 1). Allocates a 0x16480-byte (368x248) work buffer and fills in the request fdps_draw_composite_sprite reads: buffer, pitch 0x170, height 0xf8, origin (0x18,0x18), the SAF resource, the cursor's frame index, and the blit mode. Offset 0x2298 into that buffer is the pixel at (24,24), so the inner 320x200 window is what is copied in and presented out.
  3. Fades the reel in over six steps: blit mode 9 (fdps_rle_blit_translucent) with the block {DAT_000653f0 brightness ramp, level, DAT_000643f0 inverse RGB cube} and level counting 15,12,9,6,3,0. Each step zeroes the work buffer, copies the saved screen into its inner window with fdps_blit_rect, draws the reel frame with the sound flag clear, waits for the 0x3DA vertical retrace bit to go high then low, blits the window to 0xa0000, and waits for the tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change.
  4. Switches the request to opaque (mode 0) and spins the reel up: for delay counting 8 down to 1, rand()%10+1 frames are stepped with fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0), which wraps at the end of the ten-frame clip; each frame is drawn with the sound flag set and then presented delay times, one retrace and one tick per present, so the hold per frame shrinks and the reel accelerates.
  5. Calls fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, then runs the reel at one frame per tick while fdps_read_keyboard_queue keeps returning a code above 0x7f, i.e. until the player presses a key.
  6. Spins the reel down: for delay counting 1 up to 8, rand()%3+1 frames each held delay ticks, so it slows to a stop.
  7. Awards the prize by switching on the local at [EBP-0xc], which nothing has written yet -- see the rebuild note. Case 0 loads "Bonus.wav" from "MISC.VFS", starts it with fdps_audio_start_wav, hands every roster member item 0xbf + DAT_00069cf4/10 through fdps_roster_add_item_to_all (the 斬鐵劍, one of three power tiers picked by the chapter decade) and waits on fdps_audio_sample_is_playing until the fanfare ends; case 1 calls fdps_roster_add_item_to_all(0xb9) ten times (水晶粒); case 2 adds 0x4e20 (20000) to the party gold at DAT_000643a4; anything else hands out one 0xb4 (藥草). The Bonus.wav buffer is never freed.
  8. Snapshots the screen again, stores prize_table[cursor frame index] into the local the switch has already read, then announces the result: window frame open, message 0x225 + prize_table[cursor frame index], frame closed; then the same again for the closing message 0x229.
  9. Frees the second snapshot, the SAF resource, the work buffer and the first snapshot, and sets DAT_00064110 to 1 so the draw cannot happen again in this run.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [game strings "MISC.VFS" / "Bonus-1.saf" / "Bonus.wav" and game globals, and it calls fdps_vfs_load_entry, fdps_saf_advance_tick, fdps_draw_composite_sprite and fdps_blit_rect, which no linked library object could reference; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The prize is awarded from an uninitialised stack slot. The switch at 0003691a reads [EBP-0xc] and the only store to that slot is at 00036a05, after the switch has already run, so the player is given whatever the previous call left at that address while the message printed afterwards is the real reel result from prize_table[cursor frame index]. Written the obvious way -- read where the reel stopped, then award that prize -- the 斬鐵劍, the ten 水晶粒 and the 20000 gold all become reachable, which is not what the original does: in the original the announcement names the prize the reel landed on and the player always receives the consolation 藥草.

=== 00036af0 [PLATE]
Hands one item to every member of the party roster that still has room for it.

Algorithm:
Loops the index i from 0 while i is below the roster member count DAT_00064114 (the same bound fdps_roster_add_character appends at, and the count of roster records FUN_00022be0 copies into the map unit array). For each i it calls fdps_unit_item_count(i) and skips the member when that returns 8, i.e. when all eight inventory slots are already occupied. It also skips roster slot 3 outright once the current chapter index DAT_00069cf4 has reached 0x17 (chapter 24 as the player counts): that is the slot the village member-select loops at 00032c40 and 000336d0 stop letting the player move onto from the same chapter, because the character holding it leaves the party after chapter 23. Every member that survives both tests gets fdps_unit_add_item(i, item_id), whose result is discarded. Both accessors reach the record through fdps_get_unit_record, which indexes the array pointed at by DAT_00069cd8; during the field/village phase fdps_load_field_chapter_resources points that global straight at the roster array DAT_00064108, so the loop is reading and writing roster records.

Returns:
  Nothing. No result is reported for members that were skipped or whose insertion failed.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set and a unique body hash in the image; the body is domain logic over game globals, calling only game routines and called only by game code]

Rebuild note:

=== 00036bb0 [PLATE]
Chapter 3's turn-scheduled reinforcement event: on each of the player turns 3 through 14 it brings that turn's wave of 石巨神 onto the map, and on the first and the last of those turns the chapter speaks a line as well.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0) and stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14], which it never reads back.

Everything it does is decided by DAT_00069ce8, the battle turn counter -- fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 1, fdps_load_savegame restores it from the save image, and fdps_battle_advance_turn raises it once per turn cycle.

When the counter is 3 it calls fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x13, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d): entry 0x13 of the chapter's text block, drawn straight onto the mode-13h screen at 0xa0000 with a 0x140-byte pitch in the standard message colours -- glyph fill 0xd0, no cell background, outline 0x6d, the three colours every ordinary line of game text is drawn with. Whether a portrait panel opens around the line is decided by the entry's own token stream rather than here: entry 0x13 opens with the speaker token -0x11 followed by character id 0x66, the chapter's 魔導士, so fdps_draw_text opens the message window at that unit and closes it again on the terminator. When the counter is 0xe it draws entry 0x15 instead, also spoken by 0x66; the two tests are mutually exclusive. DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" block for the current map number plus one -- FDETXT03.TXT here -- loaded out of Field.vfs by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources.

Then, unconditionally, fdps_deploy_wave(2, DAT_00069ce8 - 1, 0): the wave number is the turn counter minus one. The literal 2 names only the placement file. fdps_deploy_wave loads "map02.cod" for the spawn coordinates but takes the deployment records themselves from whichever map%02d.dat is resident at DAT_0006013c -- 0x1a-byte records from +0x83, selected on the wave byte at record +0x15 -- so it is the resident map's units that arrive, not map 2's. The two always agree here because map02.dat is the only thing in the shipped data that reaches this handler. Every hit is appended to the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 by fdps_deploy_unit as a 0x50-byte record, raising the unit count at DAT_00060150; the trailing 0 makes fdps_deploy_unit put each unit on the nearest free walkable tile to its scripted spawn point rather than on that tile itself.

Last, when the counter is 3 again, it draws entry 0x14, spoken by character id 6, 尤利安. That test is repeated after the deployment call, so the second line is spoken only once the giants are already standing on the map.

The entry is never called by name: its address is the pointer at 0x000601c4, slot 0 of the 50-entry chapter-event handler table based there. Four kinds of dispatch reach that table -- the turn-event table walked by fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the tile events armed by fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event, the searchable-cell records read by fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor, and the opcode-2 unit death scripts run by fdps_run_death_scripts -- and across every shipped map exactly one of them names slot 0: map02.dat's turn-event table (image offset 0x33 downward, 16 records of {turn, slot, phase}), whose first twelve records are {3, 0, 0} through {14, 0, 0}. Phase 0 is the enemy pass, and fdps_battle_advance_turn runs fdps_battle_run_turn_events(0) after the EnyPhase.saf banner and before it increments the counter at 0001e5fd, so the counter still names the player turn that has just ended -- what the player sees is reinforcements arriving as his own turn closes.

Turns 3 through 14 therefore select waves 2 through 13 of map02.dat: 25 units of enemy id 0x47 at level 6, four on turn 3, three on turn 11, one each on turns 13 and 14 and two on every other turn.

Parameters:
  event_arg -- the one dword every slot of the table at 0x000601c4 is called with. fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches slot 0, pushes a literal 0 at 0002e13e; the tile, searchable-cell and death-script dispatchers of the same table forward a unit index instead. Overwritten with 0 at 00036bbc and never read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom 10.0x or the ailv3.lib set; both callees are game code, and every dispatcher of its handler table is game code]

Rebuild note:
The test DAT_00069ce8 == 3 appears twice, once before the deployment call and once after, because entry 0x13 is spoken before the giants arrive and entry 0x14 after them. Collapsing the two into one if-block puts both lines on screen before the units appear.

Watcom inter-function alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov eax,eax (14 bytes, aligns next entry to 0x36c70).

=== 00036c70 [PLATE]
Chapter 3's ambush trigger: the first time a unit steps onto the trigger region in the middle of map 2 it plays the chapter's scripted line and brings the five wave-1 enemies onto the battlefield.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with an empty local area and stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14], which it never reads back. If the one-shot latch DAT_000640e8 is already non-zero it falls straight through to the epilogue; otherwise it raises that latch to 1 and does two things.

First it calls fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x12, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d), which draws message 0x12 of the current map's text block straight to the mode-13h VGA framebuffer at 0xa0000 with a 0x140-byte pitch; 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the three colour values it forwards unchanged to the glyph drawer fdps_draw_glyph. DAT_00060124 holds "fdetxt%02d.txt" for the current map number plus one -- FDETXT03.TXT for map 2 -- loaded out of Field.vfs by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources. Entry 0x12 of that file is a 30-token stream of three lines totalling 26 glyph ids, broken by two -2 line breaks, with one -17 control carrying 12 in the middle.

Then it calls fdps_deploy_wave(2, 1, 0). That loads "map02.cod", the spawn-point table for map 2, and runs fdps_deploy_unit over every one of the 80 deployment records of the loaded "map%02d.dat" at DAT_0006013c -- 0x1a bytes each from image offset 0x83 -- whose wave byte, record + 0x15, equals 1, appending a 0x50-byte unit record per hit to the array at DAT_00069cd8 and raising the unit count at DAT_00060150. In map02.dat those are records 2 through 6: five level-5 units of enemy id 0x52, whose spawn points in map02.cod are (23,16), (25,15), (24,15), (25,13) and (22,15). The trailing 0 makes fdps_deploy_unit scan for the nearest unoccupied walkable tile to each record's scripted coordinates instead of using those coordinates verbatim.

DAT_000640e8 is not private to this handler. It is one of the 0x20 bytes fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) when a chapter starts, and the one-shot scripted events of several other chapters latch the same byte; chapter 3's other ambush, fdps_chapter_03_event_deploy_wave_14, uses the neighbouring byte DAT_000640e9 so that the two do not block each other.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x000601c8, entry 1 of the 50-entry scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event parks the tile's event code in DAT_00069d90 and fdps_battle_unit_turn calls table[DAT_00069d90](unit_index) once the acting unit's turn is over; fdps_battle_run_turn_events, fdps_battle_system_menu, fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase, fdps_run_death_scripts and fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor reach the same table by their own routes. In the shipped data the only thing that selects entry 1 is map02.dat -- map number 2, the player's chapter 3 -- whose tile-trigger table at map header + 0x31 + 2 * event_id gives event id 1 the pair (handler 1, occasion 0). Occasion 0 is what the four single-step walk animations fdps_walk_step_down, fdps_animate_move_step_up, fdps_animate_move_step_left and fdps_animate_move_step_right report, so the tile trips on the step itself rather than at the end of a turn. Event code 1 is written on 24 cells of M02.dtl, the per-cell event-code layer that fdps_map_load_tile_info republishes in DAT_00069d06: a block spanning x 22..27, y 15..19 plus the lone cell (22,11), which is where the five wolfmen's own spawn points sit.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, in 0 .. DAT_00060150-1: the unit the dispatcher is acting on, here the one that walked onto the trigger tile. Overwritten with 0 at 00036c7c and never read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own handler table, shares the game globals DAT_000640e8 and DAT_00060124 with the rest of that handler family, and has no Function ID hit in the Watcom or ailv3 library sets]

Rebuild note:
DAT_000640e8 is a chapter-scoped latch, not a private one: fdps_chapter_state_reset clears it (with the 0x1f bytes around it) by memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) every time a chapter starts, and fdps_load_savegame restores the same block. Rewriting the guard as a function-local static char done inside this handler is the obvious C for what the assembly does, and it would fire the ambush only once per process -- replaying chapter 3 after a Game Over or a save load would silently skip the wolves. The flag has to stay the shared byte inside the block fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes.

Alignment padding: single 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0x0] NOP form between FUN_00036c70 and FUN_00036cd0.

=== 00036cd0 [PLATE]
Scripted Game Over: ends the current battle in defeat by setting the chapter-event/battle-end code to 1.

Algorithm:
Zeroes its own incoming argument slot, which it never reads -- the family idiom, Watcom reusing the dead parameter slot as the first local -- then stores 1 into the chapter-event/battle-end code at 00069da0 and returns. Value 1 is what main tests for after fdps_battle_player_phase_loop returns: it runs fdps_show_game_over and then fdps_title_screen, and clears 00069da0 back to 0 before looping. The other codes on that global are 0 (battle still running, the value main and fdps_chapter_state_reset install, and the only value fdps_battle_player_phase_loop and fdps_battle_advance_turn keep going on) and 2 (chapter cleared, which sends main through the per-chapter epilogue table at 00060304 and into fdps_run_village_phase).

The function has no static callers. It is entry 2 of the chapter-event handler table based at 000601c4 -- fifty slots, 000601c4..0006028b, with the per-chapter post-action pointers at 0006028c following contiguously -- occupying the pointer slot at 000601cc. The three dispatchers of that table are fdps_battle_run_turn_events (turn-scheduled events, pushes a literal 0), fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor (a searched cell whose record is scripted) and fdps_run_death_scripts (death-script opcode 2), and all three take the slot index out of the loaded map%02d.dat image at 0006013c, the third of them by way of unit record field +0x31, which fdps_deploy_unit copies from the map's deployment record.

Nothing in the shipped data selects this slot. Across all sixty-three map%02d.dat, none of the four fields that carry a handler index names 2: not the 16-entry turn-event table at offset 3 (3 bytes: turn, handler, side), not the 16-entry tile-trigger table at 0x33 (2 bytes: handler, occasion), not a searchable-cell record with kind >= 2 at 0x53 (3 bytes: kind, payload word -- the only two such records in the game, map07.dat cells 6 and 7, carry payload 0), and not a deployment-record death script (0x83 + 0x1a * i, opcode at +0x16, signed operand at +0x17). Every one of the other forty-nine slots is named at least once. Scripted defeat is written in the data as death-script opcode 5 instead, which fdps_run_death_scripts handles inline by storing the same 1 into 00069da0; seven deployment records across map00, map01, map03, map04, map05, map07 and map14 use it, and those are the guard units whose death loses the chapter. So this handler is the table's one unused entry, functionally superseded by that opcode.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the unit whose event fired; fdps_battle_run_turn_events passes 0 for events with no unit attached. Present only because every slot of the table shares one function-pointer type; this handler ignores it.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the Watcom or ailv3.lib sets and the body hash is unique in the image; its one data reference, 00069da0, is game state shared with main, fdps_chapter_state_reset, fdps_battle_advance_turn and fdps_battle_player_phase_loop, and it is dispatched from a game-owned table]

Rebuild note:
Unreferenced is not removable. The handler table is indexed unchecked by a byte out of the map file, so this function has to be emitted and it has to stay in slot 2; dropping it as dead code and closing the gap in the table initialiser renumbers slots 3..49 and misfires every later chapter's scripted events.

=== 00036d00 [PLATE]
Chapter 2's turn-10 event: takes seven of the cave's enemies out of their hold-position behaviour so that they start advancing on the player.

Algorithm:
Stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot at 00036d0c and never reads it again, then runs four copies of one loop, one per unit index range: 0x13..0x15, 0x11..0x11, 0x0d..0x0d and 0x08..0x09. Each copy parks its three constants (first index, last index, and the value 0) in one set of locals, copies them into a second set, and then walks i from first to last inclusive (CMP [EBP-0x8],[EBP-0x10] / JLE at 00036d43, and the same shape at 00036da3, 00036e03 and 00036e63), calling fdps_get_unit_record(i) and storing back (record[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0. The four loops are fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range expanded inline with the constant argument triples (0x13, 0x15, 0), (0x11, 0x11, 0), (0x0d, 0x0d, 0) and (8, 9, 0); the single-index ranges do run once, because the comparison is inclusive.

The low nibble of unit record byte 0x34 is the behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on, and the high nibble is left alone because bits 0x40 and 0x80 of the same byte are independent flags. Clearing the mode to 0 takes a unit off the hold-position chain (mode 2, which acts only once its threat weights cross a threshold) and puts it on the default chain that paths it toward the nearest opposing unit.

The function has no static callers. It is entry 3 of the event-handler table based at 000601c4, occupying the pointer slot at 000601d0, and is reached from fdps_battle_run_turn_events, FUN_0001d990 (script opcode 2) and FUN_000184f0, all of which call through that table with a single pushed dword. map01.dat, chapter 2's map, is the only file in the game that names slot 3: its 16-entry turn-event table (three-byte records at offset 3, turn / handler / side) holds the single live record (turn 10, handler 3, side 0), so the event fires once, on turn 10 of chapter 2. map01.dat reserves two player deployment slots, so the seven unit indices resolve to its deployment records 6 and 7 (enemy id 0x4f), 11 (id 0x52), 15, 17 and 18 (id 0x4a) and 19 (id 0x65, the chapter's lone level-8 caster) -- and those are exactly seven of the thirteen records the map deploys in behaviour mode 2.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the unit whose event fired; fdps_battle_run_turn_events pushes 0 for turn-scheduled events, which is the path this handler is reached by. Present only because every slot of the table shares one function-pointer type; this handler ignores it.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and mutates the game's unit records; reached only through a game-owned dispatch table; no Function ID hit in the Watcom or ailv3.lib sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

=== 00036e9a [EOL]
Alignment padding: single 6-byte Watcom NOP form 8d 80 00 00 00 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]).

=== 00036ea0 [PLATE]
Chapter 3's tile-triggered reinforcement: the first time a unit that is not enemy-side finishes acting on the map's trigger tile, the chapter speaks a line and map 2's four wave-14 enemies come onto the battlefield.

Algorithm:
Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and does nothing unless two conditions both hold: the one-shot latch DAT_000640e9 is still 0, and the unit's side byte at record+6 is non-zero. Side 0 is the hostile side -- fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies wipes exactly the side-0 units, and FUN_000232b0 stamps that byte from byte 0 of the map's deployment record -- so the non-zero test stops an enemy that walks over the tile from firing the event. When both hold it raises DAT_000640e9 to 1 and does two things.
First it calls FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x16, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d): message 0x16 of the chapter text table whose base is DAT_00060124, rendered straight onto the mode-13h framebuffer at 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140 = 320 and the three glyph palette indices 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d that this whole handler family passes.
Then it calls FUN_00023830(2, 0xe, 0), which walks the 0x1a-byte deployment records of map 2 -- map02.dat, 80 records starting at +0x83 -- and deploys every record whose wave key at +0x15 is 0x0e. Map 2 has four such records, all with side byte 0, so wave 14 is four enemy units.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, naming the unit that has just finished acting. The dispatchers of the chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4 (fdps_battle_unit_turn at 0x00015839 for a player-controlled unit, FUN_00012960 at 0x00012a33 for an AI-driven one) push it once fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event has left this handler's id, 4, in DAT_00069d90. The other dispatcher of the same table, fdps_battle_run_turn_events, pushes a constant 0, which this handler would read as unit 0.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the watcom or ail sets; calls fdps_get_unit_record, reads and writes the game globals DAT_000640e9 and DAT_00060124, and its entry is held in slot 4 of the game's chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4]

Rebuild note:
DAT_000640e9 is not this handler's private latch. It is one byte of the 0x20-byte chapter-event state block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) at every chapter start and that fdps_load_savegame memmoves in from the save image (save offset +0x30a3), and other chapters give the same byte other jobs -- FUN_00037600 uses it as an incrementing counter, FUN_00038400 and FUN_00039060 as their own one-shot latches. Writing the guard as the obvious function-local 'static char done = 0;' compiles and looks right, but it would fire the reinforcement only once per process (replaying chapter 3 after a Game Over or a save load would silently skip it) and would drop the byte out of the saved state. Second, the map number handed to FUN_00023830 is the literal 2, not the current-chapter global DAT_00069cf4; substituting the global would load the wrong MAP%02d.COD spawn coordinates for the four units.

=== 00036f0f [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP: alignment padding between FUN_00036ea0 and FUN_00036f10.

=== 00036f10 [PLATE]
Chapter 3's turn-limit defeat: when the 22-turn deadline for killing the chapter's mage runs out, the sealed stone giants pour onto the map and the chapter ends in defeat.

Algorithm:
Zeroes its own incoming argument slot at 00036f1c and never reads it again. Renders game message string 0x17 straight onto the mode-13h VGA framebuffer through the message-token renderer fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x17, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) -- the chapter text table, the message index, destination 0xa0000, pitch 0x140 = 320, then the three glyph colours the whole handler family passes (0xd0 foreground, 0 background, 0x6d outline); those last three are forwarded to fdps_draw_glyph and are not a blit geometry. String 0x17 is the last of the 24 entries in the chapter's text file and opens with the portrait control code -0x11 followed by 102, so the line is spoken by enemy template 0x66, chapter 3's mage. Then calls fdps_deploy_wave(2, 0xf, 0): map 2 is chapter 3, the chapter ids being 0-based, and every deployment record of that map's script whose trigger byte at record+0x15 equals 0x0f is placed -- in chapter 3's script 44 records of enemy template 0x47 at level 6, the stone giants; place_exact 0 means each one is put not on its scripted tile but on the free tile nearest to it. Finally stores 1 into the chapter-event/battle-end code at 00069da0 and returns. 1 is the defeat code main tests for after fdps_battle_player_phase_loop returns, sending it into fdps_show_game_over and then fdps_title_screen; the other codes on that global are 0 (battle still running) and 2 (chapter cleared), as fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions records.

Unlike the other handlers that bring units on, this one never shows them: fdps_chapter_04_event_for_turn deploys and then moves the map cursor and runs twelve frames of fdps_render_view_frame, and chapter 3's own slots 1 and 4 at least leave the battle running so the next redraw picks the new units up. Here the store to the battle-end code is the instruction after the deployment and the handler returns, so on the code alone the 44 giants enter the unit array and the battle ends.

The function has no static callers. It is entry 5 of the event-handler table based at 000601c4, occupying the pointer slot at 000601d8. Chapter 3's script image is the only file in the game that names slot 5: its 16-entry turn-event table of three-byte records at offset 3 (turn / handler / side) schedules handler 0 on turns 3 through 14 -- the twelve turn-end reinforcement waves the strategy guide lists for this chapter -- and holds one further record, turn 0x16 with handler 5 and side 0, so this handler fires once, on the enemy pass of turn 22, the turn on which the chapter's stated victory deadline expires.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the unit whose event fired; fdps_battle_run_turn_events pushes 0 for turn-scheduled events, which is the path this handler is reached by. Present only because every slot of the table shares one function-pointer type; this handler ignores it.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own handler table at 000601c4, whose dispatchers are all settled fdps; writes the battle-end code 00069da0 it shares with main, fdps_chapter_state_reset and fdps_battle_advance_turn, and calls the game routines fdps_draw_text and fdps_deploy_wave; no Function ID candidate in the Watcom or ailv3.lib sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
The trailing arguments 0xd0, 0, 0x6d that this handler and its whole family pass to fdps_draw_text are the foreground, background and outline palette indices forwarded to fdps_draw_glyph -- they are not a 320x208 region and a colour key, even though 0xd0 next to the pitch 0x140 reads exactly like one. Emitting the call as a full-screen blit instead of a message render loses the dialogue entirely.

Second, the map number handed to fdps_deploy_wave here is the literal 2, not the current-chapter global DAT_00069cf4 that most sibling handlers pass; substituting the global would load the wrong MAP%02d.COD spawn coordinates for the 44 giants.

Third, do not add a redraw after the deployment. Writing this handler the obvious way -- deploy the reinforcements, show them, then end the battle -- inserts a frame the original never draws: the store to the battle-end code follows the deploy call immediately, and the one handler in the family that does want its reinforcements seen spells the redraw out. Whatever the player sees at turn 22 comes from the battle-end path, not from here.

=== 00036f64 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte LEA NOP forms aligning next function entry to 0x36f70.

=== 00036f70 [PLATE]
Chapter 4's turn-scheduled event handler: on the enemy pass of turn 3 it speaks the chapter's scripted line, and on the enemy pass of turn 5 it brings the map's wave-5 enemy reinforcements onto the battlefield, shows them to the player and announces them.

Algorithm:
Reads the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 to tell its two scheduled firings apart.

When the counter is 3 it renders game message 0x17 straight onto the mode-13h VGA framebuffer through the message-token renderer FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x17, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) -- the chapter text buffer that fdps_load_field_chapter_resources loads as "fdetxt%02d.txt" for chapter index + 1, the message index, destination 0xa0000, pitch 0x140 = 320, then the three glyph colours the whole handler family forwards to fdps_draw_glyph (0xd0 foreground, 0 background, 0x6d outline) -- and returns. Message 0x17 of fdetxt04.txt opens with the portrait control code -0x11 followed by 98 and switches to -0x11 101 half way through, so the line is an exchange between enemy templates 0x62 and 0x65.

Otherwise -- turn 5, the only other turn map03.dat schedules this slot for -- it runs the reinforcement sequence:
  1. FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 5, 0) deploys every deployment record of the current map whose wave byte (record+0x15) is 5, each placed on the free tile nearest its scripted tile rather than on the tile itself. In map03.dat that is seven enemies: one level-8 mage (template 0x66), four level-7 infantry (0x62) and two level-6 cavalry (0x58), scripted along the low-x, high-y edge of the map.
  2. fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(0x1f) parks the map cursor on unit 0x1f, one of the seven records just appended, and fdps_render_view_frame then runs twelve times so the player sees the view sitting over the arrivals. The loop counter is the function's own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14], overwritten at 00036fca.
  3. Message 0x18 is rendered exactly as message 0x17 was; it is the announcement line, spoken by enemy template 0x65.
  4. The behaviour-mode nibble of unit records 0xf..0x12, and then of unit record 0xd, is cleared: for each index fdps_get_unit_record(i) is called and rec[0x34] is rewritten as (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0. The low nibble is the behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on, mode 0 being the default chain that paths a unit toward the nearest opposing unit; the high nibble is masked back in because bits 0x40 and 0x80 of the same byte are independent per-unit flags. Both ranges are inclusive, and both are the inline expansion of the same three-argument (first, last, mode) set-range helper that the other chapter event handlers expand: the constants are staged at [EBP-0x20]/[EBP-0x1c]/[EBP-0x18] and [EBP-0x24]/[EBP-0x28]/[EBP-0x2c], copied into the inlined callee's own parameter slots, and only then walked. map03.dat already authors all five of those units at mode 0 (deployment record byte 0x11, which FUN_000232b0 copies into record byte 0x34 at 0002379d), so against the shipped data this step changes nothing unless play has moved them off mode 0.

The entry has no static callers. Its address sits in the relocated pointer at 000601dc, slot (0x601dc - 0x601c4) / 4 = 6 of the chapter-event handler table based at 000601c4, which fdps_battle_run_turn_events, FUN_0001d990 and FUN_000184f0 all call through with a single pushed dword. In the shipped Field.vfs the only thing that names slot 6 is map03.dat's turn-event table -- the three-byte (turn, handler, side) records at file offset 3, which hold (3, 6, 0) and (5, 6, 0) -- so the handler fires twice, both times on the enemy pass, i.e. immediately after the player's third and fifth turns end. Map 3 is chapter index 3, the chapter the player sees as chapter 4.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the unit whose event fired; fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches this slot, pushes 0. Present only because every slot of the table shares one function-pointer type. The incoming value is never read: the turn-5 path stores 0 over the slot at 00036fca and uses it as the 0..11 frame counter.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own event-handler table at 000601c4, whose dispatchers are all settled fdps; calls the game routines FUN_0001ff60, FUN_00023830, fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, fdps_render_view_frame and fdps_get_unit_record, and edits the game's unit records; no Function ID candidate in the Watcom or ailv3.lib sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
The two behaviour-mode loops have to stay read-modify-writes that mask with 0xf0; they must not be written as rec[0x34] = 0. The mode being stored is a constant zero, so clearing the whole byte looks equivalent, but bits 0x40 and 0x80 of that byte are independent per-unit flags that FUN_00012c10 tests at 00012c6f and FUN_000132b0 at 0001337d, and zeroing them changes how those units behave for the rest of the battle. Both loops are also inclusive of their last index -- 0xf..0x12 and 0xd..0xd -- so the natural half-open for (i = 0xf; i < 0x12; i++) drops unit 0x12, and a half-open second loop skips unit 0xd altogether.

=== 000370d2 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov eax,eax, 14 bytes to 16-byte boundary at 000370e0

=== 000370e0 [PLATE]
Chapter 5's ambush trigger: takes every enemy on the map out of its hold-position behavior and puts it into the mode that walks it toward the player, so the imperial army starts its all-out attack. Runs once per chapter.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with a 0x20-byte local area and stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] at 000370ec, never reading what the dispatcher passed. It then tests the one-shot flag DAT_000640e8 and returns immediately when it is already 1; otherwise it sets it to 1 and runs the rest of the body. DAT_000640e8 is element 0x10 of the 0x20-byte per-chapter event flag array based at DAT_000640d8, which fdps_chapter_state_reset clears with memset(DAT_000640d8, 0, 0x20) at 00022788 and which fdps_battle_system_submenu copies into the save image at +0x30a3 (000151a6), so the flag survives a save and reload but not a change of chapter. Chapter 5's opening script uses no opcode 0x13, so it writes none of those flags and this one is 0 when the battle opens.

The guarded body is the inline expansion of a range-set helper called with (6, 0x22, 0): the three argument values are staged as the locals 6, 0x22 and 0 at [EBP-0x20]/[EBP-0x1c]/[EBP-0x18], copied into the inlined routine's own parameter slots [EBP-0xc]/[EBP-0x10]/[EBP-0x14], and the loop then runs i from 6 while i <= 0x22 (CMP [EBP-0x8],[EBP-0x10] / JLE at 00037133, so an inclusive range), calling fdps_get_unit_record(i) and writing rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0.

The low nibble of unit record byte 0x34 is the actor behavior mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step masks with 0xf at 00010062 and dispatches on; the high nibble carries separate per-unit flags that fdps_map_actor_take_best_action tests at 00012c6f (bit 0x40) and fdps_score_targets_for_item tests at 0001337d (bit 0x80), which is why the write masks with 0xf0 instead of storing 0. Mode 0's handler chain is fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, resting through fdps_unit_rest only when all three decline. map04.dat deploys most of these units in mode 2 (deployment record byte 0x11, which fdps_deploy_unit copies into record byte 0x34 at 00023177); mode 2's chain is fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack -- which only scores and always returns 0 -- and fdps_unit_rest, so a mode-2 unit fights whatever comes within reach and never advances.

Which units indices 6..0x22 are is settled by the shipped data, deployment order included. map04.dat's header gives 5 player slots (byte 1) and 33 deployment records (byte 2), each 0x1a bytes wide from +0x83. fdps_build_map_unit_array lays the 5 party records at indices 0..4; fdps_chapter_state_reset then deploys wave 0, whose single record is the map's only side-1 unit -- the level 10 guest hero, character index 0x0c -- so he takes index 5. Everything else is appended by chapter 5's opening IconAni script Icon04.dat, whose opcode 0x04 calls fdps_deploy_wave three times and in this order: wave 2 (one record, index 6), wave 3 (one record, index 7), wave 1 (27 records, indices 8..0x22). Three of the 33 records carry wave 0xff and are never deployed. The whole map is therefore on the battlefield before the trigger tile can fire, and the loop never runs past the end of the unit array.

Indices 6 and 7 are the two enemy-side actors of that opening scene, and the same script retires both with opcode 9 before it ends, so the live enemies are 8..0x22: by the class byte +1 of their EnemyDat.dat records those 27 are 5 mages, 6 swordsmen, 8 knights and 8 archers, exactly the enemy roster the chapter's walkthrough lists. Six of the 27 -- deployment records 13..18, three knights and three archers -- already carry behavior byte 0x00, so for them this write changes nothing; they are the group the walkthrough singles out as the one that attacks of its own accord from the start, every other enemy staying put until the trigger fires.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the relocated pointer at 0x000601e0, slot (0x601e0 - 0x601c4) / 4 = 7 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped Field.vfs the only thing that names slot 7 is map04.dat's tile-trigger table, the 2-byte entries at file offset 0x31: trigger id 1 holds {handler 7, phase 0} and all fifteen other entries are 0xff, while the map's sixteen turn-event records at file offset 3 are 0xff throughout. fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event latches that handler index into DAT_00069d90 when the tile a unit is standing on carries that trigger id and the phase byte equals its own third argument; the four movement-step routines fdps_animate_move_step_down / fdps_walk_step_up / fdps_animate_move_step_left / fdps_animate_step_right that fdps_animate_move_path calls once per traced step pass 0 there, while fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and fdps_battle_unit_turn pass 1 at the end of an action. So this event fires the moment a unit walks across the trigger tile. Each dispatcher resets DAT_00069d90 to 0xff before the action and, if it is no longer 0xff afterwards, calls that slot with the acting unit's index pushed, cleaning the stack with ADD ESP,0x4.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the unit whose movement latched this event; the single dword every slot of the table at 0x000601c4 is called with. Overwritten with 0 at 000370ec and never read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [slot in the game's own event-handler table at 000601c4, whose other slot owners are all fdps; its only callee is the game routine fdps_get_unit_record at 0002d210, which a separately compiled library object could not reference, and Function ID finds no candidate in the Watcom 10.0x libraries or in ailv3.lib]

Rebuild note:
Two ways the obvious C goes wrong. The write is rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, not rec[0x34] = 0: the high nibble of that byte holds separate per-unit flags read by fdps_map_actor_take_best_action at 00012c6f (bit 0x40) and fdps_score_targets_for_item at 0001337d (bit 0x80), so modelling byte 0x34 as a plain behavior-mode field and storing 0 wipes them and sends the affected units down a different AI path. And the loop bound is inclusive -- CMP/JLE, i <= 0x22 -- so the literals 6 and 0x22 are the first and last unit index, not a half-open range; writing for (i = 6; i < 0x22; i++) leaves the last enemy holding position.

=== 0003716a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte Watcom NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0] between FUN_000370e0 and FUN_00037170.

=== 00037170 [PLATE]
Chapter 6's cavalry-death ambush: when the enemy cavalryman posted in the lower right of the map is killed, the map's second wave of enemy reinforcements marches in at the lower left, the chapter's guest hero speaks his line over it, and every enemy already on the map is released from hold-position into the all-out attack.

Algorithm:
Standard Watcom four-push frame with a 0x20-byte local area. It never reads the dword the dispatcher passed; [EBP+0x14] is reused at 00037199 as the counter of the frame-hold loop.

1. fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, 2, 0) at 00037187 deploys wave 2: every 0x1a-byte deployment record of the resident "map%02d.dat" whose wave byte +0x15 is 2, appended to the unit array in file order. For map05.dat those are records 19, 20, 21, 22, 25, 26 and 28 -- three of id 0x62 at level 10, two of id 0x5d at level 9, one of id 0x58 at level 8 and one of id 0x66 at level 10 -- landing at unit indices 0x1d..0x23. The third argument 0 is place_exact: 0 makes fdps_deploy_unit sweep the map grid for the nearest free walkable tile instead of taking the placement anchor verbatim. It has to be 0 here. The seven MAP05.COD anchors for these records are (3,8), (4,8), (3,9), (4,9), (2,9), (5,9) and (5,8) -- the lower left corner -- and the wave-0 guest hero starts at (3,8), inside that block.
2. fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(0x1e) parks the map cursor, and with it the view, on the second of the seven arrivals, and twelve calls to fdps_render_view_frame hold the picture there long enough for the player to see them.
3. fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0xd, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) paints message 0x0d of the chapter's text table straight onto the mode-13h framebuffer with a 0x140-byte pitch, in the glyph colours 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d -- the same three constants fdps_run_death_scripts uses for the scripted lines it prints itself. DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" blob loaded for chapter index + 1, here FDETXT06.TXT, whose 14-entry 16-bit offset table makes 0x0d its last message; that message opens with the word pair ef ff 0c 00 -- portrait token -0x11 carrying character id 0x0c -- and id 0x0c is map05.dat's one side-1 record, the chapter's guest hero, so he is the speaker.
4. The rest of the body is fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range(4, 0x22, 0) expanded inline: the three argument values are staged as the locals at [EBP-0x20]/[EBP-0x1c]/[EBP-0x18], copied into the inlined routine's own parameter slots [EBP-0xc]/[EBP-0x10]/[EBP-0x14], and i then runs from 4 while i <= 0x22 (CMP [EBP-0x8],[EBP-0x10] / JLE at 0003720a, so inclusive at both ends), calling fdps_get_unit_record(i) and writing back (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0.

The low nibble of unit record byte 0x34 is the actor behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on: mode 0 walks the unit toward the nearest opposing unit, mode 2 -- which 16 of map05.dat's 32 records deploy in (deployment byte +0x11) -- only fights what comes within reach and never advances. The high nibble carries per-unit flags that other code tests (fdps_map_actor_take_best_action reads bit 0x40, fdps_score_targets_for_item reads bit 0x80), which is why the write masks with 0xf0 instead of storing 0.

What the range covers. Byte 1 of map05.dat is 4, the player deployment count, so the party holds units 0..3; byte 2 is 0x20, its 32 deployment records, and no record carries wave 0xff, so all 32 reach the map and the live unit count ends at 0x24. Wave 0 is records 0 and 31 and takes units 4 (an enemy) and 5 (the guest hero, side byte 1, deployed in behaviour mode 3); wave 1 is 23 records and takes 6..0x1c; wave 2 is the seven records above and takes 0x1d..0x23. So the loop covers everything on the map except the player party and the last arrival, and the low bound 4 is chosen rather than copied: the address neighbour fdps_chapter_05_event_enemies_advance starts its own copy of this loop at 6 to skip its allied hero at index 5, while this one starts at 4 and pulls the guest hero out of mode 3 into mode 0 with the enemies. Only the wave-0 and wave-1 units are actually changed by it: all seven wave-2 records deploy with behaviour byte +0x11 already 0, so iterations 0x1d..0x22 rewrite what is already there and the omission of 0x23 changes nothing.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the relocated pointer at 0x000601e4, slot (0x601e4 - 0x601c4) / 4 = 8 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. Scanning all 63 shipped MAP*.DAT over the three tables that can name a slot -- the 16 three-byte turn-event records at file offset 3, the 2-byte tile-trigger records that follow them, and the script at +0x16 of every deployment record -- names slot 8 in exactly one place: map05.dat deployment record 7, {opcode 2, operand 8}. fdps_run_death_scripts turns opcode 2 into a call of that slot with the acting unit's index pushed and ADD ESP,0x4 after it, and it runs the scripts of the units a battle action has just killed, so this is a unit's on-death script. Record 7 is an id 0x58 level-8 unit that wave 1 puts at unit index 0x0c in behaviour mode 2, with the MAP05.COD anchor (23,8) -- the lower right of the map.

The guide's chapter 6 page describes the same event and its two enemy groups match the file record for record. First group LV10 魔導士 x3 / LV10 步兵 x9 / LV9 弓兵 x7 / LV8 騎兵 x5 against waves 0+1's id 0x66 level 10 x3, 0x62 level 10 x9, 0x5d level 9 x7 and 0x58 level 8 x5; second group LV10 魔導士 x1 / LV10 步兵 x3 / LV9 弓兵 x2 / LV8 騎兵 x1 against wave 2's 0x66 x1, 0x62 x3, 0x5d x2 and 0x58 x1. That fixes id 0x58 as 騎兵, the cavalryman of the event line 當右下方第一個騎兵被殺死時，左下方立即出現敵方援軍，同時開始總攻擊 -- and the one 騎兵 of the five that carries a death script is the one at (23,8). The friendly listed on the same page, LV10 英雄索爾, is the side-1 character id 0x0c who speaks message 0x0d.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array whose base pointer is at DAT_00069cd8, in 0 .. DAT_00060150-1; the single dword every dispatcher of the table at 0x000601c4 pushes. On the one path that reaches this slot it is the dying cavalryman, unit 0x0c. Overwritten with 0 at 00037199 and never read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [dispatched from a game function-pointer table whose other slot owners are all fdps; calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_render_view_frame and mutates the game's unit records; no Function ID candidate in either library set]

Rebuild note:
Keep the behaviour write as rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0; storing 0 over the whole byte clears the high-nibble flags at 0x40 and 0x80 that other code tests. Keep 4 and 0x22 as literals with an inclusive upper bound, and keep place_exact 0 on the deployment call.

=== 00037250 [PLATE]
Chapter 7's turn-2 event: puts all five of the arena's opponents into the behaviour mode in which they close on the player, so the champion stops holding her ground.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with a 0x20-byte local area and stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] at 0003725c -- the source reuses the parameter as a scratch variable and never reads what was passed in. The rest of the body is the inline expansion of fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range(4, 8, 0): the three actual arguments are materialised as the locals 4, 8 and 0 at [EBP-0x20]/[EBP-0x1c]/[EBP-0x18], copied into the inlined routine's own parameter slots [EBP-0xc]/[EBP-0x10]/[EBP-0x14], and the loop then runs i from 4 while i <= 8 -- JLE, so an inclusive range covering units 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 -- calling fdps_get_unit_record(i) and writing rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0.

The low nibble of unit record byte 0x34 is the actor behaviour mode that fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on; the high nibble carries flags other code tests (FUN_00012c10 reads bit 0x40, FUN_000132b0 reads bit 0x80) and the AND 0xf0 preserves it. Mode 0 is the mode whose handler chain runs FUN_00012c10, then FUN_000126b0 (step along the traced movement path), then FUN_000127c0 (move toward the nearest opposing unit), and rests via FUN_000120d0 only when all three decline. Mode 2 replaces those two movement steps with FUN_00012230, which only scores and always returns 0, so a mode-2 unit acts where it stands and never advances.

Indices 4..8 are exactly this chapter's five enemies, and the opening cutscene names them. map06.dat header byte 1 = 4 is the player deployment count (DAT_00064118) and byte 2 = 5 the map's own unit count (DAT_0006410c); fdps_build_map_unit_array lays the 4 party records down at indices 0..3 and then calls fdps_deploy_wave(map_no, 0, 1), which places nothing, because all five deployment records carry wave tag 1 or 2 at +0x15. The waves come from Icon06.dat, the IconAni script fdps_chapter_07_init runs: its opcode 4 is fdps_deploy_wave(chapter, wave, phase), and the script contains 04 01 00 at file offset 0xe4 followed by 04 02 00 at 0x112. Wave 1 is deployment records 1..4, four identical units with level byte +4 = 0x0e and behaviour byte +0x11 = 0x00, and the walk opcode immediately after that deploy addresses units 4, 5, 6 and 7. Wave 2 is record 0, the one 0x0f unit, deployed with behaviour byte 0x02, and the walk opcode after it addresses unit 8. All five carry deployment byte 0 == 0, which fdps_deploy_unit stores as unit record side byte +6 (0002366c), the enemy side. That is the guide's chapter 7 roster: one LV15 裘娜 and four LV14 mercenaries.

So four of the five are already in mode 0 when this fires and the loop is a no-op for them: no code path between the cutscene and turn 2 writes byte 0x34 -- fdps_icon_script_run and every one of its opcode handlers leave the byte alone, slot 9 is the only handler-table slot map06.dat names, and the only other writers in the image are fdps_deploy_unit, which sets it from the deployment record, and the one branch of fdps_map_actor_behavior_step that writes 7 alongside "Chess.wav". The event's real effect is on unit 8, the champion, who is deployed in mode 2 and begins advancing from turn 2 on. The loop covers the whole enemy force because that is how the shared helper is called, not because the other four need it.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the relocated pointer at 0x000601e8, slot (0x601e8 - 0x601c4) / 4 = 9 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the whole of the shipped Field.vfs the only thing that names slot 9 is map06.dat's turn-event table -- the single entry {turn 2, slot 9, phase 0} at file offset 3. fdps_battle_run_turn_events fires it during the phase-0 pass that follows the player's second turn, pushing a literal 0 at 0002e13e.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit the dispatcher is acting on, in 0 .. DAT_00060150-1. Every dispatch site through the table at 0x000601c4 pushes one; fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only one that reaches this slot, always pushes 0. Overwritten with 0 at 0003725c and never read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only callee is fdps_get_unit_record and every dispatcher of its table is game code]

Rebuild note:
Unit record byte 0x34 is packed: the low nibble is the behaviour mode, the high nibble carries flags that FUN_00012c10 (bit 0x40) and FUN_000132b0 (bit 0x80) test. The event sets the mode with rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, so the obvious rewrite rec[0x34] = 0 -- natural if the byte is modelled as a plain mode field -- silently clears those flags as well. The loop bound is inclusive too: the literals 4 and 8 are the first and last unit index, not a half-open range, so writing for (i = 4; i < 8; i++) leaves the fifth unit, the champion at index 8, in the standing mode she was deployed in -- and she is the only one of the five the event actually changes.

=== 000372ca [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0x0] NOP form between FUN_00037250 and FUN_000372d0

=== 000372d0 [PLATE]
Chapter 8's turn-scheduled event handler: the one slot map07.dat names for all five of the chapter's turn events, running whichever of them is due for the turn the player has just finished.

Algorithm:
Stores 0 over its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] at 000372dc and never reads it back. Rebuild note:

Rebuild note:
Two ways the obvious C diverges. The store is a read-modify-write, record[0x34] = (record[0x34] & 0xf0) | 4, not record[0x34] = 4: the high nibble of that byte holds separate per-unit flags that fdps_map_actor_take_best_action (bit 0x40, at 00012c6f) and fdps_score_targets_for_item (bit 0x80, at 0001337d) test, so modelling byte 0x34 as a plain behaviour-mode field and storing 4 wipes them and sends the unit down a different AI path. And unit 0x13 is written with no existence check: fdps_deploy_unit sizes the array at DAT_00069cd8 to exactly DAT_00060150 * 0x50, and until the turn-3 cutscene deploys map07.dat's single wave-1 record the battle holds 19 records, indices 0..0x12, so if the soldier of record 18 dies before then the original writes offset 0x13 * 0x50 + 0x34 = 0x624 of a 0x5f0-byte allocation. Adding the natural guard `if (0x13 < DAT_00060150)` removes an out-of-bounds write the original performs, and neither version makes 費塔加 walk -- which is the guide's 如果在費塔加出現前就已經清光敵人，那麼他便不會去開牢門 (clear the enemies before he appears and he never goes to open the cell).

=== 00037600 [PLATE]
Chapter 8's villager-escape event: one of the four captive villagers walks off the battlefield and speaks its line, and once the last of the four is gone the chapter's reward item lands in 費塔加's bag, scaled to how many villagers got out alive.

Algorithm:
Does nothing unless unit_index is one of chapter 8's four villagers, 15 through 18. Bumps the escaped-villager count DAT_000640e9, a byte of the chapter event flag block that fdps_chapter_state_reset memsets to 0 on chapter entry, then draws message unit_index + 13 -- 0x1c through 0x1f, one line per villager -- with FUN_0001ff60, taking the message table pointer from DAT_00060124 and painting straight onto the mode-13h screen at 0xa0000 (pitch 0x140, 0xd0 rows, colour key 0x6d). Then it asks fdps_unit_is_retired about each of units 15..18 and counts how many are already out of the battle. When exactly 3 are out -- meaning this villager is the last one still in -- and DAT_000640e9 is above 1, so at least two of the four escaped rather than died, it draws the closing line (0x20 when the last villager out is unit 15 or 16, 0x21 when it is 17 or 18) and calls fdps_unit_add_item(0x13, item) to put the reward in the guest mage 費塔加's bag: item 0xc8 炎之寶石 for two escapes, 0xda 速度藥水 for three, 0xdd 風精之羽 for all four. Whatever the count, it finishes by writing 1 into byte 5 of this unit's record, fetched through fdps_get_unit_record -- the retired flag fdps_unit_is_retired reads -- which takes the villager out of the battle. fdps_chapter_08_post_action then reads the same two things: all four villagers retired with DAT_000640e9 non-zero is victory, all four retired with it still zero is defeat.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array whose base pointer is at DAT_00069cd8, supplied by the chapter script event dispatcher that reaches this handler through the table slot at 000601f8. Only 15..18, chapter 8's four captive villagers, do anything; every other value returns immediately.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_unit_add_item and the game's message renderer, and is entered only through a game handler-table slot; zero Function ID candidates against the Watcom 10.0x libraries and ailv3.lib, hash unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
Two literal details of the tail decide whether the chapter's reward is ever paid. The retired flag is stored as a whole byte, record[5] = 1, not OR-ed in, so the obvious record[5] |= 1 preserves bits of that byte which the original discards. And the count of retired villagers is taken before this unit is marked retired, which is why the test reads "exactly 3"; moving the mark above the count without also changing the 3 to a 4 makes the reward unreachable.

=== 000378a0 [PLATE]
Chapter 10's stairway ambush: the first time a player-side unit stops on the map's trigger tile, brings on the ten enemy reinforcements of wave 10.

Algorithm:
Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and does nothing unless two conditions both hold: the shared one-shot chapter-event latch DAT_000640e8 is still 0, and the unit's side byte at record+6 is non-zero. Side 2 is the player's own roster (fdps_roster_add_character stamps 2 there), so the non-zero test keeps a side-0 unit that walks over the tile from firing the event. When both hold it sets DAT_000640e8 to 1 and calls FUN_00023830 (0x00023830) with DAT_00069cf4, 10 and 0. DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, which FUN_00023830 formats into "map%02d.cod"; the 10 is the wave key it matches against byte 0x15 of each 0x1a-byte deployment record, ten of which carry wave 10 in MAP09.DAT; the 0 is the placement flag, telling FUN_00023830 to put each unit on the nearest free tile to its scripted coordinates rather than on the coordinates themselves.

The entry is reached only through slot 16 of the chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4, called as 0x601c4 + id*4 by fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_battle_run_turn_events. MAP09.DAT is the only map that names handler 16, in tile-event entry 1, which makes this chapter 10 (map index 9). Chapter 10's other handler, slot 15 at 0x00037780, covers the same map's turn-scheduled waves.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit array at DAT_00069cd8 of the unit that triggered the tile event; fdps_battle_unit_turn passes the unit whose turn just ended. Only the side byte at record+6 is read from it.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls game code fdps_get_unit_record; no Function ID hit in any library]

Rebuild note:
DAT_000640e8 is not this event's own flag. One byte serves as the one-shot latch for a dozen different chapter event handlers (0x36c70, 0x370e0, 0x374e0, this one, 0x37b70, 0x37cd0, 0x381d0, 0x38380, 0x38b60, 0x38e60, 0x39230, 0x39770) and is read as a completion test by the chapter 14, 15 and 26 post-action handlers; no code anywhere writes 0 to it, and it lives inside the 0x20 bytes at 0x000640d8 that fdps_load_savegame memmoves in from the save image, so it is saved and restored rather than reset. Rewriting the guard as the obvious function-local `static int fired = 0;` would compile and look right, but it would drop the byte out of the save-state block and decouple these handlers from each other and from the post-action tests that read it.

=== 000378f0 [PLATE]
Chapter 11's turn-scheduled reinforcement event: on turn 4 it brings on the enemy wave that appears around the four corners of the map, on turn 7 the two groups that appear at the top-left and top-right, panning the view onto each of them, and either way it finishes by speaking the chapter's line.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0), so the counter the body's two loops use is the incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] itself.

Everything branches once on DAT_00069ce8, the battle turn counter that fdps_chapter_state_reset sets to 1 and fdps_battle_advance_turn raises once per turn cycle. fdps_battle_run_turn_events reaches this handler only on the turns map10.dat schedules for it, and its 16-entry turn table (file offset 3, three bytes per entry: turn, handler slot, phase) names this slot exactly twice, for turn 4 and turn 7, both in phase 0 -- the end of the player's phase.
