Control then jumps straight to the message draw, with no camera work.

Any other turn -- turn 7, the only other one scheduled: FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 4, 0) brings on map10.dat's sixteen wave-4 records, two tight groups of level-13 units at the top-left (tiles around x 2..5, y 4..6) and top-right (x 16..20, y 1..5). fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(0x34) then puts the map cursor on the top-left group and twelve calls to fdps_render_view_frame hold the view there for twelve rendered frames; fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(0x2c) and twelve more frames do the same for the top-right group. Those two indices are the eleventh and the third unit of that wave: the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 opens with map10.dat's nine player slots (header byte 1), gains the three wave-0 units placed at their exact coordinates when the chapter starts and the fourteen wave-1, wave-2 and wave-3 units that make up the chapter's starting enemy force, then the sixteen wave-5 units on turn 4, so wave 4 lands on indices 0x2a..0x39.

Both paths end on the same call, FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0xf, (byte *)0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d): message 15 of the chapter's text image at DAT_00060124, drawn straight into mode 13h VGA memory at 0xa0000 with a 320-byte destination pitch, in foreground colour 0xd0 over a transparent background with outline colour 0x6d -- the last three values are forwarded unchanged to fdps_draw_glyph. fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads that text image out of Field.vfs as "fdetxt%02d.txt" for map number + 1, so fdetxt11.txt here; its message 15 opens with token -0x11, the code that switches the speaker portrait, so it is a spoken line rather than a caption.

Parameters:
  event_arg -- the single dword every slot of the handler table at 0x000601c4 is called with. The only dispatcher that reaches slot 17 is fdps_battle_run_turn_events, which pushes a literal 0. The body writes 0 over the slot and runs both twelve-frame loops on it, so the incoming value is dead.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through slot 17 of the game's own chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4, whose slots are all fdps; its callees fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, fdps_render_view_frame, FUN_00023830 and FUN_0001ff60 are game code that a separately compiled library object could not reference, and Function ID finds no candidate in the Watcom 10.0x libraries or in ailv3.lib]

Rebuild note:
The turn-to-wave mapping is inverted: turn 4 deploys wave 5 and turn 7 deploys wave 4, and the code tests `turn == 4` with wave 4 in the else branch rather than testing both turns. Writing the obvious `if (turn == 4) deploy(4); else if (turn == 7) deploy(5);` swaps the two waves -- turn 4 would put wave 4's sixteen units in the two top corners and turn 7 would scatter wave 5 around all four -- and it would also send the two camera pans to the wrong place, because unit indices 0x34 and 0x2c are fixed constants that only land on wave-4 units when wave 5 was appended to the unit array first.

=== 000379cb [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning next function entry to 0x379d0

=== 000379d0 [PLATE]
Chapter 13's scripted event that takes the map's enemies out of their hold-position behaviour: it clears the behaviour-mode nibble of 36 consecutive unit records, so those units start walking toward the player instead of waiting to be lured out one at a time. It fires when the dark mage posted in the middle of the map is killed.

Algorithm:
Stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot, which it never reads afterwards, then parks the three compile-time constants 9, 0x2c and 0 in locals and copies them into a second set of locals -- the shape Watcom leaves when the loop that fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range implements out of line is written inline here with fixed arguments.
It then walks the unit index range 9 through 0x2c inclusive (CMP EAX,[EBP-0x10] / JLE at 00037a13, so the bound is the last index and not a limit). For each index it resolves the 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record and stores back (record[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, clearing the low nibble of byte 0x34 and leaving the high nibble alone. That low nibble is the behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step masks out at 00010062 and dispatches on. Mode 0 runs fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, falling back to fdps_unit_rest, so a mode-0 unit closes on the player. Mode 2 -- the mode every one of map12.dat's units is deployed in, byte 0x11 of all 37 deployment records being 0x02, which fdps_deploy_unit copies into record byte 0x34 at 0002379d -- runs fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, then fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack, then fdps_unit_rest; fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack only scores and always returns 0, so a mode-2 unit that cannot act from where it stands simply rests. The state change is therefore exactly stop holding position, start advancing, which is what the chapter's guide entry describes of chapter 13: the enemies never attack on their own initiative and have to be lured out one at a time.

Which units the range covers:
map12.dat is a 131-byte header followed by 37 deployment records of 0x1a bytes (1093 = 0x83 + 37 * 0x1a; fdps_deploy_unit computes a record's address as map_base + 0x83 + 0x1a * index at 00023457). Header byte 1 is 9, the player deployment count fdps_build_map_unit_array lays down first at indices 0..8, so the map's own records 0..36 become unit indices 9..0x2d. All 37 are side 0 (deployment byte 0, which fdps_deploy_unit stores as record byte 6 at 0002366c) and all 37 are on the map from the first turn. The loop stops at 0x2c, so it reaches records 0..35 and leaves record 36 -- unit index 0x2d, a level-16 unit deployed at tile (15,9) -- in the mode the map gave it.

Map 12 is chapter index 12, chapter 13, and the deployment table matches that chapter's guide roster class for class and level for level: three level-20 units of types 0x44/0x45/0x46 (the three bosses), nine level-15 of type 0x4c, seven level-16 of type 0x6c, seven level-11 of type 0x5e, four level-13 of type 0x67, four level-13 of type 0x59 and two level-17 of type 0x58 -- 36 units, every count exact. The 37th record is record 20, unit index 0x1d, at tile (5,5) beside the three bosses: its type byte is 0x0d, below the 0x3c at which fdps_deploy_unit splits roster characters from the generic enemy table (0002348b takes the fdps_get_character_base_record branch at 00023537 for it rather than fdps_get_enemy_record), and character 0x0d is an unnamed row with all-zero growth. The guide's roster does not account for it. So the loop's 36 records are the same count as the guide's 36 enemies but not the same set: they include that unlisted unit and exclude the seventh of the seven level-16 units the guide does list.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x0006020c, slot 18 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. Scanning every shipped MAP*.DAT for slot 18 in all three ways that table is indexed -- the 16-entry turn-event table at offset 3 (stride 3, {turn, slot, phase}, read by fdps_battle_run_turn_events), the 16-entry cell-trigger table at 0x53 (stride 3, subtype byte plus signed word operand, read by fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor), and the per-unit script field at deployment record + 0x16 / + 0x17 -- finds exactly one selector in the whole game: map12.dat record 28, opcode 2 operand 18, at file offset 0x371. That record is a level-13 type-0x67 dark mage standing at tile (14,9), one of the four the guide lists, and it becomes unit index 0x25. fdps_collect_death_scripts picks that 3-byte field up once the unit's signed HP word at record + 0x40 has fallen to 0 or below, and fdps_run_death_scripts executes it, its opcode 2 meaning call slot <operand> of the table at 0x000601c4. So this event fires when that dark mage is killed.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the single dword every slot of the table at 0x000601c4 is called with. The only dispatcher that reaches slot 18 is fdps_run_death_scripts, which forwards its own first argument, the index of the unit whose action is being resolved. This handler overwrites it with 0 at 000379dc and never reads it.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [slot in the game's own event dispatch table at 000601c4, whose other slot owners are all fdps; its only callee is the game function fdps_get_unit_record at 0002d210, which a separately compiled library object could not reference, and Function ID finds no candidate in the Watcom 10.0x libraries or in ailv3.lib]

Rebuild note:
The loop bounds are the literal constants 9 and 0x2c, and 0x2c is one short of map12.dat's last deployed unit (index 0x2d): the event flips 36 of the map's 37 enemies and leaves the last one holding position. Rewriting the loop any of the obvious ways -- from the first deployed unit up to DAT_00060150 - 1, over the map's deployment record count, or over the 36-enemy roster the strategy guide prints, which is a different set of 36 -- switches that 37th unit too and changes how chapter 13 plays. Keep the literals. The store is a read-modify-write for the same reason its siblings are: record[0x34] = (record[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, not record[0x34] = 0, because the high nibble of that byte carries per-unit flags that fdps_map_actor_take_best_action (bit 0x40, at 00012c6f) and fdps_score_targets_for_item (bit 0x80, at 0001337d) test independently, and a plain store wipes them.

=== 00037a4a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte Watcom NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0]

=== 00037a50 [PLATE]
Chapter 14's turn-6 event: brings on wave 4 of the map -- sixteen level-13 warriors along the bottom edge and the treasure-grabbing level-17 werewolf in the upper left -- shows the player the two arriving groups, and paints the line that announces them.

Algorithm:
Stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot at 00037a5c and never reads it as an argument again; that slot is the counter of both frame-hold loops below.
fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, 4, 0) deploys the wave. DAT_00069cf4 is the number of the map the chapter is playing, which fdps_deploy_wave formats into "map%02d.cod" and loads into DAT_00060140; it then walks the 0x1a-byte deployment records of the resident map%02d.dat image at DAT_0006013c (records from +0x83, count in byte +2) and runs fdps_deploy_unit on every record whose wave byte +0x15 equals 4, each of which appends a 0x50-byte record to the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 and raises the unit count DAT_00060150. map13.dat holds seventeen wave-4 records: sixteen of character id 0x63 at level 13 and one of character id 0x52 at level 17. The third argument 0 is fdps_deploy_unit's place_exact flag: 0 sweeps the map grid for the nearest free tile of walkable terrain instead of using the scripted tile as it stands, the scripted tiles being the 6-byte records from +0x0b of map13.cod, x and y as signed words. Those coordinates put the sixteen warriors in two blocks on the bottom edge, (4..7, 21..22) and (14..18, 21..22), and the werewolf at (0,3).
fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(0x24) then parks the map cursor on the first block and twelve calls to fdps_render_view_frame hold the view there; fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(0x2a) and twelve more frames do the same for the second. The map reserves 9 player slots (byte 1 of map13.dat) and has the 20 units of waves 1 and 2 on it before this event, so the wave-4 units take unit indices 0x1d through 0x2d in record order: 0x24 is the warrior scripted for tile (4,22) and 0x2a the one scripted for (16,22), one from each block. The werewolf, index 0x2d, is not shown.
Finally fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x11, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders message 0x11 of the chapter's text bank. DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" image fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads for the current chapter, here fdetxt14.txt, whose 18-entry 16-bit offset table makes 0x11 its last message; it opens with the portrait token -0x11 for character id 0. 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140 aims the glyphs straight at the visible mode-13h screen, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the foreground, background and outline colours.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x00060210, slot 19 of the chapter-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped data the only thing that names slot 19 is map13.dat's turn-event table -- 16 three-byte records from file offset 3, {turn, slot, phase} -- in its single live entry, {turn 6, slot 19, phase 2}. fdps_battle_run_turn_events runs a record when its turn byte equals the turn counter DAT_00069ce8 and its phase byte equals the side argument it was called with; fdps_battle_advance_turn passes 2 at 0001e630, just after incrementing DAT_00069ce8 and playing PlyPhase.saf, so this fires at the start of the player's sixth turn. Map 13 is chapter index 13, chapter 14.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the single dword every dispatcher of the table at 0x000601c4 pushes before calling through it: the battle unit index of the unit whose action fired the event. fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches this slot, pushes a literal 0 because a turn-scheduled event has no triggering unit. This handler overwrites the slot at 00037a5c and uses it as its loop counter, so the value passed makes no difference here.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail library set; reached only through the game's own event dispatch table at 000601c4, and every callee and global it touches is game code]

=== 00037aee [EOL]
2-byte alignment padding (8b c0, mov eax,eax) between FUN_00037a50 and FUN_00037af0

=== 00037af0 [PLATE]
Chapter 15 event handler: releases the nine-unit enemy group that holds the bridgehead in the top-right corner of the map, so it stops standing its ground and starts advancing on the party.

Algorithm:
Zeroes its own incoming argument slot, which it never reads, then runs an inclusive loop over unit indices 0x1d..0x25. For each index it calls fdps_get_unit_record and rewrites byte 0x34 of the returned record as (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0 -- the low nibble is cleared, the high nibble is left alone. That low nibble is the behavior mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step masks out at 00010062 and dispatches on. MAP14.DAT gives every unit it deploys mode 2 (deployment record byte 0x11, which fdps_deploy_unit copies into unit record byte 0x34 at 0002379d), and mode 2 chains fdps_map_actor_take_best_action -> fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack -> fdps_unit_rest: the unit strikes whatever is already within reach but never takes a step. Mode 0 replaces the scoring step with fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent and fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, so the unit walks toward the nearest opposing unit. Clearing the nibble is therefore exactly stop holding position, start advancing. The high nibble has to survive: bit 0x40 of the same byte is tested by fdps_map_actor_take_best_action at 00012c72 and bit 0x80 by fdps_score_targets_for_item at 00013380, so they are independent per-unit flags.

The loop is the body of fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range inlined with the constants 0x1d, 0x25 and 0: the three argument values are staged at [EBP-0x20], [EBP-0x1c] and [EBP-0x18], copied into the inlined callee's own parameter slots at [EBP-0xc], [EBP-0x10] and [EBP-0x14], and only then walked.

Which chapter, which units, and what fires it:
The function has no static caller. Its only reference is the relocated pointer at 00060214, slot (0x60214 - 0x601c4) / 4 = 20 of the chapter-event handler table based at 000601c4. Slot 20 is named in exactly one place in the shipped data, across all 63 MAP*.DAT: record 8 of MAP14.DAT, opcode 2 in the death script at record + 0x16. MAP14.DAT is chapter index 14, the player's chapter 15 (the fortress-cannon chapter). That file has no turn events and no tile triggers at all -- every entry of both tables is 0xff -- so this handler is reachable only as a death script, through fdps_collect_death_scripts and fdps_run_death_scripts, and only when the unit deployed from record 8 is killed: a LV19 ice mage (character id 0x65) standing at (18,1) inside the stockade at the top of the map.

The unit indices resolve through the file's own header: 9 player slots and 45 deployment records, of which records 1..43 are wave 0 and are put on the map in file order at battle start, so unit index = record index + 8 and 0x1d..0x25 are records 21..29. MAP14.COD places eight of them in one block at the top-right bridgehead -- three LV14 barbarian warriors at (23,3), (24,3), (25,3), two LV19 ice mages at (23,4) and (25,4), three LV15 archers at (23,5), (24,5), (25,5) -- and the ninth is record 27, the LV16 beam turret at (16,10), the fortress cannon that is this chapter's victory condition and whose own death script is slot 21, fdps_chapter_15_event_boss_defeat. The cannon has no movement allowance and both behavior chains open with fdps_map_actor_take_best_action and close with fdps_unit_rest, so raising it from mode 2 to mode 0 changes nothing it does; it is inside the range because the range is contiguous, not because the handler is about the cannon.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the single dword every dispatcher of the table at 000601c4 pushes. The only route that reaches this slot is fdps_run_death_scripts, which pushes its own actor_unit_index at 0001dcad: the index of the unit that landed the killing blow, not of the unit that died. This handler never reads it.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record, read-modify-writes a packed nibble field of the game's unit-record struct, and is dispatched from the game's own event-handler table; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set]

Rebuild note:
The write is rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | value, not rec[0x34] = 0. Writing the obvious "reset the behavior mode" as a plain store of 0 also wipes bits 0x40 and 0x80 of the same byte, which are separate per-unit flags: fdps_map_actor_take_best_action tests bit 0x40 at 00012c72 and fdps_score_targets_for_item tests bit 0x80 at 00013380, so the affected units would take a different AI path afterwards. The loop bound is inclusive as well: i <= 0x25, so unit 0x25 is included and a C rewrite using i < 0x25 silently leaves the last of the nine units alone.

=== 00037b6a [EOL]
Alignment padding: single 6-byte NOP form 8d 80 00 00 00 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]).

=== 00037b70 [PLATE]
Chapter 15's boss-death event: the fortress cannon has fallen, so the chapter is over -- except that when it fell on turn 25 or earlier with 裘娜 still standing, a challenger walks onto the cleared map first and offers her a duel.

Algorithm:
fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies runs first, unconditionally, zeroing the HP of every unit still on the enemy side and playing them off the map. That is why fdps_chapter_15_end, alone in its family, has no destroy call of its own.

Two gates then decide whether the duel is offered. The battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 must be 0x19 or less -- CMP dword ptr [0x00069ce8],0x19 / JG at 00037b81, so turn 25 itself still qualifies -- and fdps_unit_is_retired(4) must return 0. Unit 4 is 裘娜: FUN_00022be0 sizes the map's roster block from MAP14.DAT header byte +1, which is 9, so unit indices 0..8 are roster members 0..8 and 裘娜, who joins in chapter 7, is the fifth of them. Either gate failing stores 2 -- the code that means the chapter is cleared -- into the battle-end global DAT_00069da0 and returns.

Both gates passing, FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 2, 0) deploys the current map's wave-2 records. In MAP14.DAT that is record 44 alone, the level 17 unit of enemy id 0x23 that the guide lists as the chapter's unnamed opponent, and it is appended as unit 0x35: 9 roster units, then the 43 wave-0 records FUN_00022be0 brings on at chapter start, then the wave-1 unit that Icon14.dat deploys during the opening cutscene. The trailing 0 makes FUN_000232b0 look for the nearest free walkable tile to the record's scripted coordinates instead of using them verbatim.

The offer is then put to the player, in order: FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x12, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders message 0x12; FUN_000205b0(3) plays the reveal animation of the 302x73 message panel; FUN_0001ff60 renders message 0x13 into the panel interior at 0xaa44a, VGA offset 0xa44a, row 131 column 138; fdps_prompt_two_choice runs the modal left/right prompt; FUN_00020820 retracts the panel. DAT_00060124 is the chapter's dialogue resource, FDETXT15.TXT, loaded out of Field.vfs by fdps_load_field_chapter_resources; 0xa0000 is the mode-13h frame buffer, 0x140 the destination pitch, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d the three colour arguments forwarded to fdps_draw_glyph.

Option 0 accepts. Message 0x14 is rendered, then everything that is not one of the two duellists is taken off the map: for i = 0 through 8, skipping 4, fdps_get_unit_record(i) is fetched and 1 is stored into its byte +5 -- a whole-byte store that raises the retired bit 0x01 which fdps_unit_is_retired reads and clears the has-acted bit 0x80 with it -- and unit 0x34 gets the same store. Unit 0x34 is the map's wave-1 unit, MAP14.DAT record 0: side 2, character id 5, level 20, the archer 瑪麗安 the guide lists on the player's side. Finally DAT_000640e8, one of the 0x20 chapter-event flag bytes at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes when a chapter starts, is raised to 1. DAT_00069da0 is deliberately left alone, so the battle keeps running with unit 4 against unit 0x35 and fdps_chapter_15_post_action -- which branches on that same flag -- settles the duel and awards the 妖刀村雨.

Any other answer, the -1 that fdps_prompt_two_choice returns on cancel included, declines: message 0x15 is rendered and DAT_00069da0 is set to 2, ending the chapter without the duel.

Reached as slot 21 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4 -- the relocated pointer at 0x00060218 -- and never called by name. MAP14.DAT record 27, the level 16 unit of enemy id 0x80 that is the chapter's victory condition, carries the unit script (opcode 2, operand 21) at record +0x16; FUN_000232b0 copies it into unit record +0x31..+0x33, fdps_collect_defeated_unit_events collects it once that unit's HP word at +0x40 reaches 0, and FUN_0001d990 dispatches opcode 2 as handler[operand](DAT_00063f74). MAP14.DAT declares no turn events and no tile triggers at all, and its only other unit script is record 8's, which reaches slot 20, fdps_chapter_event_clear_unit_behavior_1d_25.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit array at DAT_00069cd8, in 0 .. DAT_00060150-1: the unit FUN_0001d990 was acting on when the cannon died. It is never read. The slot is overwritten at 00037c05 with the prompt result and again at 00037c3a as the retire loop's counter.

Returns:
  Nothing. The outcome is left in DAT_00069da0 and DAT_000640e8.

Pool: fdps  [dispatched only from the game's own event-handler table at 0x000601c4; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set; every callee is proven game code, and it is a full 348-byte routine, not a jump island or shim]

Rebuild note:
The accept branch must leave DAT_00069da0 untouched. Two of the three exits store 2 into it and the control flow invites folding that into one store at the end -- do that and chapter 15's duel ends the chapter the instant the player says yes. fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies likewise has to stay ahead of both gates and stay unconditional, or the over-25-turn path hands a map full of live enemies to fdps_chapter_15_end. And the turn test is turn <= 25, not < 25: the stricter comparison silently takes the 妖刀村雨 away from a 25-turn clear.

=== 00037ccc [EOL]
4-byte Watcom multi-byte NOP (8d 44 20 00) aligning next function entry to 0x10

=== 00037cd0 [PLATE]
Chapter 16's wandering-smith event: when Randis ends his turn on the smith's tile inside the first twenty battle turns still carrying one of the two named swords, the smith reforges it -- 修佩魯 comes back as 灼烈之劍, 雷德 breaks and is paid off with 5000 gold plus the player's pick of 神的聖印 or 金屬礦.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an 8-byte local area: [EBP-0x4] holds the message index of the smith's reaction line, which doubles as which sword was found (0 = neither yet), and [EBP-0x8] the inventory slot that sword sits in.

Three gates at 00037ce3-00037cfb, and the whole body is skipped unless all three pass: unit_index is exactly 0, the one-shot byte DAT_000640e8 is still 0, and the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 is at most 0x14 (CMP 0x14 / JLE, so twenty turns inclusive). Battle unit 0 is Randis, always the first unit deployed. DAT_00069ce8 is set to 1 by fdps_chapter_state_reset, raised once per turn cycle by fdps_battle_advance_turn and restored from the save image by fdps_load_savegame. DAT_000640e8 is element 16 of the 32-byte per-chapter flag array at 000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset clears when a chapter starts.

Every line of the scene is spoken the same way: FUN_000205b0(0x81) reveals the 302x73 message panel and leaves it standing at (9,120), FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, index, 0xaa44a, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders the message into the mode-13h framebuffer 0xa44a bytes in -- pixel (138,131) -- at a 0x140-byte pitch, with 0xd0/0/0x6d forwarded unchanged to the glyph drawer, and FUN_00020820 retracts the panel. DAT_00060124 is the chapter text image fdetxt16.txt that fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads out of Field.vfs; it carries 23 strings, so 0x16 is its last one. The two prompt lines are the exception: message 0xf and message 0x15 are left on screen while fdps_prompt_two_choice runs, and the panel is retracted only after the answer comes back.

The order of events:
1. Message 0xc, the smith's greeting, then DAT_000640e8 is raised to 1 at 00037d37 -- before anything is checked about what Randis is carrying.
2. fdps_unit_find_item_slot(0, 0x58) looks for 修佩魯; a hit sets the reaction line to 0xd. Otherwise fdps_unit_find_item_slot(0, 0x59) looks for 雷德 and a hit sets it to 0xe. Either way the slot number is kept. With neither sword the reaction line is still 0 and the handler returns here, the greeting played and the latch spent.
3. Message 0xd or 0xe, the smith's verdict on the sword, then message 0xf and the first two-choice prompt. A non-zero answer means the offer was declined: message 0x10 is the parting line and nothing else happens.
4. On answer 0 the forging runs: messages 0x11 and 0x12, then fdps_unit_remove_item(0, slot) takes the sword out of Randis's eight-slot inventory, which also frees the slot every fdps_unit_add_item below fills.
   - Reaction line 0xd (修佩魯): message 0x13 and fdps_unit_add_item(0, 0xa0) -- 灼烈之劍, the sword fdps_chapter_20_event_upgrade_randis_sword later trades for 火光之劍 and chapter 25's handler at 00038fd0 turns into 真炎龍劍.
   - Reaction line 0xe (雷德): message 0x14 says the forging failed, DAT_000643a4 -- the party gold global fdps_draw_party_gold prints -- gains 0x1388 = 5000, and message 0x15 asks whether to try again on something else. Answer 0 gives message 0x16 and fdps_unit_add_item(0, 0xa9), 神的聖印; any other answer gives fdps_unit_add_item(0, 0xa3), 金屬礦, followed by the same parting line 0x10.
   Then fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(0) rebuilds Randis's four derived combat stats, the weapon he is carrying having changed.

The three inventory calls and the stat rebuild all pass a literal 0 rather than unit_index; the entry gate has already forced the two to be equal.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x0006021c, slot 22 of the chapter-event handler pointer table based at 0x000601c4. MAP15.DAT is the only map image that names handler 22: the first entry of its tile-event table (image offset 0x33, two bytes per entry, indexed by the cell's event code minus one), with occasion 1. Occasion 1 is what fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event is given immediately after fdps_battle_mark_unit_done, i.e. a unit ending its turn on the cell; that function leaves the handler index in DAT_00069d90 and the battle loop calls 0x000601c4[index](unit_index) once the unit is done. Map number 15 is chapter index 15, the player's chapter 16, and M15.DTL marks cell (2,12) with event code 1.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8 of the unit that ended its turn on the trigger tile, pushed by fdps_battle_unit_turn or by the enemy-phase dispatcher; fdps_battle_run_turn_events would pass a literal 0. Tested against 0 so that only Randis can spring the event, and never read again: the slot at [EBP+0x14] is reused at 00037dee and 00037f3b to hold fdps_prompt_two_choice's answer.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; dispatched from the game's own chapter-event handler table and every callee and global it touches is game-side]

Rebuild note:
The one-shot latch DAT_000640e8 is raised straight after the greeting, before the inventory is searched, so a Randis who reaches the tile carrying neither 修佩魯 nor 雷德 burns the encounter for the rest of the chapter and can never come back with the right sword. Raising it where the trade actually happens, which is what the sibling chapter events do and what the obvious C would write, hands the player a second chance at 灼烈之劍 and with it 真炎龍劍 twenty chapters later. The two prompt tests are also written as "answer == 0 means yes"; fdps_prompt_two_choice returns -1 when the player cancels, so writing "answer == 1 means no" turns a cancel into an acceptance.

=== 0003801b [EOL]

=== 00038020 [PLATE]
Chapter 16's turn-scheduled release event: takes one group of the map's enemies out of its hold-position behavior and puts it into the mode that walks it toward the player, choosing which group by the battle turn that has just been played.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with a 0x40-byte local area and stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] at 0003802c, never reading what the dispatcher passed. It then compares the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 against 5 (00038033) and runs one of two otherwise identical loops:

  turn == 5   -- unit indices 0x19 through 0x22 inclusive (constants staged at 0003803c/00038043)
  otherwise   -- unit indices 0x0a through 0x19 inclusive (constants staged at 0003809e/000380a5)

DAT_00069ce8 is the battle turn counter: fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 1, fdps_battle_advance_turn raises it once per turn cycle, and fdps_load_savegame restores it from the save image.

Each branch parks its three constants -- first index, last index and the value 0 -- in one set of locals and copies them into a second set before walking, the shape Watcom leaves when the loop that fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range implements out of line is written inline with fixed arguments. For every index in the range it resolves the 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record and stores back (record[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, clearing the low nibble and leaving the high nibble alone. That low nibble is the behavior mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step masks out at 00010062 and dispatches on: mode 0 chains FUN_00012c10 -> FUN_000126b0 -> FUN_000127c0 -> FUN_000120d0, and FUN_000127c0 heads for the nearest opposing unit; mode 2, the mode most of this map's units are deployed in, chains FUN_00012c10 -> FUN_00012230 -> FUN_000120d0 and never takes a pursuit step. FUN_000232b0 copies that mode per unit out of byte 0x11 of the map's 0x1a-byte deployment record, so the handler discards whatever mode the map data authored for the units in range.

The entry has no static caller. Its address is the pointer at 0x00060220, slot 23 of the chapter-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped data the only thing that selects slot 23 is the turn-event table of map15.dat -- map 15, chapter 16 -- which holds the two entries {turn 5, slot 23, phase 0} and {turn 15, slot 23, phase 0}; no tile-trigger record and no death-script record in any MAP*.DAT names the slot. fdps_battle_run_turn_events fires a turn-event record while the counter still holds the turn whose phase has just ended, so the counter reads 5 at the first firing and 15 at the second: turn 5 takes the 0x19..0x22 branch and turn 15 the 0x0a..0x19 branch. The else branch is the fallback, not a test for turn 15.

map15.dat deploys 10 player units (header byte 1, published as DAT_00064118 by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources and used by FUN_00022be0 to size the unit array) ahead of its 25 enemy deployment records (header byte 2), so the map's own units occupy indices 0x0a upward in record order, wave by wave: 0x0a..0x16 the thirteen wave-0 samurai, archers and knights, 0x17..0x18 the two wave-1 dark mages, 0x19..0x1c the four wave-2 flying units, 0x1d..0x20 the four wave-3 samurai, 0x21..0x22 the two wave-4 dark mages. The turn-5 branch therefore releases the whole second attack wave -- waves 2, 3 and 4, ten units, every one of them deployed in hold mode 2 -- and the turn-15 branch releases the units that opened the battle plus the first wave-2 flying unit.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, present only because every slot of the table at 0x000601c4 shares one function-pointer type. fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches this slot, pushes a literal 0. Overwritten with 0 at 0003802c and never read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [dispatched from the game's own chapter-event handler table, and read-modify-writes a packed nibble field of the game's unit-record struct through fdps_get_unit_record; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set]

Rebuild note:
The store is record[0x34] = (record[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, not record[0x34] = 0: writing the obvious reset-the-behavior-mode as a plain store also wipes the high-nibble flags of the same byte, which FUN_00012c10 (00012c6f) and FUN_000132b0 (0001337d) test independently, and the affected enemies then take a different AI path. Both loop bounds are inclusive as well -- i <= 0x22 and i <= 0x19 -- so a rewrite using < leaves the last dark mage of the second wave, and the first flying unit, holding position.

Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx, 11 bytes to 16-byte boundary at 00038110

=== 00038110 [PLATE]
Chapter 17's turn-scheduled reinforcement event: brings on the wave of the current map's units that is due for the turn just played.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0) and stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] -- the source reuses the parameter as a scratch variable and never reads what was passed in. It then calls fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, DAT_00069ce8 - 7, 0), cleans the 12 argument bytes itself and returns. DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, the value that names "map%02d.dat" and "map%02d.cod". DAT_00069ce8 is the battle turn counter: fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 1, fdps_load_savegame restores it from the save image, and fdps_battle_advance_turn raises it once per turn cycle. fdps_deploy_wave loads "map%02d.cod" for that map number and runs fdps_deploy_unit over every deployment record of the loaded "map%02d.dat" image at DAT_0006013c -- 0x1a-byte records from +0x83, count in byte +0x2 -- whose wave byte, record + 0x15, equals its wave_no argument, so each unit of wave (turn - 7) is appended as a new 0x50-byte record on the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 with the unit count DAT_00060150 raised once per unit. The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x00060224, slot 24 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped data the only thing that selects slot 24 is the turn-event table of map16.dat -- map 16, chapter 17 -- which holds the two entries {turn 8, slot 24, phase 0} and {turn 9, slot 24, phase 0}. fdps_battle_advance_turn runs fdps_battle_run_turn_events(0) after the enemy-phase banner and before the INC of the turn counter at 0001e5fd, so the counter still holds the turn whose player phase has just ended: turn 8 selects wave 1, the six level-15 records 23..28 of map16.dat, and turn 9 selects wave 2, its single level-14 record 29. All seven have spawn points in the map's lower-left corner, tiles (2..4, 22..24).

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the one dword every slot of the table at 0x000601c4 is called with. The dispatchers that have a unit in hand push its index into the array at DAT_00069cd8: fdps_battle_unit_turn at 00015835, fdps_run_death_scripts at 0001dcaa, fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor at 000188d4, and the two AI phase loops at 00012a2f and 00012ae6. A turn-scheduled event has no unit attached, so fdps_battle_run_turn_events -- the only dispatcher that reaches this slot -- pushes a literal 0. Overwritten with 0 at 0003811c and never read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; its sole callee is the game's map deployment loader and every dispatcher of its table is game code]

Rebuild note:
The wave number is turn - 7 read from the 1-based counter DAT_00069ce8 at a moment when it has NOT yet been incremented -- fdps_battle_advance_turn calls fdps_battle_run_turn_events(0) at 0001e5bc and only reaches the INC at 0001e5fd afterwards -- so writing the counter as 0-based, or hoisting the increment ahead of the phase-0 events, shifts every reinforcement by one turn. Do not add the obvious guard either: the raw subtraction is passed straight through with no lower bound, and clamping a negative key to 0 would re-deploy the map's entire starting army, the 23 wave-0 records of map16.dat.

Rebuild note:
The turn counter DAT_00069ce8 is compared for equality against a wave byte stored in the shipped MAP*.DAT, so its base is fixed by the data files and is not a free choice in a rebuild: fdps_chapter_state_reset must set it to 1 and fdps_battle_advance_turn must raise it before the phase in which the turn events are dispatched, exactly as they do now. Making the turn counter 0-based, or moving the increment to after the turn-event dispatch, compiles and looks right but shifts every one of chapter 18's nine scheduled waves by one turn, and the same for every other map's turn-event table.

=== 000381d0 [PLATE]
Chapter 19's flank ambush: the first time a unit that is not enemy-side finishes a step onto the map's trigger tile, it brings on the map's twenty-two wave-6 enemy reinforcements, pans the view over all three places they arrive, and speaks the chapter's line about them.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with a single 4-byte local and returns without doing anything unless both gates pass. The first gate is the one-shot latch DAT_000640e8, which must still be 0; the second is the acting unit's side byte, fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) + 6, which must be non-zero. Side 0 is the enemy's, so an enemy that walks over the tile cannot spring the ambush.

It first stores 0 into DAT_00069cd0, the cursor draw mode fdps_draw_map_cursor dispatches on -- mode 0 matches none of its cases, so no cursor is painted for the rest of the sequence.

Then FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 6, 0). DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, the value that names "map%02d.dat" and "map%02d.cod". FUN_00023830 reloads "map%02d.cod" for that number and runs FUN_000232b0 over every deployment record of the loaded "map%02d.dat" image at DAT_0006013c -- 0x1a-byte records from +0x83, count in byte +0x2 -- whose wave byte, record + 0x15, equals 6, appending each as a new 0x50-byte record on the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 and raising the unit count DAT_00060150 once per unit. The trailing 0 is the placement flag, telling FUN_000232b0 to drop each unit on the nearest free walkable tile to its scripted spawn point rather than on that tile verbatim.

It then shows the arrival three times over, once per group. fdps_map_cursor_move_to(0x108, 0) walks the map cursor to map pixel (264, 0), tile (11, 0), dragging the viewport with it, and twelve calls to fdps_render_view_frame hold the picture there for twelve retrace-paced frames. fdps_map_cursor_move_to(0, 0x210) then does the same for map pixel (0, 528), tile (0, 22), and fdps_map_cursor_move_to(0x300, 0x210) for map pixel (768, 528), tile (32, 22); both are past the far edge of the playfield and fdps_map_cursor_move_to clamps them, so the two of them park the view on the left and the right flank. All three frame loops keep their 0..11 counter in the incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14], which the body zeroes and never reads as an argument again.

It stores the literal 1 into DAT_00069cd0 -- the plain-cursor mode, not whatever mode was there on entry -- and calls FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x13, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d), which walks message 0x13 of the chapter's text image and paints it straight onto the mode-13h VGA screen at 0xa0000 with a 0x140 = 320 byte pitch; DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" bank fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads for map number plus one, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the three colour values the whole handler family forwards to the glyph drawer. Last it raises DAT_000640e8 to 1, so the ambush cannot fire a second time.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x00060230, slot 27 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4 -- (0x60230 - 0x601c4) / 4 = 27 -- which fdps_battle_unit_turn calls as PUSH unit_index / CALL dword ptr [id*4 + 0x601c4] / ADD ESP,4 at 00015839, and fdps_battle_run_turn_events, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase, fdps_battle_system_menu, FUN_00012960, FUN_000184f0 and FUN_0001d990 call the same way. In the shipped data slot 27 is named in exactly one place: map18.dat's tile-event table (image offset 0x33, two bytes per entry) entry for cell event code 1, the bytes 1b 00, with occasion 0 -- the occasion a unit reports as it finishes stepping onto a cell. Map 18 is chapter index 18, the player's chapter 19; the same image's turn-event table names handler 26 for turn 6, which is fdps_chapter_19_event_lancelot_joins, and the guide's chapter 19 entry has Lancelot arriving on turn 6. map18.dat carries exactly twenty-two wave-6 records: fourteen of character id 0x60 at level 17 and eight of character id 0x6d at level 15, whose spawn points in map18.cod are tiles (30..32, 17..19), (0..2, 17..19) and (13..16, 0..1) -- the right flank, the left flank and the top edge, the three areas the pan visits, and what the guide describes as the reinforcements appearing on both sides and above.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit the dispatcher is acting on, in 0 .. DAT_00060150-1, into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; here the unit that stepped onto the trigger tile. Only its side byte at record+6 is read. Overwritten with 0 at 00038231 and reused as the frame counter for all three pan holds.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it is reached only through the game's own handler table at 0x000601c4, all five callees are game routines, and every global it touches -- DAT_000640e8, DAT_00069cd0, DAT_00069cf4, DAT_00060124 -- is game state a separately compiled vendor object could not reference]

Rebuild note:
Two ways the obvious rewrite diverges. DAT_000640e8 is not this handler's private flag: it is element 0x10 of the 0x20-byte chapter-event block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) at every chapter start and that fdps_load_savegame restores from save-image offset 0x30a3, and a dozen handlers in other chapters latch the same byte. Writing the guard as a function-local static char fires the ambush once per process, so replaying chapter 19 after a Game Over, or loading a save made before the trigger, would silently skip the reinforcements. Second, the exit stores the literal 1 into the cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 instead of restoring what it held on entry; writing it as the obvious save/restore pair around the pan changes what the cursor looks like afterwards.

=== 000382f0 [PLATE]
Chapter 20's sword-upgrade event: when Randis steps onto the map's trigger tile still carrying 灼烈之劍 and the battle is no more than twenty turns old, the fire god takes that sword and gives him 火光之劍 in its place.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with a 4-byte local area, then calls fdps_unit_find_item_slot(unit_index, 0xa0) and keeps the slot number in [EBP-0x4]. Item 0xa0 is 灼烈之劍, the sword the chapter-16 smith forges.

It then does nothing at all unless all three gates pass, tested in this order at 00038310-00038325: unit_index is exactly 0, the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 is at most 0x14 (CMP 0x14 / JLE, so twenty turns inclusive), and the slot search hit (result != -1). Battle unit 0 is Randis, who is always the first unit deployed. The turn counter is set to 1 by fdps_chapter_state_reset, raised once per turn cycle by fdps_battle_advance_turn and restored from the save image by fdps_load_savegame.

On the taken path it runs four steps in order.
1. FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x13, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders message 0x13, the fire god's line, straight into the mode-13h VGA framebuffer at 0xa0000 with a 0x140-byte pitch; 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the three values FUN_0001ff60 forwards unchanged to the glyph drawer. DAT_00060124 holds the "fdetxt%02d.txt" image for the current map number plus one, loaded out of Field.vfs by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources; FDETXT20.TXT carries exactly twenty strings, so 0x13 is its last one.
2. fdps_unit_remove_item(unit_index, slot) takes 灼烈之劍 out of Randis's eight-slot inventory.
3. fdps_unit_add_item(0, 0xa1) gives him 火光之劍. The unit index here is the literal 0, not unit_index; the guard above has already forced the two to be equal.
4. fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(unit_index) rebuilds his four derived combat stats, the sword he is wearing having changed.

There is no one-shot latch and the cell is never marked consumed. The swapped item is what stops the event repeating, and a unit that is not Randis leaves the tile live for him to come back to.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x00060234, slot 28 of the chapter-event handler pointer table based at 0x000601c4. MAP19.DAT is the only map image in Field.vfs that names handler 28: the first entry of its tile-event table (image offset 0x33, two bytes per entry, indexed by the cell's event code minus one), with occasion 0. Occasion 0 is what the single-step walk animations report to fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event as a unit finishes a step onto a cell; that function leaves the handler index in DAT_00069d90 and fdps_battle_unit_turn calls 0x000601c4[index](unit_index) once the unit's turn is over. Map number 19 is chapter index 19, the player's chapter 20. Its twin is the handler at 00038fd0, the same body without the turn gate, which swaps 0xa1 for 0xa2 (真炎龍劍) in chapter 25.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8 of the unit that stepped onto the trigger tile; fdps_battle_unit_turn passes the unit whose turn just ended, fdps_battle_run_turn_events would pass a literal 0. Forwarded to fdps_unit_find_item_slot, fdps_unit_remove_item and fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats, and tested against 0 so that only Randis can spring the event.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; the dispatch table, every callee and every global it touches are game-side]

Rebuild note:

=== 00038380 [PLATE]
Chapter 21's first ambush trigger: the first time a player-side unit steps onto the map's trigger tile, it brings on the map's sixteen wave-1 enemy reinforcements and speaks the chapter's line.

Algorithm:
Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and does nothing at all unless both gates pass: the one-shot latch DAT_000640e8 is still 0, and the unit's side byte at record+6 is exactly 2. Side 2 is the player's own side and 0 the enemy's (fdps_battle_count_remaining_units_on_side matches the same byte), so an enemy that walks over the tile cannot spring the ambush.

When both hold it calls FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 1, 0). DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, which FUN_00023830 formats into "map%02d.cod" and whose "map%02d.dat" image it walks; the 1 is the wave key matched against byte 0x15 of each 0x1a-byte deployment record, and MAP20.DAT carries sixteen wave-1 records (indices 38..53); the trailing 0 is the placement flag, telling FUN_00023830 to drop each unit on the nearest free walkable tile to its scripted coordinates rather than on those coordinates verbatim.

It then calls FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x14, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d), which renders message 0x14 of the chapter's text image straight into the mode-13h VGA framebuffer at 0xa0000 with a 0x140-byte pitch; 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the three values FUN_0001ff60 forwards unchanged to the glyph drawer. Last it raises DAT_000640e8 to 1, so the event cannot fire a second time. When either gate fails the branch at 000383b4 jumps straight to the epilogue and nothing happens.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x00060238, slot 29 of the chapter-event handler pointer table based at 0x000601c4, which fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_battle_run_turn_events call as table[id](unit_index). Map number 20 is chapter index 20, the player's chapter 21. The same map's tile-event entry 2 routes to slot 30 at 0x00038400, the twin handler that deploys wave 2 off the neighbouring latch DAT_000640e9 and then puts units 0xb through 0x50 into behaviour mode 0.

Parameters:

DAT_000640e8 is not this handler's private flag. === 000384e0 [PLATE]
Chapter 22's turn-scheduled event handler: the one slot map21.dat names for all five of the chapter's turn events, running whichever of them is due for the turn the player has just finished.

Algorithm:
An if/else ladder on the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 -- set to 1 by fdps_chapter_state_reset and bumped once per turn cycle by fdps_battle_advance_turn -- with one branch per scheduled turn and no default branch; every branch jumps to the single epilogue at 0003889b. The incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] is never read, and the turn-5 and turn-8 branches reuse it as their own 0..11 frame counter.

Two step shapes repeat through the ladder:

  Speak a line -- FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, index, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders one message of the chapter's text out of the "fdetxt%02d.txt" buffer fdps_load_field_chapter_resources holds in DAT_00060124 (fdetxt22.txt for this chapter) straight to the mode-13h VGA framebuffer at 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140; 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the glyph arguments it forwards to fdps_draw_glyph.

  Pan the camera -- DAT_00069cd0 = 0 blanks the map cursor (fdps_draw_map_cursor draws nothing unless that global holds 1..6, and fdps_map_cursor_move_to renders a frame per step while it is 0), fdps_map_cursor_move_to walks the view to a map pixel position at 0x18 pixels per tile, twelve fdps_render_view_frame calls hold it there, and DAT_00069cd0 = 1 restores the ordinary cursor at the end of the branch.

  turn 1 (000384ec) -- message 0x0c, then FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 1, 0) deploys every map21.dat record whose wave byte (+0x15) is 1: sixteen units, the reinforcements that arrive in the three corridors and behind the boss.

  turn 3 (00038530) -- message 0x0d, then wave 2, eight units beside the boss.

  turn 5 (00038574) -- message 0x0e and wave 3 (four units), then pans to (0, 0x60) and (0x1b0, 0x60); then message 0x0f and wave 5 (four more units), the same pair of pans again; then message 0x10.

  turn 8 (000386eb) -- message 0x11, then wave 4, twenty-two units, then three pans: (0, 0x60), (0x1b0, 0x60), (0x1b0, 0x1f8).

  turn 9 (000387ce) -- no message and no deployment. Two copies of fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range expanded inline, the first over the inclusive index range 0x0b..0x0b with value 0x0b, the second over 0x0c..0x41 with value 0; each takes the record from fdps_get_unit_record and writes record[0x34] = (record[0x34] & 0xf0) | value. The low nibble of byte 0x34 is the behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on. map21.cod places 66 units and map21.dat holds 55 deployment records, so indices 0..0x0a are the roster and the map's single wave-0 record -- the level-20 boss 巫湯婆婆, whose death script is fdps_chapter_22_event_boss_defeat -- lands at index 0x0b, with 0x0c..0x41 covering all 54 units the five waves have put on the map by then. So the boss moves to behaviour mode 0x0b, the branch fdps_map_actor_behavior_step takes at 00010652, and every reinforcement is handed back to mode 0, the default map AI.

The entry has no caller. Its address sits in the relocated pointer at 00060240, slot (0x60240 - 0x601c4) / 4 = 31 of the scripted-event handler table based at 000601c4, and all five live entries of map21.dat's turn-event table at file offset 3 name that slot: {turn 1, slot 31, phase 0}, {3,31,0}, {5,31,0}, {8,31,0}, {9,31,0}. fdps_battle_run_turn_events fires them during the phase-0 pass, the one fdps_battle_advance_turn runs as the player's phase ends, pushing a literal 0 at 0002e13e.

Parameters:
  event_arg -- the single dword every slot of the handler table at 000601c4 is called with. fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches slot 31, always pushes 0, and the body overwrites the slot before reading it, so nothing here depends on the value.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls only game routines and touches only game globals; no Function ID candidate in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The turn-to-wave mapping is not the identity and has to be copied literally: turn 5 deploys wave 3 and then wave 5, and turn 8 deploys wave 4, so ordering the deployments by wave number puts wave 4's twenty-two units on the map three turns early and leaves wave 5's four for turn 8. Byte 0x34 of the unit record is packed -- the low nibble is the behaviour mode, the high nibble carries flags other code tests -- so turn 9's two writes have to stay read-modify-write; assigning 0x0b and 0 outright clears those flags.

=== 00038a30 [PLATE]
Chapter 23's turn-scheduled event handler: on each of the seven turns the chapter's map schedules it brings on that turn's wave of units, speaks the chapter's line on the two turns that carry one, and on the last of them puts one battle unit into a driven AI mode instead.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with a 0x20-byte local area and stores 0 over its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14], which it never reads back.

Everything else branches on DAT_00069ce8, the battle turn counter -- fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 1 and fdps_battle_advance_turn raises it once per turn cycle.

First, whenever the counter is 5 or less, FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, turn + 4, 0). DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, 22 for this chapter; the second argument is the wave key, so turns 1 through 5 bring on waves 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 in that order -- one map22.dat deployment record each, all of them NPC-side. FUN_00023830 reloads "map%02d.cod" and deploys every 0x1a-byte record of the map script image at DAT_0006013c whose wave byte (record +0x15) equals the key.

Then a three-way chain on the same counter, which is entered whatever the first test did:
  turn 3  -- message 0x15, then wave 3 (fifteen enemy records)
  turn 7  -- message 0x16, then wave 4 (twenty-seven enemy records)
  turn 15 -- no message and no deployment. fdps_get_unit_record(0x20) resolves one battle unit and the low nibble of its record byte 0x34 is rewritten to 0x0b, one of the two driven behaviour modes fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on that nibble. The rewrite is spelled out as an inclusive index loop over the one-element range 0x20..0x20, the same shape fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range has, with the range and the value first parked in three stack slots.
The chain is a separate statement from the turn <= 5 test, not an else of it, so turn 3 deploys twice: wave 7 from the first test and then wave 3 from the chain.

Speaking a line is FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, message, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d): DAT_00060124 is the chapter text image fdetxt23.txt loaded by fdps_load_field_chapter_resources, the destination is the mode-13h frame buffer at a 0x140-byte pitch, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the three glyph arguments forwarded unchanged.

The handler is reached only through slot 34 of the vector at 0x000601c4. map22.dat's turn-event table schedules that slot on turns 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the enemy phase, turn 7 of the player phase and turn 15 of the enemy phase, and it is the chapter's only scheduled turn event; the chapter's tile trigger goes to slot 35 instead.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the single dword every slot of the handler vector at 0x000601c4 receives. fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches this entry, pushes a literal 0, and this handler stores 0 over the slot on entry and never reads it.

=== 00038cc0 [PLATE]
Chapter 24's turn-scheduled event handler: on each of the six battle turns the chapter's map schedules, it speaks that turn's line and brings on that turn's wave of units.

Algorithm:
Tests the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 against six values in this order -- 5, 8, 7, 10, 13, 15 -- runs at most one of them and does nothing on any other turn. Speaking a line is fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, text_id, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d): DAT_00060124 is the chapter text block fdetxt24.txt, the destination is the mode-13h frame buffer with pitch 0x140, and 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d are the standard message foreground, background and outline colours. Deploying a wave is fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, wave, 0), which brings on every deployment record of the current map (map 23) whose wave byte +0x15 equals the second argument.
  turn 5  -- text 0x10, then wave 2
  turn 8  -- text 0x11, no deployment
  turn 7  -- wave 6, then text 0x0e
  turn 10 -- wave 4, then text 0x12
  turn 13 -- text 0x13, then wave 3
  turn 15 -- text 0x14, then wave 5
Wave 6 is the one player-side record of map23.dat, the guest mage Shan who joins on turn 7; waves 2, 3, 4 and 5 are enemy reinforcements. The two calls are made in a different order on different turns, and that order is what the player sees. Nothing here gates on the chapter boss being alive: the reinforcement turns fire on the turn counter alone.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the single dword every slot of the handler vector at 0x000601c4 receives. This handler stores 0 over it on entry and never reads it; fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches this entry, pushes a literal 0.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the handler-vector slot at 00060254, whose sibling slots are all game code, and both callees are fdps engine routines; no Function ID candidate in either library set and a unique body hash]

Rebuild note:
The message call and the deployment call are emitted in a different order in different turn cases -- turns 5, 13 and 15 speak first and deploy second, turns 7 and 10 deploy first and speak second, and turn 8 only speaks -- so the natural rewrite that folds the six near-identical cases into one table of (turn, text_id, wave) and one fixed call order changes what the player sees on three of the six turns. The order has to be preserved case by case. The turn tests are also emitted out of numeric order (5, 8, 7, 10, 13, 15) and the chain is if / else-if, so sorting them looks harmless and is, but only because the tests are mutually exclusive; the call order inside a case is not.

The entry is never called by name. Messages 0x17 and 0x18 open and close their own panels through their leading -0x11 tokens, which is why neither is bracketed by FUN_000205b0 and FUN_00020820 the way message 0x16 is. The entry is never called by name. === 00039190 [PLATE]
Chapter 26's turn-4 event: the two holding groups of the tower garrison stop holding position and start advancing on the player, after a line of the chapter's text is painted straight onto the screen.

Algorithm:
Stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot at 0003919c and never reads it again. Then fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x16, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders message 0x16 of the chapter's text bank: DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" image fdps_load_field_chapter_resources loads for chapter index + 1, here Fdetxt26.txt, whose 25-entry 16-bit offset table (its first entry is 50, so the table is 25 words long) makes 0x16 the twenty-third message, at file offset 2450. 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140 aims the glyphs at the visible mode-13h screen, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the three values fdps_draw_text hands unchanged to fdps_draw_glyph as foreground, background and outline colour. That message's token stream opens with the speaker code -0x11 and operand 0x43, so the line is spoken by character id 0x43, one of the chapter's four level-30 commanders.

Then an inclusive loop over unit indices 0x1a..0x2d: for each index fdps_get_unit_record(i) resolves the 0x50-byte record and byte 0x34 is rewritten as (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0 -- the low nibble is cleared, the high nibble is left alone. The low nibble is the behavior mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on (it masks the byte with 0xf at 00010062): mode 0 is the default movement chain that paths a unit toward the nearest opposing unit, whereas mode 2, the mode all twenty of these units were deployed in, holds position until threat weights cross a threshold. The high nibble has to survive because bits 0x40 and 0x80 of the same byte are independent per-unit flags, read by fdps_map_actor_take_best_action at 00012c6f and fdps_score_targets_for_item at 0001337d. The loop is fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range inlined with the constant triple (0x1a, 0x2d, 0): the three values are staged at [EBP-0x20], [EBP-0x1c] and [EBP-0x18], copied into the inlined callee's own parameter slots at [EBP-0xc], [EBP-0x10] and [EBP-0x14], and only then walked.

The entry has no static callers. Its address is the pointer at 0x00060264, entry 40 of the chapter-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. Everything that dispatches through that table takes its index out of the chapter's map%02d.dat: fdps_battle_run_turn_events from the 16 three-byte turn-event records at image offset 3, fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event from the 16 two-byte tile-trigger entries at 0x33 (which the four battle-loop sites in fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase, fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_battle_system_menu then call through the pending slot DAT_00069d90), fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor from the three-byte cell records at 0x53, and fdps_run_death_scripts from opcode-2 unit scripts, which fdps_collect_death_scripts and fdps_collect_defeated_unit_events copy out of unit record +0x31 and which fdps_deploy_unit fills from deployment record +0x16 at 00023783. Across all 63 shipped map%02d.dat, entry 40 is named in exactly one place: map25.dat's turn-event record 0, (turn 4, handler 40, side 0), that file's only live turn event. Side 0 is the enemy phase, so the event fires as the enemy phase of turn 4 opens -- immediately after the player's fourth turn ends. Map25.dat is chapter index 25, the player's chapter 26.

Which units the index range covers follows from the deployment table. map25.dat's header byte +1 is 0x0c, so fdps_build_map_unit_array lays out 12 player slots first; header byte +2 is 0x50, its 80 deployment records at image offset 0x83, stride 0x1a; fdps_deploy_wave(map, 0, 1) then appends the 68 records whose wave byte +0x15 is 0, in file order, so unit index 0x1a..0x2d is deployment records 14..33. Those twenty records are two identical ten-unit groups -- one character id 0x68, two 0x4e, two 0x5f and five 0x64 -- and every one of them carries behaviour byte +0x11 = 2. The range stops one short of record 34, where the map's eighteen already-advancing mode-0 records begin. Records 0..13 (the four commanders, ids 0x40..0x43, plus one more ten-unit group) and 52..61 / 67..72 (the sixteen id-0x61 units) stay in mode 2 until fdps_chapter_26_event_deploy_waves_2_and_3, entry 41 of the same table, deploys the map's wave-2 and wave-3 records and then clears the low nibble over unit indices 0x0c..0x4f, the whole wave-0 block.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the unit whose event fired. fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the dispatcher that reaches this entry, pushes a literal 0; the table's other dispatchers forward a battle unit index. Present only because every slot of the table shares one function-pointer type; this handler stores 0 over the slot and never reads it.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and read-modify-writes the packed nibble field of the game's own unit record, paints the chapter's text bank onto the VGA screen, and is reached only through a game-owned dispatch table; no Function ID candidate in the Watcom or ailv3.lib sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
The write is rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, not rec[0x34] = 0. Writing the obvious "reset the behaviour mode" as a plain store also wipes bits 0x40 and 0x80 of the same byte, which are separate per-unit flags that fdps_map_actor_take_best_action (00012c6f) and fdps_score_targets_for_item (0001337d) test, and the twenty released units would take a different AI path afterwards. The loop bound is inclusive as well -- i <= 0x2d -- so a rewrite using i < 0x2d silently leaves unit 0x2d holding position.

=== 00039230 [PLATE]
Chapter 26's mid-map ambush trigger: the first time a player-side unit walks onto the marked tile, the map's enemy reinforcements and its allied relief force both come onto the battlefield and the tower garrison stops holding position and charges the party.

Algorithm:
Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and does nothing at all unless the one-shot guard byte DAT_000640e8 is still 0 and that record's side byte at +6 is 2. Side 2 is the player, 0 the enemy and 1 the allied/neutral side, so an enemy or an ally crossing the same tile changes nothing. When both gates pass it runs, in this order:
  1. FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 2, 0) -- deploys every deployment record of the current map whose wave byte (record offset +0x15) equals 2. In map25.dat those are records 73..79: seven side-0 enemies, the wave whose death script is fdps_chapter_26_event_wave_2_defeated_line.
  2. FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0xa, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) -- paints line 10 of the chapter text image (fdetxt26.txt, held at DAT_00060124) straight onto the visible mode-13h screen at 0xa0000, 320 bytes per row.
  3. Clears the map-cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so fdps_draw_map_cursor draws nothing, pans the view with fdps_map_cursor_move_to(0xf0, 0x378) -- pixel (240, 888), which at 0x18 pixels per tile is tile column 10, row 37, the bottom of the map where both waves arrive -- then calls fdps_render_view_frame twelve times to hold that view, and restores the cursor mode to 1.
  4. Paints line 11, then FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 3, 0) deploys the wave-3 records -- in map25.dat records 62..66, five side-1 allied units, the guide's 英雄索爾 and his four 侍衛 -- then paints line 12.
  5. Walks unit indices 0x0c through 0x4f inclusive and stores (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0 back into each record's byte 0x34. The low nibble of +0x34 is the AI behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on: the garrison carries mode 2 from the scenario file, which only strikes what is already in reach and never leaves its tile, while mode 0 also advances along a traced path and closes on the nearest opposing unit. The four high bits are separate flags and are preserved. The range covers deployment records 0..67 -- the tower garrison plus the five allies that have just landed, which is why they start moving too -- and stops short of units 0x50..0x5b, so six garrison units and all seven wave-2 arrivals keep holding position.
  6. Sets DAT_000640e8 to 1, so the whole sequence runs at most once. fdps_chapter_state_reset memsets the 0x20-byte block at 0x000640d8, which is what clears this flag when the chapter is entered again.

The entry is never called by name. Its address is the pointer at 0x00060268, slot 41 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped data the only thing that selects slot 41 is the tile-event table of map25.dat -- map 25, chapter 26 -- whose entry for cell event code 1, the two bytes at file offset 0x33, is {slot 41, occasion 0}. fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event arms DAT_00069d90 with that slot when the cell a unit occupies carries a non-zero event code and the entry's second byte equals its own trigger_kind argument; the single-tile movement steppers pass 0 while the end-of-turn callers pass 1, so this fires as a unit walks across the tile rather than when it stops on it. The turn driver then calls the armed handler with the index of the unit that just moved, through PUSH index / CALL [0x601c4 + slot*4] / ADD ESP,4.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit whose movement armed the trigger, 0x00..0x5b on this map (0x00..0x0b are the twelve party slots, 0x0c upward the map's 80 deployment records). Read from [EBP+0x14], passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, and only the side byte of that record is looked at. The frame slot holding it is reused as the 0..11 counter of the twelve-frame hold afterwards.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; every callee and every global is game code, and its only reference is a slot of the game's own chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4]

Rebuild note:
Update the behaviour byte as rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, never as rec[0x34] = 0. The OR operand is the constant 0, so the whole store looks like a plain zeroing, but bits 0x40 and 0x80 of that byte are independent unit flags that other map-AI code reads; clearing them changes how those units behave. The release range is likewise 0x0c..0x4f inclusive, not "every deployed unit": units 0x50..0x5b are meant to go on holding position.

=== 000393aa [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0] aligning FUN_000393b0 to 16 bytes.

=== 000393b0 [PLATE]
Chapter 26's wave-2 wipe line: the death script of the seven enemy reinforcements the chapter's tile trigger brings on runs it, and once the last of them is gone it paints the guest hero's line onto the screen and latches itself off.

Algorithm:
Clears its local flag, then falls straight through to the epilogue if the one-shot latch DAT_000640ea is already non-zero. Otherwise it runs i = 0 .. 6, calling fdps_unit_is_retired(0x50 + i) on each, and raises the flag as soon as one of those seven units answers 0. If the flag is still 0 -- every one of the seven is retired -- it calls fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x17, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d), which walks message 0x17 of the chapter's text image and paints it straight onto the mode-13h screen at 0xa0000 with a 0x140-byte pitch; 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the foreground, background and outline colours it forwards unchanged to fdps_draw_glyph. It then stores 1 into DAT_000640ea so the line is drawn once. DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" entry fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads out of Field.vfs at 0002286f-00022894 for the chapter index DAT_00069cf4 plus one, here fdetxt26.txt. The incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] is overwritten with 0 at 000393cc and reused as the loop counter; the value the dispatcher pushed is never read.

Unit indices 0x50 .. 0x56 are the chapter's seven wave-2 enemy reinforcements. fdps_build_map_unit_array opens the battle with DAT_00064118 player slots -- map25.dat header byte 1, which is 12 -- at 0x00 .. 0x0b, then lays the map's 68 wave-0 records into 0x0c .. 0x4f; when a player-side unit walks across the map's trigger tile, fdps_chapter_26_event_deploy_waves_2_and_3 calls fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, 2, 0), which appends map25.dat's seven wave-2 records (records 73 .. 79, enemy id 0x64, level 0x12) at 0x50 .. 0x56, and only afterwards brings the five allied wave-3 records on behind them at 0x57 .. 0x5b. 12 + 68 + 7 + 5 is the map's whole complement, and 0x50 .. 0x56 is exactly the range this body polls.

Those same seven records carry the death script 02 2a 00 at record + 0x16, and that is what reaches this entry. fdps_run_death_scripts walks the 3-byte scripts fdps_collect_death_scripts copied out of the units a battle action has just killed, and its opcode 2 calls table[operand] through 0x000601c4 at 0001dcae with operand 42.

The all-retired test can only ever succeed because of the order fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack runs the three steps in: fdps_collect_death_scripts at 00012fde takes the script of every unit at 0 HP whose retired bit is still clear, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead at 00012fe9 then stores 1 into record + 5 of each of them, and only then does fdps_run_death_scripts at 00012ffc dispatch the collected scripts. So the seventh unit already reads as retired on the pass that kills it.

The entry is never called by name; its address is slot 42 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4, the relocated pointer at 0x0006026c. Nothing else in the shipped data selects slot 42: over all 63 MAP*.DAT, the number 42 appears in none of the turn-event tables (header + 3, stride 3) and none of the tile-trigger tables (header + 0x31, stride 2), and as a death-script operand (opcode 2 at record + 0x16, signed operand at + 0x17) only in map25.dat records 73 .. 79.

Message 0x17 of fdetxt26.txt opens with the -0x11 portrait token carrying character id 0x0c, and 0x0c is map25.dat's single wave-3 ally, deployment record 62 -- the guide's LV40 英雄索爾, the level-40 guest hero it says can take the wave-2 group on by himself. So the line is his. What it actually says has not been read: the rest of the entry is 16-bit indices into the Fdetxt.fon glyph sheet rather than Big5 code points, and no index-to-character mapping exists yet.

DAT_000640ea is not private to this handler. It is one of the 0x20 bytes fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) when a chapter starts, and fdps_chapter_27_event_deploy_wave_1 latches the same byte in the chapter that follows.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the dword every slot of the table at 0x000601c4 is called with. The dispatcher that reaches this entry, fdps_run_death_scripts, forwards its own first argument at 0001dcaa-0001dcad: the index of the unit that made the killing action -- the same value it hands to fdps_get_unit_record at 0001d9aa, pays the drops and the gold to, and tests for player side and not-retired -- not the index of the dead unit whose script is running. Overwritten with 0 at 000393cc and used as the 0 .. 6 loop counter, so its incoming value has no effect here.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own handler table, both callees are fdps game routines, and the state it touches is game state -- the chapter latch DAT_000640ea and the chapter text pointer DAT_00060124; no Function ID candidate in either library set and the hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
Keep the guard a chapter-scoped byte in the block fdps_chapter_state_reset clears, not a function-local static: a static fires the line once per process and would skip it on a replay of chapter 26. And keep the caller's collect / mark-dead / run-scripts order, because this handler's all-retired test depends on the dead already carrying the retired bit when it runs.
