=== 00056bb7 [PLATE]
Blit mode 3 of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface, recolouring every pixel it writes by arithmetic on the palette index rather than through a lookup table.

Algorithm:
Entry state is whatever fdps_blit_dispatch set up before the CALL at 00056953 (the CMP BH,0x3 arm): ESI = the packed pixel stream, EDI = the first destination pixel, EDX = pitch - width (the end-of-row advance), ECX = 0, and EBP still pointing at the dispatcher's own stack frame. The first three instructions lift the recolour operands out of that frame -- tint_offset = [EBP+0x1c], color_base = [EBP+0x1d], band mask = [EBP+0x1e], the three low bytes of the dispatcher's sixth argument -- into DH, DL and AH; only then does PUSH EDX / POP EBP replace EBP with the row advance, which is why those reads come first.
Each row begins by loading BX from the width word at 00070024, the count of destination columns still to fill. A token byte is read from ESI and its top two bits pick one of the four ops of the RLE 4-op stream, the run length in every case being (token & 0x3f) + 1:
  00 -- fill: one source byte, recoloured, REP STOSB'd len times; BX -= len.
  01 -- stretched fill: one source byte, recoloured, written to every other destination byte starting at EDI+1 (the INC EDI at 00056c09 precedes the STOSB), EDI advancing by 2 per pixel; BX -= 2 * len, so the run covers 2 * len columns and leaves the even ones untouched.
  10 -- literal copy: len source bytes, each recoloured and stored in turn; BX -= len.
  11 -- skip: EDI += len with nothing written, leaving the destination pixels as they were; BX -= len.
The recolour applied before every store is AL = ((src + tint_offset) & mask) + color_base, each step in 8 bits (00056be5 / 00056be7 / 00056be9, and the same three instructions on each of the other two writing paths). It never reads the pixel already on the destination, so nothing here blends. This is the construct the predecessor project settled as ((src + tint_offset) & 7) + color_base (fd2_tile_blit_24x24_with_tint_offset, and the 'translucent overlay' palette_op mode of fd2_rle_blit_sprite), generalised here by making the band mask a parameter instead of a literal 7: with mask 7 the sprite is folded into the 8-colour palette band anchored at color_base while tint_offset rotates which colour of the band each pixel lands on; with mask 0 the whole sprite collapses to the single index color_base.
A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero -- the test is OR BX,BX / JNZ, not a bound -- whereupon EDI += the row advance held in EBP, the row counter at 00070022 is decremented, and the next row starts by reloading BX. The routine returns when that counter reaches zero, so the blit consumes the counter and leaves it at zero.
Every call site that selects mode 3 with a literal reaches it through fdps_blit_unit_sprite with 0x0000ff00 as the dispatcher's sixth argument -- tint_offset 0, color_base 0xff, mask 0 -- which is the collapsing case: the unit is painted as a flat silhouette in palette index 0xff. fdps_unit_rest and fdps_battle_advance_turn both use that for the white rest flash. Other call sites take the mode from data (fdps_draw_tilemap_cell reads it out of a draw-request record, fdps_cel_blit_sprite from its own argument), so other tint_offset / color_base / mask triples can reach this kernel.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. The contract is by register and through the caller's frame: ESI = packed 4-op RLE pixel stream, EDI = destination pixel pointer, EDX = end-of-row advance (pitch - width), ECX = 0, EBP = fdps_blit_dispatch's frame pointer, whose bytes at +0x1c, +0x1d and +0x1e supply tint_offset, color_base and the band mask. Width and height come from the 16-bit words at 00070024 and 00070022, which fdps_blit_dispatch writes from its own width and height arguments.

Returns:
  nothing. It destroys EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI and EBP without saving them; fdps_blit_dispatch restores EBX, ESI, EDI and EBP from its own prologue after the call.

Pool: fdps  [called only by fdps_blit_dispatch; shares the blitter's state globals at 00070022 and 00070024; no library byte match on either the Watcom or the ail set]

Rebuild note:
Three things a straight rewrite gets wrong. (1) The 01 stretched-fill run writes the odd destination columns: INC EDI precedes STOSB at 00056c09, so the pixels land at dst[1], dst[3], ... while the run still charges 2*len against the column budget; the obvious `for (i = 0; i < len; i++) dst[2*i] = px;` puts every pixel one column to the left of the original. (2) The three recolour bytes are the low bytes of fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument, read straight out of the dispatcher's frame as an immediate value, but that same argument is a 256-byte remap table pointer for modes 1 and 2 and a descriptor pointer for the blend modes, so giving it one C type across all thirteen kernels is wrong. (3) The byte packing is not the predecessor's. FD2 packs this same recolour as color_base = op & 0xff and offset = (op >> 8) & 0xff with the mask hardcoded to 7; FDPS packs the offset in the low byte (+0x1c, added before the mask), color_base in byte 1 (+0x1d, added after it) and the band mask in byte 2 (+0x1e). Carrying FD2's expression or its packed constants across swaps the two operands, and because the observed FDPS constant 0x0000ff00 relies on mask 0 to collapse the output to one index, the swap turns a flat white silhouette into a scrambled sprite rather than into an obvious crash.

=== 00056bf4 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler

=== 00056c14 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler, no references

=== 00056c38 [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler, unreachable, interior to FUN_00056bb7 after an unconditional jmp

=== 00056c5e [PLATE]
Blit mode 4 of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface rescaled to an arbitrary destination width and height.

Algorithm:
Reads its two scale words straight out of the caller's stack frame -- [EBP+0x1c] is the destination width and [EBP+0x1e] the destination height, the low and high halves of fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument -- and publishes them into the shared graphics parameter block as DAT_00070028 and DAT_0007002a. It then zeroes EBP and reuses it as a Bresenham accumulator for the rest of the routine. DAT_0007002c is seeded with the destination height as the count of destination rows still to write, DAT_00070026 with the same value as the vertical accumulator, and DAT_00070030 with the destination pitch (DAT_0007002e) minus the destination width, the advance from the end of one destination row to the start of the next.

Each destination row loads DX with the source width (DAT_00070024), BX and BP with the destination width, and pushes ESI, which points at the first control byte of the current source row. It then decodes control bytes until BX destination pixels have been written. The top two bits of a control byte select the operation and the low six bits plus one give its length: 00 is a run of the one following byte, 01 is a half-tone run of the one following byte written to every other pixel over twice the length, 10 is a literal copy of length bytes, 11 skips length pixels and leaves the destination untouched. Every operation drives the same horizontal Bresenham inner loop: while BP is below the source width it adds the destination width and consumes one pixel of the run (for op 10 that also advances ESI, for op 01 it flips the half-tone phase held in AH); once BP has reached the source width it subtracts the source width and emits one destination pixel, decrementing BX. A source pixel is therefore emitted more than once when scaling up and dropped when scaling down, and a run may be abandoned part-way when the destination row fills.

At the end of a destination row ESI is popped back to the start of the source row, and the vertical Bresenham runs: while the accumulator is not above the source height (DAT_00070022) it calls fdps_rle_skip_row to step ESI over one whole encoded source row and adds the destination height; then it subtracts the source height once and stores the accumulator back into DAT_00070026. EDI advances by DAT_00070030 and DAT_0007002c is decremented; the routine returns when no destination rows are left. A source row is thus re-decoded from its start as many times as the vertical scale calls for.

Parameters:
  none in C terms -- the routine takes no stack arguments. Its inputs arrive in registers and in the parameter block fdps_blit_dispatch fills: ESI = the source RLE stream, EDI = the destination surface, EBP = the caller's own frame pointer, from which the packed destination width and height are read; DAT_00070022 = source height in rows, DAT_00070024 = source width in pixels, DAT_0007002e = destination pitch in bytes.

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in Watcom 10.0x or ailv3.lib; shares the graphics parameter block at 0x00070022-0x00070033 with its caller fdps_blit_dispatch and its callee fdps_rle_skip_row]

Rebuild note:
The kernel reads its two scale words out of fdps_blit_dispatch's own stack frame at [EBP+0x1c]/[EBP+0x1e], then zeroes EBP at 00056c74 and uses it as the Bresenham accumulator for the whole routine without ever restoring it, so it destroys the caller's frame pointer and only survives because fdps_blit_dispatch's epilogue pops EBP off ESP instead of relying on it -- a rewrite that keeps this as inline assembly must not assume EBP is live across the call, and one that turns it into a real C function must have the dispatcher unpack that argument and pass it. Second, the source cursor is pushed at the top of every destination row and popped back at 00056d84, so a row whose decode stopped part-way (the destination row filled before the run was exhausted) still advances to the next source row only through fdps_rle_skip_row: writing the obvious C that carries one source pointer straight on from wherever the decode stopped desynchronises the stream, and re-decoding the same row for vertical upscaling stops working.

=== 00056d25 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler inside the FUN_00056c5e address range

=== 00056d5b [EOL]
Three 0x90 NOP bytes: alignment filler, not reachable code.

=== 00056dc9 [PLATE]
Advances a source pointer past one encoded scanline of a 4-op RLE pixel stream without drawing anything, so a scaling blitter can drop the source rows it is not going to show.

Algorithm:
Loads the source bitmap width in pixels from the word at 0x00070024 into BX, the count of source pixels still unaccounted for in this row. Then repeats: LODSB one control byte from ESI and dispatch on its top two bits, the run length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as SHL CL twice to test the two flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL.
  00 fill:    one pixel byte follows and covers count pixels -- ESI ends two bytes on, BX -= count.
  01 stretch: one pixel byte follows and covers 2*count columns, the blitters writing it into the second pixel of each pair -- ESI ends two bytes on, BX -= count twice.
  10 literal: count pixel bytes follow -- ESI ends 1 + count bytes on (ADD ESI,ECX after the LODSB), BX -= count.
  11 skip:    no bytes follow, count transparent columns -- ESI ends one byte on, BX -= count.
That is the op table resource_info/cel.md records for this encoding, under the names fill / stretch / literal / skip.
After each op the loop continues while BX is non-zero, so it stops when the width counter lands on exactly zero, with ESI then on the first control byte of the next row. The four NOP runs are branch-target padding, not code.

Both call sites drive it the same way: fdps_rle_blit_scaled (00056d99) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (000574d1) restore ESI to the start of the row they have just blitted and then call this routine once per source row that the vertical Bresenham accumulator, compared against the source height word at 0x00070022 and stepped by the destination height at 0x0007002a, says to consume.

What the stream is: the pixel payload of a .CEL sprite or of a .SAF tilemap tile. fdps_cel_blit_sprite computes sheet + *(i32 *)(sheet + index * 4 + 0x0f) and passes it to fdps_blit_dispatch as the source argument that becomes ESI, and fdps_draw_tilemap_cell hands a tile's stream to the same dispatcher; the encoding is the same in both cases.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register contract: ESI is the pointer to the first control byte of an encoded row, and the row width in pixels is read from the word at 0x00070024, which the caller's blit parameter block already holds.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the side effect: ESI is left just past the encoded row. BX and CL are destroyed. The literal case adds all of ECX to ESI while only CL is ever loaded, and what makes that safe is upstream: fdps_blit_dispatch does XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d before every one of its thirteen mode calls, and neither blitter ever writes above CL -- the one 16-bit write in each, SHL CX,1 at 00056cf2 and 000572f9, doubles a value of at most 0x40 and so never carries into CH.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; shares the game's blit parameter globals at 0x00070022/0x00070024 with its two callers, and no runtime or Miles AIL routine takes a program global as an implicit argument]

Rebuild note:
This cannot be rewritten as the C function its prototype suggests: its argument and its result are both ESI, and it destroys ESI, BX and CL, which every Watcom convention requires a callee to preserve -- the callers depend on that, reloading BX at the top of each row and taking the advanced ESI as the return value. Give it a real C signature such as void fdps_rle_skip_row(unsigned char **p) and the two hand-written assembly blitters that call it stop working, so it has to stay in the assembly module with them.

Second, the loop ends only when the 16-bit counter reaches exactly zero; writing the obvious while (width > 0) changes behaviour on a row whose runs overshoot its width, where the original wraps BX and keeps decoding. resource_info/cel.md records the same wrap on the drawing side, where it walks off the end of the destination instead.

Third, if this is ever rewritten in C, the literal case must add a count narrowed to 8 bits. The original adds the whole of ECX while only ever loading CL, relying on fdps_blit_dispatch's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d having cleared the rest once at the top of the whole blit; a rewrite that reaches this routine by any other path, or that keeps a wider count variable live across rows, loses that guarantee silently and corrupts the source pointer.

=== 00056e2a [PLATE]
Blit mode 5: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface rotated (and uniformly shrunk), by walking the destination along two perpendicular fixed-point vectors built from the single (dx, dy) pair the dispatcher's sixth argument carries.

Algorithm:
Setup. Clears the two row-to-row fractional accumulators at 0x00070048 and 0x0007004a, reads dx from the word at [EBP+0x1c] and dy from the word at [EBP+0x1e] -- the low and high halves of fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument, still live in the dispatcher's frame -- and loads the destination pitch from the word at 0x0007002e into EBP. It then branches on the signs of dx and dy into four arms that write the same four quantities with the signs of that quadrant folded in, and store the absolute values of dx and dy at 0x0007004c and 0x0007004e:
  0x00070034 = sign(dx)          -- x step taken while walking along a source row
  0x00070038 = -sign(dy) * pitch -- y step taken while walking along a source row
  0x0007003c = sign(dy)          -- x step taken when moving to the next source row
  0x00070040 = sign(dx) * pitch  -- y step taken when moving to the next source row
So one source pixel advances the destination by (dx, -dy) / 0x1000 and one source row advances it by (dy, dx) / 0x1000. Those two vectors are perpendicular and of equal length, which is what makes this a rotation: with dx = k*cos and dy = k*sin, k = 0x1000 is unit scale and a shorter k shrinks the image. The four sign arms are the four quadrants of that vector, not four mirroring modes.

Row loop, entered at 0x00056f19. Each pass reloads BX from the sprite width at 0x00070024 (the source columns still to be consumed on this row), zeroes the two within-row accumulators DX and BP, and pushes EDI so the row's origin can be restored at the end.

Within a row it LODSBs one control byte from ESI and dispatches on its top two bits, the run length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as two SHL CL,1 that test the flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL. These are the four ops of the CEL pixel encoding, decoded exactly as fdps_blit_rle_passthrough decodes them:
  00 fill:    one pixel byte follows and is stored count times; BX -= count.
  01 stretch: one pixel byte follows and covers 2*count columns, an AH flag toggled each step suppressing the store on the first column of every pair so only the second is painted; BX -= 2*count.
  10 literal: count pixel bytes follow, one LODSBed and stored per step; BX -= count.
  11 skip:    no bytes follow and nothing is stored, the destination merely advances count steps; BX -= count.
Every step of every op advances the destination the same way: DX += |dx| and, if DX reaches 0x1000, DX -= 0x1000 and EDI += the x step at 0x00070034; then BP += |dy| and, if BP reaches 0x1000, BP -= 0x1000, the pixel is stored a second time at the current EDI, and EDI += the y step at 0x00070038. That second store is the gap filler: on a diagonal step it paints both the horizontal and the vertical neighbour so the rotated run stays connected. A single 0x1000 is subtracted per step, not a modulo, so an accumulator increment larger than 0x1000 still advances at most one destination pixel -- the routine can shrink but never magnify.
A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero.

Row advance, at 0x000570a8. EDI is popped back to the row origin, then 0x00070048 += |dy| stepping EDI by 0x0007003c on carry, and 0x0007004a += |dx| stepping EDI by 0x00070040 on carry -- the perpendicular vector, accumulated across the whole blit rather than reset per row. The row counter, the word at 0x00070022, is then decremented and the routine returns once it reaches zero.
The MOV DX,[0x00070026] at 0x000570a9 is dead: DX is reloaded from 0x00070048 at 0x000570b0 before any use. 0x00070026 is written only by the scaling kernel FUN_00056c5e. The four-NOP runs after conditional jumps and the three-byte fillers after unconditional ones are assembler padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register-and-frame contract established by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the destination pixel the source's top-left corner maps to, EBP still points at the dispatcher's frame so that dx = word [EBP+0x1c] and dy = word [EBP+0x1e] can be read out of its sixth argument, and ECX must have its upper 16 bits clear because only CL is ever loaded while LOOP consumes all of ECX. The geometry comes from the blit parameter words the dispatcher has just published: sprite width at 0x00070024, row count at 0x00070022, destination pitch at 0x0007002e. Unlike fdps_blit_rle_passthrough it ignores the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance, because it restores EDI to the row origin itself.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the drawn, rotated image. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI and EBP are all destroyed, the row counter at 0x00070022 is left at zero, and the eight blit parameter words at 0x00070034-0x0007004e are left holding this call's step vectors.

Reachability: no code path in FDPS.LE selects mode 5. Every operand that can reach the mode byte at fdps_blit_dispatch's [EBP+0x20] was enumerated -- the 46 direct call sites pass the literals 0, 8, 9 and 0xb or forward a wrapper's own argument; fdps_cel_blit_sprite's mode argument (its eighth, not its seventh) is a literal 0 at 50 sites and a literal 4 at four; fdps_blit_unit_sprite is given 0 or 3; fdps_draw_scene_layer passes 9 or 0xa; and the draw request that fdps_draw_tilemap_cell forwards carries 0, 3 or 9 in its +0x20 field, with no store of 5 into any +0x20 field anywhere in the image. The kernel is compiled in and called from the dispatcher's mode-5 arm, but that arm is not taken in the shipped game.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the Miles AIL set and the body hash is unique in the image; it shares the game's blit parameter block at 0x00070022-0x0007004e with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, and 737 bytes of sprite decode logic is neither a runtime primitive nor a linker artifact]

Rebuild note:
Three things a faithful rewrite has to keep. First, each accumulator subtracts a single 0x1000 on carry rather than taking a modulo, so an increment larger than 0x1000 still advances at most one destination pixel per step: the obvious 'pos += dx; dst += pos >> 12; pos &= 0xfff' magnifies where the original clamps, and the mode silently becomes a different transform. Second, the vertical carry stores the pixel a second time at the current EDI before stepping (00056f79, 00056fe1, 00057043); dropping that as a redundant write leaves one-pixel holes along every diagonal run. Third, the two row-to-row accumulators at 0x00070048/0x0007004a are cleared once at entry and deliberately carry across rows, unlike the within-row DX/BP pair which is zeroed at the top of every row -- resetting them per row turns the rotation into a shear. As with its sibling kernels it also cannot be given a real C signature: it takes its inputs in ESI, EDI and the caller's own EBP frame, requires the upper 16 bits of ECX to be clear (fdps_blit_dispatch's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d supplies that), destroys EBX, ESI, EDI and EBP, and ends its row loop only when BX reaches exactly zero, so a stream whose ops overrun the width wraps the counter and keeps writing. One more thing the re-read adds: no call site in the image selects mode 5, so a rewrite of this kernel cannot be validated by playing the game -- the three rules above have to be transcribed from the assembly and taken on the assembly's authority, and the dispatcher's mode-5 arm has to keep calling it even though nothing exercises that arm.

=== 00056eb5 [EOL]
3 bytes of 0x90 NOP filler, no references

=== 00056ee7 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler

=== 00057058 [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler inside FUN_00056e2a, after JMP at 00057056, before code resuming at 0005705b

=== 00057114 [PLATE]
Blit mode 6: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface both resampled to a caller-chosen destination width and height and rotated, the geometry arriving in a four-int record that fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument points at.

Algorithm:
Setup. EBP still points at fdps_blit_dispatch's frame, so MOV EBP,[EBP+0x1c] replaces it with the parameter record pointer and the four fields are read out before EBP is destroyed: the word at record+0 becomes the destination width at 0x00070028, the word at record+4 the destination height at 0x0007002a, and the words at record+8 and record+0xc become the rotation vector (dx, dy) held in DX and AX. The two row-to-row fractional accumulators at 0x00070048 and 0x0007004a are cleared, and the destination pitch is loaded from the word at 0x0007002e into EBP.
It then branches on the signs of dx and dy into four arms (00057162, 0005718f, 000571c3, 000571eb) that write the same four step quantities with that quadrant's signs folded in, and store |dx| at 0x0007004c and |dy| at 0x0007004e as the fractional increments:
  0x00070034 = sign(dx)          -- x step taken between two destination pixels of a row
  0x00070038 = -sign(dy) * pitch -- y step taken between two destination pixels of a row
  0x0007003c = sign(dy)          -- x step taken when moving to the next destination row
  0x00070040 = sign(dx) * pitch  -- y step taken when moving to the next destination row
So one destination pixel advances by (dx, -dy) / 0x1000 and one destination row advances by (dy, dx) / 0x1000. Those two vectors are perpendicular and of equal length, which makes the walk a rotation with a uniform scale on top of the resampling the row and column counters already do. This is the same vector construction fdps_rle_blit_rotated (mode 5) uses; what mode 6 adds is that the rectangle being walked is destination-sized rather than source-sized.
The row counter at 0x0007002c and the vertical resampling accumulator at 0x00070026 are both seeded with the destination height.

Row loop, entered at 0005722f. Each pass reloads BX from the destination width at 0x00070028 -- the number of destination pixels still to be emitted on this row -- copies it into BP as the horizontal resampling accumulator, zeroes the two within-row fractional accumulators at 0x00070044 and 0x00070046, and pushes ESI and EDI so the row's stream position and origin can be restored at the end.

Within a row it LODSBs one control byte from ESI and dispatches on its top two bits, the run length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as SHL CL,1 twice to test the flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL. These are the four ops of the CEL pixel encoding, the same four fdps_blit_rle_passthrough decodes:
  00 fill    (0005726a): one pixel byte follows in the stream and is the value for all count source columns.
  01 stretch (000572f4): one pixel byte follows and covers 2*count source columns, an AH flag toggled on every source column consumed suppressing the store on the first column of each pair so only the second is painted.
  10 literal (000573a5): count pixel bytes follow; the current one is read with MOV AL,[ESI] when a pixel is emitted and ESI is advanced with INC ESI when a source column is consumed.
  11 skip    (00057438): no bytes follow and nothing is stored; the destination merely advances over count source columns' worth of destination pixels.
Every op runs the same two interleaved counters. BP holds the horizontal resampling accumulator: while BP is below the source width at 0x00070024 the run's next source column is consumed (BP += destination width, CL decremented, and the run ends into the next control byte when CL reaches zero); once BP reaches the source width, BP -= source width and one destination pixel is emitted, decrementing BX. So count source columns are stretched or squeezed into however many destination pixels the width ratio calls for.
Each emitted destination pixel then walks the destination: 0x00070044 += |dx| and, on reaching 0x1000, 0x00070044 -= 0x1000 and EDI += the x step at 0x00070034; then 0x00070046 += |dy| and, on reaching 0x1000, 0x00070046 -= 0x1000, the pixel is stored a second time at the current EDI, and EDI += the y step at 0x00070038. That second store is the diagonal gap filler; in the stretch op it is suppressed on the same AH parity as the main store, and in the skip op it is absent along with the main store.
A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero.

Row advance, at 000574bb. EDI is popped back to the row origin and ESI back to the start of the source row just drawn. The vertical resampling accumulator at 0x00070026 then advances: while it is still at or below the source height at 0x00070022 the routine calls fdps_rle_skip_row to step ESI over one whole encoded source row and adds the destination height, and when it passes the source height it subtracts the source height and is stored back. A destination taller than the source therefore skips no rows and redraws the same source row; a shorter one drops rows.
EDI is then moved to the next destination row by the perpendicular vector: 0x00070048 += |dy| stepping EDI by 0x0007003c on carry, and 0x0007004a += |dx| stepping EDI by 0x00070040 on carry. Unlike the within-row pair these two are cleared once at entry and deliberately carry across rows.
The row counter at 0x0007002c is decremented and the routine returns once it reaches zero. The four-NOP runs after conditional jumps and the two three-byte fillers at 000571b6 and 000571e8 after unconditional ones are assembler padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register-and-frame contract established by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the destination pixel the source's top-left corner maps to, EBP still points at the dispatcher's frame so that [EBP+0x1c] yields the parameter record pointer, and ECX must have its upper 16 bits clear because only CL is ever loaded; the dispatcher's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d supplies that. The record is four 32-bit slots of which only the low words are read: +0 destination width in pixels, +4 destination height in rows, +8 dx and +0xc dy, the rotation vector in 1/0x1000 units. The rest of the geometry comes from the blit parameter words the dispatcher has just published: source width at 0x00070024, source height at 0x00070022, destination pitch at 0x0007002e. Like the other transforming kernels it ignores the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance, because it restores EDI to the row origin itself.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the drawn, resampled and rotated image. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, EBP, ESI and EDI are all destroyed, the row counter at 0x0007002c is left at zero, and the blit parameter words at 0x00070026-0x0007004e are left holding this call's destination size, step vectors and accumulator residues.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the Miles AIL library set and the body hash is unique in the image; it shares the game's blit parameter block at 0x00070022-0x0007004e with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, and 1079 bytes of sprite decode logic is neither a runtime primitive nor a linker artifact]

Rebuild note:
Four things a faithful rewrite has to keep. First, the two fixed-point accumulators subtract a single 0x1000 on carry rather than taking a modulo, so an increment larger than 0x1000 still advances at most one destination pixel: the obvious 'pos += dx; dst += pos >> 12; pos &= 0xfff' magnifies where the original clamps. Second, the vertical carry stores the pixel a second time at the current EDI before stepping (000572dc, 00057381, 0005741c); dropping that as a redundant write leaves one-pixel holes along every diagonal run. Third, the row-to-row accumulators at 0x00070048/0x0007004a are cleared once at entry and deliberately carry across rows, unlike the within-row pair at 0x00070044/0x00070046 which is zeroed at the top of every row -- resetting them per row turns the rotation into a shear. Fourth, the horizontal loop is bounded only by the destination pixel count BX and the vertical loop only by the row counter at 0x0007002c, and the source row's own ops are never counted out: the decoder deliberately under-consumes the stream and relies on POP ESI plus fdps_rle_skip_row to find the next row, so a rewrite that advances one shared source pointer through the decode loop desynchronises the stream. A destination width or height of zero means 65536 iterations, not none. As with its sibling kernels it also cannot be given a real C signature: it takes its inputs in ESI, EDI and the caller's own EBP frame, requires the upper 16 bits of ECX to be clear, and destroys EBX, EBP, ESI and EDI, so it has to stay in the assembly module with its dispatcher.

=== 00057551 [PLATE]
Blit mode 7: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface mirrored left to right, so art drawn facing one way can be shown facing the other. The other axis is mode 8, fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical.

Algorithm:
Reads the destination pitch once from the word at 0x0007002e into EDX, then runs one pass per destination row. Each pass reloads the sprite width in pixels from the word at 0x00070024 into BX -- the number of destination columns still to be covered on this row -- saves the row's left edge with PUSH EDI, and moves EDI forward by width-1 to the row's right-hand column, from which the whole row is decoded leftwards.

Inside a row it LODSBs one control byte from ESI and dispatches on its top two bits, the length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as two SHL CL,1 that test the flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL:
  00 fill:    one pixel byte follows; STD then REP STOSB writes it into count columns walking left, then CLD; BX -= count.
  01 stretch: one pixel byte follows; a DEC EDI / store / DEC EDI loop writes it into every other column across 2*count columns, leaving the columns it steps over untouched; BX -= count twice.
  10 literal: count pixel bytes follow, each LODSBed and stored with EDI walking left; BX -= count.
  11 skip:    no bytes follow; SUB EDI,ECX leaves count columns transparent; BX -= count.
These are the four ops of the CEL pixel encoding, and they consume the stream identically to the mode-0 kernel at 0x00056a0d; only the starting column and the direction of travel differ, so the output is the exact left-right reflection of that kernel's output within the same width-by-height destination rectangle.

A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero. EDI is then restored to the saved left edge and advanced by one full pitch, and the row counter -- the word at 0x00070022 -- is decremented; the routine returns once that reaches zero. The three four-NOP runs after the conditional jumps and the three-byte fillers after the unconditional ones are assembler padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register contract established by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the top-left corner of the destination rectangle, and the geometry comes from the blit parameter words the dispatcher has just published -- sprite width at 0x00070024, row count at 0x00070022, destination pitch at 0x0007002e. Unlike most of its sibling kernels it reads nothing out of the dispatcher's frame, and it ignores the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance the dispatcher leaves in EDX, reloading the full pitch instead because it restores EDI to the row origin itself.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the drawn rectangle. EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, and the row counter at 0x00070022 is left at zero. ECX must have its upper 24 bits clear on entry, since the skip op subtracts all of ECX from EDI while only CL is ever loaded; the dispatcher's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d supplies that.

Pool: fdps  [shares the game's blit parameter globals at 0x00070022/0x00070024/0x0007002e with fdps_blit_dispatch, which is its only caller; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the Miles AIL set, no runtime idiom, no interrupt or driver structure, and 147 bytes of real decode logic rather than a linker artifact]

Rebuild note:
The mirror is about the sprite's own box, not about EDI. EDI arrives pointing at the top-left corner exactly as it does for the mode-0 kernel, and this routine adds width-1 to it itself, so the mirrored image lands in the same destination rectangle; writing the obvious 'start at dst and walk backwards' draws it one whole width to the left. Two more things a faithful rewrite must keep: it deliberately ignores the EDX = pitch - width that the dispatcher hands every kernel and re-reads the full pitch from 0x0007002e, because it restores EDI to the row origin with PUSH/POP instead of letting it run off the row end, so reusing the siblings' end-of-row advance double-counts the width; and both loops are exit-tested, the row on BX becoming exactly zero and the pass count on a pre-decrement of 0x00070022, so a row whose ops overrun the width wraps BX and keeps writing past the row end, and a height of zero means 65536 rows rather than none. The stretch op is the one place where the reflection is not a simple index flip: mode 0 does INC EDI and then STOSB, painting the odd columns of its 2*count run, while this does DEC EDI and then the store, painting the columns that are the reflections of those, so a rewrite that mirrors mode 0's loop body without moving the decrement ahead of the store paints the complementary set of columns and the sprite comes out one pixel off. The routine also cannot carry a real C signature: its inputs and outputs are ESI/EDI plus three globals, and it destroys EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI and the row-count global, which every Watcom convention says a callee must not do, so it has to stay in the assembly module with its dispatcher.

=== 000575ed [PLATE]
Blit mode 8: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream vertically mirrored, by aiming the destination pointer at the bottom row of the target rectangle and handing the decoding itself to fdps_rle_blit_passthrough with an upward row step.

Algorithm:
Reads the three blit geometry words that fdps_blit_dispatch has just published: the destination pitch at 0x0007002e, the sprite width in pixels at 0x00070024 and the row count at 0x00070022. It zero-extends the pitch into EAX and the row count into EDX, decrements the row count with DEC DX, and multiplies them, so EAX = pitch * (rows - 1); adding that to EDI moves the destination pointer from the top-left corner of the rectangle to the left edge of its last row. It then builds its own end-of-row advance in EDX as -(pitch + width): the two words are added as 16 bits into a zeroed EDX and the sum is negated as 32 bits. Finally it tail-jumps to fdps_rle_blit_passthrough at 0x00056a0d.

That kernel is mode 0, the unmodified pass-through blit, and it decodes each row left to right, so EDI has already advanced by one full width by the time the kernel adds EDX at the end of a row (0x00056a81). Adding -(pitch + width) therefore lands EDI one pitch higher than the row started, and the kernel climbs the rectangle row by row -- its DEC word [0x00070022] / JNZ 0x00056a0d at 0x00056a83 re-enters at the very top, reloading the per-row pixel budget from 0x00070024 -- while consuming the source stream in its normal forward order. The result is the exact top-to-bottom reflection of mode 0's output inside the same width-by-height destination rectangle: the vertical counterpart of the left-to-right reflection fdps_rle_blit_mirrored performs for mode 7.

Nothing after the JMP belongs to this routine: the plain RET at 0x00056a8c that ends fdps_rle_blit_passthrough returns straight to the call site in fdps_blit_dispatch.

What mode 8 is for:
Exactly two call sites in the whole program select it, both inside fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input (the CALL at 0x0001732e and the CALL at 0x00017369), and both pass a 24x24 sprite, a pitch of 0x140 and the unit's front-facing walk-cycle frame. They are the opening phases of that window's randomly armed idle animation: frames 0..14 stamp the sprite upside down at column 161 on the row given by the 15-entry drop-and-bounce table the function copies from 0x14818, and frames 15..24 hold it upside down at the resting position (destination offset 0xd521 = row 170, column 161). From frame 25 the animation switches back to mode 0 and the character is the right way up again. So the vertical mirror in this game draws a unit head-down, and that is its only use.
No other path reaches mode 8: every other call site of fdps_blit_dispatch passes a literal 0, 4, 9 or 0xb, the three that compute the mode at run time yield 9 or 0xa (fdps_draw_scene_layer at 0x0002c603), 0 or 3 (fdps_blit_unit_sprite, whose three callers pass 3, 3 and 0-or-3) and the caller's own value (fdps_cel_blit_sprite forwards [EBP+0x30] unchanged, and every one of its call sites passes a literal 0 or 4), and nothing references the dispatcher's entry other than by CALL.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. This is hand-written assembly carrying the blit family's register contract, set up by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch (CALL at 0x000569b2, reached when the mode byte at [EBP+0x20] equals 8): ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the top-left corner of the destination rectangle, and the geometry arrives in the three globals above. It discards the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance the dispatcher leaves in EDX for its sibling kernels and substitutes the negative step described above.

Returns:
  nothing; the result is the drawn rectangle. It destroys EAX, EDX and EDI itself, and inherits everything fdps_rle_blit_passthrough destroys -- EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, and the row count at 0x00070022, which is left at zero.

Pool: fdps  [shares the game's blit geometry globals at 0x00070022/0x00070024/0x0007002e with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, as one of that dispatcher's thirteen mode kernels; no Function ID hit against the Watcom libraries or against ailv3.lib and the body hash is unique in the image, and it performs real raster arithmetic on program globals rather than merely redirecting control, so not binary_artifact]

Rebuild note:
The upward row step is -(pitch + width), not -pitch. fdps_rle_blit_passthrough adds it only after EDI has already walked one whole width across the row, so a rewrite that does the intuitive thing and steps the destination back by one pitch per row staggers the image one width further left on every row. The starting displacement is likewise pitch * (rows - 1) and not pitch * rows: the mirrored image has to occupy the very same rectangle an unmirrored blit of the same sprite would, and the off-by-one puts it a row too low. Both counts are 16-bit -- DEC DX on the row count means a row count of zero displaces the destination by 65535 pitches and then draws 65536 rows from there, far outside the surface, rather than drawing nothing. Getting any of that wrong will most likely survive playtesting: mode 8 is selected from exactly two call sites, both in fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input's idle animation, which arms itself only when a rand draw comes out a multiple of 200, so the only picture this kernel ever draws is a rarely seen easter egg. It has to be checked deliberately, not waited for.

=== 0005761b [PLATE]
Blit mode 9: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream translucently, blending every pixel it draws with the destination pixel underneath it at a caller-chosen 16-step level and resolving the blended colour back to a palette index.

Algorithm:
Entered by a plain CALL from fdps_blit_dispatch with that function's registers and stack frame still live: ESI = the RLE command stream, EDI = the first destination pixel, EDX = pitch - width (the end-of-row advance), EBP = the dispatcher's own frame pointer. EDX is parked in the scratch global at 0x00070030 straight away because the blend needs the register back, then the dispatcher's sixth argument [EBP+0x1c] is read as a pointer to a three-dword blend descriptor:
  +0x00  base of the shade-ramp table that fdps_build_palette_tables fills at 0x000653f0 -- 18 rows of 256 dwords, row k holding every palette colour packed as red in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11, blue in bits 0-3 and multiplied by the coefficient at 0x0002ae40[k], which is k for rows 0-8 and 16-(k-9) for rows 9-17.
  +0x04  blend level, 0 = opaque source through 16 = source invisible.
  +0x08  base of the 16x16x16 inverse colour cube at 0x000643f0, one palette index per 4-bit rgb triple.
From the level it picks the pair of ramp rows whose coefficients sum to 16, so the source always carries weight (16 - level)/16 and the destination level/16: at level <= 8 source pixels are looked up in row level+9 and destination pixels in row level; above 8 the same two weights are only available the other way round, so source reads row 16-level and destination row 25-level. Both row pointers, the cube base and the two constants 0x000f0f0f and 0x0000ffff are cached in the dispatcher's argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x18], which this kernel uses as its scratch area for the rest of the call.

Each row reloads the row width from the word at 0x00070024 into BX and decodes command bytes from ESI until BX is exactly zero. A command byte's low six bits give len = (cmd & 0x3f) + 1, i.e. 1..64, and its top two bits select the op:
  00 blended fill -- one pixel byte follows; its ramp value is held in EDX and blended into len consecutive destination pixels; BX -= len.
  01 stretched blended fill -- one pixel byte follows; blended into every other destination pixel starting at dst+1, across a 2*len span whose in-between pixels are left as they were; BX -= 2*len.
  10 blended literal -- len pixel bytes follow, each blended with the destination pixel under it; BX -= len.
  11 skip -- no bytes follow; EDI advances by len with nothing written, i.e. transparency; BX -= len.
All three drawing ops share the same blend: sum = src_row[src_pixel] + dst_row[dst_pixel], then (sum >> 4) & 0x000f0f0f, which cannot carry between the three channel bytes precisely because the two coefficients sum to 16 and no channel can exceed 15*16; the 12-bit cube index is then formed as (v >> 12) | (v & 0x0000ffff), putting green in bits 8-11, red in bits 4-7 and blue in bits 0-3, and the byte written out is cube[index].

At the end of a row EDI advances by the end-of-row value saved at 0x00070030, the 16-bit row counter at 0x00070022 is decremented in place, and the routine returns once that counter reaches zero, leaving the global at 0.

The level is a real per-call fade parameter rather than a fixed effect: the mode 9 call sites that build the descriptor in view pass 8 and 12 (0x00032209, 0x0003228b) and 10 (0x000332e6, 0x000339d3), and three more compute it -- fdps_draw_composite_sprite sets it to 16 minus the word at +7 of a sprite-part record (0x0001424e), so that record field is the source's own opacity and this level is its complement.

Where the three kernels that follow it stand: 0x00057793 (fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop, mode 10) and 0x00057916 (fdps_rle_blit_tint, mode 11) open with the same descriptor decode and end in the same masked add and cube lookup, but they take a fourth dword at +0x0c, fetch it once through the ramp row as a constant palette colour, and blend each source pixel against that constant instead of against the destination -- their level weights the constant colour, and mode 11 never reads [EDI] at all. Only 0x00057a74 (fdps_rle_blit_blend_color_range, mode 12) blends against the destination the way this one does, and it does so only for source pixels inside the colour band its descriptor carries at +0x0c/+0x10, storing the rest verbatim. So this kernel is the one that makes a whole sprite see-through.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register contract set up by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the RLE pixel stream, EDI the top-left destination pixel, EDX the end-of-row advance pitch - width, EBP the dispatcher's live frame, out of which [EBP+0x1c] supplies the blend descriptor pointer; the rectangle geometry comes from the words the dispatcher has just published, width at 0x00070024 and row count at 0x00070022.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the blended rectangle. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, the caller's argument slots [EBP+0x08]..[EBP+0x1c] are overwritten with scratch, the row counter at 0x00070022 is left at zero and 0x00070030 holds the end-of-row advance. Unlike the mode 0 kernel it does not rely on the caller for a clean ECX: it zeroes ECX itself at 00057667.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; shares the graphics state block at 0x00070022/0x00070024/0x00070030 with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, and blends through the game's own palette tables at 0x000653f0 and 0x000643f0 -- work no C runtime, maths library or audio driver ships]

Rebuild note:
The 12-bit index into the inverse colour cube at 0x000643f0 is built as (v >> 12) | (v & 0xffff) from a value carrying red in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11 and blue in bits 0-3, which lands green in bits 8-11, red in bits 4-7 and blue in bits 0-3: the cube is green-major, then red, then blue, so the obvious cube[(r << 8) | (g << 4) | b] returns a wrong colour for every pixel that is not grey. The level > 8 branch is not a second blend rule either -- it is the same two weights fetched from the other half of the ramp table, because rows 0-8 and 9-17 only carry the coefficients 0..8 and 16..8 -- so writing it as a special case, or picking any two rows whose coefficients do not sum to 16, breaks the masked add: a channel byte then exceeds 255 and carries into the next channel. The level's polarity is the third trap: 0 draws the source opaque and 16 makes it invisible, the opposite of the opacity the callers hold -- fdps_draw_composite_sprite stores 16 - opacity at 0x0001424e -- so passing an opacity straight through inverts every fade. Two family traps also apply here: the stretched op writes its first pixel at dst+1 and steps by 2, so for (i = 0; i < len; i++) dst[2*i] = px shifts the run one column left, and both loop terminators test for exactly zero (OR BX,BX after the subtraction, and a DEC of the word at 0x00070022), so a stream whose runs overrun the row width wraps BX and keeps painting, and a height of zero draws 65536 rows instead of none.

=== 0005771a [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler inside the address span of FUN_0005761b

=== 00057769 [EOL]
3-byte 90 90 90 alignment padding gap inside the 0005761b function range

=== 00057793 [PLATE]
Blit mode 0x0a of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one RLE 4-op sprite stream with every pixel it writes alpha-blended toward a single constant palette colour, and blends that same colour into the destination pixels showing through the sprite's transparent runs, so the whole width x height rectangle comes out tinted.

Selected by fdps_draw_scene_layer at 0002c5ee: when a scene layer's mode byte is 1 and a map tile's movement-grid cell is marked (byte 1 of the cell is not 0xff) and bit 0x80 of the tile's attribute flag is clear, that layer draws the tile through mode 0x0a rather than mode 9. Layer mode 1 is what every shipped DSC%02d.DAT in Field2.vfs gives its first layer, so this kernel is the ordinary way the battle map paints its movement/target range highlight: each marked tile is redrawn tinted toward DAT_00060154, at the blend level ramp[DAT_0006015c / 4] that pulses between 2 and 7 out of 16, and because the 0b11 op tints instead of skipping, the tint covers the whole 24x24 tile rather than only its opaque pixels.

Algorithm:
Entered by a plain CALL from fdps_blit_dispatch with that function's registers and frame still live: ESI = the RLE command byte stream, EDI = the first destination pixel of the first row in an 8bpp linear surface, EDX = pitch - width, EAX and ECX zeroed, and EBP still the dispatcher's frame pointer. EDX is spilled to DAT_00070030 at once because the body needs EDX as scratch; the end of every row adds it back to EDI from there.
[EBP+0x1c], the dispatcher's sixth argument, is a pointer to a four-dword blend descriptor: +0 blend_table, +4 alpha, +8 rgb444_lut, +0xc tint_color. blend_table is an [18][256] array of dwords holding every palette entry pre-scaled by a weight with one colour channel per byte -- the same table fdps_blit_tint_rect takes under that name, of the kind fdps_build_palette_tables builds at 000653f0. Rows 0..8 hold weights 0..8 at 0x400 bytes per row; rows 9..17 hold the complementary weights and begin 0x2400 further on. alpha is folded into 0..8 exactly as fdps_blit_tint_rect folds it: for alpha <= 8 the tint reads row alpha and the source pixels read row 9+alpha, and for alpha > 8 alpha is replaced by 16-alpha and the two rows swap, so either way the tint ends up weighted by the caller's alpha and the pixel by 16-alpha. The two row addresses are parked in [EBP+0xc] and [EBP+0x10], the masks 0x0f0f0f and 0xffff in [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], and blend_table[tint row][tint_color] is fetched once, before any drawing, into [EBP+0x1c]. Those six slots are the dispatcher's own incoming arguments, which the kernel destroys.
Every pixel is blended by the same sequence: read the scaled source colour blend_table[pixel row][pixel], add the scaled tint, shift right by 4 to divide out the /16 of the weights, mask with 0x0f0f0f to leave four bits per channel at bits 0..3, 8..11 and 16..19, fold those into a 12-bit index with (v & 0xffff) | (v >> 12), and read the palette byte at rgb444_lut[index]. That byte is what gets stored to EDI.
Each row loads BX with the row width from DAT_00070024 and decodes command bytes until BX is exactly zero. A command byte's low six bits give len = (byte & 0x3f) + 1, in 1..64, and its top two bits select the op:
  0b00 RLE fill -- read one stream byte, write its blended colour to len pixels with REP STOSB; BX -= len.
  0b01 stretched fill -- read one stream byte, write its blended colour to len pixels spaced two apart with the first landing at EDI+1, leaving the pixels in between untouched; BX -= 2*len.
  0b10 literal copy -- for each of len stream bytes write its blended colour; BX -= len.
  0b11 backdrop tint -- consume no stream byte; for len pixels read the pixel already at EDI, blend the tint into it and write it back; BX -= len. This is the op that fdps_blit_rle_passthrough, fdps_rle_blit_with_palette_remap and the kernel at 0x00057916 implement instead as a transparent skip (ADD EDI,ECX).
ECX carries every run length for REP and LOOP only because the dispatcher zeroed it, and the pixel byte indexes the tables cleanly only because EAX is re-zeroed before each load. When BX reaches zero the row ends: EDI += DAT_00070030, the remaining-row counter DAT_00070022 is decremented, and the outer loop reloads BX from DAT_00070024 for the next row. The routine returns when DAT_00070022 reaches zero.

Parameters:
  none on the stack -- the inputs arrive in registers and globals prepared by fdps_blit_dispatch:
  ESI -- base of the RLE command byte stream, pointing past the caller's header.
  EDI -- destination address of the first pixel of the first row, in an 8bpp linear surface.
  EDX -- pitch - width, saved to DAT_00070030 and added to EDI at the end of every row.
  EBP -- the dispatcher's frame pointer; [EBP+0x1c] is its sixth argument, the pointer to the blend descriptor described above, and [EBP+8..0x1c] are then reused as scratch.
  DAT_00070024 -- row width in pixels, reloaded once per row.
  DAT_00070022 -- number of rows still to draw, decremented once per row.

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are all left modified, DAT_00070030 is overwritten, and the caller's argument slots [EBP+8] through [EBP+0x1c] are destroyed; fdps_blit_dispatch survives that because it reads none of them after the call and unwinds through POPs.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; the only caller is fdps_blit_dispatch, and DAT_00070022/DAT_00070024/DAT_00070030 are that dispatcher's blit parameter block, not library state]

Rebuild note:
The 0b11 op here is not the transparent skip it is in the rest of the family: it reads each destination pixel back and blends the tint into it, so the backdrop inside the sprite's bounding box is tinted as well as the sprite. Writing the family's obvious 'advance past transparent runs' body leaves an untinted hole in the shape of the sprite's transparency. In the same vein the 0b01 stretched fill writes its first pixel at EDI+1 rather than EDI while consuming 2*len columns of row width, so a straightforward for (i = 0; i < len; i++) dst[i*2] = c is off by one pixel. The consequence is visible, not theoretical: this kernel is the battle map's movement-range highlight, so a transparent-skip body would leave the highlight tinting only the opaque pixels of each map tile and not the tile as a whole.

=== 00057883 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP filler inside the address range of FUN_00057793

=== 000578c7 [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler (90 90 90) in a gap inside FUN_00057793's address span; no refs, no code reaches it.

=== 00057916 [PLATE]
Blit mode 11: decodes an RLE 4-op sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface, alpha-blending every pixel it draws with one constant palette colour and leaving the transparent runs untouched.

Algorithm:
On entry EDX, the end-of-row advance, is spilled to DAT_00070030 because the body needs EDX as scratch. [EBP+0x1c] -- fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument, still live in its frame -- points at a four-dword tint descriptor {blend_table, alpha, rgb444_lut, tint_color}. Those fields are unpacked into the dispatcher's own argument slots, which this routine reuses as scratch: [EBP+0x08] = rgb444_lut, and [EBP+0x14] = 0x000f0f0f and [EBP+0x18] = 0x0000ffff are the two fold masks.
blend_table is the [18][256] dword table fdps_build_palette_tables writes at 000653f0: each entry is a palette colour packed one 4-bit channel per byte and pre-multiplied by that row's weight, rows 0..8 carrying weights 0..8 and rows 9..17 the complementary 16..8. alpha (0..16) is folded so both row indices stay in 0..8: for alpha <= 8 the constant colour reads row alpha ([EBP+0x0c]) and the sprite pixels read row 9+alpha ([EBP+0x10]); for alpha > 8 alpha is replaced by 16-alpha and the two rows swap. Either way the constant colour ends up weighted by alpha and the sprite pixel by 16-alpha. blend_table[tint_row][tint_color] is fetched once and parked in [EBP+0x1c].
Each row reloads the row width from DAT_00070024 into BX and then consumes command bytes from ESI until BX is exactly zero. The top two bits of the command byte select the op and the low six carry len-1, so len = (cmd & 0x3f) + 1, i.e. 1..64:
  00 fill      -- one pixel byte from the stream, blended once, REP STOSB over len destination bytes; width -= len.
  01 stretched -- one pixel byte, blended once, written into every second destination byte across a 2*len span (INC EDI then STOSB), so the even byte of each pair keeps what was there; width -= 2*len.
  10 literal   -- len pixel bytes from the stream, each blended and stored in turn; width -= len.
  11 skip      -- EDI += len with no write, a transparent run that leaves the backdrop as it was; width -= len. This op is what separates mode 11 from the otherwise identical mode 10 kernel fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop at 00057793, whose fourth op blends the destination byte instead of skipping it.
Blending one pixel index p is blend_table[pixel_row][p] plus the parked constant, shifted right by 4 (dividing out the /16 of the weights) and masked with 0x000f0f0f, which leaves 4 bits per channel at bits 0..3, 8..11 and 16..19; those are folded into a 12-bit index by (v & 0xffff) | (v >> 12), and the index selects the output byte from the 4096-entry inverse-palette table rgb444_lut. This is the same blend and fold that fdps_blit_tint_rect performs on an uncompressed rectangle.
At the end of a row EDI takes the advance saved in DAT_00070030 and the row counter at DAT_00070022 is decremented; the routine returns once that counter reaches zero.
Three NOPs sit at 00057a06 and three more at 00057a4a, right after the two-byte short JMPs at 00057a04 and 00057a48 (eb 5a 90 90 90 and eb 16 90 90 90), matching the NOP quartets that pad branch targets inside the body. They are unreachable filler, not a boundary problem.

Where it is used:
Exactly one call site in the whole image selects mode 11: 0002d198 in fdps_draw_map_unit, which draws a battle-map unit's 0x18 x 0x18 cell with alpha 8 and tint_color 0, taken when bit 0x80 of the unit's flag byte at record offset 5 is set. That bit is the acted-this-turn flag -- fdps_battle_mark_unit_done ORs it in and fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase tests it -- so on screen this kernel is what makes a unit that has already moved appear blended half-way into palette colour 0. fdps_draw_map_unit fills the descriptor's blend_table and rgb444_lut slots once at entry (0002cdbe, 0002cdc5) and writes the tint_color slot only on this path (0002d15a); its mode 9 calls leave that fourth slot alone because fdps_rle_blit_translucent reads only the first three fields.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. This is hand-written assembly; every input arrives in a register, in a global or in the caller's live frame, all set up by fdps_blit_dispatch immediately before the call:
    ESI          -- RLE command stream, advanced in place past the bytes it consumes
    EDI          -- destination pixel pointer, advanced in place
    EDX          -- end-of-row advance, computed by the caller as pitch - width
    [EBP+0x1c]   -- fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument: pointer to {uint *blend_table, int alpha, uchar *rgb444_lut, int tint_color}
    DAT_00070024 -- u16 row width in pixels, reloaded at the top of every row
    DAT_00070022 -- u16 rows remaining, decremented to zero by this routine

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, and so are the caller's argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x1c].

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; sole caller is fdps_blit_dispatch; shares the blit state globals]

Rebuild note:
This kernel is not an ordinary C function: it runs on fdps_blit_dispatch's frame and uses that function's own argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x1c] as its scratch, and it destroys EBX, ESI and EDI, which Watcom's convention says a callee preserves. Rewriting it as a plain C routine taking (stream, dest, descriptor) and calling it from a rebuilt fdps_blit_dispatch that still reads its own arguments after the call gives the wrong result. alpha is also unchecked -- 16-alpha is formed by SUB ECX,0x10 / NEG ECX with no clamp, so any value above 16 indexes blend_table below its base. And the fourth descriptor field belongs to the tint kernels alone: fdps_draw_map_unit never writes it on its mode 9 calls, so declaring one descriptor struct and dutifully initialising all four fields at every call site is not what the original does.

=== 00057a06 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP run: alignment filler in a gap inside FUN_00057916's address range

=== 00057a4a [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler inside the FUN_00057916 address range

=== 00057a74 [PLATE]
Blit mode 0x0c: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface as a translucent sprite, but only for the pixels whose palette index falls inside a caller-configured colour range; every pixel outside that range is written through opaque. Nothing in the shipped executable selects this mode.

Algorithm:
Entered by a plain CALL from fdps_blit_dispatch with that function's registers and stack frame still live and no prologue of its own: ESI = the RLE command stream, EDI = the first destination pixel, EDX = pitch - width (the end-of-row advance), EBP = the dispatcher's frame pointer.

Setup, once. EDX is parked in the dword global at 00070030. [EBP+0x1c], the dispatcher's arg6, points at a five-field blend descriptor the caller built on its own stack:
  +0x00  base of the brightness ramp table that fdps_build_palette_tables fills at 000653f0 -- 18 rows of 256 dwords, row j holding every palette colour packed with red in bits 16-19, green in 8-11 and blue in 0-3 and scaled by coefficient j (row 0 is zero, row 1 is the unscaled colour).
  +0x04  blend level, 0..16.
  +0x08  base of the 16x16x16 inverse-palette cube at 000643f0, 4096 bytes mapping a 4-bit-per-channel colour back to a palette index.
  +0x0c  low palette index of the range that gets blended; only the low 16 bits are read, and they are copied to the word at 00070050.
  +0x10  high palette index of that range, likewise 16 bits, copied to the word at 00070052.
The first three fields and the code that consumes them are fdps_rle_blit_translucent's, instruction for instruction: from the level it picks the two ramp rows that weight the two pixels -- for level <= 8 the source pixel is weighted by row level+9 and the destination by row level; above 8 the roles swap around row 16-level, so nine rows of coefficients cover all seventeen ratios. The paired coefficients sum to 16, which is what makes the later >> 4 a weighted average instead of a carry between channels, so level is the destination's share of the blend in sixteenths -- fdps_draw_composite_sprite builds the same descriptor at 000141f0 and sets this field to 16 minus the sprite part's opacity word at part+7. The two row addresses land in [EBP+0x0c] and [EBP+0x10], the channel mask 0x0f0f0f in [EBP+0x14], 0xffff in [EBP+0x18] and the cube base in [EBP+0x08] -- all of them fdps_blit_dispatch's own argument slots, used here as scratch.

Rows. Each row loads the column count from the word at 00070024 into BX and decodes command bytes from ESI until BX is exactly zero. The low six bits of a command byte give len = (cmd & 0x3f) + 1 (1..64) and the top two bits select the op:
  00 fill      -- one pixel byte follows; out of range it is REP STOSBed across len columns, in range each of the len destination pixels is blended with it in turn; BX -= len.
  01 stretched -- one pixel byte follows, written into every other column across a 2*len span starting at EDI+1 and leaving the columns in between as they were, blended the same way when in range; BX -= 2*len.
  10 literal   -- len pixel bytes follow, each range-tested and either stored or blended on its own; BX -= len.
  11 skip      -- no bytes follow; EDI += len leaves those columns untouched; BX -= len.
The range test is lo <= pixel <= hi against the two words at 00070050/00070052, done as signed 16-bit compares on the zero-extended pixel byte; the fill and stretched ops test their single pixel byte once and take a separate loop for each answer, the literal op tests every byte.
Blending one pixel: EAX = ramp_src[source pixel] + ramp_dst[*EDI], then >> 4 and & 0x0f0f0f, leaving one 4-bit channel in the low nibble of each of the three bytes; those nibbles are folded into a 12-bit index as green<<8 | red<<4 | blue and the byte read from the inverse-palette cube at that index is what gets stored.
At the end of a row EDI advances by the value parked at 00070030, the row counter at 00070022 is decremented in place, and the row loop restarts with a fresh column count; the routine returns when that counter reaches zero. The NOP runs and the three-byte gaps after the short jumps are branch-target padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. This is hand-written assembly and every input arrives in a register, a global or the caller's frame, all of them set up by fdps_blit_dispatch immediately before the CALL:
    ESI          -- RLE command stream, advanced in place past the bytes it consumes
    EDI          -- destination pixel pointer, advanced in place
    EDX          -- end-of-row advance, computed by the caller as pitch - width
    [EBP+0x1c]   -- pointer to the blend descriptor described above (the dispatcher's arg6)
    DAT_00070024 -- u16 columns per row, reloaded at the top of every row
    DAT_00070022 -- u16 rows remaining, decremented to zero by this routine
  Unlike the mode 0 kernel at 00056a0d it does not need ECX zeroed on entry; it does XOR ECX,ECX itself at 00057ad6.

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, as are the caller's argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x1c], and the globals at 00070022, 00070030, 00070050 and 00070052 are left holding this call's state.

Reachability: unreachable in the shipped executable. fdps_blit_dispatch is the only entry, it selects this kernel only when its mode argument is 0x0c, and no path in the program produces that value -- see the open_question field for the trace. The two range globals 00070050/00070052 are written and read by this function alone, so nothing else in the program observes its state either. The behaviour above therefore rests entirely on the instructions; no play-test can exercise it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it shares fdps_blit_dispatch's stack frame and blit state globals and is reached only from that dispatcher's mode == 0x0c arm]

Rebuild note:
The 12-bit inverse-palette index is folded green-major: after the & 0x0f0f0f the code ORs (packed >> 12) into (packed & 0xffff), putting green in bits 8-11, red in 4-7 and blue in 0-3, so the lookup is cube[g*256 + r*16 + b]. Writing the obvious cube[r*256 + g*16 + b] gives wrong colours, and it keeps giving them unless the cube generator is changed to match -- fdps_build_palette_tables fills 000643f0 in exactly that green-outer, red-middle, blue-inner order (loops at 0002b11a/0002b134/0002b144, arguments pushed at 0002b16a/0002b175). Second trap: the routine uses fdps_blit_dispatch's own argument slots [EBP+0x08..0x1c] as scratch, overwriting src, dst, width, height and pitch; a rewrite that keeps those as ordinary C locals and reads any of them after the blit gets the original values where the assembly has none. Third: no call site selects mode 0x0c, so this kernel's correctness cannot be established by playing the game whichever way a rebuild treats it -- keeping it earns no play-test coverage, and the only check available is reading it against the original.

=== 00057b1b [EOL]

=== 00057b8a [EOL]

=== 00057bcd [EOL]

=== 00057c36 [EOL]
Three 0x90 NOP filler bytes inside FUN_00057a74, between a short jmp and the next branch target at 00057c39.
